atoms.lesson: A one-hour response target is worth little when response means an automated acknowledgement. Define severity by business impact with concrete examples, such as production unavailable to all users for severity one and a core function degraded with no workaround for severity two. Then set separate clocks for acknowledgement, workaround and permanent fix, state whether they run in business hours or continuously, and say who may raise or lower a severity rating.

name: liability-cap-analysis
description: Sets and defends limitation of liability positions covering caps, carve-outs, excluded heads of loss and super-caps. Use when a counterparty proposes unlimited liability for a risk, when someone asks whether a cap is adequate for the deal value, or when a claim has arisen and exposure needs mapping. Covers aggregate versus annual caps and how they interact with indemnities and insurance.
expansions: they want unlimited liability for data breach
is this cap big enough
per claim or aggregate cap
carve outs keep expanding
super cap for confidentiality breach
consequential loss exclusion wording
cap versus insurance limits mismatch
claim came in what is our exposure

atoms.obligation: State whether the cap is aggregate across the term or resets annually, and fix the reference amount precisely.
atoms.lesson: Fee-based caps differ enormously depending on wording. Fees paid in the twelve months preceding the claim is the usual landing point; fees paid under this agreement grows steadily over a long term; total contract value is far larger because it includes unpaid future fees. Separately decide whether the cap is a single pot covering all claims or resets each contract year, which on a five-year deal is a fivefold difference in worst-case exposure.

atoms.obligation: Check that every carve-out from the cap is either legally required or matched by insurance or a funded indemnity.
atoms.lesson: Death and personal injury, fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation cannot be capped in most jurisdictions, so those carve-outs are unobjectionable. Negotiated carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection, intellectual property infringement and wilful misconduct should be tested against the policy: if the professional indemnity or cyber cover responds to five million, an uncapped data carve-out leaves the difference on the balance sheet. Super-caps at a multiple of fees are the usual compromise.

atoms.obligation: Confirm the excluded loss list does not remove the direct losses the customer realistically expects to recover.
atoms.lesson: Standard exclusions for indirect and consequential loss are unremarkable, but suppliers append loss of profit, revenue, savings, goodwill, data and business opportunity, sometimes qualified as whether direct or indirect. For a customer the realistic heads of loss are wasted expenditure, the cost of procuring replacement services and regulatory fines, so preserve those expressly. Remember that consequential loss carries a narrow technical meaning in English law and covers less than people assume.

atoms.obligation: Make the liability position symmetrical unless there is a stated reason for the imbalance that survives explanation.
atoms.lesson: One-sided caps invite escalation and slow deals down. A supplier capping its own liability at fees while leaving the customer uncapped should expect a mutuality argument it will usually lose, costing a negotiation round. The exceptions worth defending are payment obligations, which are conventionally excluded from the cap on both sides, and customer indemnities for its own content, data or instructions, which are genuinely different in kind from performance risk.

name: indemnity-clause-drafting
description: Drafts and reviews indemnities covering intellectual property infringement, data incidents and third-party claims, together with the procedure that makes them work. Use when a counterparty asks to be indemnified, when a third-party claim letter arrives and nobody knows who defends it, or when an indemnity looks broad but has no conduct of claim mechanism attached.
expansions: they want a broad indemnity
customer received an infringement letter
who controls the defence of the claim
indemnity has no notice procedure
cross indemnity for employee claims
indemnify defend and hold harmless
indemnity survives termination or not
open source claim under our licence

atoms.obligation: Attach a conduct of claim procedure to every indemnity covering notice, control of the defence and settlement consent.
atoms.lesson: An indemnity without procedure is unusable in practice. Specify prompt written notice, with late notice reducing recovery only to the extent of actual prejudice rather than voiding the whole indemnity; which party controls the defence and appoints counsel; the indemnified party right to participate at its own cost; and that no settlement admitting fault or imposing non-monetary obligations may be agreed without the other party consent.

atoms.obligation: Limit the infringement indemnity to the supplier own materials and preserve the full remedy ladder for the customer.
atoms.lesson: An intellectual property indemnity should cover claims that supplier deliverables infringe third-party rights, with conventional exclusions for customer-supplied specifications, unauthorised modification, combination with other products and continued use after notice. The remedy ladder of procuring the right to continue, modifying to become non-infringing, or refunding on termination must not allow the supplier to jump straight to a refund and strand the customer halfway through a deployment.

atoms.obligation: Keep indemnities anchored to third-party claims unless a first-party loss is deliberately intended and priced.
atoms.lesson: Broad drafting such as indemnify against all losses arising from breach turns every contractual failure into an indemnity claim, bypassing the usual controls of mitigation, remoteness and sometimes the liability cap itself. Anchor indemnities to claims brought by third parties. Where a first-party indemnity is genuinely wanted, for example regulatory fines following a data incident, say so explicitly and confirm whether it sits inside or outside the agreed cap.

atoms.obligation: Confirm the indemnity survives termination, state for how long, and set the deadline for notifying a claim.
atoms.lesson: Infringement and confidentiality indemnities that expire at termination are worthless, because such claims usually surface after deployment. List indemnities expressly in the survival clause and consider a long stop for notification, either matching the limitation period or a negotiated shorter window of two or three years. Check consistency, because a survival clause referring to clause numbers breaks silently once clauses are renumbered in a later draft.

name: ip-ownership-terms
description: Allocates intellectual property in services, development and collaboration deals across background rights, newly created deliverables, licences and feedback. Use when a customer demands ownership of everything produced, when engineers ask whether a component built for one client can be reused, or when a joint development term sheet needs an ownership structure.
expansions: customer wants to own all deliverables
can we reuse this component elsewhere
background ip not defined anywhere
joint ownership proposal on the table
feedback and improvements clause
open source in the deliverable
assignment versus perpetual licence
contractor built it who owns it

atoms.obligation: Separate pre-existing materials from newly created deliverables and licence the first rather than assigning it.
atoms.lesson: Suppliers cannot assign what they reuse across clients, meaning frameworks, libraries, methodologies and templates. Define background rights as anything created before the engagement or independently of it, retain ownership, and grant a perpetual non-exclusive licence to use it to the extent embedded in the deliverables. Without this split, a broad assignment of all work product arguably transfers the supplier toolkit and blocks the very next project it wins.

atoms.obligation: Avoid joint ownership and choose sole ownership with a broad licence back to the other party instead.
atoms.lesson: Joint ownership behaves differently by jurisdiction: in England each co-owner needs the other consent to license or assign, while in the United States either co-owner may license non-exclusively without accounting to the other. That divergence makes jointly owned rights a source of deadlock and unexpected competition. The workable structure is one named owner with the other receiving a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide licence for defined purposes, plus field-of-use limits where the parties compete.

atoms.obligation: Confirm that everyone who touched the deliverable has actually assigned rights, including contractors and moral rights.
atoms.lesson: An assignment from a company is only as good as its chain of title. Work created by employees in the course of employment generally vests in the employer, but contractor and freelance output does not and stays with the individual absent a written assignment. Check that subcontractor agreements contain present-tense assignment language rather than a promise to assign, and include waivers of moral rights where permitted, since those cannot be assigned in most European systems.

atoms.obligation: Narrow feedback and improvement clauses so they do not capture customer data or rights derived from it.
atoms.lesson: Vendor templates take a perpetual licence to any feedback plus rights in improvements and usage data. Feedback licences are usually acceptable when limited to suggestions about the product itself. The problematic clauses claim rights over customer content, aggregated or anonymised outputs, or models trained on customer material. Limit the grant to de-identified operational metrics, prohibit identifying the customer as a source, and exclude anything capable of re-identification.

name: dpa-data-protection-review
description: Reviews data processing addenda, controller and processor role allocation and international transfer mechanisms. Use when a vendor sends its addendum for signature, when a customer asks where personal data will be hosted or accessed, or when a new subprocessor notification arrives. Covers role mapping, transfer tools, subprocessor objection rights and breach notification timing.
expansions: vendor sent their dpa to sign
where is the data actually hosted
new subprocessor notification arrived
are we controller or processor here
transfer impact assessment needed
breach notification within how long
audit rights the vendor refuses
deletion at end of contract

atoms.obligation: Map the actual data flows to controller, joint controller or processor roles before accepting the labels in the template.
atoms.lesson: Templates assert roles rather than analyse them. The test is who decides the purposes and means of processing. A payroll bureau following instructions is a processor, while an analytics provider that decides what to measure and reuses data to improve its own product is a controller for that activity, and both roles can coexist within one service. Mislabelling a controller as a processor produces meaningless instruction clauses and leaves both parties exposed on lawful basis and transparency.

atoms.obligation: Identify every country where data will be stored or accessed, including remote support, and fix the transfer mechanism.
atoms.lesson: Hosting location is only half the picture, because round-the-clock support from a third country is a transfer even when data never leaves the European region at rest. Standard contractual clauses need the correct module for the relationship, annexes completed with real detail rather than placeholders, and a documented transfer impact assessment where local access laws are relevant. For United Kingdom flows, add the international data transfer addendum to the European clauses.

atoms.obligation: Require prior notice of new subprocessors with a right to object and a chain of equivalent contractual obligations.
atoms.lesson: General authorisation with a notice period is the workable middle ground, since case-by-case consent is unrealistic for cloud services and blanket authorisation with no notice is unacceptable. Ask for a maintained public list, at least thirty days notice of additions, a right to object on reasonable data protection grounds, and a stated consequence, usually termination of the affected service without penalty. Confirm the vendor remains fully liable for its subprocessors acts.

atoms.obligation: Set breach notification without undue delay with a stated maximum in hours and specify the minimum content required.
atoms.lesson: A processor must notify the controller without undue delay, but a vague promise to act promptly gives the controller no realistic chance of meeting its own seventy-two hour regulatory deadline. Push for an outer limit of twenty-four to forty-eight hours from becoming aware, and define the content: categories and approximate numbers of records affected, likely consequences, measures taken, and a named contact, with rolling updates rather than one late complete report.

name: export-sanctions-screening
description: Screens counterparties, end users and destinations for sanctions and export control exposure before a contract is signed or goods move. Use when a new customer sits in or ships to a restricted jurisdiction, when an owner appears on a designated list, or when someone asks whether a licence is needed. Covers ownership thresholds, classification, end-use checks and contractual protection.
expansions: new customer in a sanctioned region
shareholder appears on a list
do we need an export licence
end user certificate requested
payment routed through unexpected bank
freight forwarder flagged the destination
dual use classification unclear
add sanctions clause to the contract

atoms.obligation: Screen the counterparty, its owners, its directors and the end user, not simply the name printed on the contract.
atoms.lesson: Ownership rules bite well below the surface. Designated persons holding fifty per cent or more, aggregated across several listed owners, make the entity itself restricted under United States and European Union rules, and the United Kingdom and European Union also capture control regardless of percentage. Screen beneficial owners, directors, the consignee, the ultimate end user and the carrier or vessel, and re-screen at renewal and before each shipment, since designations change weekly.

atoms.obligation: Classify the goods, software or technology against the control lists before assuming that no licence is required.
atoms.lesson: Export control turns on classification, not on how ordinary an item feels. Dual-use items with civilian and military application, encryption above threshold strengths, and certain sensor, aerospace or materials technology carry control numbers triggering licences for specific destinations. Technology transfer counts too: sending a specification to a foreign engineer or granting remote access to controlled software is an export. Record the classification rationale, because regulators ask for the analysis rather than the conclusion.

atoms.obligation: Include suspension and termination rights that operate immediately if a counterparty or end user becomes designated.
atoms.lesson: A workable sanctions clause gives an immediate right to suspend performance and terminate without liability if a party, its owners or its end users become designated, if a licence is refused or revoked, or if performance would breach applicable restrictions. Add an obligation to notify ownership changes, a prohibition on re-export to restricted destinations, and an acknowledgement that non-performance on these grounds is not a breach giving rise to damages.

atoms.obligation: Escalate red flags for compliance review rather than resolving them commercially, and document the decision either way.
atoms.lesson: The classic indicators are payment arriving from an unrelated third country, a customer indifferent to price or delivery timing, a residential or freight-forwarder delivery address, an end user unwilling to sign a use statement, and requests to split shipments below reporting thresholds. Any of these needs review before the order proceeds. Retain the screening record, the reasoning that cleared each hit and the approval, since five years is a common retention expectation.

name: anti-bribery-diligence
description: Runs anti-bribery and corruption diligence on intermediaries such as agents, resellers, distributors, consultants and joint venture partners. Use when the business wants to appoint a local agent, when a commission rate looks unusual, or when a partner asks to be paid into an offshore account. Covers red flag assessment, contractual controls, training and ongoing monitoring.
expansions: appointing a local sales agent
commission rate looks very high
partner wants offshore payment account
government customer through a middleman
gift and hospitality question
facilitation payment requested at port
renew the distributor with no review
who actually owns this consultancy

atoms.obligation: Establish who the intermediary is connected to in government or the customer before agreeing any commercial terms.
atoms.lesson: The exposure in agency relationships is that a principal becomes liable for bribes paid on its behalf. Diligence should identify beneficial owners, whether any owner, director or close relative is a public official or politically exposed person, whether the customer itself recommended the agent, and what the agent will actually do for its fee. An agent with no office, no staff and no track record but excellent access is the archetypal conduit.

atoms.obligation: Test whether the fee is proportionate to services genuinely performed and capable of being documented.
atoms.lesson: Success fees far above local market rates, payment into a jurisdiction unconnected with the work, invoices carrying no description of services, demands for advance payment before any activity, and pressure to sign before diligence completes are the recurring red flags. Require the agent to describe deliverables, keep contemporaneous records and invoice against them. Payment mechanics matter too: pay in the country of performance into the contracting entity own account.

atoms.obligation: Include audit, certification and immediate termination rights in every intermediary agreement, and actually exercise them.
atoms.lesson: Contractual controls should cover a warranty of compliance with applicable anti-corruption laws, a prohibition on facilitation payments, no appointment of sub-agents without consent, an obligation to keep accurate books, an audit right on notice, annual written certification, mandatory training and immediate termination without compensation on credible suspicion of breach. Termination on suspicion rather than proof is the clause that matters, because proof rarely arrives in time to help.

atoms.obligation: Refuse facilitation payments and give staff a scripted response for demands at borders, ports and licensing offices.
atoms.lesson: Small payments to speed routine official action are illegal under United Kingdom law and only narrowly excepted elsewhere, and they are almost never recorded correctly in the books. Staff facing a demand should decline politely, explain that company policy and law prohibit it, ask for the request and any fee in writing on official paper, escalate to a named contact and record the incident. The only exception is genuine duress where personal safety is at risk, reported immediately afterwards.

name: insurance-certificate-review
description: Checks insurance requirements in contracts and verifies the certificates counterparties provide. Use when a supplier sends a certificate before mobilisation, when a customer demands limits that look unattainable, or when someone asks whether the cover would actually respond to the risk in the deal. Covers cover types, certificate defects, renewal tracking and endorsements.
expansions: supplier sent certificate of insurance
customer wants additional insured status
limits look higher than our policy
cyber cover required in the contract
waiver of subrogation requested
claims made versus occurrence policy
certificate expired last month
does professional indemnity cover this

atoms.obligation: Match the required cover types to the actual risk of the work rather than copying a standard schedule.
atoms.lesson: Professional indemnity responds to negligent advice or design, public liability to third-party injury and property damage, product liability to defective goods, and cyber to data incidents and business interruption from an attack, while employers liability is compulsory where staff work on site. A software vendor carrying a construction-style schedule with no cyber cover is insured against the wrong thing, and demanding marine cargo cover on a consultancy wastes negotiation time.

atoms.obligation: Check the certificate for insured entity, policy period, limit basis and cover trigger before mobilisation begins.
atoms.lesson: A certificate is evidence, not the policy. Verify that the insured is the contracting entity rather than a parent or a similarly named affiliate, that the period covers the whole engagement, whether limits apply per claim or in the aggregate, since an aggregate limit already eroded by other claims may leave nothing, and whether cover is claims-made, which means it must be maintained in run-off after completion, commonly for six years.

atoms.obligation: Require renewal evidence automatically and diarise expiry instead of discovering a lapse when a claim arises.
atoms.lesson: Insurance obligations decay quietly. Suppliers change insurer, cut limits at renewal to save premium, or let cover lapse when cash is tight, and nobody notices until an incident. Impose an obligation to provide renewal certificates within a set number of days of each renewal and to notify any cancellation, reduction or material change. Track expiry dates centrally and treat a missing certificate as a suspension trigger for high-risk or on-site work.

atoms.obligation: Understand what additional insured status and a subrogation waiver actually deliver before demanding or conceding them.
atoms.lesson: Additional insured status extends the supplier liability cover to claims made against the customer arising from the supplier work, which helps when a third party sues both parties together. It is common on liability policies and generally unavailable on professional indemnity. A waiver of subrogation prevents the insurer suing the other party after paying a claim, and it must be endorsed on the policy, because a contractual promise alone does not bind the insurer.

name: termination-exit-terms
description: Structures termination rights and exit arrangements including transition assistance, data return and surviving obligations. Use when planning an exit from an incumbent supplier, when drafting termination clauses in a new agreement, or when a counterparty has served notice and someone needs to know what happens next week. Covers notice, cure periods, exit plans and certified deletion.
expansions: supplier served termination notice
exiting the incumbent next year
termination for convenience fee
transition assistance not defined
get our data back in what format
cure period for material breach
wind down of in flight orders
what survives after termination

atoms.obligation: Separate termination for convenience, for breach and on insolvency, each with its own notice period and consequences.
atoms.lesson: Collapsing these into a single clause causes confusion at the worst possible moment. Convenience needs a notice period and, where the supplier invested upfront, an early termination charge tied to unrecovered costs rather than lost profit. Breach needs a materiality standard and a cure period, commonly thirty days, with immediate rights for non-curable breaches. Insolvency clauses need care, because automatic termination on a filing is unenforceable under some restructuring regimes.

atoms.obligation: Define exit assistance concretely by duration, scope, rate and the duty to cooperate with a successor supplier.
atoms.lesson: A promise of reasonable assistance produces a hostage negotiation on the day. Specify a transition period the customer may extend, often up to twelve months at existing rates or a stated uplift, an exit plan maintained during the term and refreshed annually, named roles who remain available, an express obligation to cooperate with the replacement supplier, and continuation of the service at existing service levels throughout the whole transition.

atoms.obligation: Fix the format, timing and cost of data return, then require certified deletion of remaining copies.
atoms.lesson: Data extraction is where exits fail. Agree the format in advance as a documented machine-readable structure with a schema rather than screenshots or a proprietary dump, plus a delivery deadline, a number of extraction runs included at no charge, and a secure transfer method. Then require deletion of remaining copies including backups within a stated window that allows for backup rotation, with written certification and any legally required retention identified explicitly.

atoms.obligation: Check the survival clause names every obligation that must outlive the agreement, by concept and not only by number.
atoms.lesson: Confidentiality, ownership and licences, indemnities, liability limits, payment for services already rendered, audit and record retention, dispute resolution and governing law should all survive. Two traps recur: survival clauses listing clause numbers that shift when a draft is renumbered, and perpetual licences drafted so they terminate with the agreement, stranding a customer that relies on delivered materials. Read the survival clause against final numbering immediately before signature.

name: renewal-notice-calendar
description: Tracks automatic renewal dates, notice deadlines and evergreen terms so decisions get made deliberately rather than by default. Use when someone asks whether a contract can still be cancelled this year, when building a renewal calendar across a portfolio, or when a supplier claims the notice window has already closed.
expansions: can we still cancel this year
auto renewed before anyone noticed
notice deadline is next month
build a renewal calendar for the portfolio
supplier says window has closed
ninety days before anniversary date
evergreen term with rolling extensions
budget season needs renewal list

atoms.obligation: Record the notice deadline as an actual date rather than a duration, and set reminders well ahead of it.
atoms.lesson: Storing ninety days before the end of the initial term leaves the arithmetic to be done at exactly the wrong moment. Compute and store the real deadline date, then work backwards to decision milestones: a review trigger perhaps one hundred and eighty days out for material spend, a business decision at one hundred and twenty, and notice served with days in hand. Most missed renewals are calendar failures rather than decision failures.

atoms.obligation: Read the notice mechanics precisely, covering method, recipient, address and when notice is deemed received.
atoms.lesson: Notice clauses defeat correct decisions. Requirements often specify a registered address, a named role such as the general counsel, a delivery method of recorded post or courier and sometimes email followed by hard copy, plus deemed receipt rules that add days to the timetable. Email to an account manager is usually not valid notice. Check the registered address still matches the public record, since a counterparty relocation invalidates an otherwise perfect letter.

atoms.obligation: Establish whether renewal extends the agreement by the original term or by a shorter rolling period.
atoms.lesson: The consequence of missing a deadline depends entirely on the renewal shape. A three-year agreement renewing for a further three years turns an administrative slip into a large committed spend, while the same slip on a monthly rolling term costs one month. Capture the renewal length, whether renewals are unlimited or capped in number, and whether price changes on renewal, because those three fields determine how urgent the deadline really is.

atoms.obligation: Confirm the current contractual position in writing whenever a counterparty asserts the notice window has passed.
atoms.lesson: Late notice disputes turn on the paper trail. Retrieve the executed version and every amendment, since a variation may have reset the term or altered the notice period; check whether the counterparty accepted late notice previously, which supports waiver or estoppel arguments; and look for any good faith negotiation obligation. Where the window genuinely closed, negotiate a shortened final term or an exit on payment rather than conceding a full further period.

name: obligation-tracking-handover
description: Extracts post-signature obligations from an executed agreement and hands them to the teams who must perform them. Use immediately after signature, when a new contract manager takes over an account, or when someone asks what the company actually committed to do. Covers reporting duties, milestones, conditional notifications and the rights the company holds but never uses.
expansions: what did we commit to in this deal
handover after signature to delivery
quarterly reporting obligation missed
new account manager needs briefing
audit right we never exercised
price review window this quarter
minimum volume commitment tracking
customer says we breached clause nine

atoms.obligation: List every obligation with an owner, a trigger and a due date, separating recurring duties from one-off ones.
atoms.lesson: Contracts contain three obligation types and each needs different handling. One-off duties such as delivering an implementation plan within thirty days need a fixed date. Recurring duties such as monthly reports, quarterly business reviews and annual certifications need a schedule. Conditional duties such as notifying a security incident within twenty-four hours or giving notice before subcontracting need a trigger description operational staff will actually recognise, because no calendar entry will ever fire for them.

atoms.obligation: Brief the people who must perform the obligations, not only the people who negotiated the agreement.
atoms.lesson: Negotiators move on and the obligations remain. A handover should give delivery, finance, security and procurement a plain-language summary of what they must do, the consequence of missing it, and where the executed document sits. Finance in particular needs the invoicing mechanics of milestone triggers, purchase order requirements, invoice content, payment terms and late payment interest, because most commercial disputes begin as rejected invoices rather than legal arguments.

atoms.obligation: Capture the rights the company holds as carefully as the duties it owes, including any exercise windows.
atoms.lesson: Negotiated rights go unused because nobody tracks them: audit rights, benchmarking clauses permitting a price review at defined intervals, most-favoured-customer terms, service credit entitlements, step-in rights and rights to test disaster recovery arrangements. Several are time limited or exercisable only inside a window. Record them alongside obligations with their trigger dates, so the value won at signature is actually collected during the term rather than quietly forfeited.

atoms.obligation: Record where the executed version lives and which amendments are in force before advising on any term.
atoms.lesson: Operational teams routinely work from the last draft they were emailed rather than the signed version, and side letters, order forms and change orders that vary it often sit with whoever signed them. Before answering a question about an obligation, confirm the executed original, list every amendment in date order and note which clauses each one varied. Disputes frequently reveal that the two parties have been performing different documents for months.

name: contract-intake-triage
description: Runs the legal request queue by capturing what is being asked, routing it and setting expectations. Use when requests arrive by direct message and disappear, when the team needs a self-service intake process, or when someone asks why a review is taking so long. Covers required intake fields, risk-based routing, published turnaround times and visible status.
expansions: requests keep arriving by chat
who is handling this contract
turnaround time expectations unclear
build an intake form for legal
prioritise the queue this week
sales says legal is the bottleneck
template request or full review
missing information delays everything

atoms.obligation: Require the counterparty document, deal value, deadline and business owner before any review work begins.
atoms.lesson: Half the delay in contract review is the round trip to collect basics. A workable intake captures the counterparty legal name, what is being bought or sold, value and term, whether personal data or third-party rights are involved, the target signature date and the reason for it, the business owner, and whether the deal is on our paper or theirs. Incomplete requests should sit in a waiting state rather than joining the queue.

atoms.obligation: Route requests by risk and value, and let low-risk standard requests bypass legal review altogether.
atoms.lesson: Treating every request identically is how a legal team becomes the bottleneck. Tier the flow: a standard template on our paper below a value threshold with no edits goes straight to signature; a template with pre-approved fallbacks goes to a deal desk or a trained non-lawyer; counterparty paper, anything above the threshold, and anything touching personal data, intellectual property or regulated activity goes to a lawyer. Publish the tiers so requesters can predict the path.

atoms.obligation: Publish turnaround times by request type and measure performance against them instead of promising case by case.
atoms.lesson: The recurring conflict is expectation rather than speed. Stated service levels, for example two business days for a confidentiality agreement, five for a standard order form and ten for negotiated counterparty terms, with an expedited path requiring a named sponsor, let requesters plan and turn queue jumping into a visible decision rather than a private favour. Measure cycle time from complete intake and track separately how long requests wait on the business.

atoms.obligation: Give each request one visible status so nobody has to ask who is handling it or where it stands.
atoms.lesson: The most common complaint about legal operations is silence. Every request should carry a status the requester can see, such as awaiting information, in review, with counterparty, awaiting approval, ready for signature or executed, plus the assignee and the date of the last update. Visible ageing also exposes the real pattern, which is usually that a third of the queue is blocked on the business rather than on lawyers.

name: clause-playbook-maintenance
description: Builds and maintains the negotiation playbook of preferred wording, graded fallbacks and walk-away limits by clause. Use when the same clause is renegotiated from scratch every deal, when a new approval threshold is agreed, or when onboarding someone who needs the standard positions. Covers approver mapping, rationale, review cadence and version control.
expansions: same clause argued every single deal
write fallbacks for the deal desk
what is our walk away position
playbook is out of date
new approver for uncapped liability
who can approve this deviation
onboarding a new contracts manager
capture the position we just agreed

atoms.obligation: Give each clause a preferred position, two graded fallbacks and a walk-away, naming the approver for each step.
atoms.lesson: A playbook entry stating only the ideal position is unusable, because the negotiation happens below it. Write the preferred wording, a first fallback anyone may accept, a second fallback needing a manager, and the point beyond which approval must come from a named role such as the general counsel or finance director. Include the actual sentences to paste into a draft, not a prose description of the concession being contemplated.

atoms.obligation: Explain why each position exists so a negotiator can argue it rather than merely assert it on a call.
atoms.lesson: Negotiators concede positions they cannot justify. Each entry needs a short rationale, such as this cap matches our insurance limit, this audit frequency reflects a regulator expectation, or this hosting requirement follows from where the customer regulated records sit. The rationale also identifies when a position genuinely does not apply, which prevents the opposite failure of defending an irrelevant clause for three weeks on a very small deal.

atoms.obligation: Refresh the playbook from concluded deals on a fixed cadence instead of when somebody happens to remember.
atoms.lesson: Playbooks decay within about a year. Review quarterly against what was actually signed: a fallback conceded in most negotiations was never the real position and should be repositioned, while a clause that never attracted a single comment can move into the no-review tier. Track deviations at approval time so the data exists to review. Record the date and owner on each entry so users can see when a position was last tested.

atoms.obligation: Keep one authoritative version and withdraw superseded copies from circulation whenever a position changes.
atoms.lesson: The characteristic failure is three versions circulating and a deal signed on the oldest. Maintain a single source carrying a version number and effective date, communicate changes with a short note explaining what moved and why, and archive superseded versions where search will not surface them. When a position changes materially, check in-flight negotiations, because switching mid-negotiation needs a deliberate decision rather than a silent substitution.

name: signature-authority-execution
description: Gets documents signed correctly with the right signatory, the right formalities and a clean executed record. Use when someone asks who is authorised to sign, when a deed or a witnessed signature may be required, or when a counterparty questions whether an electronic signature is valid. Covers delegated authority, deed formalities, execution method and filing the final version.
expansions: who is authorised to sign this
does this need to be a deed
witness required for the signature
counterparty queried electronic signature
signature blocks name the wrong entity
board resolution needed before signing
executed copy never came back
power of attorney for the branch

atoms.obligation: Confirm the signatory holds authority for this value and subject matter before the document is routed for signature.
atoms.lesson: Authority comes from the delegation framework rather than from seniority. Check the schedule of authorities for the value band and contract type, confirm the signatory is an officer of the actual contracting entity rather than the group parent, and identify whether board or shareholder approval is needed, commonly for guarantees, security, related-party transactions or disposals. A signature outside internal authority often still binds externally, making it a control failure rather than an escape route.

atoms.obligation: Identify whether the document must be executed as a deed and apply the correct formalities to it.
atoms.lesson: Deeds are required where consideration is absent, covering guarantees, powers of attorney, releases and some assignments, and they carry a longer limitation period of twelve years rather than six in England. Execution differs: a company signs by two directors, or a director and the secretary, or one director whose signature is attested by a witness physically present. Errors here can render a guarantee unenforceable, and a witness should not be a spouse or a fellow signatory.

atoms.obligation: Check that electronic execution is permitted for this document type and in the counterparty jurisdiction before circulating.
atoms.lesson: Electronic signatures are valid for most commercial contracts across the United Kingdom, the European Union and the United States, and deeds can be signed electronically provided the witness observes the signing in person. Exceptions persist for land transactions, wills, certain statutory declarations, notarised documents and jurisdictions still requiring wet ink or a company seal for filings. Confirm before circulating, because re-executing a completed signature sequence costs days.

atoms.obligation: Complete signature blocks and dating before circulation, then file the fully executed version immediately afterwards.
atoms.lesson: Recurring defects are the wrong legal entity in the block, blank date fields left for someone to complete later, schedules referenced but never attached, manuscript amendments left uninitialled, and counterparts signed but never collated into one record. Date the agreement on the day the last party signs, since back-dating is misrepresentation whereas an agreed earlier effective date stated in the document is legitimate. Store the executed version where delivery teams will find it.

name: dispute-escalation-notice
description: Handles the early stage of a contractual dispute covering reservation of rights, breach notices, escalation ladders and pre-action correspondence. Use when a counterparty is not performing, when a demand letter arrives, or when someone wants to send a strongly worded email that should really be a formal notice. Covers cure periods, waiver risk, tiered dispute clauses and limitation deadlines.
expansions: supplier has missed three milestones
received a demand letter today
send a breach notice or not
reserve our rights without escalating
escalation ladder before arbitration
withhold payment while disputing
limitation period nearly expired
customer stopped paying invoices

atoms.obligation: Serve a formal breach notice identifying the clause, the failure and the cure period the agreement requires.
atoms.lesson: A valid notice states the specific obligation breached, the facts constituting the breach with dates, the cure period the contract allows, and the consequence of failing to cure. Vague complaints do not start the cure clock, so a later termination becomes challengeable. Serve by the contractual method to the contractual address, keep proof of delivery, and check whether a mandatory escalation or mediation step must be completed before notice can validly be given.

atoms.obligation: Preserve the position with an express reservation of rights before taking any step that might waive it.
atoms.lesson: Continuing to accept defective performance, paying disputed invoices without qualification, or agreeing revised dates can amount to affirmation and lose the right to terminate for that breach. Mark correspondence as without prejudice to rights and remedies, state that no waiver arises from continued performance, and read the no-waiver clause. Note that without prejudice privilege attaches only to genuine settlement discussions, not to any letter somebody has labelled that way.

atoms.obligation: Follow the contractual escalation ladder in order and record each step before commencing any formal proceedings.
atoms.lesson: Multi-tier clauses typically require named executives to meet within a set period, then mediation, before arbitration or court. Tribunals increasingly treat these tiers as conditions precedent, so skipping one risks a stay or dismissal and a costs order. Diarise each tier deadline, hold the meetings and minute attendance and outcome. Check whether the ladder suspends time limits, because some clauses require referral within a short period of the triggering event.

atoms.obligation: Check the statutory limitation period and any contractual claim deadline before advising on timing or tactics.
atoms.lesson: Limitation in England is six years for simple contracts and twelve for deeds, running from breach rather than from discovery, but many commercial agreements impose shorter windows such as claims notified within twelve or twenty-four months, or warranty claims within a defined period after completion. Missing a contractual notification deadline extinguishes an otherwise strong claim. Where time is short, a standstill agreement can preserve the position while negotiations continue.

name: outside-counsel-spend
description: Manages external law firm engagement and cost through matter scoping, billing guidelines, budgets and invoice review. Use when instructing a firm on a new matter, when an invoice exceeds the estimate, or when someone asks why legal spend jumped this quarter. Covers rate agreements, staffing controls, alternative fee arrangements and spend attribution.
expansions: instruct a firm on this matter
invoice came in over estimate
partner rate rose again this year
too many associates on the file
fixed fee for routine work
budget approval before they start
billing guidelines nobody follows
why did spend jump this quarter

atoms.obligation: Agree scope, staffing, budget and reporting cadence in writing before the firm begins any work.
atoms.lesson: Cost control happens at instruction, not at invoice. The engagement letter should record the specific question or matter, the deliverable expected, the named partner and the maximum seniority mix, the fee basis with a phased budget, the threshold above which further approval is required, and how often progress against budget will be reported. Firms accept these terms far more readily before a matter starts than after a team has been absorbed into it.

atoms.obligation: Use fixed or capped fees for predictable work and reserve hourly billing for genuinely uncertain matters.
atoms.lesson: Volume work such as standard filings, template reviews, routine employment advice and straightforward property leases prices well as a fixed fee per unit or an annual retainer, because the firm can estimate effort reliably. Litigation and complex negotiation resist fixed pricing, so use phase-based capped fees with defined triggers to reset, or a blended rate. Collar arrangements that share over-run and under-run give the firm an incentive rather than a penalty.

atoms.obligation: Review invoices against the guidelines for block billing, staffing drift and non-chargeable administrative time.
atoms.lesson: The recurring leakages are block-billed entries hiding several tasks in one long narrative, partners performing document review, several fee earners attending the same call, unexplained attention to file entries, time billed for internal handovers after staff changes, and administrative charges for photocopying or secretarial support. State in the guidelines that these are not payable, then actually reject them, because firms adjust quickly when queries arrive consistently.

atoms.obligation: Attribute spend to matter type and requesting business unit so the trend can be explained rather than merely reported.
atoms.lesson: A single total legal spend figure invites the wrong conversation. Coding each matter to a type such as disputes, commercial contracting, employment, regulatory or corporate, and to the business unit that requested it, shows whether an increase reflects one large dispute, a structural rise in deal volume, or work that should have been handled internally. That breakdown is also the evidence supporting a decision to hire rather than instruct externally.

name: entity-corporate-records
description: Keeps corporate records in order across group entities, covering statutory registers, filings, board and shareholder approvals and powers of attorney. Use when a director resigns, when a subsidiary needs a resolution before entering a transaction, or when diligence asks for constitutional documents and nobody knows where they are. Covers filing deadlines, approval thresholds, minutes and group structure records.
expansions: director resigned last week
resolution needed for this subsidiary
diligence asked for the registers
dormant entity still filing accounts
power of attorney for local signing
shareholder approval threshold check
registered office address changed
board minutes never written up

atoms.obligation: Update the statutory registers and make the required filings within the statutory deadline for each change.
atoms.lesson: Changes to directors, secretaries, registered office, share capital, articles and beneficial ownership carry filing deadlines, commonly fourteen days for many United Kingdom appointments and changes and shorter periods in some jurisdictions. Late filing attracts penalties and, more damagingly, leaves the public record wrong when a counterparty checks signing authority during diligence. The internal registers rather than the public record are the primary legal record, so both must be kept aligned.

atoms.obligation: Check the constitution and any shareholders agreement for approval thresholds before an entity enters a transaction.
atoms.lesson: Subsidiary transactions frequently need more than a director signature. Articles and shareholder agreements commonly reserve borrowing, granting security, disposing of assets above a threshold, entering long-term commitments, commencing litigation and related-party dealings to the board or to shareholder consent, sometimes with minority veto rights. Identify the requirement first and produce the resolution in the correct form, since retrospective ratification is possible but leaves the directors exposed meanwhile.

atoms.obligation: Minute decisions contemporaneously and record how the directors considered their duties on significant matters.
atoms.lesson: Minutes are evidence. For significant decisions they should show what information the board had, which alternatives were considered, any conflicts declared and how they were managed, and the reasoning, particularly the duty to promote the success of the company and, where solvency is doubtful, the need to have regard to creditors. Minutes written months later from memory are weak evidence and are exactly what gets scrutinised in an insolvency.

atoms.obligation: Maintain one current group structure record holding entity details, officers, ownership chain and dormancy status.
atoms.lesson: Diligence exercises repeatedly uncover forgotten dormant subsidiaries, entities whose only remaining director left the group, and companies whose registered address still points at a former adviser. Hold jurisdiction, registration number, incorporation date, registered office, directors, shareholding chain, financial year end, auditor and status for every entity. Dormant companies still incur filing duties, so an explicit decision to strike off or retain each one beats quiet drift.

name: competition-law-guardrails
description: Applies competition and antitrust guardrails to commercial arrangements and industry contact, covering information exchange, distribution terms, joint bidding and trade association meetings. Use before a meeting with a competitor, when a distributor asks for resale price control, or when benchmarking data will be shared between rivals. Covers hardcore restrictions, exchange design, vertical restraints and non-competes.
expansions: meeting a competitor next week
joint bid with another supplier
distributor wants price maintenance
benchmarking data shared with rivals
trade association agenda arrived
exclusivity across the whole market
competitor mentioned pricing on a call
non compete length in the deal

atoms.obligation: Treat any discussion of price, capacity, customers or bidding intentions with a competitor as prohibited conduct.
atoms.lesson: The hardcore infringements are price fixing, market or customer allocation, output restriction and bid rigging, attracting fines of up to ten per cent of global turnover and, in some jurisdictions, criminal liability for individuals. Exposure does not require agreement, since merely receiving sensitive information without publicly distancing yourself can suffice. If it arises in a meeting, object clearly, ask for the objection to be minuted, leave if it continues, and report internally the same day.

atoms.obligation: Structure any information exchange through aggregation, delay and independent handling before data is shared.
atoms.lesson: Benchmarking and industry statistics are lawful when designed properly: data aggregated across enough participants that no single company is identifiable, historic rather than current or forward looking, collected and anonymised by an independent administrator, and outputs limited to aggregate figures. Current pricing, planned capacity, cost structures and customer-specific terms are the categories that turn a benchmarking exercise into a cartel investigation with dawn raids attached.

atoms.obligation: Check vertical restraints against the block exemption thresholds and hardcore list before agreeing distribution terms.
atoms.lesson: Vertical agreements generally benefit from exemption where each party market share sits below thirty per cent, but hardcore restrictions lose the benefit regardless of share. Resale price maintenance is the classic breach, while recommended and maximum prices are permitted provided they do not operate as fixed prices through pressure or incentives. Territorial restrictions differ between exclusive and selective distribution, and restricting passive sales is treated far more harshly than restricting active ones.

atoms.obligation: Time-limit and narrow non-compete obligations to what is genuinely necessary to protect the specific transaction.
atoms.lesson: Non-competes in commercial agreements are assessed on duration, geographic reach and product scope against what the arrangement actually requires. In distribution, obligations exceeding five years generally fall outside the exemption. In acquisitions, restrictions on the seller are usually accepted at up to three years where goodwill and know-how transfer together and two years where only goodwill does. Drafting the widest possible restriction risks losing the entire clause.

name: contract-repository-hygiene
description: Keeps the contract repository trustworthy by defining what gets stored, how records are named, which metadata is captured and what happens to the historic backlog. Use when nobody can find the signed version, when migrating records off shared drives, or when portfolio reporting is impossible because the fields are empty. Covers minimum metadata, contract families, version discipline and backlog sequencing.
expansions: nobody can find the signed version
migrating contracts off shared drives
duplicate versions everywhere
metadata fields mostly empty
which contracts have unlimited liability
naming convention keeps changing
amendments not linked to parents
backlog of paper contracts to load

atoms.obligation: Define the minimum metadata set first and refuse to accept records that arrive without those fields populated.
atoms.lesson: Repositories fail when everything is uploaded and nothing is described. A workable minimum is counterparty legal name, contracting entity, agreement type, effective date, end date, renewal type, notice period, value, governing law and business owner. Add risk fields only where they will genuinely be reported on, such as liability cap basis or whether personal data is processed. Ten reliably populated fields are worth more than forty that are half complete.

atoms.obligation: Link amendments, order forms and side letters to the parent agreement so each relationship reads as one family.
atoms.lesson: The most damaging repository defect is a master agreement stored without its amendments, because sooner or later somebody advises on superseded terms. Every child document should record its parent, its date and which clauses it varies, so the current position can be reconstructed quickly. Where a relationship carries many order forms, maintain the family view rather than treating each order as a standalone contract with its own independent renewal logic.

atoms.obligation: Mark one version as the executed record and keep negotiation drafts out of the same storage location.
atoms.lesson: Search results returning six near-identical files are exactly how the wrong version gets relied on in a dispute. Store only executed documents complete with schedules and signature pages, keep drafts in a separate working area with a retention limit, and apply a consistent naming pattern of counterparty, document type and effective date. Where a scan is the record, confirm it is complete, legible and includes annexes before the paper is archived.

atoms.obligation: Prioritise the historic backlog by risk and value instead of attempting to load every legacy document.
atoms.lesson: Full retrospective loading of a decade of contracts rarely finishes. Sequence it: active agreements above a spend threshold first, then anything auto-renewing within twelve months, then regulated or personal-data agreements, then the long tail captured as each one renews. Expired agreements usually need only a record and a retention date rather than full metadata. Agreeing what will deliberately not be loaded is what makes the programme completable at all.

name: assortment-range-review
description: Runs a structured range review for a category, deciding which lines to keep, cut or add for the next season on rate of sale, cash margin and shopper duplication. Use it when someone says they need to cut twenty percent of the SKUs in coffee, when the buying meeting needs a delist list, or when a range has grown into a pile of near-identical variants. It also covers finding the gaps a range review should backfill.
expansions: cut skus in the coffee range
range review before the buying meeting
which lines should we delist
too many facings doing the same job
tail skus not earning their space
add a premium tier to the range
duplication between two brands
assortment plan for the spring season

atoms.obligation: Rank every item in the category by rate of sale per point of distribution rather than by total units sold.
atoms.lesson: Total units flatter an item stocked in every store and punish a strong line carried in eighty doors. Rate of sale per point of distribution, meaning units per store per week, separates real demand from distribution effect. A line selling four units per store per week in eighty doors is a better keeper than one selling one point two in nine hundred. Pair it with weeks of cover so you do not reward an item that only looks fast because it was out of stock half the period.

atoms.obligation: Establish what a deletion candidate contributes in incremental spend before cutting it out of the range.
atoms.lesson: Transferable demand is the core question in a range review: if a line goes, what share of its sales walks to the item next to it and what share walks out of the store. Own-label duplicates and flavour variants typically transfer sixty to eighty percent. A unique need-state item such as gluten free, infant or halal transfers under thirty percent and its shopper may abandon the whole basket. Check basket data for solus shoppers and protect low-volume lines with a high solus share.

atoms.obligation: Fill every gap the review opens with a defined shopper need instead of another version of the best seller.
atoms.lesson: A review that cuts twenty percent of lines and backfills with extensions of the top seller shrinks the category. Build the range against a grid of need states and price tiers, entry, mainstream and premium, crossed with occasion and pack size, then find the empty cells. Categories usually leak shoppers at the two ends: a missing opening price point pushes the price-sensitive shopper to a discounter, and a missing premium tier caps basket value and blocks trade-up.

atoms.obligation: Model the margin effect of the proposed range including supplier income, not on gross margin percentage alone.
atoms.lesson: Buyers wreck category profit chasing margin percent. A premium line at forty-two percent selling one unit a week earns less cash per foot than a mainstream line at twenty-eight percent selling nine. Convert every decision to cash margin per linear foot per week. Model supplier income separately, because delisting a line often forfeits a rebate tier that was quietly funding the whole category, and show the range's cash margin both before and after that income so the trade-off is visible.

name: open-to-buy-planning
description: Builds and re-forecasts an open-to-buy plan, meaning how much inventory at cost a buyer may still commit by month given planned sales, markdowns and stock turn. Trigger it when someone asks how much OTB is left for the quarter, says a category is overbought, or wants the buy reforecast after a soft month. It also covers deciding which orders to cancel, push or cut in depth.
expansions: how much open to buy is left
overbought in outerwear this season
reforecast the buy after a soft march
cancel or push back deliveries
receipt plan by month for autumn
stock turn target not being hit
budget the buy for a new category
weeks of supply too high before peak

atoms.obligation: Derive the receipt plan from planned sales, planned markdowns and target closing stock rather than from last year's receipts.
atoms.lesson: Open to buy for a month equals planned closing stock plus planned sales plus planned markdowns and shrink, minus opening stock, all stated at cost. Copying last year's receipt flow imports last year's mistakes, including any overbuy left in the numbers. Anchor instead on target weeks of supply for that month, typically twelve to sixteen weeks entering an apparel peak and falling sharply as the season clears, and work back into the receipts you can actually justify.

atoms.obligation: Reforecast the plan against actual selling at least monthly and adjust future receipts before the season locks.
atoms.lesson: An open-to-buy plan is a control mechanism, not a budget document. Once a season is a quarter of the way through, cumulative sell-through predicts the full season reliably, and a category running ten points behind at that point rarely recovers without markdown. The only cash lever left is future receipts: cancel, delay delivery or cut depth on unsigned orders. After goods are received the sole remaining lever is markdown, which pays for the error in margin instead of cash.

atoms.obligation: Hold a reserve of uncommitted open to buy for in-season chase instead of spending the whole budget before the season starts.
atoms.lesson: Keeping fifteen to twenty-five percent of the seasonal buy open lets you repeat the winners, which is where the season's margin is actually made. What is feasible depends on supplier lead time: a nearshore vendor at four to six weeks supports two chase cycles inside a thirteen-week season, while a far-east vendor at ninety to a hundred and twenty days supports none, so those lines must be bought committed and hedged on depth. Size the reserve to the short-lead suppliers you really have.

atoms.obligation: State the plan in both cost and retail values and reconcile the difference as planned initial markup.
atoms.lesson: Retail-method retailers plan in retail while cash and supplier commitments sit in cost, and the bridge between them is initial markup, which is where errors hide. If the plan assumes fifty-five percent markup but the buy lands at fifty-one because of freight, duty or a mix shift toward branded goods, the season is short of margin dollars before a single unit sells. Restate landed cost including freight, duty and tariff lines, then revalue the buy at retail after every major order.

name: markdown-cadence-plan
description: Designs the timing and depth of markdowns through a season so stock clears by its exit date at the smallest possible margin cost. Use it when someone asks when to take the first cut on swimwear, says sell-through is behind at week six, or needs a markdown ladder before the next season lands. It covers the trigger, the step depth, the ladder spacing and which options to mark first.
expansions: when to take the first markdown on swim
sell through behind at week six
markdown ladder for end of season
how deep to go on slow colours
clear before the new season lands
too much stock left at week ten
price cut is not moving units
protect margin but hit the exit date

atoms.obligation: Trigger the first markdown from sell-through against a weekly benchmark curve rather than from a fixed calendar date.
atoms.lesson: A seasonal line should track a cumulative sell-through curve, roughly fifty to sixty percent by the halfway point of a thirteen-week apparel window. Falling more than ten points below that curve at week four to six is the signal to act, because the weeks remaining cannot absorb the units at full price. Waiting for a calendar date compresses clearance into fewer weeks and forces deeper cuts, and a twenty percent cut at week six usually costs less total margin than fifty percent at week eleven.

atoms.obligation: Make each markdown step deep enough to change the shopper's decision instead of repeating shallow cuts.
atoms.lesson: In most discretionary categories the first perceptible threshold sits around twenty to twenty-five percent off, and anything under fifteen percent moves almost no incremental units while giving margin to shoppers who would have paid full price. Price-point psychology matters more than the percentage: thirty pounds moving to twenty-four ninety-nine reads as a deal, thirty to twenty-seven does not. Plan a ladder such as twenty-five, forty then sixty percent, each landing on a clean price point with fixed weeks between steps.

atoms.obligation: Fix the exit date first and work the markdown ladder backwards from it.
atoms.lesson: The exit date is set by physical constraints, the incoming season's delivery, the planogram reset or the outlet transfer cut-off, not by the merchant's appetite to keep trying. Carrying seasonal stock into the following year recovers twenty to thirty percent of retail at best once storage, handling and further ageing are counted. Count the weeks to exit, reserve a final clearance week, and space the steps evenly; if five weeks remain against fourteen weeks of cover, the first step is already deep.

atoms.obligation: Mark down by option, size run and colour rather than applying one cut across the whole line.
atoms.lesson: What is really left in a line is broken sizes and off colours. Marking the whole option down, including core sizes still selling at full price, gives away margin on units that needed no help. Segment by size-run integrity: options with a complete run stay at price while options broken below roughly sixty percent size availability move to the next step, since a broken run converts poorly anyway. Colour behaves the same way, as the fashion shade ages far faster than the black.

name: clearance-exit-plan
description: Plans the disposal of terminal stock, meaning what is left after the markdown ladder plus returns, damages and delisted lines, across outlets, liquidators, marketplaces, donation and write-off. Use it when someone asks what to do with twelve thousand units of last year's model, when a jobber offers a fraction of cost, or when aged stock is clogging the warehouse. It covers channel choice, resale restrictions, ageing rules and provisioning.
expansions: twelve thousand units of last year's model
jobber offered eight percent of cost
clear a discontinued range without brand damage
outlet channel or liquidator
write off aged stock in the warehouse
returns and b grade piling up
terminal stock ageing past twelve months
exit inventory from a delisted supplier

atoms.obligation: Value the remaining units at realistic net recovery per channel before choosing a disposal route.
atoms.lesson: Compare routes after all handling. Outlet stores typically recover twenty-five to forty percent of original retail but need repackaging, transport and shelf time. Online clearance events recover more but cannibalise full-price traffic and carry shipping and return costs. A liquidator pays five to fifteen percent of cost and takes everything at once with no labour. Donation returns tax value and goodwill but no cash. Include the carrying cost avoided, warehouse space, insurance and tied-up capital, which is often the largest term.

atoms.obligation: Set channel, territory and timing restrictions so cleared goods do not reappear in front of full-price shoppers.
atoms.lesson: Liquidation contracts must specify geography, channel and timing or the goods surface on a marketplace at a third of your live price, undercutting your own listings and any wholesale partners. Common terms are no resale in the domestic market for ninety days, removal or defacing of brand labels on jobbed goods, and an explicit prohibition on named marketplaces. For branded stock the supplier's distribution agreement may already forbid onward sale, so check the contract before committing the units.

atoms.obligation: Group ageing inventory into cohorts and attach a mandated action to each threshold so nothing sits undecided.
atoms.lesson: Terminal stock decays predictably and the biggest cost is indecision. Bucket by weeks since last receipt or since the final markdown, for example nought to thirteen, fourteen to twenty-six, twenty-seven to fifty-two and over fifty-two, and give each bucket a required action. Stock past fifty-two weeks almost never sells at any price in its original channel, and holding it inflates stock cover, distorts replenishment maths and simply delays a write-down finance will force anyway.

atoms.obligation: Book the write-down in the period the exit decision is made instead of spreading it over future months.
atoms.lesson: Provisioning is where merchandising and finance collide. Once a line is designated terminal, accounting expects a provision down to net realisable value in that period, and deferring it to smooth the profit line leaves a stock ledger that overstates what is actually in the building and misleads the next buy. Agree a provisioning policy with finance up front, for instance a fixed percentage by age bucket, so each individual exit is not renegotiated from scratch.

name: size-curve-allocation
description: Sets how the units of an apparel or footwear line are split across sizes and pushed to individual stores or fulfilment nodes. Trigger it when someone says they are always out of medium and drowning in extra small, when a new style needs a size curve built, or when broken runs need consolidating mid-season. It covers curve construction, store clustering by size profile, warehouse hold-back and size availability as a service metric.
expansions: always out of medium drowning in xs
build a size curve for this style
reallocate stock between stores midseason
broken size runs in half the doors
how deep to allocate per door
hold back units for replenishment
size profile differs by store cluster
footwear widths not selling evenly

atoms.obligation: Build the size curve from demand measured at full availability and exclude weeks when a size was out of stock.
atoms.lesson: Raw history understates the middle sizes because they sell out first, and every rebuy of the same flawed curve makes the distortion worse. Use only weeks where the whole run was in stock in that door, or apply a lost-sales uplift to sizes that stocked out. Womenswear curves are typically single-peaked around a UK twelve to fourteen, footwear is wider and flatter, and kidswear shifts through the season as the cohort ages, so never carry one curve across departments.

atoms.obligation: Cluster doors by their observed size profile instead of sending one national curve to every store.
atoms.lesson: Size demand varies by location more than most merchants assume. City-centre and student catchments skew smaller, out-of-town family stores skew larger, and tourist locations skew to both extremes, so a single national curve guarantees broken runs at both ends. Three to five size clusters usually capture most of the variance and should be recalculated annually. Require a complete size run in every door before allocating any depth, because a store missing key sizes converts badly on the whole style.

atoms.obligation: Retain part of the initial buy at the warehouse so sizes can be replenished once the real curve appears.
atoms.lesson: The true size curve for a new style is unknown until it has traded two or three weeks. Pushing everything at launch locks the guess in and leaves store-to-store transfers as the only correction, which cost more in labour than the units are worth. A common split is sixty to seventy percent pushed at launch with the balance held for size-level replenishment on actual rate of sale. The hold-back only pays if the replenishment cycle lands inside the selling window.

atoms.obligation: Track size-run availability as a weekly service measure and act on it before it shows up in conversion.
atoms.lesson: The operational measure is size availability, the share of live doors holding every size in a style. Below roughly eighty percent availability on core sizes, style-level conversion falls sharply because a shopper who cannot find their size rarely substitutes into another. Report it weekly by style and cluster and use it to trigger consolidation: pull the single units out of doors with broken runs into a smaller number of complete runs rather than leaving fragments spread across the estate.

name: store-cluster-localization
description: Groups stores into clusters and tailors range, space and price to each so one national plan does not get sent to very different catchments. Use it when someone asks why a city-centre store and a retail park receive the same range, when clusters need rebuilding ahead of a reset, or when deciding which doors carry an extended range. It covers cluster construction, core versus tail, trialling and reassignment.
expansions: same range going to very different stores
build store clusters for the reset
which doors carry the extended range
city centre store behaves nothing like the park
space tiers for the small format
local demographic skew we keep ignoring
regional lines only sell in the north
grade stores for the new planogram

atoms.obligation: Cluster stores on selling behaviour and usable space rather than on region or store size alone.
atoms.lesson: Geography is a poor proxy: two stores twenty miles apart can differ more than two in different countries. Build clusters from category-level sales mix, average transaction value, mission indicators such as basket size and time-of-day profile, and usable linear space, then sanity-check against catchment demographics. Most chains settle on four to six clusters per category, since more becomes unmanageable for supply chain and planogram production while fewer stops capturing the differences that justified the exercise.

atoms.obligation: Define a mandatory core range every cluster carries and vary only the tail around it.
atoms.lesson: Full localisation is operationally impossible. The workable structure is a mandatory core, usually the top fifty to sixty percent of lines that drive around eighty percent of volume everywhere, plus cluster-specific modules layered on top. This keeps replenishment parameters, promotional pricing and distribution simple while still allowing real local difference. It also protects the shopper's expectation that a chain stocks the same essentials in every branch, which is exactly why they trust it for a top-up trip.

atoms.obligation: Validate a cluster range in a live trial with matched control stores before rolling it across the estate.
atoms.lesson: Cluster hypotheses fail more often than they succeed. Run fifteen to twenty-five stores for a full trading cycle, at least eight weeks and longer in a seasonal category, against a control group matched on pre-period sales rather than chosen for convenience. Measure category sales and cash margin, not just the new items, because the real question is whether the cluster range grew the category or shuffled sales between lines. Price the added supply chain complexity into the payback case.

atoms.obligation: Recheck cluster assignments on a fixed annual cycle because catchments and store estates keep moving.
atoms.lesson: Clusters drift. A competitor opening, a housing development, a road change or a refit can shift a store's behaviour inside a year. Reassign annually ahead of the main range review and flag stores whose fit has decayed, typically those whose actual category mix now sits far from their cluster mean. Tell store operations early, because a store changing cluster receives a different planogram, different space and different replenishment settings all at the same time.

name: planogram-reset-brief
description: Turns a range decision into a shelf layout: space by segment, flow and blocking, facings, adjacencies and the instructions store teams follow on reset night. Use it when someone needs a planogram for a new bay, when the shelf no longer matches the agreed range, or when capacity between deliveries is too tight. It also covers writing the execution sequence and what stores do with delisted stock.
expansions: planogram for the new four foot bay
space allocation ahead of the reset
shelf does not match the new range
how many facings for each brand
flow and blocking for the category
reset night instructions for stores
not enough capacity between deliveries
adjacency between two categories is wrong

atoms.obligation: Allocate space to segments by share of sales and margin, then set facings so each item holds enough units between deliveries.
atoms.lesson: Two different jobs get confused here. Segment space follows sales and margin share, while item facings must additionally satisfy days of supply, so facings multiplied by units per facing has to exceed expected sales between replenishments plus a buffer. A fast bulky item such as a large pack of nappies or dog food may need more facings than its sales share implies simply so staff are not refilling three times a day, while a small slow item still needs one facing to stay findable.

atoms.obligation: Build the shelf flow around the sequence in which the shopper makes the decision and keep it consistent across stores.
atoms.lesson: Shoppers decode a shelf in a hierarchy, usually need state or type first, then brand, then size or price. Vertical brand blocks inside a horizontal band of type work because vertical blocks read from the aisle at walking pace, while a long horizontal ribbon of one brand becomes a wall that hides the alternatives. Put the destination line at eye level, roughly a hundred and twenty to a hundred and sixty centimetres, heavy and bulk packs at the bottom, and premium or impulse at eye level.

atoms.obligation: State the physical constraints of every bay in the brief instead of designing against an idealised fixture.
atoms.lesson: Planograms fail on reset night for physical reasons: shelf depth is four hundred millimetres not five hundred, the gondola has five shelves not six, a pillar eats the bay, or the pack is three hundred and twenty millimetres tall under a shelf set at three hundred.
