name: kanban-loop-sizing
description: Sizes kanban loops and supermarket levels for parts feeding a line and diagnoses loops that keep running dry. Use when a line stops for a part the system says is in the warehouse, when converting a scheduled feeder to pull, when a milk-run route is being timed, or when a loop is holding far too much stock.
expansions: line stopped waiting for clips
how many cards for this part
the supermarket keeps running dry
convert the feeder cell to pull
replenishment takes two shifts
timing the milk run route
too much wip in the loop
two bin system for fasteners

atoms.obligation: Size the loop from replenishment lead time, average consumption and a stated safety factor, then round up to whole containers.
atoms.lesson: Card count equals demand per unit time multiplied by replenishment lead time, divided by container quantity, times one plus a safety factor. Lead time is the full loop: card travel, queue at the supplying process, changeover, run, and transport back — usually far longer than run time alone. Write the assumed numbers on the card or the loop sheet, because when the loop later fails the argument is always about which lead time was assumed.

atoms.obligation: Set container quantity so one card moves a practical handling unit rather than an arbitrary planning order quantity.
atoms.lesson: The container should be liftable, stackable, countable at a glance and sized so line-side space holds no more than a couple of hours of consumption. Standard totes with a fixed part count beat mixed pallets because withdrawal becomes visual. Small parts like fasteners suit a two-bin system where the empty bin is the signal; large sheet metal suits one card per rack. Container quantity drives the card count, so change it deliberately, not by whatever the supplier ships.

atoms.obligation: Withdraw material only against a card and forbid production without one, including for urgent orders.
atoms.lesson: One helpful shortage expediter pulling a tote without a card breaks the loop's arithmetic silently, and the gap appears two days later as a stoppage. If the loop truly cannot cover a demand spike, add cards deliberately and record it, or run the item on a scheduled exception. Physical discipline is enforced by card posts at the supermarket, coloured cards per loop and a rule that a supplying cell with no card in the post does not run.

atoms.obligation: Review card counts when demand or lead time moves beyond the agreed threshold and physically add or remove cards.
atoms.lesson: Loops rot when demand halves and the cards stay, leaving a supermarket full of obsolete stock, or when demand grows twenty percent and the loop starts stocking out weekly. Set a monthly review at a threshold such as fifteen percent change in average daily usage. Removing a card must be physical — pull it from circulation and mark it — otherwise the inventory reduction never happens even though the spreadsheet says it did.

name: shift-handover-brief
description: Turns a shift's events into a handover the incoming crew can act on in five minutes. Trigger at end of shift, when the oncoming supervisor asks what happened overnight, when a machine is left mid-setup, or when the same problem keeps being rediscovered every shift.
expansions: end of shift handover notes
what happened on nights
machine left in a half setup
same issue rediscovered every shift
open work orders to pass on
quality hold to flag to days
manning gaps for the next shift
shift log for the packing hall

atoms.obligation: State the physical condition each machine was left in, including part setups, bypassed guards and open maintenance work.
atoms.lesson: The dangerous handovers are the half-finished ones: a die partly clamped, a guard interlock jumpered for troubleshooting, a panel open, a hydraulic line disconnected, a machine locked out with the technician gone home. Name the machine, what state it is in, whether it is safe to start and who has the keys. A verbal 'it's fine' at the gate is how someone presses cycle start on a press with a hand tool still inside.

atoms.obligation: Carry open quality holds forward with lot numbers and the named decision owner rather than noting that a hold exists.
atoms.lesson: Holds die between shifts because the person who knew the context left. Pass the lot or batch number, the quantity, where the material physically sits, what the suspected defect is, what has already been checked and who is expected to decide and when. If a sort is running, state how many pieces are screened and where the certified stock is marked, so the next shift does not start the sort again from the beginning.

atoms.obligation: Report output against plan with the reason for the gap attached rather than the number on its own.
atoms.lesson: 'We made 4,200 of 5,000' tells the next shift nothing they can act on. 'Short 800: line down 95 minutes for a labeller jam, plus 40 minutes waiting on preforms' tells them what will bite them at two in the morning. Tie the reason to the same downtime codes used for loss analysis, so the handover log and the OEE report tell one story rather than two, and repeated causes become visible across a week.

atoms.obligation: List what the incoming shift must do in the first hour, in order, with names attached to each item.
atoms.lesson: A handover that ends in a narrative leaves prioritisation to be re-derived at the worst moment. Finish with three to five concrete actions: start the sort on lot 25-0912 with the two agency operators, call maintenance at seven about the labeller camera, run the short colour first because the tooling is already in. Order them, name owners, and mark anything that must happen before the first product runs.

name: lockout-tagout-procedure
description: Writes or verifies machine-specific energy isolation before maintenance or cleaning work. Use when a new machine arrives without an isolation sheet, when a job needs a guard removed, when contractors are working inside a cell, when a lockout spans a shift change, or after a near miss with stored energy.
expansions: no loto procedure for this press
contractor working inside the guard
stored energy in the accumulator
who holds the key on group lockout
we found a machine live during service
tagout for the conveyor drive
shift change in the middle of a lockout
trial run before removing locks

atoms.obligation: List every energy source on the machine with its isolation point, including stored, gravity and thermal energy.
atoms.lesson: Electrical supply is the one everyone finds. The ones that injure people are the pneumatic receiver still charged after the isolator is off, the hydraulic accumulator, the suspended ram or platen held only by pressure, the spring-loaded tensioner, hot dies and dryers, chemical or steam lines, and a second feed from an adjacent machine or a control transformer. Walk the machine with the electrical and pneumatic schematics and mark each isolation point physically with a numbered label.

atoms.obligation: Verify zero energy by attempting a start and by measuring, never by trusting the position of the isolator.
atoms.lesson: Try-out is a required step, not a courtesy: press the start button and operate the machine's controls after isolation, bleed pneumatics to zero on the gauge, block or lower gravity loads, and prove dead with a meter tested on a known live source before and after. Isolators fail welded closed, and dual-feed panels look dead at one switch. Return every control to the off position after the try-out so nothing restarts when power is restored.

atoms.obligation: Use a group lockout box with each worker applying a personal lock so no one can restore power while another is exposed.
atoms.lesson: For multi-trade jobs the authorised person isolates, locks each point, and puts those keys in a group box; every worker then applies their own personal lock to the box. Power cannot return until the last person removes their lock. Personal locks are uniquely keyed and never shared or lent. If the job crosses a shift change, the outgoing crew's locks come off and the incoming crew applies theirs at the box before the isolation is disturbed.

atoms.obligation: Clear people and tools, replace guards, then run a controlled trial before releasing the machine back to production.
atoms.lesson: Restoration is where the second injury happens. Account for everyone who worked on the machine, sweep for tools, rags and offcuts left inside, refit interlocks and confirm the light curtain and door switches actually stop the machine. Then restore energy and run one deliberate cycle in a controlled mode with people clear, before handing back to the operator with a note in the shift log describing what was changed.

name: near-miss-investigation
description: Investigates a near miss or minor injury on the floor and produces corrective actions that hold up under audit. Trigger with an incident card, a first-aid entry, a dropped load, a bypassed guard, or a report that someone nearly got hit by a truck.
expansions: forklift nearly hit a pedestrian
part fell from the hoist
first aid entry from last night
operator bypassed the light curtain
why do people take the shortcut
corrective actions for the safety board
repeat near miss on the same crossing
toolbox talk after the incident

atoms.obligation: Secure the scene and photograph positions, guarding, housekeeping and controls before anything is moved or cleaned.
atoms.lesson: Within twenty minutes of a near miss someone will sweep the spill, refit the guard and move the pallet, and the evidence is gone. Photograph from the injured person's eye level and from the truck driver's seat, capture the state of interlocks and e-stops, the floor marking, lighting and where stock was stacked into the walkway. Note machine settings and cycle counters, and keep any broken component rather than binning it.

atoms.obligation: Interview those involved separately, on the floor, focused on what made the unsafe route the easy or fast one.
atoms.lesson: Interview at the machine, one person at a time, within the same shift while memory is intact, and ask them to walk you through it physically. Ask what normally happens rather than what should happen. Guards get bypassed because clearing a jam through the door takes four minutes and reaching through takes ten seconds; people cut across the truck aisle because the marked route adds sixty metres. Those answers are the actual findings.

atoms.obligation: Select corrective actions by the hierarchy of controls and treat extra training or signage as the weakest option available.
atoms.lesson: Rank the options: eliminate the task, substitute a safer method, engineer it out with a jam-clearing chute, a interlocked gate or a segregated pedestrian route, then administrative controls, then protective equipment. An action list made only of 'retrain operators' and 'add a sign' will be reopened at the next audit and, more importantly, by the next incident. Give each action an owner, a date and a verification method on the safety board.

atoms.obligation: Check whether the same hazard exists on sister machines, other lines and other shifts before closing the action.
atoms.lesson: Near misses cluster by design, not by person. If one press has an unguarded feed opening, the other four presses of the same model almost certainly do; if the shortcut across the aisle exists on days it exists at three in the morning with fewer people watching. Walk the identical assets, ask the other shifts, and extend the fix. Closing an action on a single machine is how the same event reappears in the log four months later.

name: process-capability-study
description: Runs and interprets capability studies so a process can be judged against the print rather than against inspection luck. Use when a customer demands a Cpk above 1.33, when parts pass inspection but drift toward a limit, when a new machine must be qualified, or when a distribution is clearly not normal.
expansions: customer wants cpk above 1.33
capability study on the bore diameter
cp is fine but cpk is bad
how many parts for the study
process drifting toward the upper limit
qualifying the new machine
ppk or cpk for the submission
non normal data on flatness

atoms.obligation: Confirm the process is statistically stable on a control chart before calculating any capability index.
atoms.lesson: Capability indices assume one stable distribution. If the chart shows tool wear trends, a shift between operators or a spike from a bad batch of material, the calculated Cpk describes a mixture that will never repeat. Chart the study data first, deal with the special causes, then compute. A study run over a single hour on one shift is also not representative: capability for a customer submission should span setups, operators and material lots.

atoms.obligation: Report Cp alongside Cpk so a centring problem is never mistaken for a spread problem.
atoms.lesson: Cp measures whether the spread fits the tolerance; Cpk penalises the distance of the mean from the nearer limit. Cp 1.8 with Cpk 0.9 is a machine with excellent repeatability set half a tolerance band off centre, fixed in ten minutes by an offset. Cp 0.8 with Cpk 0.8 is a machine that cannot hold the tolerance no matter where it is centred, which means tooling, fixturing or a process change. The two failures need opposite responses.

atoms.obligation: Use within-subgroup variation for Cp and Cpk and total variation for Pp and Ppk, and state which was reported.
atoms.lesson: Cpk uses sigma estimated from average range or average standard deviation within subgroups, so it describes short-term potential. Ppk uses the overall standard deviation of all the data and includes drift between subgroups, so it is always the harsher number on a drifting process. Initial submissions usually require Ppk on a limited run with a target of 1.67, then ongoing Cpk of 1.33. Labelling one as the other is the most common audit finding on capability reports.

atoms.obligation: Check the distribution shape before applying normal-theory indices to bounded characteristics such as flatness or runout.
atoms.lesson: Geometric characteristics bounded at zero — position, runout, flatness, concentricity — are skewed, so a normal-based Cpk calculated on them understates or overstates capability badly and can produce indices for a one-sided tolerance that make no physical sense. Plot a histogram, test normality, and use a transformation or a non-normal method that fits the percentile points. Always show the histogram with the tolerance limits, because it convinces people the index alone never will.

name: tooling-life-management
description: Manages die, mould and cutting-tool life so tooling is changed on plan instead of failing mid-order. Trigger when a punch breaks during a run, when inserts are changed by feel, when regrind history is unknown, when burrs appear late in a run, or when a spare tool set has to be justified.
expansions: punch broke in the middle of a run
how many hits left on this die
operator changes inserts by feel
regrind history for the form tool
burrs appearing on the last parts
do we need a spare mould
tool crib has no traceability
tool life counter on the press

atoms.obligation: Track cumulative cycles or cut length against each individual tool identity rather than by tool type or machine.
atoms.lesson: Two identical dies rotating through the same press accumulate very different histories, so a counter on the machine tells you nothing about the tool now installed. Stamp or etch a unique number on every die, punch set, mould and holder, and log hits, shots or metres cut against that number at each removal. Without per-tool identity, the regrind count and remaining stock height are unknown and the tool is scrapped either far too early or far too late.

atoms.obligation: Set a change point from measured wear at which parts still hold tolerance, well before the observed failure point.
atoms.lesson: Run a wear study: measure the characteristic that degrades — burr height, edge radius, bore size, flash thickness — every few thousand cycles and plot it against tolerance. The change point is where the trend line reaches an action limit inside tolerance, typically at seventy to eighty percent of the observed life, not at the point where the last run produced scrap. A planned change costs a twenty-minute slot; a broken punch costs the tool, the die shoe and hours of the press.

atoms.obligation: Inspect and record condition at every tool removal and cap the number of regrinds by the remaining material.
atoms.lesson: At removal record chipping, galling, edge condition, vent blockage, cooling channel flow, shut-height and stack height after grinding. Each regrind removes material — often 0.2 to 0.5 millimetres from a punch face — so calculate the number of regrinds left from the drawing's minimum dimension and mark it on the tool record. Tools kept in a dirty, unprotected crib rust and get dropped, which ends more tool lives than actual wear does.

atoms.obligation: Keep a qualified spare for tooling on the constraint and prove it with sample parts before the run needs it.
atoms.lesson: A spare that has never made a part is a hope, not a spare. Run it, measure a sample against the print, record the machine settings it needed and store the setup sheet with the tool. Justify the spare by lead time and constraint downtime: a mould with a fourteen-week build time on the bottleneck press is a different risk from a drill jig the toolroom can copy overnight. Store spares with corrosion protection and a rotation plan so both sets wear evenly.

name: supplier-corrective-action
description: Raises, chases and closes a supplier corrective action when incoming material causes a line problem. Use when a second or third bad lot arrives, when the supplier's containment is not visible at your dock, when a sort is being charged back, when the supplier disputes the print, or when a defect returns after their fix.
expansions: third bad lot from the same vendor
raise a scar to the supplier
who pays for the sort
supplier says our print is wrong
certified lot failed incoming
need containment at their dock
repeat defect after their fix
downgrade the supplier rating

atoms.obligation: Send the supplier the defect evidence with lot codes, quantities affected and the line impact stated in hours and cost.
atoms.lesson: A complaint without numbers gets a generic reply. Send photographs against a scale, the measured values versus the print requirement, the supplier's own lot and date codes, the quantity received, the quantity found defective, the sort rate, the line downtime in minutes and the labour hours spent. Suppliers prioritise by demonstrated cost, and a documented impact figure is also what makes a later debit note defensible commercially.

atoms.obligation: Require certified containment at both plants and in transit, with a distinctive marking that survives handling.
atoms.lesson: Ask for containment within twenty-four hours covering their finished stock, their WIP, material in transit, and your stock and line-side inventory. Certified lots should carry a visible mark — a coloured label with the sort date and inspector, or a paint dot on each part — so your receiving team can tell screened from unscreened without opening packaging. Insist on redundant inspection at their end until root cause is proven, then step it down deliberately.

atoms.obligation: Require the supplier's process change to appear in their control plan and be verified on the next lots received.
atoms.lesson: The corrective action is only real when it changes a document that governs their production: control plan, work instruction, FMEA detection ranking, tooling drawing or inspection frequency. Ask for the before and after pages, not a narrative. Then verify on receipt: check the first lots produced after the effective date, confirm the new control is running by asking for the actual records, and require a mark on the packaging identifying post-change production.

atoms.obligation: Verify effectiveness over an agreed number of receipts before relaxing incoming inspection or closing the action.
atoms.lesson: Set the exit criterion at raise time, for example five consecutive conforming deliveries or ninety days without recurrence, whichever is longer, and hold heightened incoming inspection until then. Closing on the supplier's promise is why the same defect reappears the following quarter with a new lot number. Feed the outcome into the supplier scorecard: parts per million defective, response time on the action, and the number of repeats, which is what drives sourcing decisions.

name: production-schedule-sequencing
description: Builds or repairs a shop schedule against capacity, tooling and material constraints and sequences it to protect output. Trigger when a hot order jumps the queue, when sales pushes into a frozen window, when the sequence is wasting changeover time, or when material lands later than the plan assumed.
expansions: hot order from sales this morning
sequence to minimise colour changes
material lands wednesday not monday
question about the schedule freeze
which orders slip if we insert this
bottleneck is the paint line
campaign the same tooling together
capacity check for next week

atoms.obligation: Schedule the constraint operation first and let upstream and downstream operations follow the sequence it dictates.
atoms.lesson: Output equals what the constraint produces, so the constraint's sequence is the plan and everything else supports it. Release material to the front of the line at the rate the constraint consumes it rather than as fast as the first machine can run, or the shop fills with WIP that lengthens lead time without adding output. Identify the constraint by where queues persistently sit, not by the highest theoretical utilisation in the routing file.

atoms.obligation: Sequence within a period to cut changeover by grouping shared tooling, colour, material or specification families.
atoms.lesson: Classic rules pay for themselves: run light colours to dark and then wash out, run thin gauge to thick, group products sharing a die or a mould base, and sequence allergen or grade changes so the expensive clean-down happens once. Build a from-to changeover matrix so the cost of each transition is visible. The trap is campaigning so aggressively that a customer waits three weeks for a short-run item, so cap the campaign length.

atoms.obligation: Confirm material availability and tooling readiness before committing a date instead of after publishing the schedule.
atoms.lesson: A schedule that assumes stock the warehouse cannot find, tooling that is in the toolroom for repair, or a fixture being used on another line will fail on the day. Run a hard check per order: components on hand or firmly promised, tooling qualified and in the crib, the setup sheet present, the operator certified for the process and the QA release for the previous lot done. Flag orders failing any check before they reach the floor.

atoms.obligation: Protect a frozen window and force every insertion to name the order it displaces and the new promised date.
atoms.lesson: A typical freeze is the current shift plus the next twenty-four to forty-eight hours, chosen to cover picking, kitting and setup preparation. Inside it, changes destroy more capacity than they gain, because the kitted material goes back and the setup is redone. When an insertion is genuinely required, make the trade explicit — this order goes in, that one moves to Thursday, the customer is told today — and log the reason so repeat offenders show up in the monthly review.

name: engineering-change-rollout
description: Implements an engineering change on the floor: effectivity, old stock, work instructions, fixtures and traceability. Use when a drawing revision is released, when a supplier component changes, when old and new parts look identical, or when a customer needs the break point serial or date.
expansions: new drawing revision released
when does the change take effect
old and new parts look the same
run out existing stock first
customer wants the break point serial
update work instructions at station three
fixture needs modifying for the change
which orders build to the old revision

atoms.obligation: Define effectivity by date, serial or lot and publish the break point to production, quality and the customer.
atoms.lesson: Choose one rule and state it unambiguously: effective from serial 10450, from lot code 25-0930, or from the first order released after Monday. Date-based effectivity is simplest but ambiguous on a line running three shifts across midnight. The break point matters years later when a field failure has to be sorted into affected and unaffected units, so it goes on the change record, the shipping documents and the customer notification, not only in the meeting minutes.

atoms.obligation: Count and disposition existing stock, work in progress and the supplier pipeline before the change goes live.
atoms.lesson: Every change has four inventories to resolve: finished goods, WIP on the floor, raw and component stock in stores, and material already ordered from suppliers. For each, decide run-out, rework, scrap or return, and get it costed and approved before the effectivity date. A run-out plan needs a realistic consumption rate, otherwise old stock sits blocked for months. Tell purchasing to stop the pipeline the day the change is approved, not the day it takes effect.

atoms.obligation: Update work instructions, control plan, inspection criteria and fixtures in the same release as the drawing revision.
atoms.lesson: The drawing changing is the easy part. The change is only implemented when the station instruction shows the new sequence and the new photograph, the control plan lists the new characteristic and its frequency, the gauge or fixture has been modified and requalified, the packing and label artwork match, the FMEA has been revisited and training has been given and recorded. A change that lands as a drawing alone gets built the old way on nights.

atoms.obligation: Make old and new parts visually distinguishable, or physically segregate them when they cannot be told apart.
atoms.lesson: The worst changes are dimensionally small and visually invisible — a different alloy, a revised heat treat, a bracket two millimetres longer. Ask engineering for a distinguishing feature at design time: a moulded revision letter, a witness notch, a different coloured connector or a printed date code. Where none is possible, segregate physically with different bin locations and labels, and never keep both revisions line-side at the same station.

name: five-s-area-audit
description: Runs a 5S audit on a defined area and turns the score into a short, owned fix list. Trigger with a scheduled zone audit, a customer visit walk, an area where tools keep going missing, a full red-tag holding area, or a request to restart a programme that has stalled after the cleaning phase.
expansions: zone audit for the weld cell
tools always go missing here
customer visit on thursday
shadow board is out of date
5s score dropped again
red tag area is full
we clean but nothing sustains
audit the pallet storage lanes

atoms.obligation: Score against a written standard with photographs of the agreed condition rather than the auditor's impression.
atoms.lesson: Every criterion needs an observable test: floor markings intact and unobstructed, every item on the board present, no unlabelled containers, no material outside a marked footprint, cleaning log signed for the last seven days. Post the standard photograph at the area so the target is unambiguous. Without it, scores swing with the auditor's mood and the area learns that the audit is politics, which is what kills the programme faster than any mess.

atoms.obligation: Locate items by frequency of use and distance from the point of use rather than by what fits in the cupboard.
atoms.lesson: Items used every cycle belong within arm's reach in the strike zone; items used once a shift within a few steps; items used monthly can live centrally. Shadow boards and foam cut-outs make a missing tool visible in a second, which matters most for anything that could be left inside a machine. Order-of-use layout beats alphabetical storage on a setup cart, because it turns the cart itself into the setup sequence.

atoms.obligation: Convert cleaning into inspection by naming the leak, wear or loose fastener the operator is expected to find.
atoms.lesson: Wiping a machine is only worth the labour if it doubles as a condition check. Write into the cleaning standard what to look for and report: oil film under the gearbox, air hiss at a fitting, frayed cable, missing guard screw, chip build-up in a sensor pocket, unusual noise at startup. Route the findings to maintenance as a tag on the machine and on the board, so the area sees them closed rather than absorbed silently.

atoms.obligation: Give every finding an owner and a due date on the area board and re-audit open items before scoring again.
atoms.lesson: Sustainability is an action-closure problem, not a discipline problem. If findings from the last three audits are still open, the next audit is theatre. Track them on the area's daily management board where the team leader reviews them at the shift meeting, escalate anything needing engineering or capital, and start each audit by checking the previous list. Score trend over months is worth more than any single score.

name: andon-escalation-response
description: Defines and troubleshoots the andon call and escalation chain that governs how a line stop gets answered. Use when calls go unanswered, when response time is unmeasured, when operators have quietly stopped calling, when a stop reached the plant manager far too late, or when night shift has no defined responders.
expansions: nobody answers the andon call
operators stopped pulling the cord
escalation reached the manager too late
response time for a yellow call
who owns the red light
line stopped for forty minutes
andon board shows the wrong station
define escalation tiers for nights

atoms.obligation: Define what triggers a call at each tier and the time limit before it escalates to the next responder.
atoms.lesson: Two or three tiers is enough: yellow for help needed within the cycle without stopping, red for a stop, and a quality call for a suspect condition. Attach explicit triggers — a missing component, a repeated defect on two consecutive parts, an abnormal noise, an out-of-control chart signal — and a clock: team leader within two minutes, supervisor and maintenance at ten, plant leadership at thirty. The clock, not a judgement call, drives the escalation.

atoms.obligation: Name a responder by role and shift for every tier so a call never depends on who happens to be nearby.
atoms.lesson: Coverage gaps show up on nights, weekends, during breaks and at shift change, which is exactly when calls go unanswered. Publish a matrix of tier by shift with names and radio channels, including who covers when the team leader is at lunch. The responder must be physically able to reach the station inside the time limit, which constrains how many lines one team leader can own — usually two or three cells, not a whole hall.

atoms.obligation: Record time to respond and time to resolve for every call and review the longest ones each week.
atoms.lesson: Without those two timestamps the system cannot be improved, only complained about. Response time diagnoses the staffing and coverage design; resolution time diagnoses skills, spares and process problems. Pareto the calls by station and reason: a station generating thirty calls a shift for the same missing-clip condition is a design problem, not an attention problem, and it deserves a permanent fix rather than a faster responder.

atoms.obligation: Protect operators who stop the line and treat a silent andon as evidence of a broken system, not good performance.
atoms.lesson: If calling brings blame, a delayed answer or the machine being restarted with the problem unresolved, operators simply stop calling and defects flow downstream instead. Watch for the signature: falling call counts alongside rising end-of-line rejects. Leaders should thank the caller publicly at the shift meeting, review a call live at the board each day, and make sure the fix visible to the operator is the one that stops the call recurring.

name: inventory-cycle-count
description: Designs cycle counting and chases record accuracy for stock on the floor. Trigger when a pick fails on material the system says exists, when WIP will not reconcile after a run, when negative on-hand balances appear, when backflush consumption looks wrong, or when an audit asks for an accuracy figure.
expansions: system says we have it but we do not
negative on hand quantity again
wip does not reconcile after the run
abc cycle count frequency
scrap never got booked
count the raw material racks
backflush is wrong on the assembly
record accuracy target for the audit

atoms.obligation: Count by location and blind, without showing the counter the quantity the system expects to find.
atoms.lesson: Showing the expected figure guarantees confirmation rather than a count; people find what they are told to find, especially at the end of a shift. Count by physical location rather than by part number so that stock of the same part in a second rack is not silently merged. Freeze transactions for the location during the count, or record the cut-off time precisely, otherwise a pick during counting shows up as a variance and the investigation chases a ghost.

atoms.obligation: Count high-value and high-movement items more often, and count any part that stopped a line immediately.
atoms.lesson: Classify by usage value: A items perhaps monthly, B quarterly, C twice a year, sized so the annual count workload fits the people available. Layer event-driven counts on top — count on a stockout, on a negative balance, when a pick short occurs, and after a physical move of a rack. Those event counts find far more real errors per hour spent than the calendar routine, because they land exactly where the record has already proved wrong.

atoms.obligation: Investigate the transaction that produced each variance instead of only adjusting the balance to match the count.
atoms.lesson: Adjusting without diagnosis guarantees the same variance returns next quarter. The recurring causes on a factory floor are a short list: scrap consumed but never booked, a receipt put away in the wrong location, a pick taken without scanning during a shortage, a return to stores never transacted, a unit-of-measure error between pieces and kilograms, and a bill-of-material quantity that does not match what the line actually consumes. Each has a different owner and fix.

atoms.obligation: Reconcile scrap, rework and component backflush against actual consumption at the end of every production run.
atoms.lesson: Backflush relieves components at the standard bill quantity, so every setup piece, every scrapped assembly and every part dropped on the floor makes the record drift, always in the same direction. Close each run by counting the returned components, booking scrap by reason code and comparing issued against consumed. On a line with high setup scrap, adjusting the bill's yield factor is more honest than letting cycle counts absorb the error month after month.

name: compressed-air-survey
description: Finds, quantifies and ranks compressed air and utility waste in the plant. Use when the compressor runs loaded through a non-production weekend, when pressure drops at the far end of a line, when energy cost per unit climbs, when an air-hungry machine is being added, or before anyone proposes buying more compressor capacity.
expansions: compressor runs all weekend
pressure drops at the far end
hiss from fittings on the press
energy cost per unit went up
can we add another machine on this compressor
blow off guns left open
ultrasonic leak survey route
lower the system pressure setpoint

atoms.obligation: Measure baseline demand during a shutdown period to size total leakage before hunting individual leaks.
atoms.lesson: With production stopped and all machines isolated, whatever the compressor still delivers is leakage. Measure it by load and unload timing on a fixed-speed unit, or from the flow meter on a variable-speed one. Plants that have never surveyed commonly sit between twenty and thirty percent leakage. The baseline number is what justifies the survey time and what proves the repairs worked, because individual leak estimates always sum to more than reality.

atoms.obligation: Tag each leak with a size estimate and an annual cost so repairs can be ranked rather than merely listed.
atoms.lesson: Survey with an ultrasonic detector during a quiet period, walking a fixed route: quick-connect couplings, hose whips, filter-regulator-lubricator units, cylinder rod seals, solenoid exhausts, condensate drains stuck open and threaded joints. Tag each with a numbered card giving location, estimated hole size and cost per year at your electricity rate. A single three-millimetre leak at seven bar can run to four figures annually, which is what turns a maintenance nuisance into a funded job.

atoms.obligation: Eliminate demand-side misuse such as open blow-off, cabinet cooling and unregulated tools before adding capacity.
atoms.lesson: Compressed air is one of the most expensive utilities per unit of energy delivered, so using it to cool a panel, agitate a tank, sweep a floor or blow chips off a fixture with an open pipe is pure waste. Fit engineered nozzles with entrainment, add solenoid valves that cut air when the machine is idle, replace air-driven cabinet coolers with fans or heat exchangers, and regulate each drop to the lowest pressure the tool actually needs.

atoms.obligation: Lower the system pressure setpoint only after checking the highest-pressure machine and the worst pressure-drop point.
atoms.lesson: Every bar of reduction cuts compressor power by roughly seven percent and shrinks leakage flow as well, but the setpoint must serve the neediest legitimate user. Log pressure at the far end of the ring main during peak demand, not at the compressor house, and find whether the shortfall is generation or a restriction — an undersized drop, a clogged filter, a dryer at end of life, a hose whip. Fixing the restriction often allows a lower setpoint and solves the complaint at once.

name: operator-certification-matrix
description: Builds and maintains the skills matrix and qualification sign-off for operators on each process. Use when an untrained person is put on a job, when an auditor asks for training records, when a cell cannot flex to cover absence, when agency workers arrive for critical operations, or when someone returns after months away.
expansions: auditor asked for training records
new starter on the leak tester
nobody trained for the night shift
how do we sign someone off
cross training plan for the cell
training matrix is out of date
agency workers on critical operations
requalify after six months away

atoms.obligation: Define competence per operation with an observable sign-off rather than a signature on an attendance sheet.
atoms.lesson: Qualification means the assessor watched the person run the job unaided to takt, follow the standard work, perform the in-process checks correctly, react properly to a deliberately introduced defect and complete the paperwork. Use the four-level convention — in training, can perform with help, can perform alone, can train others — and define the evidence for each level. Attendance at a briefing proves exposure, not capability, and auditors know the difference.

atoms.obligation: Prevent uncertified operators from running special-characteristic operations and display the matrix at the line.
atoms.lesson: Operations affecting safety, regulatory or customer special characteristics — torque on a safety fastener, a leak test, a weld, a final release check — need a named qualified list, ideally enforced by badge or login at the station so an unqualified person physically cannot start. Post the matrix at the cell so the shift leader assigning people at six in the morning can see coverage instantly rather than looking for a file on a shared drive.

atoms.obligation: Plan cross-training so that every operation on a cell has at least two qualified people available on each shift.
atoms.lesson: Single points of failure show up as overtime, as a line that stops when one person is ill, and as a person who cannot take holiday. Read the matrix by column to find operations with thin coverage and by row to find people with narrow skills, then schedule rotation deliberately with the qualified operator as trainer. Prioritise the constraint operations and the awkward night-shift gaps first, and put target dates in the plan or it never happens.

atoms.obligation: Requalify people when the process changes or after a defined absence, recording the date and the assessor's name.
atoms.lesson: Set triggers rather than a blanket annual refresh: any engineering change to the operation, a defect traced to method, an absence from that job beyond a period such as six months, and a return from long-term leave. Record the date, the assessor and the version of the work instruction used, because a change made in March cannot be evidenced against training given in January. Keep the matrix current at the cell rather than in a central binder.

name: rfi-drafting-response
description: Drafts requests for information from the field to the design team and evaluates the answers that come back for cost and schedule consequences. Use when a drawing conflicts with a specification, when a detail is missing at a condition being built next week, or when a designer response quietly adds scope. Also use when the RFI log has aged open items blocking work.
expansions: detail missing at the parapet condition
architect answer changed the scope
rfi log has aged open items
plan and spec conflict on anchor size
need written direction before pouring monday
draft an rfi for the ductbank conflict
engineer response is ambiguous and unusable
track rfi turnaround against contract days

atoms.obligation: State the specific drawing, detail and specification section in question and propose an answer the designer can simply confirm.
atoms.lesson: Requests that ask an open question such as please advise take twice as long to close. A well formed request cites sheet S-301 detail 4 and Section 03 30 00 paragraph 3.2, describes the field condition with a measured dimension, then offers a proposed resolution the engineer of record can stamp with a single word. Reviewers process proposals faster than problems, and a documented proposal protects the contractor if the answer later proves impracticable.

atoms.obligation: Record a date required that is tied to the activity the question blocks, and escalate when the review period lapses.
atoms.lesson: Most general conditions give the designer a fixed review window, commonly seven to fourteen calendar days, and require the contractor to allow reasonable time. Tie every request to the schedule activity it feeds and use that activity late start as the date required. When the window lapses on a path with no float, the dated log entry becomes the evidence for a delay notice. An undated request is worthless in an entitlement argument.

atoms.obligation: Screen every returned answer for added scope, changed means or increased quantity before releasing it to the field crews.
atoms.lesson: Designers frequently answer by adding material, a heavier weld, a fourth anchor, a new waterproofing membrane, while labeling the response a clarification. Compare it against the contract documents in force at bid. If it adds work, reply in writing that the answer is understood as a change and follow with a change order request inside the notice period, before installing anything. Building it first concedes that the work was always included.

atoms.obligation: Do not use a request for information as a substitute for a coordination meeting between the affected trades.
atoms.lesson: A large share of requests are really trade coordination, with sprinkler mains and ductwork fighting for the same ceiling space above corridors. Those belong in a clash session with the mechanical, electrical and fire protection subcontractors, resolved by a signed coordinated ceiling section. Routing them to the architect adds two weeks and returns an instruction to coordinate in the field, which changes nothing. Reserve requests for genuine defects, ambiguities and omissions in the documents.

name: submittal-review-log
description: Builds and runs the submittal register covering shop drawings, product data, samples and mock-ups, from procurement log through designer review to release for fabrication. Use when setting up a register at the start of a job, when a long lead item approval is slipping, or when a submittal returns approved as noted and someone must decide what the notes mean.
expansions: build the submittal register from the specs
steel shop drawings came back approved as noted
long lead switchgear approval is slipping
who reviews the deferred design submittal
returned revise and resubmit a third time
contractor stamp missing on the product data
need release for fabrication this week
track submittals against procurement lead times

atoms.obligation: Build the register directly from the specification sections and flag the items that drive procurement lead time first.
atoms.lesson: Each specification section Part 1 lists the submittals required, so harvest them section by section rather than reacting as trades remember. Then sort by lead time. Structural steel, elevators, switchgear, air handling units, curtain wall and generators routinely carry twenty to fifty weeks of fabrication and delivery. These must go out in the first sixty days regardless of when the work installs, because approval rather than installation is the constraint sitting on the critical path.

atoms.obligation: Review and stamp each submittal yourself for field dimensions and trade coordination before forwarding it to the designer.
atoms.lesson: Standard general conditions make the contractor review a precondition, so forwarding unstamped vendor data lets the designer reject it on procedure alone. The contractor check differs from the designer check: verify field dimensions, embed locations, clearances, and that connected trades submittals agree with each other. The designer only checks conformance with the design concept. Skipping the contractor review is the usual root cause of a second and third resubmittal cycle.

atoms.obligation: Treat approved as noted comments as contract direction and confirm in writing which notes carry additional cost.
atoms.lesson: An approved as noted return releases fabrication, but the notes are binding on the fabricator. Read each one. A note correcting a dimension is a clarification, while a note adding a stiffener plate or upgrading a finish is added scope. Fabricators build to the notes and invoice the extra later. Issue a written response listing which notes are accepted at no change and which are being priced, before the fabricator cuts any steel.

atoms.obligation: Track resubmittal cycles with reason codes and charge review time back when repeat reviews stem from designer inconsistency.
atoms.lesson: Most contracts allow the designer one review and one resubmittal review at no cost, with further reviews billable to whoever caused them. Log a reason code for every rejection. A pattern of new comments appearing only on the third cycle, comments that could have been made on the first, is recoverable. More importantly it is the evidence needed to justify procurement delay that would otherwise be charged to the contractor as liquidated damages.

name: concrete-pour-planning
description: Plans a structural concrete placement end to end: mix verification, pre-placement checklist, placement sequence, weather protection, acceptance testing and curing. Use when scheduling a mat foundation or elevated deck pour, when temperatures head below freezing or above ninety, or when the pump fails mid-placement and somebody must decide about a cold joint.
expansions: mat pour scheduled for friday morning
overnight low below freezing tomorrow
pump failed halfway through the deck
cylinder breaks came back low at twenty eight days
hot weather placement with fast slump loss
where do we put the construction joint
curing plan for the slab on grade
walk the deck before ordering trucks

atoms.obligation: Hold a pre-placement walk to verify forms, reinforcement, embeds, access and equipment before any truck is ordered.
atoms.lesson: Once trucks are on the road the placement happens whether or not the deck is ready. The walk confirms bar cover and lap lengths, that sleeves, anchor bolts and embed plates match the templates, that ties and bracing are complete, and that vibrators, a spare vibrator, the finishing crew and light plants exist. It also confirms the truck route and washout location. A placement stopped for a missing embed becomes a cold joint needing engineered repair.

atoms.obligation: Set concrete temperature and protection requirements against the forecast for the placement window, not against the calendar date.
atoms.lesson: Below forty degrees Fahrenheit cold weather rules apply: heated mixing water, a minimum placement temperature that varies with section thickness, and protection holding the surface above fifty degrees for three to seven days depending on the strength needed. Above ninety, or in wind with low humidity, evaporation rate governs. Above roughly two tenths of a pound per square foot per hour plastic shrinkage cracking is likely, so fog, use retarder, or place at night. Never add water at the truck.

atoms.obligation: Cast acceptance specimens at the point of discharge on a defined frequency and cure them the way the specification requires.
atoms.lesson: Acceptance cylinders are made per class of concrete per day, typically one set per hundred cubic yards or per five thousand square feet of slab, minimum one set each day. They must be initially cured between sixty and eighty degrees and protected from movement for the first day. A set left on a cold deck overnight breaks low and triggers a false investigation. Field cured cylinders stored beside the structure are the correct basis for stripping forms or stressing tendons.

atoms.obligation: Locate construction joints where the designer permits and treat any unplanned stoppage as a structural question.
atoms.lesson: Joints belong near points of minimum shear, generally at midspan of slabs and beams, and are shown on the drawings or governed by the specification. Joints in a mat or a shear wall need the engineer to locate them. If placement stops longer than initial set, often ninety minutes and less in heat, the interface is a cold joint. Stop cleanly at a bulkhead with the specified keyway or dowels and notify the engineer rather than vibrating fresh concrete into stiffened material.

name: change-order-pricing
description: Prices and packages a change order request covering labor, material, equipment, markup, time and impact so it survives owner review. Use when directed to perform extra work, when a design response added scope, when a differing site condition surfaces, or when the owner rejects a proposal as excessive and it must be rebuilt from crew hours.
expansions: price the added scope from the rfi answer
owner says our markup is excessive
hit rock at footing grade this morning
directed change with no signed authorization
need a time extension with the cost proposal
build the proposal up from crew hours
contract unit prices do not cover this work
cumulative impact of many small changes

atoms.obligation: Build the price from crew composition and productivity rather than presenting a lump sum the reviewer cannot trace.
atoms.lesson: An owner reviewer can only attack a number they cannot follow. Show the crew, a foreman with three laborers and an operator, the hours per unit installed, wage rates including fringes as filed, equipment at published rental or ownership rates, quoted material with the vendor quote attached, and the contract markups applied in the order the contract states. Reference a recognized production rate, then explain every adjustment made for the actual working conditions.

atoms.obligation: Give written notice of the change within the contract period even when the price is not yet known.
atoms.lesson: Most contracts require notice within a fixed number of days of the event, commonly seven, fourteen or twenty-one, and make that notice a condition precedent to recovery. The notice does not need a price. It needs the date, the event, the clause relied upon and a statement that cost and time impact will follow when quantified. Waiting until the estimate is finished is the single most common way a completely valid entitlement gets lost.

atoms.obligation: Separate direct cost from time related cost and from disruption, and price each on its own stated basis.
atoms.lesson: Direct cost is the added work itself. Time related cost is extended field overhead, supervision, trailer, temporary power, fencing and small tools, priced per day and owed only if the change extends completion, which needs a schedule analysis rather than an assertion. Disruption is lost productivity on unchanged work caused by trade stacking, out of sequence working or acceleration, and is best quantified by a measured mile comparison against an unimpacted period on the same job.

atoms.obligation: Log every directed change performed without signed authorization and confirm the verbal direction in writing the same day.
atoms.lesson: Field direction from an owner representative is routinely given verbally and later denied. A same day letter reciting who directed what, when, and the position that work proceeds under protest converts a memory into a record. Track these as pending, with cost charged to a discrete cost code so actual expenditure is provable. Unsigned changes cumulatively above roughly five percent of contract value signal that the job needs a commercial reset meeting.

name: schedule-delay-analysis
description: Analyzes what delayed the work and who owns the delay, using the network schedule and contemporaneous records. Use when the owner assesses liquidated damages, when a time extension request needs support, when concurrency is argued, or when someone asks whether float belongs to the owner or the contractor.
expansions: owner threatening liquidated damages
support a time extension request
who owns the float on this path
sub is arguing concurrent delay
rebuild the as built critical path
weather days beyond the baseline allowance
update shows negative float everywhere
time impact analysis for the change

atoms.obligation: Choose an analysis method that matches the records actually available and state that method and its assumptions openly.
atoms.lesson: Prospective time impact analysis inserts a fragnet into the accepted update immediately before the event and suits forward looking change orders. Retrospective windows analysis compares the actual critical path across successive update periods and suits after the fact disputes where monthly updates exist. As planned versus as built is a last resort where updates are missing. Mixing methods, or selecting whichever yields the largest number, is the fastest way to lose credibility in a hearing.

atoms.obligation: Verify the baseline is a legitimate, accepted, logic driven schedule before using it to prove anything at all.
atoms.lesson: A baseline with open ends, excessive hard constraints, long lags substituting for real logic, or activities of unreasonable duration cannot support a delay claim. Check that every activity except the first and last has a predecessor and a successor, count constrained activities, and confirm calendars reflect real workweeks and holidays. If the baseline was never formally accepted, expect attack, so establish acceptance through transmittals and payment applications that were built on it.

atoms.obligation: Classify each delay as excusable compensable, excusable non compensable or inexcusable before quantifying any money.
atoms.lesson: Owner caused delay, late access, late design and owner changes, is excusable and compensable. Unusually severe weather, strikes and named force majeure events are excusable but time only, and weather is measured against the allowance stated in the baseline and historical norms for that location rather than one hard week. Contractor caused delay is inexcusable. Where owner and contractor delays run genuinely concurrently on the critical path, the common outcome is time without money.

atoms.obligation: Support every conclusion with contemporaneous records rather than a schedule reconstructed long after the events occurred.
atoms.lesson: Daily reports, manpower counts, timestamped photographs, delivery tickets, weather station data, meeting minutes and the monthly updates exactly as submitted carry more weight than any analysis. Reconstructed schedules invite an accusation of hindsight bias. Where daily reports are thin, cross check against certified payroll hours by cost code, which cannot easily be revised after the fact and shows precisely where each crew was working in every week of the job.

name: lookahead-pull-planning
description: Runs short interval planning, the three to six week lookahead and the weekly work plan, and makes work ready by clearing constraints before crews arrive. Use when planning the week commitments with foremen, when reliability keeps slipping and nobody knows why, or when a trade shows up to a work face that is not ready.
expansions: run the weekly work plan meeting
crew arrived at a face not ready
three week lookahead from the master schedule
clear constraints before releasing work
percent plan complete keeps dropping
pull plan the interior finishes sequence
foremen commitments are not being met
make ready the level three slab area

atoms.obligation: Break master schedule activities into crew week tasks with a named foreman accountable for each committed task.
atoms.lesson: A master schedule activity such as level three interior partitions over twenty days cannot be executed as written. Short interval planning splits it by area and crew into tasks of one to five days, such as gridline C to F metal stud layout by the framing crew Tuesday through Thursday, with a named person committing to it in the meeting. Commitment by an individual in front of peers, not assignment by a scheduler, is what makes a weekly plan hold.

atoms.obligation: Screen every candidate task against its constraints and admit only work that is genuinely ready to perform.
atoms.lesson: The standard constraint set is design information, materials, prior work complete, labor, equipment, permits and approvals, access, and safe conditions. A task enters the weekly plan only when all of them are clear. Keeping unready work in the plan is what destroys reliability, because crews mobilize, find the face occupied by another trade, and the whole downstream sequence shifts. A backlog of screened ready work also gives crews somewhere useful to go when a task fails.

atoms.obligation: Measure the fraction of weekly commitments actually completed and record a reason code for every single miss.
atoms.lesson: Percent plan complete counts tasks fully finished divided by tasks promised, with no partial credit, because half a wall is not a handoff to the next trade. Mature teams run in the seventies and eighties, and below sixty the plan is fiction. The real value lies in the reason codes: prerequisite work, design, materials, manpower, weather, changed priority. Two months of codes reveals the systemic constraint, which is almost never the trade being blamed in the meeting.

atoms.obligation: Plan each phase backward from a defined handoff milestone with the trades that perform the work present.
atoms.lesson: Pull planning starts at the completion of a phase, for example ceiling grid ready for tile on level four, and works backward, each trade stating what it needs from the trade before it and how long it requires. Overhead rough in reveals that sprinkler mains must lead duct branches, that electrical needs hangers first, and that fire alarm testing gates ceiling close. Durations agreed in that room are the ones the foremen will actually defend.

name: job-hazard-analysis
description: Produces the task level hazard analysis and the toolbox talk that goes with it, matching controls to the work actually planned that day. Use before high risk activity such as work at height, confined space entry or hot work, after a near miss, or when an inspector asks for the written analysis covering work in progress.
expansions: hazard analysis for tomorrows roof edge work
near miss with a falling tool
confined space entry at the wet well
hot work permit for mezzanine welding
inspector asked for the written analysis
toolbox talk on silica cutting
fall protection plan for the leading edge
new crew unfamiliar with site hazards

atoms.obligation: Break the task into steps, name the hazard at each step, then select controls from the highest effective level.
atoms.lesson: The hierarchy runs elimination, substitution, engineering control, administrative control, then personal protective equipment. Weak analyses jump straight to wear gloves and be careful. At a slab edge, elimination means installing the permanent guardrail before the deck is turned over, engineering means a cable guardrail system, administrative means a controlled access zone with a monitor, and equipment means a harness on a rated anchor. Write the highest control the work will realistically accept and then enforce it.

atoms.obligation: Verify anchorage capacity and the clearance available below before authorizing any personal fall arrest system.
atoms.lesson: A personal fall arrest anchor must hold five thousand pounds per attached worker, or be part of a system designed under an engineer with a safety factor of two. Bar joists, conduit and pipe are not anchors. Clearance is the real trap: a six foot lanyard with a deceleration device needs roughly eighteen and a half feet below the anchor once free fall, deceleration, harness stretch, worker height and a safety margin are added. Below that use a self retracting device.

atoms.obligation: Test and continuously monitor the atmosphere before and during every permit required confined space entry.
atoms.lesson: Test in order, oxygen first, then flammables, then toxics, because the sensors depend on oxygen to read correctly. Acceptable is nineteen and a half to twenty three and a half percent oxygen, below ten percent of the lower explosive limit, and toxics under permissible limits, with hydrogen sulfide and carbon monoxide the usual killers in sewer and vault work. An attendant stays outside, rescue is arranged before entry, and non entry retrieval is used wherever the configuration allows.

atoms.obligation: Review the analysis with the crew performing the work and redo it whenever conditions or the crew change.
atoms.lesson: An analysis signed by a superintendent and filed proves nothing about the work. The crew holding the grinder must walk the sequence, and someone must ask what changed since yesterday: a new subcontractor working overhead, rain making the surface slick, a swapped operator. Silica cutting is the standard example, because the control table selection of a water fed saw and a respirator depends on whether the cut is indoors, which changes with the weather.

name: earthwork-cut-fill-balance
description: Works the earthwork side of a site or roadway job: cut and fill quantities, shrink and swell factors, mass haul, borrow and waste, and compaction acceptance. Use when the grading plan needs balancing before bid, when haul cost is running over, when fill will not pass density, or when unsuitable material shows up in the cut.
expansions: balance the site grading before bid
fill will not pass the density test
unsuitable material found in the cut
haul cost running over the estimate
how much borrow do we need
shrink and swell factors for this clay
mass haul diagram for the roadway
overexcavate and replace the soft spot

atoms.obligation: Convert between bank, loose and compacted volumes using material specific factors before comparing cut against fill.
atoms.lesson: Cut is measured in bank cubic yards, hauled in loose cubic yards, and placed in compacted cubic yards. Sand swells roughly ten to fifteen percent loose and shrinks a few percent compacted. Ordinary clay swells twenty five to forty percent loose and shrinks ten to twenty percent compacted. Blasted rock swells fifty percent or more and never returns below bank volume. A plan that balances on raw plan quantities typically leaves the job short of fill by a tenth.

atoms.obligation: Establish the target dry density from a laboratory compaction curve run on the material actually being placed.
atoms.lesson: Acceptance is a percentage of maximum dry density within a stated moisture range, commonly ninety five percent of standard effort in embankment and ninety eight percent of modified effort beneath pavement and footings, within about two points of optimum moisture. The curve must come from the borrow currently in use, since a curve run on last month stockpile will fail against a different soil. When a fill repeatedly fails, suspect the wrong curve before blaming the roller.

atoms.obligation: Match lift thickness and compaction equipment to the soil type rather than to the habit of the crew.
atoms.lesson: Cohesive clay and silt need a kneading action from a sheepsfoot or padfoot roller in loose lifts of six to eight inches. Granular sand and gravel need vibration from a smooth drum and tolerate eight to twelve inch lifts. Running a smooth drum over wet clay builds a crust that traps moisture and gives a passing surface reading over a soft lift. Moisture conditioning by disking and drying, or adding water uniformly, usually beats repeated recompaction on cost.

atoms.obligation: Document unsuitable material and undercut quantities by survey measurement before the excavation is backfilled or covered.
atoms.lesson: Organic topsoil, peat, saturated silt and buried debris are normally paid separately as unsuitable excavation, but only where the limits are proven. Take cross sections of the undercut before placing stone, photograph with a scale in frame, log the date and the inspector present, and have the owner representative initial the field measurement the same day. Once the hole is filled, the quantity becomes whatever the owner is willing to believe about it.

name: geotech-report-interpretation
description: Turns a geotechnical investigation into construction decisions about bearing, foundation type, groundwater, excavation support and settlement. Use when a boring log shows something the design did not assume, when choosing between spread footings and piles, when the water table sits above footing elevation, or when field bearing does not match the report.
expansions: boring shows soft layer at footing depth
spread footings or piles for this building
water table above the excavation bottom
field bearing does not match the report
what does a blow count of four mean
settlement estimate for the fill embankment
expansive clay under the slab on grade
pile driving records versus predicted capacity

atoms.obligation: Read the borings for the layer beneath the bearing stratum, not only the layer the footing will sit on.
atoms.lesson: A firm crust over a compressible layer is the classic settlement trap. Stress from a footing spreads roughly two vertical to one horizontal and stays significant to about twice the footing width, so a soft clay eight feet below a wide mat still governs behavior. Look for blow counts falling into single digits, moisture content near the liquid limit, and any organic description. Bearing capacity failure is rare, while excessive and differential settlement is what actually damages finished buildings.

atoms.obligation: Treat the number and spacing of borings as a hard limit on how far the report may be extrapolated.
atoms.lesson: A report with four borings across two acres describes four points. Between them, glacial till, karst limestone, old channel deposits and undocumented fill vary sharply over short distances, and the report limitations section says exactly this. When an excavation exposes conditions unlike the logs, that is potentially a differing site condition with contractual consequences, so stop work, photograph, notify in writing, and get the geotechnical engineer into the hole before backfilling or over excavating anything.

atoms.obligation: Check groundwater elevation against the planned excavation bottom and design the control before the hole is opened.
atoms.lesson: Water levels in the logs are readings at a moment, often taken at the end of drilling before equilibrium, and a piezometer read days later tells the truth while seasonal high water may sit feet above it. In granular soil an excavation below the table will boil and lose bearing, so wellpoints or deep wells must be installed ahead of digging rather than sumps chasing the failure. In fine sand, sump pumping removes fines and undermines neighboring foundations.

atoms.obligation: Confirm the assumed bearing material in every footing excavation before any reinforcement is placed in it.
atoms.lesson: The design bearing pressure remains an assumption until somebody stands in the hole. Probe with a hand penetrometer or dynamic cone, compare the exposed material against the nearest boring description, and look for loosened, wet or disturbed bottom left by excavator teeth. Soft bottom is corrected by undercut and lean concrete or compacted crushed stone at a documented quantity. Attempting to recompact a wet clay bottom in place rarely works and buries the problem under the footing.

name: formwork-shoring-check
description: Reviews temporary works, formwork, shoring, reshoring and falsework, for load path, capacity and removal timing. Use when a shoring layout arrives from a subcontractor, when deciding whether a deck can be stripped, when reshoring must carry a pour above, or when a form shows deflection or a tie pattern that does not match the drawing.
expansions: can we strip the deck forms monday
shoring layout submitted by the concrete sub
reshore plan for the pour above
form bulged during the wall placement
tie spacing does not match the drawing
falsework over live traffic below
who stamps the temporary works design
shore landing on a slab not at strength

atoms.obligation: Trace the temporary load path continuously down to something able to carry it and verify the surface it lands on.
atoms.lesson: Shoring failures rarely begin at the post. They begin where the load lands: on a slab on grade over uncompacted fill, on a deck whose own capacity was never checked, on mudsills bearing on saturated ground, or on a post whose base plate sits off center. Check the supporting element capacity at its actual age and strength, check bearing area beneath sills, and confirm posts are plumb, because a few degrees of lean turns an axial post into a bending member.

atoms.obligation: Design formwork for lateral pressure computed from rate of placement and concrete temperature rather than assuming a habitual value.
atoms.lesson: For walls and columns, lateral pressure depends on rate of rise, concrete temperature and admixtures used. A fast placement in cool concrete, say ten feet per hour at fifty degrees, produces far higher pressure than a slow lift in warm concrete, and self consolidating mixes must be treated as full liquid head for the entire depth. Blowouts almost always follow a rate of rise faster than the form design assumed, so state the maximum rate on the drawing.

atoms.obligation: Base stripping and reshoring decisions on measured in place strength from field cured specimens or maturity, never elapsed days.
atoms.lesson: Vertical forms on walls and columns often come off within a day because they carry no structural load, but a slab or beam soffit must reach the strength the engineer specified, commonly seventy to eighty percent of design strength, before shores release. Field cured cylinders stored beside the member, or a calibrated maturity method, reflect real conditions. Cold weather can double the time, and a crew stripping on a two day habit through a cold snap will crack the deck.

atoms.obligation: Require a qualified engineer design and an erected condition inspection for falsework over traffic or unusual geometry.
atoms.lesson: Most jurisdictions and specifications require sealed temporary works design once falsework exceeds a height threshold, spans a roadway or railway, or supports post tensioned members. The design must cover the erected condition, wind and construction live load, and eccentric loading from the placement sequence. Equally important, require the designer to inspect the erected structure before the pour, since field substitutions, a different post, a missing brace line, wedges left loose, are what actually cause collapses.

name: critical-lift-planning
description: Plans crane picks including critical lifts, covering capacity charts, rigging, ground bearing, exclusion zones and the lift sequence. Use before a tandem pick, when a load approaches a high percentage of chart capacity, when setting equipment over occupied space, or when a crane must sit near an excavation or an energized line.
expansions: tandem pick for the transfer girder
load is ninety percent of chart capacity
crane setup beside an open excavation
rigging plan for the rooftop unit
outrigger pads over the parking deck
power line clearance for the boom swing
wind limit for tomorrows steel erection
who signs off the critical lift plan

atoms.obligation: Compute total lift weight including all rigging and compare it against the chart at the actual radius and configuration.
atoms.lesson: Chart capacity varies with radius, boom length, counterweight and outrigger extension, and the numbers fall sharply as radius grows. Total load is the piece weight plus block, ball, slings, spreader beam and shackles, plus any water or ice held in the piece. A pick above roughly seventy five percent of chart, a tandem pick, a pick over occupied space, or any load with a shifting center of gravity is normally critical and needs a written plan naming operator, rigger and lift director.

atoms.obligation: Verify ground bearing pressure beneath outriggers or tracks against the allowable value for the actual supporting material.
atoms.lesson: Outrigger loads can far exceed the weight being lifted, because they concentrate machine weight, counterweight and overturning moment onto four points. Compute the pressure, compare it against the allowable for the soil, and size cribbing or mats to spread it. Site specific hazards are backfilled trenches, utility vaults and basement slabs. As a rule keep outriggers outside a line drawn upward at the soil angle of repose from the toe of any open excavation.

atoms.obligation: Maintain the required clearance from energized lines and assign a dedicated spotter whose only task is watching it.
atoms.lesson: For lines up to fifty kilovolts the common minimum approach is twenty feet for any part of the crane, load or line, increasing at higher voltage, unless the utility has deenergized and visibly grounded the line or installed an insulating barrier. Encroachment is judged on swing radius rather than lift position, so the exclusion applies through the full arc. The spotter must be in direct contact with the operator, and a rigger cannot do both jobs.

atoms.obligation: Set and enforce a wind speed limit with stop criteria before the pick, using the manufacturer derating tables.
atoms.lesson: Manufacturers publish a maximum permissible wind speed at the load, commonly around twenty to twenty five miles per hour in standard configuration and far lower for large sail area loads such as wall panels, tanks or rooftop units. Wind at boom tip height exceeds ground readings, so measure at height where possible. Agree the number in the plan, name the person who calls the stop, and treat gusts rather than average speed as the trigger to set down.

name: progress-payment-application
description: Prepares and defends the monthly payment application covering the schedule of values, percent complete, stored materials, retainage and lien waivers. Use at month end, when the owner representative disputes a line, when a supplier wants payment for material sitting off site, or when retainage reduction becomes due.
expansions: build the schedule of values for approval
owner disputes percent complete on drywall
stored materials off site not being paid
retainage reduction at fifty percent complete
lien waivers missing from two subs
pay application rejected for missing backup
lender consultant flagged front loading
final payment and closeout documentation

atoms.obligation: Structure the schedule of values so every line is measurable and matches how progress will actually be verified.
atoms.lesson: A line reading mechanical, two million dollars guarantees a monthly argument. Break it by system and by floor so progress is countable: underground rough in level one, overhead duct level two, equipment set, controls, test and balance. Carry general conditions as a separately identified time related line, and keep mobilization and bonds honest, because a lender consultant will flag front loading and can suspend an entire application over one suspicious line item.

atoms.obligation: Support percent complete with a physical measurement agreed with the owner representative before the application is submitted.
atoms.lesson: The productive path is a joint walk in the final week of the period, marking installed quantities, linear feet of pipe, tons of steel erected, square feet of slab placed, and initialing the sheet on the spot. Submitting a number first and defending it later invites an across the board cut. Where progress is genuinely hard to see, such as controls programming or commissioning, agree milestone based earning rules at the start of the job instead of percentages.

atoms.obligation: Meet every documentary condition for stored material, including title, insurance and segregated protected storage with access.
atoms.lesson: Contracts allow payment for suitably stored material under conditions: a paid invoice or bill of sale transferring title, insurance covering the material at that location, and for off site storage a bonded warehouse, segregation and labeling for the project, plus the owner right of access. Photographs showing the project name are standard practice. Missing any single one gives a reviewer clean grounds to zero the line, and the cash flow effect on a fabricator can be severe.

atoms.obligation: Collect conditional and unconditional lien waivers matched exactly to the amounts and periods actually paid down the chain.
atoms.lesson: The normal sequence is a conditional waiver through the current application submitted with it, exchanged for an unconditional waiver covering the prior period once that payment clears. Amounts and through dates must match payment records exactly, since a waiver naming the wrong date leaves the window open. Missing waivers from second tier suppliers are the usual gap, and in most jurisdictions an unpaid supplier keeps lien rights against the owner regardless of what the general contractor paid.
