name: punchlist-substantial-completion
description: Runs the closeout end of a project: punch list generation, substantial completion determination, correction tracking and final acceptance. Use when the owner wants to occupy part of a building, when the punch list keeps growing after it was supposed to close, when arguing whether an item is punch or incomplete work, or when occupancy approval gates handover.
expansions: owner wants to occupy the second floor
punch list keeps growing after signoff
is this punch or incomplete work
occupancy certificate is holding closeout
warranty start date dispute with the owner
sub will not return to close punch items
assemble the closeout and warranty documents
final inspection scheduled next week

atoms.obligation: Require each trade to punch and certify its own work before the formal owner walk is ever scheduled.
atoms.lesson: The purpose of substantial completion is beneficial occupancy, not the owner first look at unfinished work. A three stage approach works: the subcontractor punches itself, the general contractor punches the subcontractor and rejects the area if it is not close, then owner and designer walk. Skipping the first two stages produces a two thousand item owner list, months of churn, and a delayed occupancy certificate whose cost usually lands on the general contractor.

atoms.obligation: Distinguish incomplete work from punch items, because only minor correction is compatible with substantial completion.
atoms.lesson: Substantial completion means the work is sufficiently complete that the owner can occupy or use it for its intended purpose. Missing life safety systems, an untested fire alarm, an uninspected elevator or an unusable restroom are incomplete work and defeat it, while scratched paint, a misaligned door and missing keys are punch. The consequences turn on this line, since warranty periods start, liquidated damages usually stop, retainage reduces, and risk of loss and utilities normally transfer.

atoms.obligation: Assign an accountable party and a due date to every punch item and reinspect rather than accepting a claimed fix.
atoms.lesson: Track by room or area, by responsible subcontractor, with a photograph and a date on each item. Items claimed complete but never verified are the reason lists reopen weeks later. Where a subcontractor has demobilized and refuses to return, the supplementation clause permits correction by others after written notice, commonly forty eight to seventy two hours, with cost back charged. The notice must go out before hiring the replacement or the back charge will not hold.

atoms.obligation: Assemble operation manuals, warranties, record drawings and documented training before requesting release of final payment.
atoms.lesson: Closeout documents are contractual deliverables, and owners increasingly withhold final payment and retainage against them. The package typically includes operation and maintenance manuals by system, equipment warranties with start dates tied to substantial completion rather than delivery, spare parts and attic stock with signed receipts, record drawings showing actual routing of buried and concealed work, air and water balance reports, and owner training sessions with dated attendance sheets.

name: claim-notice-drafting
description: Handles contract administration around disputes: notices, reservation of rights, differing site conditions, suspension and termination correspondence. Use when the owner directs work believed to be out of scope, when access is denied, when payment runs late, or when a letter arrives that demands a careful response inside a stated number of days.
expansions: owner denied access to the work area
respond to the cure notice within ten days
differing site condition notice needed today
payment thirty days late what are our rights
reserve rights while proceeding under protest
suspension of work letter from the owner
termination for convenience just arrived
preserve records for the coming dispute

atoms.obligation: Identify the governing clause and its deadline before writing a single line of the letter.
atoms.lesson: Notice periods differ by contract and by subject. Differing site conditions usually require notice promptly and before the condition is disturbed, changes commonly within seven to twenty one days of the event, and claims for time and money within a further period with supporting detail. Many are conditions precedent, meaning late notice bars an otherwise valid claim. Read the executed contract and its supplementary conditions rather than a remembered standard form, since owners routinely shorten these periods.

atoms.obligation: State facts, dates and contract references without characterizing motives or assigning blame to the other party.
atoms.lesson: Correspondence written in anger becomes an exhibit later. An effective notice recites the event and its date, cites the clause, states the effect on cost and time so far as known, reserves the right to supplement, and requests specific relief or direction. Avoid adjectives, avoid alleging bad faith, and avoid conceding facts not yet verified. A single sentence such as we accept responsibility for the delay while we investigate is worth more to the other side than any argument.

atoms.obligation: Continue performing directed work under a written reservation rather than stopping and exposing the company to default.
atoms.lesson: Nearly every contract obliges the contractor to keep performing while a dispute is resolved, so stopping without a clear contractual right hands the owner a default and possible termination. The correct move is a letter stating the direction is disputed, that work proceeds under protest and under the changes clause, that costs are tracked in a separate account, and that a claim will follow. Stopping is justifiable only for nonpayment where the contract expressly permits it after notice.

atoms.obligation: Preserve and segregate project records the moment a dispute becomes reasonably foreseeable, and start discrete cost tracking.
atoms.lesson: Issue a hold on routine deletion, then gather daily reports, photographs, schedules as submitted, meeting minutes, correspondence, cost reports by code and certified payrolls into one indexed set. Instruct staff that internal notes are discoverable and should stay factual. Cost tracking must begin immediately in a dedicated code, because reconstructing what a change cost from a blended labor account six months later reduces a defensible claim to an estimate a reviewer can dismiss.

name: quantity-takeoff-estimate
description: Produces quantity takeoffs and unit priced estimates for bidding or budgeting, with productivity, waste and pricing assumptions written down. Use when a bid is due, when a conceptual budget is needed from partial documents, when reconciling two estimates that differ, or when checking a subcontractor number against your own build up.
expansions: bid due friday need a takeoff
conceptual budget from schematic drawings
reconcile our number against the subs
how much waste on the rebar
price the cast in place concrete package
productivity assumptions for the block wall
escalation on steel over eighteen months
check the earthwork quantity in the bid form

atoms.obligation: Record a basis of estimate capturing every assumption, exclusion and document revision the price was built from.
atoms.lesson: Estimates get compared, argued over and reused months later by people who were not there. Write down the drawing and addendum numbers priced, the wage basis, the assumed duration and crew sizes, escalation to the midpoint of construction, exclusions such as permits, testing, hazardous material and owner furnished equipment, and what each allowance covers. When the number is attacked, that document is the defense, and when scope changes it shows exactly which assumption broke.

atoms.obligation: Separate net measured quantity from waste and apply waste factors by material and by geometry.
atoms.lesson: Waste is not one percentage across a job. Reinforcing steel typically runs three to five percent for laps beyond those detailed plus cutting drop. Concrete adds three to eight percent for subgrade irregularity and over excavation, more on soft ground. Drywall and tile scale with the number of openings and cuts, and pipe and duct waste rises in fitting heavy layouts. A flat five percent everywhere hides a real overrun in one trade behind a false cushion in another.

atoms.obligation: Convert quantities to cost through crew hour productivity suited to the conditions rather than through published unit prices.
atoms.lesson: A published unit price embeds somebody else crew, height, access and repetition. The same masonry crew laying block along a warehouse wall achieves a fraction of that rate in a stair core with scaffolding and small returns. Build labor from crew composition and hours per unit, then apply factors for work above forty feet, winter conditions, night shifts, congestion and sustained overtime, where fifty or sixty hour weeks measurably erode hourly output over consecutive weeks.

atoms.obligation: Reconcile the estimate against independent order of magnitude checks on the driving quantities before the number goes out.
atoms.lesson: Ratio checks catch the errors that lose money: cubic yards of concrete per square foot of building area, pounds of reinforcement per cubic yard, tons of structural steel per square foot, and total cost per square foot against comparable completed jobs. A takeoff showing a hundred and ninety pounds of reinforcement per cubic yard in a simple frame is either an unusually heavy design or a double count. Reconcile the difference before bid day while there is time.

name: subcontractor-bid-leveling
description: Prequalifies subcontractors and levels their bids so scope gaps surface before award rather than during construction. Use on bid day when three numbers are far apart, when a low bidder scope letter looks thin, when checking bonding and crew capacity, or when writing the scope exhibit for a subcontract.
expansions: three bids and one is way low
scope letter is missing the flashing
check bonding capacity for this sub
level the electrical bids before award
write the scope exhibit for the subcontract
sub already has too much work
who covers hoisting and daily cleanup
prequalify a new drywall subcontractor

atoms.obligation: Level bids against a written scope checklist so every bidder is compared on identical inclusions and exclusions.
atoms.lesson: Differences between subcontractor numbers are usually scope rather than price. Build a line by line matrix from the specification and drawings and mark each bidder inclusion or exclusion for layout, hoisting, unloading, scaffold, fire caulking at their own penetrations, patching, temporary protection, daily cleanup, record markups, warranty duration and taxes. The low number nearly always excludes two of these, and buying it without adding them back is how a package loses money by month three.

atoms.obligation: Assess capacity against the subcontractor current backlog and the crews it can genuinely field for this job.
atoms.lesson: Financial prequalification examines bonding capacity, single job limit, work in progress and the ratio of backlog to annual revenue. The practical question is people: how many crews they run, who the foreman on this job will be by name, and what else that foreman is scheduled to run this year. A firm bidding a job worth half its annual volume, or committing its only competent superintendent to two projects, will fail regardless of a clean financial statement.

atoms.obligation: Verify insurance, licensing and safety record against the project actual requirements before issuing any award letter.
atoms.lesson: Check that the license class covers this work in this jurisdiction, that certificates match required limits including owner mandated excess coverage, that additional insured endorsements are the correct form for both ongoing and completed operations, and that waiver of subrogation is present. Safety screening uses the experience modification rate, often with a threshold around one, plus recordable incident rates and citation history. Discovering an uninsurable subcontractor after mobilization leaves no good options at all.

atoms.obligation: Write the subcontract scope exhibit from the leveling sheet rather than by referencing specification sections alone.
atoms.lesson: A scope reading all work in Division 9 invites argument over who carries plywood backing, metal stud framing for soffits, or sealant at dissimilar materials. The exhibit should list included specification sections and drawings by number and revision, then enumerate the interface items resolved during leveling and the ones assigned elsewhere. State the schedule commitment, the expected manpower ramp, and the notice period for schedule changes, since those terms matter most when the job compresses.

name: rebar-placement-inspection
description: Inspects reinforcing steel before a concrete placement: bar size and grade, spacing, cover, laps, development, supports and openings. Use when signing off a mat, wall or deck before pour, when the placing drawing does not match the structural drawing, when bars conflict with embeds, or when a bar must be cut or bent in the field.
expansions: walk the mat before tomorrows pour
placing drawing differs from the structural sheet
rebar conflicts with the anchor bolt cage
can we field bend this bar
cover looks short at the wall face
lap length for the number eight bars
opening in the slab needs trim bars
coated bar damaged during handling

atoms.obligation: Verify concrete cover at the actual exposure condition and confirm supports will hold under the placement crew.
atoms.lesson: Cover is the primary defense against corrosion and is specified by exposure, commonly three inches cast against earth, two inches at formed surfaces exposed to weather for larger bars, and less for interior conditions. Bolsters, chairs and wheels must be spaced closely enough, often three to four feet, that the mat does not sag when workers walk it, and plastic tipped or coated supports are required at exposed faces. Top bars pushed to the bottom of the mat are a common serious defect.

atoms.obligation: Check lap lengths, splice staggering and splice locations against the class specified for that bar size.
atoms.lesson: Tension lap length depends on bar size, concrete strength, cover, spacing, epoxy coating and whether the bar is a top bar with more than twelve inches of concrete cast below it, which adds roughly thirty percent. Splices should be staggered and kept away from points of maximum stress unless detailed otherwise, so column bars lap just above the floor and wall bars lap near midheight. Crews lapping forty diameters from habit will be short on coated top bars.

atoms.obligation: Do not cut, heat or field bend reinforcement without written direction from the engineer of record.
atoms.lesson: Bars are routinely in the way of an embed, a sleeve or a post tensioning anchor. Heating alters the steel properties and is generally prohibited, and rebending a bar already bent can crack it, particularly in larger sizes and higher grades. The correct response is to document the conflict, propose a resolution such as relocating the sleeve, adding trim bars around the opening, or splicing in a bent replacement, and get it in writing. Cut bars found after the pour become costly repairs.

atoms.obligation: Confirm added trim and corner reinforcement at every opening, corner and discontinuity before signing the placement off.
atoms.lesson: Openings interrupt primary reinforcement, and the drawings usually carry a typical detail requiring bars equivalent to those interrupted placed each side, plus diagonal bars at corners to control cracking. Crews frame the opening and forget the diagonals almost every time. Also check corner bars in walls and footings, dowels matching the verticals above, hooks correctly oriented, and that any epoxy coating damaged during handling has been patched before concrete arrives on site.

name: erosion-sediment-control
description: Sets up and maintains construction site stormwater compliance: the pollution prevention plan, perimeter controls, stabilization, inspections and discharge records. Use before disturbing ground, when a rain event is forecast, when sediment has left the site, when an inspector issues a notice, or when a stabilized area should be released from inspection.
expansions: rain forecast and the slope is bare
sediment tracked onto the public road
inspector issued a notice of violation
set up perimeter controls before clearing
silt fence undermined along the east line
when can we stop inspecting the stabilized area
concrete washout overflowing near an inlet
weekly inspection report is overdue

atoms.obligation: Install perimeter and inlet protection before clearing begins and phase disturbance to limit the area left open.
atoms.lesson: Controls installed after grading starts never catch up with the work. Perimeter silt fence must be trenched in and backfilled rather than stapled to the surface, or runoff simply undercuts it within one storm. Sequence the work so only the actively worked area is bare, stabilizing completed slopes as they finish. Permits commonly require stabilization to begin within seven to fourteen days of the last disturbance, and inspectors judge compliance by open acreage as much as by devices.

atoms.obligation: Inspect on the required schedule and after qualifying rainfall, recording every corrective action with the date completed.
atoms.lesson: Typical permit terms require inspection every seven days, or every fourteen days plus within twenty four hours of a storm above a threshold, often a quarter or half inch, with a rain gauge kept on site. Each report names the inspector, the areas walked, deficiencies found, and the date each was corrected, generally within seven days. Enforcement almost always begins with missing or backdated reports rather than an observed discharge, because paperwork gaps are easy to prove.

atoms.obligation: Control concrete washout, fuel storage and vehicle tracking as deliberately as sediment leaving the graded areas.
atoms.lesson: Washout from concrete trucks and pumps is highly alkaline and is a frequent violation. Use a lined containment sized for the pours, sited away from inlets and drainage paths, with signage so drivers actually use it, and remove hardened material before it overtops. Stabilized entrances of coarse stone over fabric, long enough for a full tire rotation, plus prompt street sweeping, address tracking. Fuel and equipment washing need secondary containment and spill kits at the point of use.

atoms.obligation: Update the written plan whenever site layout, sequence or control measures change on the ground.
atoms.lesson: The plan is a living permit document and the site drawing inside it must reflect where the controls actually are. When a stockpile moves, a basin converts to permanent detention, or a new entrance opens, amend the plan and log the change with a date and signature. Inspectors compare the plan drawing against the field, and a mismatch is a violation even where the field arrangement performs better. Keep the plan and all reports on site and available.

name: work-zone-traffic-control
description: Designs and reviews temporary traffic control for work in and near roadways: taper lengths, advance signing, lane closures, pedestrian routes and flagging. Use when planning a lane closure, when a crane or delivery blocks a travel lane, when pedestrians must be routed around the site, or when a near miss or complaint arrives about the work zone.
expansions: lane closure for the utility tie in
pedestrian route around the sidewalk closure
taper length for a forty five mile road
night work signing and lighting plan
flagger setup at the single lane section
driver complaint about confusing signs
crane blocking a travel lane saturday
police detail required for the detour

atoms.obligation: Size the advance warning area and the merging taper from the posted speed and the offset being closed.
atoms.lesson: Merging taper length derives from offset width and speed. At forty five miles per hour and above it is roughly the offset times the speed, and below that it is the offset times speed squared divided by sixty. Closing a twelve foot lane at fifty miles per hour therefore needs around six hundred feet of taper, with advance warning signs spaced hundreds of feet apart on a high speed road. Short tapers are the most common and most dangerous work zone defect.

atoms.obligation: Provide a continuous accessible pedestrian route or a signed detour whenever a walkway is affected by the work.
atoms.lesson: Closing a sidewalk and posting pedestrians use other side without a marked crossing puts people into the roadway and is a frequent source of liability. The route must be firm, stable, slip resistant, at least the required clear width, detectable by cane along its whole length with continuous barriers rather than tape or cones, and free of overhead hazards. Where a covered walkway is used, lighting and drainage matter. Plan the pedestrian route before the vehicle route.

atoms.obligation: Assign trained flaggers with the required equipment and never let one control a section they cannot see fully.
atoms.lesson: Flaggers need certification where the jurisdiction requires it, high visibility apparel of the correct class for the speed and lighting, a paddle rather than a flag, and a planned escape path. On a single lane section too long or curved for line of sight, use radios, a pilot vehicle or portable signals instead. Flaggers stand on the shoulder rather than in the lane, positioned far enough ahead of the work that a stopped queue never reaches the crew.

atoms.obligation: Inspect the setup at the start of every shift and after weather, removing or covering devices that no longer apply.
atoms.lesson: Devices drift over time. Cones get knocked flat, signs rotate in the wind, and barricade lights fail overnight without anybody noticing. Drive the zone in each direction at the posted speed at shift start, and again after dark to check retroreflectivity. Equally important, cover or remove signs once their condition ends, because a lane closed ahead sign standing over an open lane trains drivers to ignore the whole setup and undermines the defense if a crash is litigated.

name: utility-conflict-resolution
description: Finds, verifies and resolves conflicts with existing buried and overhead utilities before and during excavation. Use when a design line crosses an unknown existing one, before any digging, when locate marks look questionable, when a line is struck, or when a relocation must be negotiated with the utility owner.
expansions: new storm crosses an unmarked gas line
locate marks do not match the plan
pothole the crossing before excavating
struck a fiber line during trenching
utility owner will not commit to a date
record drawing shows the main two feet off
abandoned duct bank in the way
who pays for the relocation

atoms.obligation: Establish the quality level of every utility depiction and upgrade the critical ones by physically exposing them.
atoms.lesson: Subsurface utility information runs from records only, through surveyed surface features, to designating with geophysical methods, up to physically exposing the utility and surveying its top elevation and size. Records are frequently wrong on depth and can sit several feet off horizontally, especially older water and gas. Any crossing with tight clearance, or a parallel run inside the excavation influence zone, should be exposed by vacuum excavation before design is finished rather than on the day of digging.

atoms.obligation: Place the one call notice inside the legal window and keep the marks valid for the duration of the excavation.
atoms.lesson: Statutes require notice a set number of business days before excavating, commonly two or three, with the ticket valid for a limited period, often ten to twenty one days, after which it must be renewed. White line the intended excavation so locators mark only what matters. Marks fade, get graded off, or are covered by stockpiles, so renew rather than dig on a stale ticket, because statutory damage protection generally depends on holding a valid ticket.

atoms.obligation: Hand dig or vacuum excavate within the statutory tolerance zone of any marked line whatever the schedule pressure.
atoms.lesson: The tolerance zone is typically eighteen to twenty four inches either side of the mark, and mechanical excavation inside it is prohibited. Gas and fiber are the high consequence strikes, since fiber cuts carry enormous consequential damages from service outages. A gas strike requires immediate evacuation upwind, a call to the operator and emergency services, and no attempt to stop the leak or operate any ignition source, including the machine that struck the line.

atoms.obligation: Start relocation coordination with the utility owner months ahead and track their committed dates in the schedule.
atoms.lesson: Utility owners work on their own capital cycles and are rarely bound by the construction contract schedule. Relocations routinely need six to twelve months for design, easement acquisition, material procurement where transformers and large valves carry long lead times, and crew scheduling. Put each relocation into the project schedule as an activity with the utility named as responsible party, obtain written commitment dates, and report slippage monthly, because unrelocated utilities are a leading cause of delay on public work.

name: bridge-condition-inspection
description: Carries out and reports condition inspections of bridges and similar structures: element level condition states, defect characterization, capacity concerns and follow up actions. Use when a routine inspection cycle is due, when spalling or section loss is reported, when a vehicle strikes a girder, or when deciding whether a finding requires load posting or immediate closure.
expansions: routine inspection due on the overpass
spalling with exposed rebar on the pier
truck struck the fascia girder last night
section loss at the bearing seat
do we need to post this bridge
fatigue crack found at a weld detail
scour at the abutment after the flood
write up the condition report findings

atoms.obligation: Record defects by element with quantities in each condition state rather than as narrative description alone.
atoms.lesson: Element level inspection assigns each element a total quantity and distributes it across four condition states from good to severe, by defect type: delamination and spall, cracking, corrosion, section loss, settlement. A note reading some spalling on the pier cap cannot be trended or programmed for funding. Twelve of forty linear feet in condition state three, with two square feet of exposed reinforcement showing measurable section loss, can be compared against the last cycle and priced for repair.

atoms.obligation: Treat any finding affecting load capacity or public safety as requiring same day notification, not a report entry.
atoms.lesson: Cracks in fracture critical members, severe section loss at a bearing or truss connection, a shifted bearing, substructure settlement, or scour exposing a footing all demand escalation to the owner that day and consideration of closure or load posting. The report cycle is measured in weeks while a member losing capacity is measured in traffic passes. Photograph, measure, mark the extent with the date on the member, and put the notification in writing immediately.

atoms.obligation: Inspect for scour and channel change after flood events and assess the substructure below the waterline.
atoms.lesson: Scour is the leading cause of bridge failure in service. Compare current streambed elevations against the previous cycle at every pier and abutment, probe for undermining, and look for exposed pile caps, displaced riprap, debris accumulation and channel migration. A pier appearing sound above water may be standing on exposed piles below it. Where visibility prevents assessment, arrange an underwater inspection rather than recording the substructure as satisfactory by default.

atoms.obligation: Characterize cracking by orientation, width and location before concluding whether it is structural or not.
atoms.lesson: In concrete, fine map cracking usually indicates shrinkage or alkali reaction, flexural cracks run perpendicular to the span on the tension face, and shear cracks run diagonally near supports. Width, leakage, efflorescence and rust staining indicate severity. In steel, any crack at a weld toe, a coped beam end, or a cover plate termination is treated as fatigue related and serious until an engineer determines otherwise, and its ends should be marked and dated for future comparison.

name: systems-commissioning-turnover
description: Plans and runs commissioning of building systems from prefunctional checks through functional testing, issue tracking and turnover. Use when a mechanical system nears completion, when a functional test fails and nobody agrees who owns the fix, when writing the commissioning plan and scripts, or when the owner is about to take over operation.
expansions: functional test failed on the air handler
write the commissioning plan and scripts
prefunctional checklists from the mechanical sub
balance report looks fabricated
integrated test of the smoke control sequence
owner training before turnover next month
issues log still open at handover
seasonal testing after the building opens

atoms.obligation: Complete and verify prefunctional checks before scheduling any functional performance test on a system.
atoms.lesson: Functional testing exercises the control sequence and is not the place to discover that a damper actuator was never connected or a valve is installed backwards. Prefunctional checklists confirm installation, power, labeling, filters, alignment, manufacturer startup where required, point to point verification of every input and output, and that test and balance is finished. A failed test caused by incomplete installation wastes a room full of people and is the usual reason commissioning falls behind.

atoms.obligation: Write test scripts that exercise the sequence of operations including failure modes and setpoint transitions.
atoms.lesson: Scripts should be drawn from the specified sequence line by line: occupied to unoccupied changeover, economizer changeover at the stated outdoor conditions, heating to cooling transition without simultaneous operation, static pressure reset, freeze protection, smoke detection shutdown, and loss of power with automatic restart. The interesting failures live in transitions and failure modes rather than at steady state. State the expected result and acceptance tolerance for each step beforehand so nobody negotiates a pass afterwards.

atoms.obligation: Log every deviation with a responsible party and retest after correction rather than accepting a verbal fix.
atoms.lesson: The issues log is the commissioning deliverable that carries lasting value. Each entry needs the system, the test step, observed versus expected behavior, the assigned party whether contractor, designer or vendor, the date, and the resolution with a retest date and result. Disputed items where the specified sequence itself is wrong belong to the designer and often need a change. Letting them sit unassigned is how buildings open with disabled sequences nobody ever revisits.

atoms.obligation: Deliver systems manuals and hands on owner training before turnover and record who actually attended.
atoms.lesson: Operating staff inherit systems they did not design or install. Training should happen at the equipment, covering the sequence in plain language, seasonal changeover, alarm response, what the setpoints are and why, filter and belt schedules, and the location of shutoffs. Record the session and include it in the systems manual alongside the final sequence, balance report, control drawings and setpoint schedule. Deferred seasonal testing must be scheduled in writing with retainage or warranty attached.

name: construction-survey-layout
description: Sets and checks construction survey control and layout: control networks, benchmarks, stakeout, as built verification and tolerance checks. Use when establishing control on a new site, when two crews layouts disagree, when an element is discovered out of position, or when checking anchor bolt or shaft tolerances before the next trade arrives.
expansions: set control network for the new site
two crews layouts do not agree
anchor bolts out of position for steel
verify the elevator shaft plumb and size
benchmark elevation disagrees with the plan
check building corners before foundations
as built the underground before backfill
column line drifted over four floors

atoms.obligation: Establish a control network of redundant protected monuments and tie every layout task back to it.
atoms.lesson: Control points must sit outside the construction footprint, protected from equipment, with at least three visible from any working position so a setup can be checked rather than trusted. Record coordinates, the datum and projection, and the source and elevation of each benchmark. Sites go wrong when a crew sets a nail in a curb as a temporary point, the curb is later removed, and three weeks of layout traces back to something that no longer exists.

atoms.obligation: Check into a second known point before laying out anything from a new instrument setup.
atoms.lesson: The discipline is simple and routinely skipped. After occupying and backsighting, shoot a third known point and confirm the coordinate and elevation agree within tolerance. This catches a mistyped instrument height, a transposed point number, a bumped tripod and a wrong backsight, the four errors behind nearly every serious layout failure. Repeat the check at the end of the setup, because an instrument disturbed midway otherwise leaves hours of work wrong with no evidence.

atoms.obligation: Verify critical embedded items against their placement tolerance before the concrete that fixes them is placed.
atoms.lesson: Anchor bolts for structural steel carry tight tolerances, often around an eighth of an inch within a bolt group and a quarter to half inch for group location, and correcting them after the pour means an engineered repair or field modified base plates. Survey the template after the reinforcing crew has worked around it and again immediately before placement, since cages get bumped. The same discipline applies to hoistway dimensions and plumbness and to embed plates for facade attachment.

atoms.obligation: Record as built positions of concealed and buried work before it is covered by backfill or concrete.
atoms.lesson: Buried utilities, embedded conduit, post tensioning tendon layouts and blockouts become unrecoverable once covered. Survey the actual horizontal position and invert elevation of pipe as installed rather than the design line, and photograph with the survey rod and a visible reference in frame. This record settles later conflicts about who put a line where, supports quantity claims for depths beyond plan, and prevents the next contractor coring through a tendon, a mistake that closes a floor for weeks.

name: course-timetable-build
description: Builds and de-conflicts a teaching timetable across cohorts, rooms and staff availability. Use when someone says the autumn grid needs drafting, two classes clash for the same year group, a room is double-booked, or a module has more registrations than the lab has seats. Also use for mid-term reshuffles after a staff absence or a room closure.
expansions: two lectures clash for the same cohort
seminar room double booked on tuesday
draft the grid for autumn term
lab seats forty but sixty registered
tutor is only available monday mornings
students cannot take both options
room flooded need to move classes
timetable must be out before registration

atoms.obligation: Resolve cohort clashes before optimising room use, because a student who cannot attend outranks a room left half empty.
atoms.lesson: Every timetable has two objectives that pull apart: student clash-freedom and estate utilisation. Utilisation targets of 65 to 75 percent are normal and chasing higher numbers packs rooms so tightly that any single change cascades. Build the compulsory core for each cohort first as fixed blocks, then place option modules into the gaps those blocks leave. Only when the clash matrix is clean should you swap rooms to raise fill rates.

atoms.obligation: Model realistic movement time between buildings and never schedule back-to-back sessions across sites without a changeover gap.
atoms.lesson: Published start times usually assume a 5 or 10 minute changeover, which works within one building but not across a split campus. Walk the longest realistic route yourself, add time for lifts and for students with mobility needs, and encode a minimum gap between paired sessions. Timetables that ignore this look valid in the grid and fail in week one, with lecturers losing the first ten minutes of every class to stragglers.

atoms.obligation: Collect staff availability constraints and their reasons in writing before drafting, and record which are contractual and which are preferences.
atoms.lesson: Constraints arrive as a flat list, but they are not equal. Contractual part-time fractions, caring responsibilities covered by flexible working agreements, and shared appointments with another department are hard. Preferring no Friday afternoons is soft. Tag each one at intake, because when the grid is over-constrained you must relax something, and relaxing a hard constraint invites a grievance while relaxing a soft one only invites a complaint.

atoms.obligation: Freeze the timetable at a published date and route later changes through a single change-control log with notified parties.
atoms.lesson: Students book childcare, part-time jobs and travel against the published grid, so late moves cause real harm and generate appeals. Set a freeze date roughly two weeks before teaching starts. After it, changes need a named approver, a reason, and a notification to every affected cohort, tutor and room owner. Keeping one log also prevents the classic failure where two staff fix the same clash in opposite directions and reintroduce it.

name: enrolment-forecast-planning
description: Produces intake and roll forecasts and turns them into section counts, staffing and space plans. Trigger when someone asks how many students to expect next September, whether to open another form entry or teaching section, why applications are down against last year, or how many places to hold for late arrivals.
expansions: how many starters expected in september
applications down against last year
do we open another section
roll projection for the next three years
melt rate between offer and enrolment
planning staffing for the new intake
waiting list longer than places
budget needs a pupil number line

atoms.obligation: Forecast each stage of the funnel separately rather than applying one conversion rate from enquiry to enrolled student.
atoms.lesson: Enquiry to application, application to offer, offer to acceptance, and acceptance to actual arrival each behave differently and move for different reasons. Summer melt between acceptance and arrival is the stage most often forgotten and is highly sensitive to accommodation availability, visa timing and competitor clearing activity. Track each stage against the same week of the prior cycle, not against the final total, so you see movement while there is still time to respond.

atoms.obligation: State the assumptions behind every projection and show at least a low, central and high case for planning.
atoms.lesson: A single number invites a single staffing decision and no contingency. Give three cases with the driver that separates them, such as sibling yield in a school roll or offer-to-acceptance rate for a university course. Note the decision each case would change: the high case may need an extra section and a room, the low case may need a hiring pause. Planners can act on a range; they cannot act on a point estimate that quietly hides a ten percent error band.

atoms.obligation: Anchor forecasts in cohort progression and local birth or feeder data before adjusting for judgement about demand.
atoms.lesson: Most of next year is already known. Continuing students progress at fairly stable rates, and only entry cohorts and repeaters are genuinely uncertain. For schools, published birth cohort counts and feeder school rolls give a five-year horizon on the reception intake. For universities, the strongest anchor is prior-year applications by course at the equivalent cycle week. Judgement should adjust that base by a stated percentage, not replace it.

atoms.obligation: Convert forecasts into thresholds that trigger a decision, naming the number and the date each decision must be taken.
atoms.lesson: A forecast is only useful if it changes something. Write the operational triggers explicitly: if confirmed acceptances pass a set count by a named date, open an additional section and start recruitment; below another count, merge sections. Tie each threshold to the lead time it needs, since hiring a teacher takes months and a room fit-out takes weeks. Without dated thresholds, teams argue about the forecast instead of acting on it.

name: admissions-application-review
description: Runs consistent, defensible review of applications against published criteria. Use when reading a batch of applications, calibrating readers who score differently, deciding borderline cases, applying contextual data, or answering a parent or applicant asking why they were not offered a place.
expansions: reading a batch of applications this week
two readers scored the same file differently
borderline candidate needs a decision
applicant asking why they were rejected
contextual flags for widening participation
oversubscribed and need tie breakers
reference contradicts the personal statement
setting the offer threshold this cycle

atoms.obligation: Score every application against the published criteria only, and never against a criterion that was not advertised to applicants.
atoms.lesson: Admissions decisions are challengeable, and the first question in any appeal or regulatory review is whether the published criteria were the criteria actually applied. School oversubscription criteria must be applied in their stated order, with distance or random allocation as the stated tie-breaker. University readers must not credit an unadvertised preference such as a particular school type. If a criterion matters, publish it before the cycle opens rather than applying it silently.

atoms.obligation: Calibrate readers on a shared sample before the batch opens and re-calibrate whenever scores drift apart.
atoms.lesson: Reader drift is the largest source of unfairness in holistic review. Run a calibration session on six to ten anonymised files spanning the range, have readers score independently, then discuss every disagreement of two points or more until the rubric language is shared. Repeat mid-cycle, because readers harden or soften as they see more files. Double-read a random sample throughout and monitor the gap between readers as a running check.

atoms.obligation: Record a short written reason for each decision at the moment it is made, in the language of the criteria.
atoms.lesson: Reasons reconstructed weeks later are unreliable and read as post-hoc justification. Two or three lines written at decision time, referencing the specific criterion and the evidence in the file, will carry an appeal, a subject access request or an ombudsman enquiry. Avoid comparative phrasing about other candidates and avoid any comment on protected characteristics. Where contextual data changed the outcome, say so plainly, since that is a policy decision and should be visible.

atoms.obligation: Separate eligibility checks from judgement, and confirm eligibility evidence before spending reader time on the file.
atoms.lesson: Eligibility items are binary and verifiable: catchment address on the qualifying date, date of birth for the year group, subject prerequisites, English language test score and validity date, or a required qualification still pending. Clear these first. Files that fail eligibility should never enter the judgement queue, and files where evidence is merely missing should be chased rather than rejected, because a rejection for missing paperwork is the most commonly overturned decision on appeal.

name: financial-aid-packaging
description: Assembles and explains a student aid package from need assessment, bursaries, grants and loans. Use when a family submits a means form, a student asks why their award fell, income changed mid-year, an appeal for reassessment arrives, or the bursary budget must be allocated across more applicants than funds.
expansions: family submitted the means test form
bursary award dropped from last year
parent lost their job mid year
appealing the assessed contribution
bursary fund smaller than demand
student asking how to cover the gap
verifying income evidence looks inconsistent
hardship request needs a decision this week

atoms.obligation: Assess need with a documented formula applied identically to every applicant before any discretionary adjustment is considered.
atoms.lesson: Discretion applied at the start produces awards that cannot be defended or reproduced. Run the standard calculation first: assessed household income, dependants, and any published disregards for items such as pension contributions or care costs. Record the resulting contribution. Then log any discretionary uplift separately, with its reason and approver. This keeps the base assessment consistent across the cohort and confines subjectivity to a visible, reviewable layer.

atoms.obligation: Present the package as the full cost of attendance minus all awards, showing the remaining gap the family must meet.
atoms.lesson: Families make decisions on the gap, not on the headline award. Set out tuition, compulsory fees, and realistic living or incidental costs such as uniform, trips, travel and equipment, then subtract each grant, bursary, fee remission and loan. Show the residual figure per term as well as per year, because cash flow is what causes withdrawal. Flag which elements are guaranteed for the full course and which are reassessed annually.

atoms.obligation: Verify income evidence against a stated document list and query inconsistencies before making an award, not after payment.
atoms.lesson: Common inconsistencies include self-employment income declared far below the assets shown, a separated parent whose income is omitted without evidence of the arrangement, and benefit letters from the wrong tax year. Ask for the specific missing document rather than restating the whole list, give a deadline, and hold the file rather than awarding provisionally. Clawing back an overpaid bursary from a family in hardship is damaging and rarely succeeds.

atoms.obligation: Run a mid-year reassessment route for material change in circumstances and tell every family that it exists.
atoms.lesson: Job loss, bereavement, separation and a parent moving into care all change need immediately, but assessments usually run on the previous tax year. Define what counts as material, typically a sustained income drop of a stated percentage or a change in household composition, and what evidence is needed. Publish the route in the award letter itself. Families who do not know reassessment exists withdraw quietly instead of asking, and the withdrawal is usually discovered too late.

name: student-conduct-case
description: Handles a student disciplinary or academic misconduct case from allegation through hearing to outcome and sanction. Trigger when a plagiarism or contract cheating referral arrives, an exam room incident is reported, a behaviour case escalates towards exclusion, or a student asks what happens at their hearing.
expansions: plagiarism referral from a marker
suspected paid essay service
phone found in the exam hall
fight in the corridor needs investigating
student facing permanent exclusion
preparing papers for the conduct panel
student wants to bring a supporter
deciding a proportionate sanction

atoms.obligation: Give the student the allegation, the evidence and reasonable notice in writing before any hearing takes place.
atoms.lesson: Procedural fairness is the ground on which most conduct outcomes are overturned. The notice must state the specific rule alleged to be broken, summarise the evidence including any similarity report or witness account, give the date and format of the hearing, and explain the right to be accompanied. Five working days is a common minimum. Handing over evidence in the room denies the student a chance to respond and taints whatever the panel decides.

atoms.obligation: Keep investigation separate from decision, so nobody who gathered the evidence also determines the outcome.
atoms.lesson: The investigator collects statements, secures records such as door access logs or submission timestamps, and writes a factual report without recommending a sanction. A separate decision maker or panel weighs it. In small institutions this is hard but not optional; borrow a chair from another department rather than collapsing the roles. Where the same person does both, the student can reasonably argue the conclusion was fixed before they spoke.

atoms.obligation: Decide facts on the balance of probabilities and only then consider sanction, mitigation and prior record.
atoms.lesson: Panels regularly muddle these steps, letting a strong mitigation story soften the finding of fact or letting a prior record make a weak case look proven. Establish first whether the conduct happened, using the civil standard. Then hear mitigation, including any disability, mental health or safeguarding context, and only then look at previous findings. Record the two stages separately in the outcome letter so the reasoning survives scrutiny.

atoms.obligation: Screen every conduct case for a safeguarding or support issue and pause the process if one is disclosed.
atoms.lesson: Behaviour that looks like defiance is often the visible edge of a home situation, an undiagnosed need, exploitation or a mental health crisis. Conduct and support run on parallel tracks, and the support referral should not wait for the hearing. Where a disclosure suggests risk of harm, safeguarding takes precedence and the disciplinary process is paused and reviewed. Excluding a child who is being exploited removes the last stable adult contact they have.

name: accreditation-self-study
description: Prepares a programme or institution for accreditation, inspection or periodic review. Use when a review visit is scheduled, a self-evaluation needs assembling against a standards framework, evidence for a specific standard is missing, or a previous condition or recommendation must be shown as closed.
expansions: inspection visit booked for november
mapping evidence to the standards
closing out last cycle recommendations
programme revalidation coming up
reviewers asked for outcome data
which standard is this evidence for
preparing staff for reviewer meetings
self evaluation draft needs a critical eye

atoms.obligation: Map every standard to named evidence and an owner, and treat an unmapped standard as a finding waiting to happen.
atoms.lesson: Reviewers work standard by standard, so the self-evaluation must too. For each one, name the evidence, where it lives, who owns it and what period it covers. Gaps found in the mapping months ahead are fixable; gaps found by a reviewer become conditions. Watch particularly for standards about how the institution acts on information, since these need a documented loop from data to decision to change, not just the underlying report.

atoms.obligation: Write the self-evaluation evaluatively, judging quality and naming weaknesses rather than describing processes.
atoms.lesson: The commonest weak submission describes what happens and never says how well it works. Reviewers read description as an absence of self-knowledge. For each standard state the judgement, the evidence supporting it, the known weakness and the action already underway with a date. Naming a weakness you are already fixing builds credibility; a document with no weaknesses signals either complacency or concealment, and reviewers will hunt for what was hidden.

atoms.obligation: Close prior recommendations with evidence of the change and its effect, not merely evidence that an action was taken.
atoms.lesson: Reviewers return to the previous report first. A recommendation about assessment feedback timeliness is not closed by a new policy; it is closed by turnaround figures before and after, plus student feedback showing the change was felt. Build a tracker holding each recommendation, the action, the completion date, and the measure that demonstrates impact. Anything still open needs an honest status and a revised date rather than silence.

atoms.obligation: Brief every staff member and student who may meet reviewers on the themes, honestly, without scripting their answers.
atoms.lesson: Reviewers triangulate: they test whether what the document claims is recognised by the people living it. Coached answers are transparent and destroy trust in the whole submission. Instead ensure staff and student representatives know the main themes, where to find things such as the assessment policy or the complaints route, and what improvements are underway. Tell them it is fine to say they do not know. A confident do-not-know beats a wrong confident answer.

name: exam-logistics-plan
description: Plans and runs an examination series: seating, invigilation, materials, access arrangements and incident handling. Use when building the exam timetable, allocating invigilators, arranging separate rooms or extra time, handling a candidate arriving late, or dealing with a paper shortage or fire alarm during a sitting.
expansions: seating plan for the sports hall
not enough invigilators for friday
candidate needs extra time and a scribe
student arrived forty minutes late
fire alarm went off mid paper
two exams clash for one candidate
secure storage for question papers
script collection and dispatch

atoms.obligation: Verify access arrangements against approved evidence and set up the rooms and staff for them well before the series starts.
atoms.lesson: Extra time, rest breaks, a reader, a scribe, a word processor or a separate room each require approved evidence of need and normal way of working, and each has staffing and room consequences. Build a per-candidate arrangements list, then translate it into room allocations and staff rotas. Arrangements discovered on the morning cannot be honoured, and a candidate sitting without their approved arrangement is grounds for a special consideration claim.

atoms.obligation: Keep question papers in secure storage with a signed access log and open packets only at the published time in the room.
atoms.lesson: Security breaches invalidate results for the whole cohort, not just one candidate. Papers stay in a locked, alarmed store with two-person access recorded by signature and time. Check packet seals and paper codes against the timetable before opening, since the classic error is opening the wrong tier or the wrong sitting. Any early opening, damaged seal or discrepancy must be reported to the awarding body immediately rather than quietly corrected.

atoms.obligation: Write incident procedures for late arrival, illness, alarm and disruption before the series, and log every incident as it happens.
atoms.lesson: Invigilators need a decision rule at the moment, not a phone call. Define the point beyond which a late candidate can no longer be admitted, how far a paper may be extended, when a candidate may leave and return, and how a room evacuation is timed and restarted. Record the clock times, candidate numbers and actions contemporaneously, because special consideration applications are assessed on the detail of that log.

atoms.obligation: Build the seating plan to prevent collusion by subject and version, and keep a copy showing where every candidate actually sat.
atoms.lesson: Seat candidates taking the same paper apart where the hall allows, alternate versions or subjects along rows, and keep sightlines to screens and neighbours in mind. The plan is also the evidence base if malpractice is alleged, so record actual seats including moves made on the day. Leave spare seats near the front for late admissions and for candidates who need to be moved without disturbing a whole row.

name: academic-appeals-review
description: Handles appeals against academic decisions and claims of extenuating or mitigating circumstances. Trigger when a student disputes a mark or a progression decision, submits evidence of illness affecting an assessment, asks for a deadline extension on medical grounds, or escalates because an earlier decision went against them.
expansions: student appealing a failed module
mitigating circumstances form with a sick note
asking for an extension after the deadline
disputes the exam board decision
bereavement during assessment week
appeal says the marking was unfair
escalating to stage two review
deciding whether grounds are met

atoms.obligation: Check the appeal against permitted grounds first and explain plainly when a submission is really a disagreement with judgement.
atoms.lesson: Almost all schemes permit appeals on procedural irregularity, on circumstances not previously known for good reason, and on evidence of bias, while excluding challenges to academic judgement itself. Most rejected appeals fail because the student disputed the mark. Explain the distinction in concrete terms and point to what would have worked, such as evidence that a stated criterion was not applied. A refusal that only cites the rule invites escalation.

atoms.obligation: Require evidence that is independent, dated and covers the assessment period, and say exactly what is missing when it is not.
atoms.lesson: Useful evidence is contemporaneous and from someone other than the student: a medical note with dates, a death certificate or funeral notice, a police reference number, a counsellor letter. Retrospective notes written months later carry little weight, and self-certification usually covers only short absences. When evidence is thin, name the document you need and give a deadline, because students frequently hold the right evidence and never knew it counted.

atoms.obligation: Apply remedies to the assessment opportunity rather than adjusting marks to compensate for circumstances.
atoms.lesson: Standard remedies are an extension, a deferral to the next sitting as a first attempt without penalty, discounting an attempt, or a repeat of a period of study. Marks are not raised because a student was unwell, since that undermines the standard and treats identically affected students differently. Choose the remedy that restores the missed opportunity, and check its knock-on effects on progression dates, visa sponsorship and funding.

atoms.obligation: Complete each stage within the published deadline and issue a completion of procedures point when internal routes end.
atoms.lesson: External ombudsman and regulator schemes generally accept a complaint only after internal procedures conclude, and they run their own clock from the letter confirming that. Missed internal deadlines are themselves a procedural irregularity and hand the student a second ground. Acknowledge on receipt, give a realistic date, tell the student when it slips, and end with a letter that states the outcome, the reasons, and the external route with its time limit.

name: safeguarding-incident-handling
description: Manages a safeguarding concern or disclosure from first report through referral, recording and follow-up. Use when a student discloses harm, a staff member reports a concern about a child or vulnerable adult, an allegation is made against a member of staff, or someone asks what the threshold for referral is.
expansions: pupil disclosed something at breaktime
bruising noticed by a teaching assistant
allegation made against a staff member
worried about a student not seen for days
does this meet the referral threshold
recording a concern properly
parent asking what we reported
handover of concerns to a new school

atoms.obligation: Pass any concern to the designated safeguarding lead the same day and never hold it pending more information.
atoms.lesson: Individual staff see fragments. The lead holds the pattern: three low-level notes from different teachers may together cross a threshold that none crosses alone. Report the same day, in the standard record, even when it feels minor or already known. Where the lead and deputy are unreachable and a child is at immediate risk, contact children's services or the police directly rather than waiting, and record that you did.

atoms.obligation: Record exactly what was said and seen in the person's own words, with time, date and signature, keeping fact separate from opinion.
atoms.lesson: The record may later be evidence in a criminal or care proceeding, so paraphrase is a loss. Write the child's words verbatim, note who was present, describe any injury by location and appearance without speculating on cause, and mark clearly which parts are your interpretation. Do not photograph a child's injuries. Sign and time the note and store it in the safeguarding file, not in the general pastoral or behaviour record.

atoms.obligation: Receive a disclosure calmly, avoid leading questions, and never promise confidentiality you cannot keep.
atoms.lesson: Leading or repeated questioning can contaminate an account and collapse a later prosecution. Use open prompts only, such as asking the child to tell you more about that, and let them stop when they stop. Say early that you may have to tell someone whose job is to keep them safe, because a broken promise of secrecy destroys the trust that made the disclosure possible and makes the next one less likely.

atoms.obligation: Route allegations against staff through the separate managing-allegations process and inform the designated officer before internal action.
atoms.lesson: Allegations against adults have their own track because the employer has both a safeguarding duty and an employment duty, and mishandling either can prejudice a police investigation. The head or chair refers to the local authority designated officer, usually within one working day, before any suspension decision or witness interview. Suspension is not automatic. Keep the person informed as far as the investigation allows, and record every consultation.

name: attendance-intervention-plan
description: Monitors attendance and engagement and builds graduated intervention for students who are slipping. Trigger when a register shows a pattern of absence, a student stops attending seminars, persistent absence figures need explaining to governors, or a family needs a formal attendance meeting before legal steps.
expansions: pupil has missed nine sessions this term
attendance dropped below ninety percent
student stopped turning up to seminars
holiday requested in term time
persistent absence figures for governors
preparing an attendance contract meeting
same child late every morning
checking a child missing education referral

atoms.obligation: Read the pattern of absence, not just the total, because scattered days and single-lesson gaps mean different things.
atoms.lesson: Ninety percent attendance hides very different problems. Absence every Monday suggests weekend transitions or a contact arrangement; absence in one subject suggests a teacher relationship, bullying on that corridor or an unmet learning need; a block of days suggests illness, a family event or a hospital pattern. Break the data by day, by period and by subject before contacting anyone, so the first conversation asks about the actual pattern rather than the headline number.

atoms.obligation: Escalate through a graduated response, recording support offered at each step before any formal or legal action.
atoms.lesson: Sanctions imposed without a documented support history rarely survive challenge and rarely work. The usual ladder runs from an informal call, to a meeting with an agreed plan, to a written attendance contract with review dates, to statutory routes such as a penalty notice or an education supervision order. Each step needs a dated record of what was offered, what barriers the family named, and what changed. Skipping steps is the commonest reason cases collapse.

atoms.obligation: Treat sudden disengagement as a welfare signal and make direct personal contact rather than sending another automated reminder.
atoms.lesson: In universities, a student who was attending and stops is far more concerning than one who was always erratic. Common causes are mental health crisis, bereavement, money trouble, caring responsibilities and, for sponsored students, an unresolved immigration problem. A phone call from a named tutor within a few days recovers students that three automated emails will not. Log the contact attempt, because engagement monitoring also carries sponsorship reporting duties.

atoms.obligation: Check the register coding is accurate and consistent before drawing conclusions or reporting figures anywhere.
atoms.lesson: Attendance data is only as good as the codes. Off-site sports fixtures, medical appointments, alternative provision, exclusion, religious observance and educational visits all have distinct codes with different statutory meanings, and staff routinely default to a generic authorised absence. Audit a sample each term. Miscoding distorts persistent absence rates, triggers interventions for children who were actually in supervised provision, and misleads governors and inspectors.

name: learning-support-plan
description: Builds and reviews support plans and reasonable adjustments for students with additional needs or disabilities. Use when a diagnostic report or needs assessment arrives, a teacher asks what adjustments apply in class, an annual review is due, a plan is not being implemented, or a request for adjustments is contested.
expansions: educational psychologist report just arrived
teacher asking what adjustments apply
annual review meeting due next month
plan agreed but nobody follows it
requesting extra time in assessments
parent wants a needs assessment
transition to secondary with support in place
adjustment refused as unreasonable

atoms.obligation: Translate every diagnosis into specific classroom and assessment actions naming who does what, when and where.
atoms.lesson: Reports describe cognition and need; teachers need instructions. A slow processing speed becomes advance provision of slides, chunked instructions, and extra time in timed assessments. A hearing impairment becomes a seating position, a radio aid checked each morning by a named person, and captioned video. Write actions in the imperative with an owner. Plans written in diagnostic language get filed and forgotten, and the student experiences no change at all.

atoms.obligation: Consult the student and the family about what actually helps, and record where their view differs from the professional recommendation.
atoms.lesson: Students know which adjustments they will use. Many refuse a support assistant sitting beside them, or a separate exam room that marks them out, and will silently decline support that was arranged at expense. Ask directly what has helped before and what they would rather not have. Recording a difference of view protects everyone later, especially when an adjustment is declined and an outcome is subsequently appealed.

atoms.obligation: Set measurable outcomes with review dates and check implementation, not only intention, at each review.
atoms.lesson: Reviews drift into describing the child rather than testing the plan. Each outcome should be observable within the review period, such as reading a set text independently or completing a timed paper using the agreed arrangement. At review ask three things: was each adjustment actually delivered, did it move the outcome, and does it still fit. Non-implementation is the most common finding and the least often recorded.

atoms.obligation: Share the plan with everyone who teaches or supervises the student, including supply staff, trip leaders and placement supervisors.
atoms.lesson: Support fails at the edges of the timetable. A cover teacher who does not know a student has an anxiety-related plan will escalate a refusal into a confrontation; a placement supervisor who never received the adjustments cannot honour them. Keep a concise shared summary that carries the key adjustments and triggers without disclosing more sensitive detail than necessary, and make handover part of cover and placement arrangements rather than an afterthought.

name: faculty-workload-allocation
description: Allocates teaching, marking, tutoring and administrative load fairly across academic staff. Trigger when building next year's allocation, a colleague says their load is unmanageable, someone goes on leave and their duties need reassigning, or a new programme adds teaching that nobody has been budgeted to deliver.
expansions: allocating teaching for next academic year
colleague says their load is impossible
maternity leave cover needs reallocating
new module and nobody to teach it
marking load uneven across the team
research time squeezed out by teaching
sessional hours over budget
personal tutoring numbers per academic

atoms.obligation: Count all workload categories, including marking, tutoring, admissions duties and committee roles, not only scheduled contact hours.
atoms.lesson: Contact hours are the visible tenth. Marking a large cohort with feedback, supervising dissertations, personal tutoring, open days, admissions interviews, programme leadership and external examining consume the rest. Use published tariffs per activity, such as minutes per script or hours per supervised project, so that categories are comparable. Any model that counts only timetabled teaching systematically overloads the people who do the invisible work and rewards those who avoid it.

atoms.obligation: Publish the full allocation to the whole team, showing each person's totals and the tariffs used.
atoms.lesson: Perceived unfairness in workload comes far more from opacity than from actual imbalance. When everyone can see the tariffs and every colleague's total, disputes shift from suspicion to arguing about a specific tariff, which is a solvable conversation. Publish before the year starts and mark protected allocations such as research time, sabbatical and role remission explicitly, so their cost is visible rather than being silently absorbed by colleagues.

atoms.obligation: Hold contingency capacity for absence and student demand rather than allocating every available hour at the start.
atoms.lesson: Illness, bereavement, resignation and unexpected recruitment happen every year. If the model is fully committed in June, September cover comes from whoever is easiest to lean on, usually the same reliable few, or from sessional staff hired in a rush at premium cost. Reserve a stated percentage of capacity across the team as unallocated. Also model the high-recruitment case, since an extra seminar group is teaching that must come from somewhere.

atoms.obligation: Check the allocation for equality effects before publishing, including how caring duties and pastoral work fall across groups.
atoms.lesson: Workload models can quietly disadvantage particular groups. Pastoral and student-support load often falls on women and on minority staff because students seek them out; part-time colleagues frequently carry a full share of fixed duties such as committees on a fraction of the hours. Compare distributions by contract type, grade and protected characteristic, and pro-rate fixed duties genuinely. These patterns surface later in pay gap reporting and grievances if not caught here.

name: transfer-credit-evaluation
description: Evaluates prior study for credit, advanced standing or exemption. Use when a transfer student sends transcripts, an applicant claims exemption from modules through prior professional learning, a partner institution's programme must be mapped to yours, or a study abroad period needs converting back into credit.
expansions: transfer student sent foreign transcripts
wants exemption from first year modules
mapping a partner diploma to our programme
study abroad grades need converting
credit for professional qualifications
entering with advanced standing
checking the awarding institution is recognised
how much prior credit can we allow

atoms.obligation: Match learning outcomes and level rather than course titles, and demand a syllabus when the title alone is ambiguous.
atoms.lesson: Two modules called Introduction to Statistics can differ by a full level of study, and a title in translation tells you almost nothing. Ask for the syllabus, the assessment pattern, contact hours and the credit value, then compare stated outcomes against your own module. Where outcomes match at a lower level, the correct decision is often general credit toward the total rather than a specific module exemption that would leave a prerequisite gap.

atoms.obligation: Verify the awarding institution's recognition status and confirm the transcript directly with the issuing body when anything looks irregular.
atoms.lesson: Check that the institution is recognised in its own national system and that the qualification sits in that country's framework. Diploma mills reproduce plausible transcripts. Warning signs include perfect grade profiles, missing credit values, fonts that vary within a page, and a verification address that is a webmail account. Verify with the registrar directly using contact details you found independently, never those printed on the submitted document.

atoms.obligation: Apply the published limits on how much credit may be imported and where it may sit in the programme.
atoms.lesson: Awarding rules normally cap imported credit, typically allowing no more than a third to a half of a degree, and usually forbid credit against the final level where the classification is determined. Recency limits also apply, often five years for fast-moving fields. Check whether the imported credit carries a grade into the final calculation or is recorded as pass only, because that decision changes the student's achievable classification.

atoms.obligation: Give the decision in writing with the exact modules exempted, the credits granted, and the remaining requirements to graduate.
atoms.lesson: Students plan their finances, visa duration and employment around this letter. State the entry point, the total credit granted, each module exempted, what must still be taken and passed, and the expected completion date. Note explicitly anything not transferred and why. Vague confirmations that a student is entering with advanced standing generate disputes in the final year when a missing prerequisite blocks graduation.

name: registration-cycle-operations
description: Runs the registration and enrolment period end to end: module choices, holds, waitlists, capacity and late changes. Trigger when registration is about to open, a student cannot register because of a hold, a popular module fills instantly, waitlists need clearing, or the add-drop deadline is approaching.
expansions: registration opens on monday
student blocked by a finance hold
module filled in four minutes
clearing the waitlist fairly
add drop deadline this friday
prerequisite check failing wrongly
students registered on the wrong pathway
late enrolment after term started

atoms.obligation: Define every registration hold with an owner, a clearing route and a stated response time before the window opens.
atoms.lesson: Holds are how the institution enforces obligations, but each one blocks a student from the thing they came for. Inventory them: unpaid fees, missing immunisation or right to study documents, unreturned equipment, library debt, incomplete academic advising. For each, name who can lift it, what the student must do, and how fast it will be cleared. Unowned holds strand students for days and generate the largest complaint spike of the year.

atoms.obligation: Publish the waitlist rule in advance and apply it mechanically, resisting individual overrides that displace waiting students.
atoms.lesson: Whatever the rule, publish it before registration: strict time order, priority by progression need, or priority for students in the programme where the module is compulsory. Once places are contested, every override granted to a persuasive emailer pushes back someone who followed the process and cannot see what happened. If the module genuinely needs more capacity, the fix is another section or a bigger room, not a quiet exception.

atoms.obligation: Test prerequisite and capacity rules with real student records before opening, including edge cases like resits and transfers.
atoms.lesson: Rules that look right in the abstract fail on real records. Students carrying a trailing module, returning from interruption, entering with transfer credit, or repeating a year all break naive prerequisite checks and get blocked from modules they are entitled to take. Pull a sample of such records and walk them through the rules in advance. Fixing this before the window opens saves hundreds of manual overrides in the first week.

atoms.obligation: Reconcile registrations against the timetable, fee status and funding records at a fixed census point each term.
atoms.lesson: Registration data drives funding claims, sponsorship reporting, class lists, assessment records and graduation eligibility, and errors propagate everywhere. At the census date compare registered modules with attendance, fee liability, funding eligibility and timetabled capacity. Look for students registered on nothing, registered on more credit than the maximum, or registered on modules that no longer run. Correcting after the census usually requires an amended return and explanations.

name: school-budget-cycle
description: Builds and monitors the annual budget for an institution or department, from funding allocation to in-year variance. Use when setting next year's budget, a funding allocation changes, staffing costs drift above plan, a department requests additional spend mid-year, or a deficit recovery plan is required.
expansions: building next year budget
funding allocation letter came in lower
staffing costs above plan again
department wants extra spend this term
three year deficit recovery plan
pay award not funded in the allocation
carry forward from last year
explaining variance to the finance committee

atoms.obligation: Build staffing costs from the actual establishment list, including on-costs, increments and known changes, before any other line.
atoms.lesson: Pay is typically seventy to eighty percent of an education budget, so precision here dominates everything else. Build post by post with salary point, expected increment date, employer pension and national insurance, and any allowances. Layer in known retirements, maternity leave and cover, and fixed-term end dates. Percentage uplifts applied to last year's total are wrong by more than the entire non-pay budget, because increments and pension rate changes do not move together.
