atoms.obligation: Model at least three funding scenarios and identify which committed costs cannot be reversed once the year starts.
atoms.lesson: Income moves with pupil or student numbers, with allocation formulas and with recruitment outcomes that land after commitments are made. Model the pessimistic case and mark every irreversible commitment: permanent contracts, multi-year leases, contracted catering and cleaning, and software or maintenance agreements. The share of budget that is genuinely flexible in-year is usually small, which is why a mid-year income shortfall lands almost entirely on supplies, trips and staff development.

atoms.obligation: Report variance monthly against a phased profile rather than against a flat share of the annual budget.
atoms.lesson: Spend is not even across the year. Examination fees, textbook and resource purchases, trips, and utility costs all concentrate in particular months, so a flat twelfth comparison generates false alarms in autumn and false comfort in spring. Phase each budget line to its expected pattern, then investigate variances against that profile. Explain each material variance as timing or as a genuine over or underspend, because only the second needs corrective action.

atoms.obligation: Separate one-off funds from recurrent income and never use non-recurrent money to create ongoing commitments.
atoms.lesson: Catch-up grants, capital allocations, in-year supplements and reserves are one-off. Appointing a permanent teaching assistant from a one-year grant creates a cost that outlives its funding and forces a redundancy later. Tag each income line as recurrent or non-recurrent and match it to expenditure of the same type: fixed-term posts, equipment, or contracted services with end dates. Auditors and governing bodies check this pairing specifically.

name: family-communication-plan
description: Plans and drafts communication to parents, carers and students about decisions, incidents and changes. Trigger when a closure or disruption must be announced, an incident on site needs a message home before rumours spread, a policy change will be unpopular, or complaints show that an earlier message was misread.
expansions: snow closure message tonight
incident on site parents will hear about
announcing a uniform policy change
rumours spreading on the parents group
message misread and now complaints
communicating an exam timetable change
letter home about a staff departure
translating a notice for families

atoms.obligation: Lead with what changes for the reader's own child and the action they must take, before any context or rationale.
atoms.lesson: Parents read the first two lines on a phone, often while doing something else. Put the decision, the date and the required action first: which year groups are affected, what time, what to bring, what to do if it does not work for them. Rationale, thanks and background belong below. Messages that open with a paragraph about the review process generate a wave of questions already answered further down.

atoms.obligation: Say what is known, what is not yet known and when the next update will come, rather than waiting for full information.
atoms.lesson: In an incident, silence is filled within minutes by parent group chats and local social media, and the version that forms first is the one that sticks. A short early message that confirms all students are safe, states that the site is closed while an issue is resolved, and promises an update by a named time buys the room to establish facts. Then meet that time, even if the update is that there is nothing new.

atoms.obligation: Protect the privacy of individual students and staff, and never confirm details of a person in a general message.
atoms.lesson: Even without a name, a message can identify a child through year group, timing and circumstance, and families and staff have data protection rights that survive a crisis. Describe what happened institutionally and what has been done, not who was involved or what condition they are in. Where a death or serious incident has occurred, agree the wording with the family first and coordinate with any police or coronial process before sending anything.

atoms.obligation: Check reach and accessibility across every channel and language before sending, and provide a route for those who cannot use the main one.
atoms.lesson: Some households never open the app, some share one phone, some read no English, some have parental responsibility but no longer live at the address. For anything critical, use at least two channels and check the contact list for families flagged as hard to reach. Provide translation for the main community languages and plain-language versions. Assuming a single notification reaches everyone is how children are collected late from an unannounced early closure.

name: student-records-requests
description: Handles requests for and disclosures of student records and personal data. Use when a subject access request arrives, a separated parent asks for their child's file, a police or social work request comes in, a reference or verification of study is requested, or someone asks how long a record must be kept.
expansions: subject access request from a former student
separated parent asking for school records
police asking for a pupil address
employer verifying a degree
how long do we keep this file
student wants their pastoral notes
sharing records with the new school
redacting third party names

atoms.obligation: Confirm the requester's identity and legal basis for access before disclosing anything, including to someone claiming to be a parent.
atoms.lesson: Parental responsibility is not the same as residence or contact, and a parent without it has no automatic right to records. Court orders can restrict disclosure precisely because of safeguarding risk, so check the file for any such restriction before responding. For third parties, ask which power they are relying on and get it in writing. Disclosing a child's address to the wrong adult is the most damaging error in this area.

atoms.obligation: Redact information about other people while keeping the requester's own data intact, and record every redaction decision.
atoms.lesson: Student files contain other students, staff opinions and family members. Remove third party identities unless that person has consented or it is reasonable to disclose without consent, weighing their expectation of confidentiality. Do not delete the requester's own data because it is unflattering; opinions about them are their data. Keep an unredacted master and a schedule listing each redaction and its reason, since the schedule is what you rely on if the decision is challenged.

atoms.obligation: Log the request on arrival, track the statutory deadline, and tell the requester promptly if an extension applies.
atoms.lesson: Response clocks are short, commonly one month for a subject access request and fifteen school days for a pupil record request under education rules, and they run from receipt regardless of holidays. Complex or voluminous requests can often be extended, but only if you notify within the original period. Log the date received, the clarification sought, and the date sent. Most breaches are missed deadlines rather than wrong disclosures.

atoms.obligation: Apply the published retention schedule and dispose of records securely rather than keeping everything indefinitely.
atoms.lesson: Different categories have very different periods: safeguarding records are typically retained for decades, examination and award records permanently, general pastoral and behaviour files only for a few years past leaving, and accident records for long statutory periods. Holding data beyond its period is itself a breach and enlarges every future request. Record disposals with date, category and method, because the absence of a file must be explainable as policy rather than loss.

name: degree-audit-clearance
description: Checks that finishing students have met every requirement for their award and clears them for conferment. Trigger when the graduation list is being assembled, a student is short of credit, a classification sits on a borderline, a resit outcome arrives late, or someone asks whether a student can walk at the ceremony.
expansions: building the graduation list
student is fifteen credits short
borderline between two classifications
resit result came in after the board
can they attend the ceremony
checking placement hours completed
wrong award title on the list
professional body requirement not met

atoms.obligation: Check credit total, level distribution, compulsory modules and any professional requirements separately, since passing enough credit is not sufficient.
atoms.lesson: Students accumulate credit in the wrong shape all the time. A degree needs a minimum volume at the highest level, specific core modules, and often a capstone or dissertation. Accredited programmes add placement hours, practice competencies, or a fitness to practise sign-off that sits outside the credit framework entirely. Audit each dimension as its own check. A student can hold three hundred and sixty credits and still be ineligible for the named award.

atoms.obligation: Apply borderline and classification rules exactly as written and record which rule produced each raised classification.
atoms.lesson: Classification algorithms differ in ways that decide degrees: how many credits fall in the weighted calculation, whether the best modules are counted preferentially, whether the borderline zone is one or two percent, and whether a preponderance of marks in the higher band lifts a candidate automatically or only on discretion. Never apply discretion case by case without the rule that authorises it, and minute which rule applied, because unexplained uplifts are indefensible when a neighbouring candidate misses out.

atoms.obligation: Reconcile the audit against the assessment records after every board and resit round before publishing any award list.
atoms.lesson: Late-arriving results, upheld appeals, condoned credit and deferred assessments all change eligibility after the main board has met. Re-run the audit at a fixed cut-off before names go to print or to the conferment resolution. Errors discovered later are painful to unwind: an award conferred in error must be formally rescinded, and a student wrongly omitted from a ceremony experiences it as the institution failing them in public.

atoms.obligation: Separate eligibility to graduate from permission to attend the ceremony and communicate any outstanding debt or condition early.
atoms.lesson: These are different decisions and students conflate them. Academic eligibility rests on requirements met; ceremony attendance may also depend on outstanding tuition debt, returned equipment or a completed conduct case. Whatever the policy, tell the student weeks ahead, not on the morning, and state exactly what must be resolved and by when. Withholding a certificate for academic reasons and withholding it for debt are different acts and should be worded differently.

name: emergency-drill-planning
description: Plans, runs and reviews emergency procedures and drills across a site. Use when scheduling a fire evacuation or lockdown drill, updating the invacuation procedure, reviewing why a drill took too long, planning for a site with vulnerable students, or briefing new staff on what to do in an alert.
expansions: fire drill due this term
lockdown procedure needs updating
evacuation took nine minutes
wheelchair user on the second floor
new staff briefing on alarms
roll call at the assembly point failed
bomb threat call procedure
reviewing what went wrong in the drill

atoms.obligation: Write personal emergency evacuation plans for anyone who cannot use stairs or respond to standard alarms, and rehearse them.
atoms.lesson: Standard procedures assume a person who hears an alarm and walks downstairs. Wheelchair users, students with limited mobility, deaf students, and those with autism or anxiety who may freeze or run all need a named plan: refuge location, who assists, which evacuation chair and who is trained on it, visual or vibrating alert devices. Rehearse each plan with the individual. A plan written and never practised fails at the moment it matters most.

atoms.obligation: Test different scenarios and conditions, not the same announced fire drill at the same convenient hour every term.
atoms.lesson: An announced drill during a mid-morning lesson tests only the easiest case. Vary it: lunchtime with students dispersed, during an examination with candidates in a hall, at changeover in corridors, after dark in winter, with a primary exit blocked. Lockdown and invacuation need their own rehearsals because the instinct to leave the building is exactly wrong. Record which scenarios have been tested so gaps are visible before an incident finds them.

atoms.obligation: Account for every person at the assembly point using a reliable roll method, and time how long that takes.
atoms.lesson: Evacuation time is usually reported to the point when the building is clear, but the operational question is when the fire service can be told nobody is inside. Registers held in classrooms are useless when the alarm sounds during free time. Decide how visitors, contractors, part-time staff and students on study periods are counted, and who reports unaccounted names to the incident controller. Most drills that look fast fail this stage.

atoms.obligation: Debrief within a day, record the timings and the failures, and assign fixes with owners and deadlines.
atoms.lesson: The value of a drill is entirely in the review. Capture the clock times for alarm, building clear and roll complete, then the specific failures: a door that stuck, a class that took the wrong route, a fire marshal absent with no deputy, a visitor nobody checked for. Assign each fix to a person with a date and test it in the next drill. Undebriefed drills teach staff that the alarm is a routine interruption.

name: international-student-compliance
description: Manages sponsorship and immigration compliance duties for international students. Trigger when issuing a study confirmation for a visa, checking right to study documents at enrolment, reporting a withdrawal or long absence, handling a student whose course length changes, or preparing for a sponsor audit.
expansions: issuing a visa sponsorship confirmation
checking passport and visa at enrolment
student withdrew must we report it
course extension changes the visa end date
sponsor compliance audit next month
student missed engagement checkpoints
deferring entry to january intake
work placement allowed on this visa

atoms.obligation: Check and record right to study documents in person at enrolment, before the student attends any teaching.
atoms.lesson: Sponsorship duties require verified evidence held from the start, not collected later. Inspect the original passport or the digital status, confirm the identity matches the applicant, check the visa conditions and expiry, and keep a dated copy with the name of the checker. Watch for visas issued for a different institution or course, and entry stamps that do not match the stated arrival. A student taught before this check is a compliance breach even if their status is valid.

atoms.obligation: Report the reportable events within the specified deadline, treating withdrawal, suspension and non-enrolment as immediate triggers.
atoms.lesson: Sponsors must notify authorities when a student fails to enrol by the deadline, withdraws, is suspended or expelled, defers, or stops engaging with the course, usually within ten working days of the decision. The clock starts at the internal decision, not at the paperwork. Build the trigger into the registry processes that record those decisions, because the standard failure is a withdrawal processed correctly in the student record and never passed to compliance.

atoms.obligation: Keep engagement monitoring evidence for every sponsored student and act on missed checkpoints as a support matter first.
atoms.lesson: Audits ask to see how you know a student is studying. Define checkpoints such as attendance at scheduled sessions, supervision meetings for research students, or assessment submissions, and record them consistently. When checkpoints are missed, contact the student directly before starting a withdrawal, since the cause is often illness, travel disruption or a family emergency. Withdrawing a student for non-engagement ends their permission to remain, so the evidence must be solid.

atoms.obligation: Align course dates, extensions and interruptions with the sponsorship record and tell the student what it means for their status.
atoms.lesson: A repeat year, a resit period, a placement, an interruption for illness or an extended thesis submission all change the sponsored course end date and may require a new confirmation or a fresh application. Students frequently discover this only when their visa is about to expire. Whenever an academic decision changes duration, check the sponsorship consequence at the same meeting and give the student written notice of what they must do and by when.

name: curriculum-approval-proposal
description: Takes a new or changed course, module or programme through governance approval. Use when someone wants to launch a programme, retire a module, change assessment weightings, respond to a validation panel's conditions, or check what approvals a proposed change actually needs.
expansions: proposing a new masters programme
changing the assessment weighting
retiring a module with students still on it
panel set three conditions to clear
does this change need full approval
adding an option to the third year
new subject option for key stage four
aligning outcomes to the framework

atoms.obligation: Classify the change as minor or major against the published thresholds and route it to the right committee first.
atoms.lesson: Most schemes distinguish minor changes, approved locally, from major changes needing a full panel: altering an award title, changing more than a set share of credit, changing the mode of study or the assessment strategy, or anything touching an accredited pathway. Misrouting wastes a whole committee cycle and can leave a change implemented without valid approval, which is a finding at audit. Check the threshold before drafting rather than after.

atoms.obligation: Write learning outcomes at the correct level, then show that assessment actually tests each one.
atoms.lesson: Panels probe the alignment between outcomes, teaching and assessment more than any other point. Outcomes must use verbs that match the level descriptor of the qualifications framework, so critical evaluation at higher levels rather than describing or listing. Then map each outcome to at least one assessment task. Orphan outcomes that nothing assesses, and assessments testing something not in the outcomes, are the two findings that generate conditions.

atoms.obligation: Set out the resource implications honestly, naming staffing, space, equipment and library needs and who will fund them.
atoms.lesson: Proposals routinely assume existing staff will absorb new teaching and that a lab or studio will be free. Quantify the teaching hours the new provision creates, the technician support, the specialist equipment and its maintenance, the licence or subscription costs, and any accreditation fee. Get the resource owner to confirm in writing. Approval granted on optimistic resourcing produces a programme that runs badly in year one and damages the student experience that recruited it.

atoms.obligation: Plan the teach-out for students already on the old version whenever a programme or module is changed or withdrawn.
atoms.lesson: Continuing students have a contractual expectation of the programme they enrolled on, including students on interruption who will return in two years and those who must resit a retired module. Set out how each affected cohort completes: running the old version to a stated date, mapping to an equivalent module, or an agreed alternative with the student's consent. Consumer protection expectations require consultation on material changes, not just notification.

name: staff-hiring-onboarding
description: Runs recruitment and safe onboarding for teaching and support staff. Trigger when a post needs advertising, a shortlist must be defended, safer recruitment checks are outstanding, a reference raises a concern, or a new starter needs to be cleared to work with students before term begins.
expansions: advertising a maths teacher post
shortlisting against the person specification
reference came back vague
clearance not through before term starts
gap in the employment history
interview questions for safer recruitment
induction plan for a new lecturer
checking qualifications are genuine

atoms.obligation: Shortlist and score against the person specification with agreed criteria, and keep the scoring records after the decision.
atoms.lesson: Each criterion should be marked essential or desirable and be assessable from the application. Panel members score independently before conferring, then reconcile. Keep the scores, notes and reasons for six to twelve months, because unsuccessful applicants may raise a discrimination claim and the contemporaneous record is the defence. Free-form impressions written after the panel disperses are worth nothing and often read as rationalising a decision already made.

atoms.obligation: Explore any employment gap or unexplained departure at interview and record the explanation given.
atoms.lesson: Safer recruitment treats chronology as evidence. Ask about every gap over a few months and about the reason for leaving each role involving children or vulnerable adults, in the interview rather than by email. Note the answer verbatim. Patterns matter: short stays in several settings, a departure during an investigation, or references only from personal contacts warrant further questions before any offer, however strong the candidate looks on paper.

atoms.obligation: Take references directly from the employer's official channel, ask specific questions, and never accept an open testimonial.
atoms.lesson: Request references from the organisation rather than an individual's personal address, addressed to the human resources or head's office, and ask directly whether any safeguarding or disciplinary concerns were raised and whether they would re-employ. A vague or purely factual reference from a setting that would normally comment is itself information; follow it up by phone and record the conversation. Testimonials the candidate supplies are not references.

atoms.obligation: Confirm all pre-employment checks are complete and recorded before the person starts unsupervised work with students.
atoms.lesson: The set typically includes identity, right to work, criminal record disclosure at the correct level, barred list check, qualification verification, prohibition checks for teaching roles, medical fitness and, for overseas service, an equivalent check from that country. Record each in a single register with dates and who verified. Where a start is genuinely urgent and one check is outstanding, a documented risk assessment and supervised working arrangement is required rather than an informal exception.

name: governing-board-cycle
description: Supports the governing body or board through its annual cycle of meetings, decisions and oversight. Use when planning the year's agenda coverage, preparing a committee for a decision, chasing actions that never close, handling a conflict of interest, or checking whether a matter needs board approval or is delegated.
expansions: planning the annual agenda coverage
governors keep asking the same question
actions from last meeting still open
trustee has a conflict on this item
is this delegated or board level
committee needs to decide on friday
preparing the chair for a hard item
recording a decision properly in minutes

atoms.obligation: Plan agendas across the year so every statutory and oversight duty is scheduled at the point it can influence a decision.
atoms.lesson: Boards drift into reacting to whatever arrives. Build a cycle placing budget approval before the financial year, safeguarding and health and safety reports at fixed points, outcomes review after results, policy renewals at their expiry dates, and risk register review each term. Time items to the moment they can change something: approving a budget after commitments are made, or reviewing admissions after offers went out, is ratification dressed as governance.

atoms.obligation: Separate items for decision from items for assurance or information, and state the recommendation and the decision sought.
atoms.lesson: Meetings run out of time on the interesting items and rush the ones that carry legal weight. Mark each item with its purpose, its owner and the time allowed, and for decisions state the proposition, the options considered, the risks and the recommendation. Assurance items should say what question the board is being helped to answer. Without this, boards approve things nobody realised were approvals and debate reports that needed no action.

atoms.obligation: Declare and manage conflicts of interest at the start of each item, recording who withdrew from the discussion.
atoms.lesson: Conflicts in education boards are common and often innocent: a governor whose child attends, a trustee whose firm could tender for works, a staff governor on an item about pay. Maintain a register updated annually and check it against each agenda in advance. At the meeting, declare, decide whether the person may speak, must abstain or must leave, and minute it. Undeclared interests are what turn a routine procurement into a public finding.

atoms.obligation: Minute the decision, the reasoning and the challenge offered, not the narrative of who said what.
atoms.lesson: Minutes are legal records and the evidence that the board exercised oversight. Record the decision, the alternatives considered, the questions governors pressed and the answers given, and any dissent. Inspectors and auditors look specifically for evidence of challenge. Carry every action into a tracker with an owner and a due date, and review that tracker as the first substantive item, because unclosed actions are the clearest sign a board is not holding the executive to account.

name: lease-classification-schedules
description: Classifies leases and builds the right-of-use asset and lease liability schedules that support the balance sheet. Use it when a new lease is signed, when a lease is modified or terminated early, when the lease rollforward stops tying to the trial balance, or when someone asks whether a contract is finance or operating and what discount rate to use. Also covers embedded leases hiding inside service and hosting contracts.
expansions: we signed a new office lease last week
lease liability rollforward does not tie
is this forklift lease finance or operating
need an incremental borrowing rate for a lease
landlord gave us six months free rent
renewal option we may exercise in 2029
lease modification added two floors mid term
auditor asked for our embedded lease analysis

atoms.obligation: Test every lease against all five classification criteria at commencement and record which criterion drove the finance or operating answer.
atoms.lesson: The five criteria are transfer of ownership, a purchase option reasonably certain of exercise, a term covering the major part of remaining economic life, present value of payments amounting to substantially all of fair value, and an asset so specialized it has no alternative use. Many firms operationalize major part as 75 percent and substantially all as 90 percent. Failing all five gives operating treatment with a single straight-line cost; finance treatment splits amortization and interest, front-loading expense and moving cost below EBITDA.

atoms.obligation: Use the rate implicit in the lease when it is determinable and otherwise develop a collateralized incremental borrowing rate for the same term and currency.
atoms.lesson: The implicit rate is rarely determinable because the lessor's unguaranteed residual value is not disclosed, so most lessees fall back to an incremental borrowing rate. That rate must reflect secured borrowing, the lease term, the lease currency, and the commencement date, not the reporting date. Support it with a bank quote or a published yield curve plus a credit spread and keep the derivation in the file. Private entities may elect the risk-free rate by asset class, but the lower rate inflates the recognized liability.

atoms.obligation: Include optional renewal or termination periods in the lease term only when exercise is reasonably certain, and reassess only when a triggering event occurs.
atoms.lesson: Reasonably certain is a high threshold, evidenced by below-market renewal rents, leasehold improvements with useful lives extending past the base term, relocation costs, or a facility central to operations. A month-to-month holdover after expiry is not automatically a new lease term. Reassessment is required only on a significant event within the lessee's control, such as building out the space, not on a change of intent alone. Twelve-month leases with no purchase option can use the short-term exemption if elected by class.

atoms.obligation: Reconcile the lease subledger rollforward to the general ledger every close and explain additions, accretion, payments, and remeasurements line by line.
atoms.lesson: The liability rollforward should move from opening balance plus new leases plus interest accretion less cash payments plus remeasurements to the closing balance, and the closing balance must tie to the ledger and to the maturity table disclosure. Common breaks come from payments booked directly to rent expense, variable payments incorrectly amortized, indexation increases treated as remeasurements when they should hit expense, and terminations left in the schedule. Reconcile the asset separately, since impairment or termination gains break the mirror relationship.

name: revenue-recognition-analysis
description: Works a contract through the five-step revenue model and produces the memo and journal entries that follow. Use it when a new or unusual customer contract arrives, when a deal bundles software with implementation and support, when there are rebates, milestones, or termination rights, or when someone asks whether revenue is recognized over time or at a point in time. Also covers gross versus net presentation for resellers and marketplaces.
expansions: customer contract bundles license and implementation
can we recognize this milestone payment now
is this revenue gross or net as agent
rebate tiers make the price variable
need a memo on a nonstandard deal
multi year saas contract with ramped pricing
customer has a right of return clause
should setup fees be deferred over the term

atoms.obligation: Identify performance obligations by testing whether each promised good or service is capable of being distinct and distinct within the contract context.
atoms.lesson: Both tests must pass. A software license plus routine installation that any vendor could perform is usually two obligations; the same license plus significant customization that materially modifies it is one combined obligation recognized over the build. Watch for free or discounted future goods that create a material right, which is its own obligation. Setup and activation fees rarely transfer anything to the customer and are typically deferred over the expected service period rather than recognized at signing.

atoms.obligation: Estimate variable consideration using expected value or most likely amount and then constrain it to the amount not probable of significant reversal.
atoms.lesson: Expected value fits large populations of similar contracts such as volume rebates and returns; most likely amount fits binary outcomes such as a single performance bonus. The constraint bites when the amount depends on third-party actions, the uncertainty resolves far in the future, or the entity has little experience with similar contracts. Reassess every reporting period and true up cumulatively. Sales-based royalties on licensed intellectual property are an exception recognized only as the underlying sales occur.

atoms.obligation: Determine whether control transfers over time by applying the three over-time criteria before defaulting to point-in-time recognition.
atoms.lesson: Over time applies when the customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefit, when the entity creates or enhances an asset the customer controls, or when the asset has no alternative use and the entity holds an enforceable right to payment including a reasonable margin for work completed to date. That last criterion carries most custom manufacturing and construction. If none apply, look at point-in-time indicators such as physical possession, legal title, risks and rewards, and customer acceptance.

atoms.obligation: Assess whether the entity controls the specified good before transfer to decide between gross principal and net agent presentation.
atoms.lesson: Control indicators are primary responsibility for fulfillment, inventory risk before or after transfer, and discretion in setting the price. Collecting cash from the end customer or bearing credit risk is not determinative. Marketplaces, travel resellers, and drop-ship arrangements usually land on net presentation, which does not change net income but can cut reported revenue by an order of magnitude, so the conclusion belongs in a documented memo before the first filing that uses it.

name: external-confirmation-workflow
description: Runs the external confirmation process for receivables, bank balances, debt, and legal matters from selection through exception clearing. Use it when planning confirmation coverage for an audit, when confirmations come back with differences or do not come back at all, when a client wants to route confirmations through their own staff, or when someone asks what alternative procedures are acceptable for non-responses.
expansions: customer never returned the ar confirmation
confirmation came back with a difference
client wants to mail the confirmations themselves
which customers should we confirm this year
bank confirmation missing the loan covenants
need alternative procedures for non responses
confirmation reply came from a personal email
attorney letter response is vague on exposure

atoms.obligation: Keep control of the confirmation from address validation through receipt and never let client personnel handle the requests or the replies.
atoms.lesson: Confirmation fraud almost always exploits a break in auditor control. Validate addresses independently against public registries, the customer's own website, or a directory rather than the client's master file, and be alert to newly added addresses, mail drops, and free email domains. Send from and receive at an address the audit team controls. Replies arriving by fax, forwarded email, or through client staff are not reliable evidence without direct follow-up contact with a person whose identity and authority you verified.

atoms.obligation: Use positive confirmations for material or unusual balances and reserve negative requests for large populations of small, homogeneous, low-risk items.
atoms.lesson: A negative confirmation only produces evidence when the recipient disagrees, so silence proves nothing. It is acceptable only when risk of material misstatement is low, the population is many small similar balances, an exception rate near zero is expected, and recipients are likely to read the request. Anything overdue, disputed, from a related party, or with a credit balance takes a positive request. Blank positive forms asking the customer to state the balance give stronger evidence but lower response rates.

atoms.obligation: Investigate every returned difference to root cause and classify it as a timing item, a customer error, or a real misstatement before projecting.
atoms.lesson: Most receivable differences are timing: cash in transit at the confirmation date, goods shipped but not yet received under destination terms, credits or returns not yet processed, or unapplied payments. Clear these against subsequent cash receipts, shipping documents, and credit memos issued after the date. What remains is a misstatement to schedule and project across the untested population. Disputed amounts and short payments are also collectability evidence and should feed the allowance analysis, not just existence.

atoms.obligation: Perform alternative procedures for every non-response and document why the substituted evidence addresses the same assertion.
atoms.lesson: For receivables the strongest alternative is examining cash received after the period end and tracing it to the specific invoices confirmed, since payment evidences both existence and collectability. Where cash has not been received, inspect the sales order, shipping document, and invoice together. Alternative procedures do not work for a bank confirmation, where a non-response must be pursued until answered. If a customer refuses to confirm as a matter of policy, document the policy and treat the refusal itself as a risk indicator.

name: inventory-count-observation
description: Plans and executes attendance at a physical inventory count and evaluates the results. Use it when scheduling year-end or cycle counts, when inventory is held at third-party warehouses or in transit, when count sheets show large book-to-physical adjustments, or when someone asks how many test counts to make and how to handle cutoff at the loading dock.
expansions: year end count is scheduled for saturday
inventory sits at a third party warehouse
book to physical adjustment looks large
how many test counts should we make
consignment stock on the count sheets
count date is two weeks before year end
obsolete parts still valued at full cost
trucks loading during the count window

atoms.obligation: Observe the client's count procedures and independently make two-way test counts from the floor to the sheets and from the sheets to the floor.
atoms.lesson: Floor-to-sheet counts test completeness and catch inventory the client failed to record; sheet-to-floor counts test existence and catch recorded stock that is not there. Doing only one direction leaves half the risk untested. Record the tag numbers, part numbers, locations, and quantities you counted in your own working papers rather than annotating client sheets, so the comparison later is genuinely independent. Note tag sequences issued, used, and voided to control the population of count records.

atoms.obligation: Establish cutoff by recording the last receiving and shipping document numbers used before the count and freezing movement during it.
atoms.lesson: Cutoff errors are the most common inventory misstatement and they hit both inventory and cost of sales. Capture the final receiver and bill of lading numbers at the count moment, photograph the dock, and confirm that goods received but unrecorded are physically segregated and included, while goods shipped are excluded. Trace several documents on each side of the cutoff into the ledger afterward. Where terms are FOB shipping point, goods in transit at year end belong to the buyer even though nobody counted them.

atoms.obligation: Identify and exclude inventory that the entity does not own, including consigned goods, customer-owned material, and items held for repair.
atoms.lesson: Consignment cuts both ways: goods the entity holds on consignment must be excluded and tagged as such on the floor, while goods the entity has out on consignment at customer sites must be included and separately confirmed with the consignee. Watch for customer-supplied components in a contract manufacturing setting, demo units at sales offices, and returned goods pending disposition. Third-party warehouse balances need a confirmation plus, when material, attendance or a service organization report on the warehouse controls.

atoms.obligation: Evaluate condition and slow movement during the count and link observations to the excess and obsolete reserve tested later.
atoms.lesson: The count floor is the only time the team sees dust, rust, damaged packaging, quarantine areas, and pallets that have not moved in years. Note item numbers and locations rather than general impressions, then tie them to the aging and turnover analysis. A reserve policy driven only by months-on-hand buckets will miss product superseded by a new model or tied to a lost customer program. Inventory must be carried at the lower of cost and net realizable value, so selling price less completion and disposal costs is the ceiling.

name: going-concern-evaluation
description: Assesses whether substantial doubt exists about an entity's ability to continue as a going concern and drafts the resulting disclosure and report wording. Use it when there are recurring losses, negative working capital, a covenant breach, a loan maturing within a year, or a funding round that has not closed. Also use it when management asserts a mitigation plan and someone must decide whether the plan is probable of being effectively implemented.
expansions: cash runway ends in nine months
we tripped a debt covenant this quarter
term loan matures within twelve months
third year of operating losses
management says a raise will close soon
do we need a going concern paragraph
parent letter of support for the subsidiary
auditor is asking for a cash flow forecast

atoms.obligation: Evaluate conditions and events over the full year following the date the financial statements are issued, not the balance sheet date.
atoms.lesson: The assessment window runs one year from issuance, so a March issuance for a December year end reaches into the following March. A revolver maturing thirteen months after year end can still fall inside the window. Gather the negative indicators as a set rather than individually: recurring operating losses, working capital deficiency, negative operating cash flow, defaults, arrears on dividends, loss of a principal customer or supplier, uninsured catastrophe, and adverse legal or regulatory outcomes.

atoms.obligation: Test the cash flow forecast supporting management's plan by challenging revenue assumptions, payment timing, and the availability of committed funding.
atoms.lesson: Compare the forecast to recent actuals and to the prior forecast's accuracy, since a plan built on a step change in bookings after four flat quarters is not credible. Check that collections use realistic days sales outstanding, that payables are not stretched beyond supplier terms, and that discretionary cost cuts are actually within management's control and already approved. Only committed, executable financing counts; a term sheet, a letter of intent, or an unsigned parent support letter is not committed funding.

atoms.obligation: Distinguish substantial doubt that is alleviated by management plans from doubt that remains, because the disclosure wording differs.
atoms.lesson: When conditions raise substantial doubt but management's plans are probable of being both implemented and effective in mitigating it, the notes describe the conditions, the plans, and the alleviation, and the auditor's report carries no emphasis. When doubt is not alleviated, the notes must state that substantial doubt exists using that phrase, and the report includes a separate going-concern section. Silence is not an option once the conditions exist; the difference is which of the two disclosures applies.

atoms.obligation: Check whether balance sheet classification and impairment conclusions still hold once going concern doubt is identified.
atoms.lesson: A covenant breach that is not waived before issuance for at least twelve months makes long-term debt current, which can itself create the working capital deficiency being assessed. A waiver obtained after year end but before issuance is a nonadjusting subsequent event for classification unless it covers the full twelve months. Doubt also pressures deferred tax asset realizability, goodwill and long-lived asset recoverability, and any liquidation-basis question, so the conclusions must be reworked together rather than in sequence.

name: goodwill-impairment-test
description: Runs the annual or triggering-event goodwill impairment test, from reporting unit identification through the fair value comparison and the loss entry. Use it when the market capitalization falls below book value, when a acquired business misses its plan, when a reorganization changes segments, or when someone asks whether the qualitative assessment is enough this year. Also covers the ordering of long-lived asset and goodwill tests.
expansions: market cap dropped below book equity
acquired unit missed its plan badly
annual impairment test is due in october
can we do a qualitative assessment this year
reorganization changed our reporting units
discount rate for the dcf model
goodwill from the 2023 acquisition looks stale
do we test the asset group before goodwill

atoms.obligation: Identify reporting units as operating segments or one level below where discrete financial information exists and management regularly reviews results.
atoms.lesson: A component one level below the operating segment is a reporting unit only if discrete financial information exists and segment management reviews it. Components with similar economic characteristics are aggregated. Getting this wrong changes everything, because goodwill impairment can hide inside a large aggregated unit where a strong business subsidizes a failing one. Goodwill is assigned to the units expected to benefit from the acquisition's synergies, which is not always the legal entity acquired, and reassignment after a reorganization uses a relative fair value approach.

atoms.obligation: Test long-lived assets and other asset groups for recoverability before the goodwill test whenever the same events triggered both.
atoms.lesson: The prescribed order is other assets such as receivables and inventory first, then indefinite-lived intangibles, then long-lived asset groups under the undiscounted cash flow recoverability test, and goodwill last. Any impairment recognized earlier reduces the reporting unit's carrying amount before goodwill is measured, so reversing the sequence overstates the goodwill charge. The long-lived asset test uses undiscounted cash flows to decide whether a loss exists and fair value to measure it, which is a different threshold from the goodwill test.

atoms.obligation: Reconcile the sum of reporting unit fair values to market capitalization and explain any implied control premium with observable evidence.
atoms.lesson: If the aggregate of discounted cash flow values sits far above market capitalization, the implied control premium must be defensible against observed premiums in comparable transactions, typically a modest range rather than a multiple. A persistent gap usually means the cash flow forecast is more optimistic than the market's view or the discount rate is too low. Check that the discount rate is a weighted average cost of capital built from market participant assumptions, and that the terminal growth rate does not exceed long-run economic growth.

atoms.obligation: Document the qualitative assessment with specific evidence when relying on it, and abandon it and measure fair value once negative evidence accumulates.
atoms.lesson: The optional qualitative screen concludes whether it is more likely than not that fair value is below carrying amount, weighing macroeconomic conditions, industry trends, cost factors, actual versus forecast financial performance, entity-specific events, and share price. It is not a formality: a unit whose fair value cushion was thin last year, whose forecast has been cut, and whose sector multiples have compressed cannot credibly pass. The entity may enter and exit the qualitative option freely by unit and by period.

name: income-tax-provision
description: Prepares or reviews the income tax provision, including current and deferred computations, the rate reconciliation, and valuation allowance judgments. Use it at quarter and year end close, when the effective tax rate moves unexpectedly, when a return-to-provision true-up lands, or when someone asks whether a deferred tax asset can be recognized after a loss year. Also covers interim reporting using an estimated annual effective rate.
expansions: effective tax rate jumped this quarter
return to provision true up posting
do we need a valuation allowance now
deferred tax rollforward will not balance
second year of pretax losses
interim provision needs an annual effective rate
state apportionment changed our blended rate
stock comp windfall hit the rate

atoms.obligation: Build deferred taxes from a balance sheet temporary difference schedule that reconciles book basis to tax basis for every account.
atoms.lesson: Deferred taxes are the tax effect of differences between book carrying amounts and tax bases that will reverse in future periods, not the accumulation of prior journal entries. Rebuild the schedule each year end from the tax basis balance sheet so errors do not roll forward indefinitely. Permanent differences such as fines and tax-exempt income never enter deferred taxes and belong only in the rate reconciliation. Apply the enacted rate expected in the reversal period, and run the effect of any rate change through continuing operations in the enactment period.

atoms.obligation: Assess valuation allowance by weighing all positive and negative evidence, giving objective verifiable evidence more weight than forecasts.
atoms.lesson: A cumulative pretax loss over the current and two preceding years is significant negative evidence that is hard to overcome, and projections of future income carry little weight against it. Positive evidence includes existing taxable temporary differences that reverse in the carryforward period, available carryback capacity, contracted backlog, and prudent feasible tax planning strategies. Schedule reversals by year and by jurisdiction and by character, since a capital loss carryforward can only be realized against capital gains regardless of ordinary income.

atoms.obligation: Prepare a rate reconciliation that explains every item moving the effective rate from statutory and investigate any unexplained residual.
atoms.lesson: Start at the federal statutory rate applied to pretax book income and walk through state taxes net of federal benefit, permanent differences, valuation allowance changes, uncertain tax position accruals, foreign rate differentials, credits, and discrete items. Stock compensation windfalls and shortfalls hit discretely in the settlement period and can swing a quarterly rate sharply. An unexplained plug is a red flag for an error in the deferred schedule, not a rounding item, and reviewers should require it be resolved rather than labeled other.

atoms.obligation: Compute interim provisions using a forecast annual effective rate applied to year-to-date income and record discrete items in the period they occur.
atoms.lesson: The estimated annual effective rate is applied to year-to-date ordinary income, with the prior year-to-date provision subtracted to get the quarter. Jurisdictions in a loss position with no expected benefit are excluded from the combined rate and computed separately. Discrete items such as settlements of audits, enacted rate changes, and share-based payment windfalls are recorded entirely in the quarter they occur. When small changes in forecast pretax income cause large rate swings, the actual year-to-date effective rate may be the better estimate.

name: transfer-pricing-documentation
description: Builds and defends intercompany pricing policy and the local file, master file, and benchmarking that support it. Use it when a new foreign subsidiary starts charging management fees, when a tax authority requests documentation, when intercompany margins drift outside the tested range, or when someone asks how to price a cost-sharing or intragroup loan arrangement.
expansions: new subsidiary charging a management fee
tax authority requested our local file
distributor margin fell outside the range
how do we price an intercompany loan
royalty rate for the brand license
benchmarking study is three years old
year end true up to the target margin
cost plus markup on shared services

atoms.obligation: Delineate the actual transaction by mapping functions performed, assets used, and risks assumed and controlled by each entity before selecting a method.
atoms.lesson: Pricing follows substance, not the contract. An entity that contractually bears inventory or market risk but lacks the people and decision-making capacity to control it will not be respected as the risk bearer, and profit follows control. Document who makes pricing decisions, who owns and develops intangibles, who directs research, and where the decision makers physically sit. A limited-risk distributor with no local pricing authority earns a routine return; the same entity making all commercial decisions is not limited risk.

atoms.obligation: Select the most appropriate pricing method for the tested party and justify why rejected methods fit worse.
atoms.lesson: The transactional net margin method dominates in practice because reliable internal comparables are rare, but comparable uncontrolled price is preferred when a genuine third-party equivalent exists, as with commodity sales or licensed software sold externally on the same terms. Cost plus suits routine services and contract manufacturing; resale price suits distributors adding little value. Profit split is for cases with unique and valuable contributions on both sides. Test the least complex entity that owns no unique intangibles, so the residual profit stays with the entrepreneur.

atoms.obligation: Refresh benchmarking with a documented screening trail and update the financial data of the comparable set annually.
atoms.lesson: A search that cannot be reproduced from the database screens, rejection reasons, and manual review notes will not survive audit. Most administrations accept a full search refresh every three years with annual financial updates, provided functions and markets are unchanged. Use multi-year weighted averages of comparables to smooth cycles, apply working capital adjustments where the intensity differs materially, and state whether the policy targets the median or merely within the interquartile range, since some jurisdictions adjust to the median on any deviation.

atoms.obligation: Operate the policy in-year with monitoring and post true-up entries before year end close rather than after the returns are filed.
atoms.lesson: Monthly or quarterly monitoring against the target margin lets an adjustment be booked as a price change with the corresponding customs and value added tax treatment considered. True-ups posted after year end raise questions about whether they are genuine pricing or after-the-fact income shifting, and downward adjustments in some jurisdictions are simply denied. Ensure the adjustment flows through the same intercompany accounts as the original charges, that both sides book it in the same period, and that supporting service evidence exists for management fees.

name: sales-tax-nexus-study
description: Determines where an entity has an obligation to collect and remit sales or use tax and how to fix exposure once found. Use it when remote sales grow into new states, when a marketplace or reseller relationship changes who collects, when a customer questions why tax was charged on a service, or when someone discovers years of uncollected tax and asks about voluntary disclosure.
expansions: sales into thirty states with no registrations
do we owe tax on saas in texas
marketplace says they collect for us
sales rep now works from another state
customer refused to pay the tax we billed
missing exemption certificates from resellers
we found four years of uncollected tax
should we do a voluntary disclosure agreement

atoms.obligation: Test each state for both physical and economic presence and record the first date each threshold was crossed.
atoms.lesson: Physical presence still creates nexus through employees, remote workers, inventory in a fulfillment warehouse, contractors performing installation or repair, and even trade show attendance beyond a state's day limit. Economic nexus thresholds are commonly two hundred thousand to five hundred thousand dollars of sales, with some states retaining a separate transaction count. The crossing date drives the registration date and the size of the exposure, so build a rolling twelve-month sales-by-ship-to-state analysis rather than a current-year snapshot.

atoms.obligation: Determine taxability by product and by state before assuming a service or digital offering is exempt.
atoms.lesson: Taxability of software as a service varies sharply: some states tax it as tangible personal property or as a data processing service, several tax it only partially, and others exempt it entirely. Bundling taxable software with exempt professional services on one invoice can make the whole invoice taxable under state bundling rules, so separately state and separately price components. Shipping charges, installation, and maintenance contracts each follow their own rules, and the sourcing rule for services is often the customer's benefit location rather than the seller's.

atoms.obligation: Collect and validate exemption certificates before the sale and re-request them on the state's expiration cycle.
atoms.lesson: In an audit the seller carries the burden, and a missing or invalid certificate converts an exempt sale into an assessment against the seller plus interest and penalty, even though the tax was the customer's. Validate that the certificate names the right seller, has a valid permit number, states an exemption reason the state recognizes for that product, and is signed. Some states expire certificates after a set number of years or require renewal on inactivity, and blanket certificates only cover the transaction types they describe.

atoms.obligation: Quantify historical exposure by state and choose between voluntary disclosure and prospective registration before any state contacts the entity.
atoms.lesson: Voluntary disclosure programs typically limit the lookback to three or four years and waive penalties, but eligibility ends the moment the state initiates contact, so timing is the whole game. Registering prospectively without addressing history leaves an open trail the state can follow backward. Where customers are exempt or self-assessed use tax, the exposure may be far smaller than gross sales suggest, so gather evidence of customer accruals first. Accrue the estimated liability under loss contingency rules once probable and estimable.

name: rd-credit-substantiation
description: Identifies qualifying research activities and builds the contemporaneous evidence the credit claim depends on. Use it when engineering wage costs are being evaluated for the credit, when an examiner requests project-level documentation, when contractor arrangements raise questions about who bears the risk, or when someone asks whether routine product improvement counts as qualified research.
expansions: which engineering salaries qualify this year
examiner asked for project level support
does routine bug fixing count as research
contractor built the prototype for us
need a nexus between wages and projects
payroll tax offset for a startup
internal use software credit questions
time tracking does not exist for engineers

atoms.obligation: Test each activity against all four qualification criteria and exclude work that fails any one of them.
atoms.lesson: Qualified research must have a permitted purpose of developing or improving a business component's function, performance, reliability, or quality; be technological in nature relying on physical, biological, engineering, or computer science; involve elimination of technical uncertainty about capability, method, or appropriate design; and follow a process of experimentation such as modeling, simulation, or systematic trial and evaluation of alternatives. Style, taste, cosmetic changes, market research, routine data collection, quality control testing, and adaptation of an existing component to a customer fail the test.

atoms.obligation: Build the claim at the business component level and connect qualified wages to specific projects rather than to departments.
atoms.lesson: The shrinking-back rule allows testing at a subcomponent level when the whole product does not qualify, which often rescues part of a claim. Examiners increasingly demand identification of each business component, the research performed, the individuals who performed it, and the information sought. Where formal time tracking does not exist, contemporaneous engineering artifacts such as design review notes, sprint records, test logs, and issue trackers plus structured interviews with technical leads carry the nexus, but interview-only support built years later is weak.

atoms.obligation: Classify qualified research expenses correctly across wages, supplies, contract research, and cloud computing, applying the statutory limits to each.
atoms.lesson: Wages cover direct performance, direct supervision, and direct support of research, and an employee who spends substantially all of their time on qualified activity can have all wages counted. Supplies must be used and consumed, so capital equipment and general overhead do not count. Contract research is limited to a percentage of amounts paid and only qualifies where the taxpayer retains substantial rights to the results and bears the economic risk of failure, which a fixed-fee deliverable contract usually defeats.

atoms.obligation: Reconcile the credit computation to the capitalized research expenditure treatment and to the payroll tax offset election where applicable.
atoms.lesson: Research expenditures must be capitalized and amortized over five years domestically and fifteen years for foreign research, which changes taxable income while leaving the credit computation on its own definition, so the two populations overlap but are not identical. A qualified small business with gross receipts under the threshold and limited history may elect to apply part of the credit against employer payroll taxes, claimed on a quarterly employment return, which is often more valuable to a loss company than a carryforward.

name: month-end-close-orchestration
description: Runs and tightens the monthly close calendar, from subledger cutoffs through the flux review and the final ledger lock. Use it when the close is slipping past its target day, when late adjustments keep appearing after reporting, when a new entity or system joins the consolidation, or when someone asks which accounts need a certified reconciliation before the books close.
expansions: close is running to day twelve again
late entries keep landing after reporting
which reconciliations must be done before lock
new subsidiary joins the consolidation
accruals keep reversing incorrectly
need a flux explanation for opex
subledger to gl differences at cutoff
who owns the intercompany step this month

atoms.obligation: Sequence close tasks by dependency with named owners and hard cutoff times, and publish the critical path rather than a flat task list.
atoms.lesson: The critical path usually runs subledger cutoffs, then payroll and accruals, then intercompany matching and elimination, then revenue and cost of sales, then tax provision, then consolidation and reporting. A flat checklist hides that the tax provision cannot start until pretax income is final, so tasks that could run in parallel are serialized and true blockers go unnoticed. Assign each task a single accountable owner, a predecessor, and a clock time, and track the day the task actually completed to find where days are lost.

atoms.obligation: Require a reviewed reconciliation with supporting detail for every balance sheet account before releasing results, and risk-rank the review depth.
atoms.lesson: The test is whether the balance is supported by identifiable items, not whether it agrees to last month. High-risk accounts are cash, receivables, inventory, accrued liabilities, intercompany, and any suspense or clearing account, which should clear to zero every month by design. Aged reconciling items are the leading indicator of a future write-off, so age them and set an escalation threshold. Preparer and reviewer must be different people, and the reviewer should be checking support rather than initialing a schedule.

atoms.obligation: Perform a flux analysis against both prior period and budget with thresholds, and require causal explanations rather than restatements of the variance.
atoms.lesson: Set thresholds in both percentage and absolute terms so a large account moving two percent is still reviewed and a small account doubling is not noise. Useful explanations name the driver: a headcount addition, a contract that ended, a rate change, a one-time settlement. Explanations that repeat the number, such as higher expenses due to increased spend, add nothing and hide errors. Flux review is often the control that catches a missed accrual or a posting to the wrong period before anyone outside the department sees it.

atoms.obligation: Lock the period after reporting and route any subsequent adjustment through a documented reopen approval with an assessed materiality conclusion.
atoms.lesson: Unlocked prior periods destroy the reliability of every report already issued and make audit trail testing fail. Once results are released, corrections normally go to the current period unless the error is material to a prior period, in which case an out-of-period adjustment analysis under the rollover and iron curtain approaches decides between correcting currently and restating. Keep a log of passed adjustments through the year, since individually immaterial items can aggregate into a material misstatement by year end.

name: bank-reconciliation-triage
description: Investigates and clears differences between bank statements and ledger cash, and hardens the process against fraud. Use it when a reconciliation will not balance, when stale outstanding checks or deposits in transit persist across months, when unidentified debits appear on the statement, or when someone asks whether a suspicious payment pattern warrants escalation.
expansions: reconciliation is off by a few hundred
outstanding checks from eight months ago
deposit in transit never cleared the bank
unknown ach debit on the statement
duplicate payment to the same vendor
merchant deposits net of fees will not tie
who approves the reconciliation each month
positive pay exceptions piling up

atoms.obligation: Prove the reconciliation both ways by starting from the bank balance and separately from the book balance to a common adjusted figure.
atoms.lesson: The bank side adjusts for deposits in transit and outstanding checks, both of which are timing items that should clear within days. The book side adjusts for bank fees, interest, returned items, and direct debits or credits the entity did not record, all of which require a journal entry. Items sitting only on one side and never clearing are not reconciling items but errors. A forced plug labeled unreconciled difference is the single strongest indicator that cash controls have failed.

atoms.obligation: Age every reconciling item and escalate anything outstanding beyond one full cycle for investigation and write-off decision.
atoms.lesson: A deposit in transit older than three business days for a domestic account means the deposit was never made, was made to a different account, or was recorded twice. Checks outstanding beyond six months are stale-dated by most banks and eventually fall under state unclaimed property rules, which require due diligence letters and escheatment on a jurisdiction-specific dormancy schedule rather than a write-back to income. Reissue or escheat deliberately; voiding old checks straight to miscellaneous income creates both a liability and an audit finding.

atoms.obligation: Keep reconciliation preparation, cash disbursement authority, and vendor master maintenance in separate hands and require independent review with evidence.
atoms.lesson: The classic scheme has one person who can create a vendor, release a payment, and reconcile the account, so the fraudulent debit is simply written off as a reconciling item. Effective review means the reviewer opens the bank statement directly from the bank rather than accepting a copy from the preparer, checks that support exists for each adjustment, and inspects cleared check images for altered payees. Positive pay exceptions and any change to bank account details for an existing vendor deserve callback verification to a known number.

atoms.obligation: Reconcile merchant processor and payment platform settlements gross, separating fees, chargebacks, reserves, and holdbacks from the deposit amount.
atoms.lesson: Processors deposit net, so a single deposit line can contain gross sales less discount fees, less refunds, less chargebacks, plus release of a prior reserve. Recording only the net amount understates both revenue and expense and makes the receivable from the processor invisible. Build a clearing account that debits gross sales at transaction date and credits on settlement, so the balance equals funds in transit at any moment, and reconcile that clearing balance to the processor's own settlement report every month.

name: unrecorded-liability-search
description: Searches for liabilities and expenses that belong in the period but were not recorded, and tests purchase cutoff at the boundary. Use it when planning completeness procedures over payables and accruals, when subsequent-period invoices are dated before year end, when unbilled legal or consulting work is suspected, or when someone asks how far into the next period the search should run.
expansions: invoices dated december paid in february
law firm has not billed us yet
goods received not invoiced balance is huge
how far after year end should we search
vendor statement shows items we do not have
accrual for the annual bonus looks light
consultant work finished but no invoice
receiving report dated after the cutoff

atoms.obligation: Examine cash disbursements after the period end above a defined threshold and trace each to the period in which the goods or services were received.
atoms.lesson: The receipt date, not the invoice date or the payment date, determines the period. Run the search through a window long enough to capture the entity's normal vendor billing lag, commonly forty-five to ninety days after year end, and set the scrutiny threshold below performance materiality since completeness errors aggregate. For each item, inspect the receiving document or service period on the invoice, then confirm whether the liability was accrued. Extend the window for vendors known to bill slowly, such as law firms and audit firms.

atoms.obligation: Test the goods received not invoiced balance and the open purchase order file rather than relying only on posted payables.
atoms.lesson: The received-not-invoiced account is where cutoff errors hide, because the receipt was recorded operationally but the accounting entry depends on a periodic accrual run. Reconcile the quantity received to the accrual and confirm the pricing source is the purchase order rather than a stale standard cost. Review open purchase orders with receipts recorded shortly before and after the cutoff, and test that receipts dated in the last days of the period were physically received then, since operations sometimes post receipts early to hit a metric.

atoms.obligation: Obtain vendor statements for major and high-risk suppliers and reconcile them to the recorded payable balance.
atoms.lesson: Vendor statements are stronger than confirmations for completeness because the supplier lists everything it believes is owed, including invoices the entity never entered. Prioritize vendors with high activity and low or zero balances, which is the classic signature of unrecorded purchases, over vendors with large recorded balances. Reconcile differences to timing, disputed invoices, and credits, and check that any credit balances in payables are genuine vendor credits rather than duplicate payments or misapplied cash.

atoms.obligation: Recompute recurring accruals for payroll, bonuses, vacation, rebates, and legal matters against the underlying obligation rather than rolling last period forward.
atoms.lesson: A liability exists when a present obligation arises from a past event, so an earned but unpaid bonus accrues even if the payout is discretionary in form but established in practice. Test the bonus accrual against the plan formula and current-year performance, vacation against the policy and the balance report, and volume rebates against contract tiers and actual customer purchases to date. For legal matters, read the counsel letter and accrue when a loss is probable and reasonably estimable, disclosing reasonably possible exposures with a range.

name: capitalization-policy-review
description: Decides what gets capitalized versus expensed for fixed assets, internal-use software, and improvements, and keeps the asset register clean. Use it when a large project mixes construction, labor, and consulting, when repairs and maintenance spikes, when useful lives look out of step with reality, or when someone asks whether a cloud implementation cost can be deferred.
expansions: warehouse buildout mixes repairs and improvements
can we capitalize this cloud implementation
internal software project labor allocation
repairs and maintenance spiked this quarter
useful life of the machinery seems long
asset register has fully depreciated ghosts
interest capitalization during construction
scrapped a line still on the books

atoms.obligation: Capitalize costs that extend useful life, increase capacity, or improve efficiency, and expense costs that merely maintain the asset's existing service potential.
atoms.lesson: Replacing a roof section that keeps the building watertight is maintenance; replacing the entire roof with a longer-lived system is an improvement. Set and apply a written capitalization threshold, commonly between one and five thousand dollars per unit, applied to the invoice line rather than the total project, so a hundred identical chairs do not become a capital asset. Book value of components replaced should be derecognized when identifiable, otherwise the register accumulates assets that no longer exist.

atoms.obligation: Split internal-use software spending across the preliminary, development, and post-implementation stages and capitalize only the development stage costs.
atoms.lesson: Preliminary-stage activities such as evaluating alternatives and selecting a vendor are expensed, as are post-implementation training and data conversion. Development-stage coding, configuration, interface building, and testing are capitalized, including allocable employee compensation supported by time records and external consultant fees. Upgrades qualify only when they add functionality. For a hosted arrangement that is a service contract, implementation costs are capitalized as a prepaid and amortized over the term including reasonably certain renewals, and the expense sits in the same line as the subscription fee, not in depreciation.

atoms.obligation: Set useful lives and salvage values from expected service in the entity's operations and revisit them when usage patterns change.
atoms.lesson: Book lives should reflect how long the asset will actually serve, which is frequently different from the tax recovery period; using tax lives for book creates permanent noise in the deferred tax schedule. Leasehold improvements are depreciated over the shorter of their useful life and the remaining lease term including renewals reasonably certain of exercise. A change in useful life is a change in estimate applied prospectively over the remaining life, never a restatement, and the entity must disclose the effect when material.

atoms.obligation: Reconcile the fixed asset register to the ledger and to physical existence, and retire disposed and idle assets promptly.
atoms.lesson: Perform a periodic physical verification by tagging significant assets and confirming location, since registers routinely carry equipment that was scrapped, sold, or moved to another site years earlier. Fully depreciated assets still in use should remain listed with the gross cost and accumulated depreciation shown, but items no longer in service must be derecognized with any gain or loss recognized. Construction in progress that has been in service for months while still sitting in the account understates depreciation and is a frequent audit adjustment.

name: journal-entry-fraud-testing
description: Designs and runs targeted testing of journal entries and other adjustments for evidence of management override. Use it when scoping the required fraud procedures on an audit, when the ledger extract needs risk-based filtering, when unusual manual entries appear near the period boundary, or when someone asks which entry characteristics deserve testing this year.
expansions: need journal entry testing criteria
manual entries posted on the last day
round dollar entries to revenue accounts
entries posted by someone outside accounting
backdated entry after the period closed
top side adjustments at consolidation
same person prepared and approved the entry
ledger extract will not tie to the trial balance

atoms.obligation: Validate the completeness of the extracted ledger population by reconciling debits, credits, and net movement to the trial balance before any filtering.
atoms.lesson: Testing an incomplete population produces meaningless results. Confirm total debits equal total credits, that opening balance plus net entries equals closing balance for every account, and that the entry count matches the system's own reporting. Watch for entries excluded by the extract parameters, such as subledger-generated postings, consolidation-level top-side adjustments held outside the ledger, and entries in a separate elimination company. Consolidation adjustments are frequently where override happens precisely because they sit outside routine controls.

atoms.obligation: Select entries using fraud risk characteristics and combine several criteria rather than sampling the population randomly.
atoms.lesson: Productive criteria include entries posted after the period closed or on weekends and holidays, entries by users who do not normally post, round-dollar and repeating amounts, entries with blank or vague descriptions, entries hitting revenue or reserve accounts from unrelated sources, entries just below an approval threshold, seldom-used account combinations, and reversing entries with no clear operational reason. Intersecting two or three criteria narrows a large population to a testable set that is far more likely to contain something.

atoms.obligation: Examine underlying support for selected entries and interview the preparer about the business purpose rather than accepting the description.
atoms.lesson: The evidence question is whether an external or independently generated document supports the amount and the timing.
