An entry moving costs from expense to a balance sheet account, or releasing a reserve into income in the final week of the year, needs the original calculation and evidence that conditions changed in that period. Interview the preparer and the approver separately, ask who directed the entry, and treat unwillingness to explain, reliance on a spreadsheet with no source, or an answer that changes after questioning as a significant finding.

atoms.obligation: Test the segregation between entry preparation and approval and identify accounts where the same identity performed both.
atoms.lesson: Pull the user identifier for prepare, post, and approve on every entry above a threshold and search for matches, shared credentials, generic service accounts, and users with both roles assigned. Check whether the system enforces approval or merely records it, since a workflow that allows self-approval when the preparer holds a higher role gives false comfort. Include the period after the close date, when access should be locked, and reconcile any post-close postings to the approved out-of-period adjustment log.

name: control-walkthrough-documentation
description: Documents a business process end to end and evaluates whether the controls in it are designed and implemented effectively. Use it when scoping internal control work for a new process or entity, when a walkthrough reveals the narrative no longer matches practice, when deciding which controls are key, or when someone asks how to test a control that depends on a system-generated report.
expansions: walkthrough the order to cash process
narrative does not match what they actually do
which controls should we call key
control relies on a system generated report
review control has no evidence of what was checked
new erp changed the approval flow
management review control precision question
segregation of duties in a five person team

atoms.obligation: Trace one transaction from initiation through recording to reporting, inspecting the actual documents rather than asking how the process works.
atoms.lesson: A walkthrough combines inquiry with observation, inspection, and reperformance; inquiry alone confirms nothing. Follow a single order from the customer purchase order through credit approval, shipment, invoicing, cash application, and the ledger posting, holding each artifact and seeing each screen. Ask the person doing the work what they do when something looks wrong, since exception handling is where controls actually fail. Confirm that the described control existed on the transaction date, not just today, when covering a full period.

atoms.obligation: Identify the risks of what could go wrong at each point and select as key only the controls that address a material risk.
atoms.lesson: Start from the assertion at risk, such as revenue recorded for goods never shipped, then find the control that would catch it. A process typically has many procedures but few key controls, and naming forty key controls in a purchase cycle guarantees shallow testing of all of them. Distinguish preventive from detective controls and note the frequency, since an annual control leaves eleven months uncovered. Where several controls address one risk, pick the most precise and most reliably evidenced.

atoms.obligation: Establish the completeness and accuracy of any report, query, or spreadsheet the control operator relies on.
atoms.lesson: A review control is only as good as the data under it. For a system-generated report, verify the report logic and parameters, agree key totals to a source the entity did not choose, and confirm that the operator ran it themselves or received it through a controlled channel. For an end-user spreadsheet, test formulas, access restrictions, version control, and any manual input. Auditors frequently find the report was filtered to exclude precisely the items the control was supposed to catch.

atoms.obligation: Evaluate the precision of management review controls by determining what threshold triggers investigation and what the reviewer does next.
atoms.lesson: A reviewer who examines variances over ten percent and one hundred thousand dollars operates at a precision that will not detect a misstatement of fifty thousand, so the control cannot address a risk at that level. Ask for the criteria, the evidence of items investigated, the questions asked, and the resolution reached, then look for a period where an exception clearly existed and check that it was caught. A signature on a report with no record of investigation is documentation of review, not evidence of an operating control.

name: audit-sampling-plan
description: Designs the sampling approach for a test, sets sizes, and evaluates the results including projection of misstatement. Use it when deciding how many items to test for a control or a balance, when a sample throws up an exception and the team must decide whether to extend, when a population contains a few very large items, or when someone asks whether to sample at all.
expansions: how many invoices should we test
one exception in a sample of forty
population has a few huge balances
should we sample or test everything
projecting the error to the population
monetary unit sampling for receivables
control operates daily how many selections
sample item has no supporting document

atoms.obligation: Define the population and the sampling unit precisely and stratify or separately test high-value and unusual items before sampling the remainder.
atoms.lesson: The population must match the assertion: for existence of receivables it is recorded balances, but for completeness it must be a source outside the ledger, since sampling recorded items can never find what was omitted. Remove individually significant items above performance materiality and test them all, along with items with specific risk indicators, then sample only the residual. Stratifying the residual by value reduces the required sample size sharply compared with an unstratified selection across a skewed population.

atoms.obligation: Set sample size from assessed risk, tolerable misstatement or deviation rate, and expected error, and record the basis for each input.
atoms.lesson: Sample size rises as tolerable misstatement falls, as expected error rises, and as reliance on other procedures falls. For controls testing, common baselines are around twenty-five selections for a daily control, forty for many-times-daily, five to fifteen for weekly or monthly, and all instances for annual or quarterly controls. For substantive tests, monetary unit sampling gives higher-value items a proportionally greater chance of selection, which suits overstatement testing of balances such as receivables and inventory.

atoms.obligation: Select items in a way that gives every unit a chance of selection and never substitute a replacement for an item you cannot examine.
atoms.lesson: Random or systematic selection with a random start preserves the statistical basis; haphazard selection is acceptable only for nonstatistical approaches and still must avoid bias toward easy or familiar items. If support for a selected item cannot be located, that item is a deviation or a misstatement, not an item to be swapped out. Substituting is one of the most common ways an otherwise sound test becomes worthless, because it silently removes exactly the items most likely to be wrong.

atoms.obligation: Project sample misstatement to the population, add known errors from items tested one hundred percent, and compare the total to tolerable misstatement.
atoms.lesson: Projection uses the ratio of misstatement to sample value applied to the population value, or the tainting approach under monetary unit sampling, and must include an allowance for sampling risk before concluding. Errors in items tested in full are known misstatements added directly, not projected. Before extending the sample, analyze whether the exception is an isolated event with a demonstrable cause; that argument requires evidence that the cause could not affect other items, which is rarely available.

name: deficiency-communication-letter
description: Evaluates the severity of identified control deficiencies and drafts the written communication to management and those charged with governance. Use it when a control failure is found and the team must decide between a deficiency, a significant deficiency, and a material weakness, when aggregating related failures, or when management pushes back on the wording of a finding.
expansions: is this a significant deficiency or worse
several small findings in the same process
management disputes our finding wording
deadline for the governance letter
compensating control might reduce severity
prior year finding is still open
no segregation of duties in the finance team
write up the observation for the audit committee

atoms.obligation: Assess severity by the magnitude of the potential misstatement the deficiency could allow and the likelihood it would not be prevented or detected.
atoms.lesson: Severity depends on what could happen, not on whether a misstatement actually occurred, so a control that failed all year with no detected error can still be a material weakness. Magnitude considers the account balance or transaction volume exposed and the future exposure, not just the current period. Likelihood considers the nature of the accounts, susceptibility to loss or fraud, subjectivity of the amounts, interaction with other deficiencies, and how the control interacts with other controls in the same process.

atoms.obligation: Aggregate related deficiencies affecting the same account or assertion and evaluate their combined severity before concluding on each individually.
atoms.lesson: Individually minor failures across a single cycle frequently combine into a significant deficiency or material weakness, because together they leave the assertion with no effective coverage. Indicators that push a finding to material weakness include identified fraud by senior management, a restatement to correct a material misstatement, a material misstatement found by the auditor that the entity's controls would not have caught, and ineffective oversight by those charged with governance. Repeat findings from prior periods also weigh toward higher severity because remediation failed.

atoms.obligation: Test any claimed compensating control at the same precision level before allowing it to reduce the severity of a finding.
atoms.lesson: A compensating control must operate at a level of precision sufficient to prevent or detect a misstatement of the same magnitude, and it must be tested, not merely asserted. In small teams the common answer is owner review of results, which only compensates if the owner reviews at transaction-level detail with defined criteria and leaves evidence. A control that reduces likelihood but not magnitude, or that operates quarterly against a monthly risk, does not fully compensate and the residual severity must be stated.

atoms.obligation: Write each finding with the condition, criteria, cause, effect, and a specific recommendation, and communicate in writing on the required timetable.
atoms.lesson: State what was observed, what should have happened, why it happened, what it could lead to, and what to change, avoiding language that names individuals or implies fraud where none was concluded. Material weaknesses and significant deficiencies go in writing to those charged with governance before the report is issued; other deficiencies may go to management. Include management's response and remediation plan where offered, and clearly state that the communication is not a complete list of all deficiencies that might exist.

name: share-based-payment-accounting
description: Accounts for equity awards from grant through vesting, modification, and settlement, including expense attribution and the related tax effects. Use it when a new option or restricted stock grant is approved, when awards are repriced or accelerated on a departure, when performance conditions become probable, or when someone asks why the expense in the ledger no longer matches the plan administrator's report.
expansions: board approved a new option grant
expense does not match the equity report
we repriced underwater options
accelerated vesting for a departing executive
performance condition now looks probable
valuation inputs for the option model
rsu withholding taxes on vest
cheap stock question before a raise

atoms.obligation: Measure awards at grant-date fair value once the grant date is established by mutual understanding, board approval, and communication to the recipient.
atoms.lesson: Grant date requires board or committee approval of the key terms, a shared understanding with the employee, and no remaining approval condition. Offer letters promising options before board action do not establish grant date but may start service. Options are valued with a model whose inputs are expected term, volatility, risk-free rate, and dividend yield; private entities often use the simplified expected term and peer-group volatility. Restricted stock units are valued at the share price, and a private company share price needs a defensible independent valuation.

atoms.obligation: Attribute expense over the requisite service period and account for forfeitures using a consistent elected policy.
atoms.lesson: Service-condition awards with graded vesting may be recognized straight-line over the total period, provided cumulative expense always equals at least the vested portion, or by accelerated attribution treating each tranche separately. The entity elects either to estimate forfeitures or to account for them as they occur, applied consistently. Performance conditions change the accounting entirely: expense is recognized only while achievement is probable, with a catch-up when probability changes, whereas market conditions are baked into fair value and expense is never reversed for failure to achieve them.

atoms.obligation: Treat any change in award terms as a modification and recognize incremental fair value measured immediately before and after the change.
atoms.lesson: Repricing underwater options, extending an exercise window, accelerating vesting on termination, or changing performance targets are all modifications. Compute fair value under the original terms and the new terms at the modification date; the excess is incremental cost recognized immediately for vested awards or over the remaining service period for unvested ones. Original grant-date expense continues unless the award was improbable of vesting before the change, in which case the whole modified fair value is recognized.

atoms.obligation: Track the book and tax difference for each award type and record windfalls and shortfalls in the income statement at settlement.
atoms.lesson: A deferred tax asset builds as book expense is recognized for awards expected to generate a future deduction, such as nonqualified options and restricted stock units. At exercise or vest, the actual deduction is based on intrinsic value or share price on that date, and the difference from the recorded deferred tax asset hits income tax expense as a discrete item, making the effective rate volatile. Incentive stock options generate no deduction absent a disqualifying disposition, so no deferred tax asset is recorded for them.

name: currency-translation-remeasurement
description: Determines functional currency and applies remeasurement and translation for foreign operations and transactions. Use it when a foreign subsidiary is set up or its business model changes, when translation adjustments swing unexpectedly, when intercompany balances generate unexpected gains and losses, or when someone asks whether a currency movement should hit income or other comprehensive income.
expansions: new subsidiary in a different currency
cta balance moved a lot this quarter
intercompany loan creating fx gains
which rate for the equity accounts
functional currency of the sales office
highly inflationary economy subsidiary
should this fx hit income or oci
we are selling the foreign entity

atoms.obligation: Determine each foreign entity's functional currency from the primary economic environment in which it generates and expends cash.
atoms.lesson: Weigh the currency of sales prices and the market that determines them, the currency of labor, materials, and other costs, the currency in which financing is obtained and receipts are retained, and the degree of autonomy from the parent. A sales branch that merely resells parent-produced goods, prices in parent currency, and remits cash promptly usually has the parent's functional currency, while a self-contained manufacturing subsidiary selling locally does not. The determination changes only when underlying facts change, and it is applied prospectively without restating prior periods.

atoms.obligation: Remeasure monetary items at the closing rate and nonmonetary items at historical rates when books are kept in a currency other than the functional currency.
atoms.lesson: Remeasurement gains and losses flow through the income statement. Monetary items are cash, receivables, payables, and debt; nonmonetary items carried at historical cost such as inventory, fixed assets, prepaid amounts, and equity stay at the rate on their original transaction date, and the related expense lines like depreciation and cost of sales follow those historical rates. Mixing rates incorrectly here is the most common error, because it produces a plug that has to be forced into the income statement to make the trial balance agree.

atoms.obligation: Translate functional-currency statements at closing rates for assets and liabilities and average rates for income, taking the difference to other comprehensive income.
atoms.lesson: Equity accounts translate at historical rates, so the cumulative translation adjustment is the balancing figure that keeps the translated balance sheet in agreement, and it accumulates in other comprehensive income rather than earnings. Average rates are acceptable for income statement items only when rates have not fluctuated significantly; a sharp devaluation calls for more frequent averaging. If the economy becomes highly inflationary, the functional currency becomes the reporting currency and remeasurement through income replaces translation.

atoms.obligation: Classify intercompany balances as long-term investment or trading and route the resulting exchange differences accordingly, and release accumulated translation on disposal.
atoms.lesson: Exchange differences on an intercompany balance for which settlement is neither planned nor anticipated in the foreseeable future are treated as part of the net investment and go to other comprehensive income; ordinary trading balances go to income. Document the intent at inception, since changing the designation later is a change in facts, not a free election. On sale or complete liquidation of the foreign entity, the accumulated translation adjustment attributable to it is reclassified from other comprehensive income into the gain or loss on disposal.

name: worker-classification-review
description: Evaluates whether workers are properly treated as employees or independent contractors and quantifies payroll tax exposure. Use it when contractors have been engaged full time for long periods, when a worker files for unemployment or files a determination request, when an agency notice arrives, or when someone asks how to bring misclassified workers onto payroll without triggering a full assessment.
expansions: contractor has worked full time for two years
former contractor filed for unemployment
state agency sent a classification notice
should this consultant be on payroll
we issue 1099s to twenty developers
workers use our equipment and our hours
voluntary classification settlement question
remote worker in a state where we are not registered

atoms.obligation: Apply the relevant control test to the actual working relationship and weigh behavioral control, financial control, and the parties' relationship.
atoms.lesson: Behavioral control looks at instructions on when, where, and how work is done, and at training provided. Financial control looks at unreimbursed investment, opportunity for profit or loss, availability of services to the market, and method of payment, since hourly pay suggests employment while a fixed project fee suggests independence. Relationship factors include written contracts, benefits, permanency, and whether the services are a key activity of the business. Several states apply a stricter three-part test where the worker must perform work outside the hiring entity's usual course of business.

atoms.obligation: Quantify exposure separately for federal employment taxes, state unemployment and withholding, and benefit plan consequences before choosing a remediation path.
atoms.lesson: Federal exposure includes the employer and employee shares of social security and medicare, federal unemployment tax, and income tax withholding, with reduced statutory rates available where information returns were filed and the treatment was not intentional. State exposure runs separately by jurisdiction with its own lookback and penalty regime, and unemployment claims often trigger the audit. Do not overlook benefit plan effects, since reclassified workers may become eligible participants retroactively, threatening plan qualification, and workers compensation premiums are recalculated too.

atoms.obligation: Preserve any available relief position by checking whether consistent treatment and a reasonable basis existed from the beginning of the engagement.
atoms.lesson: Statutory relief can bar reclassification where the entity never treated the worker or any substantially similar worker as an employee, filed all required information returns consistently, and had a reasonable basis such as judicial precedent, a prior audit, or long-standing industry practice. The relief fails entirely if any similarly situated worker was ever on payroll, so a hybrid arrangement where some developers are employees and identical ones are contractors destroys the defense. Assess this before making prospective changes that create the inconsistency.

atoms.obligation: Document the classification decision for each engagement at the outset with a written analysis and matching contract terms and operational practice.
atoms.lesson: Contracts stating that the worker is an independent contractor carry little weight if daily practice contradicts them. Align the paperwork with reality: a scope of work with deliverables rather than hours, no company email or equipment where practical, no set schedule, no supervision of method, and evidence the worker serves other clients such as their business registration and insurance. Collect the taxpayer identification certification before the first payment, since backup withholding obligations arise when it is missing, and file the annual information returns on time.

name: partnership-allocation-k1
description: Handles partnership and LLC income allocations, capital account maintenance, and the partner schedules that come out of them. Use it when a new partner is admitted mid-year, when the operating agreement has a waterfall or preferred return, when capital accounts go negative, or when someone asks why a partner's taxable income does not match their cash distributions.
expansions: new partner admitted in june
waterfall allocation with a preferred return
partner capital account went negative
why is taxable income above distributions
contributed property with built in gain
guaranteed payment versus profit allocation
partner wants a basis calculation
k1 deadline and extensions for investors

atoms.obligation: Maintain capital accounts under the agreement and separately track tax basis capital, since the two rarely equal each other.
atoms.lesson: Book capital accounts start with contributions at fair value, increase for allocated income and additional contributions, and decrease for distributions and losses. Tax basis capital uses tax-basis contributions and tax allocations. A partner's outside basis differs again because it includes the partner's share of partnership liabilities, which is why a partner can have negative capital yet positive basis. Reporting requires tax basis capital on the partner schedule, so a partnership that only kept book capital must build a conversion supported by contribution and distribution history.

atoms.obligation: Allocate income under the agreement only where the allocations have substantial economic effect, and follow the partners' interests otherwise.
atoms.lesson: Substantial economic effect requires capital accounts maintained under the regulations, liquidating distributions in accordance with positive capital accounts, and either an unconditional deficit restoration obligation or a qualified income offset with the related limitation on loss allocations. Allocations that merely shift tax character between partners without changing their economics fail the substantiality test. Where the agreement uses a distribution waterfall rather than stated percentages, targeted allocations that force capital accounts to match the hypothetical liquidation amount are the usual mechanism.

atoms.obligation: Apply the required method for built-in gain or loss on contributed property and track forward differences between book and tax basis.
atoms.lesson: When a partner contributes appreciated property, the pre-contribution gain must ultimately be allocated back to that partner rather than shared. The traditional method allocates tax items to eliminate the disparity but is limited by the ceiling rule; the curative and remedial methods correct that limit with offsetting allocations. Reverse allocations arise when capital accounts are restated on admission of a new partner. These layers must be tracked by property and by partner for the life of the asset, which spreadsheets frequently lose after a few years.

atoms.obligation: Allocate items for partners entering or leaving mid-year using a permissible proration or interim closing method stated consistently.
atoms.lesson: The varying interest rules require either an interim closing of the books at the date of the change or a proration of the year's items by days, with certain extraordinary items always allocated to the date they occur. Interim closing gives a more accurate result when income is uneven but requires a hard cutoff of the ledger. Guaranteed payments for services or capital are allocated to the recipient and are not part of the profit split, and they create ordinary income to the partner regardless of partnership profitability.

name: intercompany-reconciliation-cleanup
description: Matches and clears intercompany balances and transactions across entities so consolidation eliminates cleanly. Use it when intercompany accounts do not net to zero at consolidation, when entities disagree on a cross-charge, when unrealized profit sits in inventory transferred between affiliates, or when someone asks how to settle years of accumulated imbalances.
expansions: intercompany accounts do not net to zero
two subsidiaries disagree on a cross charge
unrealized margin on transferred inventory
elimination entry leaves a plug at consolidation
fx difference on an intercompany balance
years of unsettled intercompany balances
who books the shared services allocation
intercompany invoice posted in the wrong month

atoms.obligation: Match intercompany balances by counterparty and account with a monthly cutoff both sides must respect, and assign a dispute owner.
atoms.lesson: Most imbalances are timing: one entity books a charge in the month incurred while the counterparty books it on invoice receipt. Set a fixed intercompany cutoff several days before the ledger close, require both sides to post in the same period, and use a single agreed transaction currency per relationship. Publish a matching report by pair with an aging, name an owner for each open item, and escalate anything above a threshold outstanding beyond one cycle, since aged intercompany differences almost always become a write-off charged to one entity.

atoms.obligation: Eliminate unrealized profit on assets still held within the group before consolidating, and release it as the asset is sold or consumed externally.
atoms.lesson: When one entity sells inventory to another at a markup, the consolidated group has no profit until the goods leave the group, so the margin remaining in ending inventory must be eliminated along with the intercompany revenue and cost of sales. Track it by transferring entity and product using the actual transfer markup, not an average. The same principle applies to fixed assets transferred internally, where the gain is reversed and depreciation is adjusted back to the original basis for the remaining life.

atoms.obligation: Separate intercompany balances that carry currency exposure from those that do not and record differences in the entity that bears the risk.
atoms.lesson: A payable denominated in a currency other than the entity's functional currency generates remeasurement gains or losses in that entity's income statement, while the counterparty may have no exposure at all. That asymmetry means the two sides will not agree when converted, and the difference is real accounting, not an error. Fix the reporting currency of the pair, record the exchange effect only once, and confirm whether balances designated as long-term net investments should route their exchange differences to other comprehensive income instead.

atoms.obligation: Settle intercompany balances on a defined cash cycle and document the legal basis and pricing for every recurring cross-charge.
atoms.lesson: Balances that never settle drift toward looking like equity contributions or disguised loans, attracting deemed interest, withholding tax, and thin capitalization scrutiny, and they distort each entity's standalone statements used for local statutory filings and covenants. Establish a netting and settlement run on a set cadence, support recurring management fees and cost allocations with a written service agreement and an allocation key that reflects benefit received, and keep evidence that the service was actually delivered.

name: fnol-intake-triage
description: Captures a first notice of loss and routes it onto the right handling track during the first contact. Use when a policyholder or agent reports a new claim, when a loss notice arrives with half the detail missing, or when deciding whether a loss needs a field adjuster, a desk adjuster or straight-through handling. Also use when setting up the file and its initial diary.
expansions: customer just called reporting a rear-end collision
loss notice came in with no policy number
water damage reported at insured warehouse
need to set up a new claim file
decide if this needs a field adjuster
caller reporting a theft over the weekend
intake form is missing the date of loss
assign severity and route this new claim

atoms.obligation: Verify the policy was in force on the stated date of loss before assigning a claim number or setting reserves.
atoms.lesson: In-force verification catches lapse, cancellation for non-payment and mid-term endorsement gaps before money moves. Check effective and expiration dates against the reported date of loss, confirm the loss location appears as a scheduled location, and confirm the driver or entity is a named insured or permissive user. A loss inside a grace period or after a rescission is a coverage question for coverage review, not something the intake desk should decide.

atoms.obligation: Record the date, time, location and mechanism of loss in the reporter's own words before asking any closed questions.
atoms.lesson: The first narrative is the least rehearsed evidence in the file. Capture the sequence verbatim, what the insured was doing, what failed, who else was present, then follow with closed questions on injuries, witnesses, police report number and other insurance. Later recorded statements get compared against this narrative, and drift between the two drives both fraud referrals and liability disputes, so paraphrasing the caller into adjuster shorthand destroys the comparison.

atoms.obligation: Assign a severity track at intake so low-complexity losses do not consume scarce field inspection capacity.
atoms.lesson: Most personal auto and homeowner losses are low severity and settle from photographs and an estimate with no site visit. Route on triggers rather than instinct: reported injury, fatality, airbag deployment, commercial vehicle, suspected total loss, structural damage, third-party bodily injury, or an unrepresented claimant mentioning counsel. Anything with potential injury or a large-loss dollar trigger goes to a field or large-loss unit at once, because early inspection preserves evidence and controls the reserve.

atoms.obligation: Send the acknowledgement and required disclosures to the claimant within the deadline set by the state of loss.
atoms.lesson: Unfair claims settlement practices rules impose state-specific clocks, commonly acknowledgement within ten to fifteen days of notice, a coverage decision within fifteen to forty days of proof of loss, and payment within a set number of days after agreement. The clock runs from notice, not from file assignment, so an unassigned claim still accrues exposure. Document the date and method of every required contact in the file notes.

name: auto-liability-determination
description: Works through fault allocation on a motor claim using statements, physical evidence and the traffic law of the loss state. Use when both drivers blame each other, when the police report conflicts with the damage pattern, when setting a comparative negligence percentage, or when a claimant disputes a partial-fault decision.
expansions: both drivers say the light was green
damage pattern does not match the story
need to assign comparative fault percentages
claimant disputes our seventy thirty split
lane change accident with no witnesses
police report blames our insured
parking lot backing collision liability call
rear-end but claimant stopped suddenly

atoms.obligation: Reconcile the reported impact sequence with the physical damage profile before accepting either driver's account.
atoms.lesson: Contact points, crush direction, paint transfer and ride height show whether an impact was overtaking, angled or head-on. A left-front to left-front sideswipe is not consistent with a claimed rear-end. Underride and override marks indicate relative speed and braking. When physical evidence contradicts both statements, a scene photograph set or a reconstruction costs far less than the liability differential on a disputed injury claim.

atoms.obligation: Apply the negligence rule of the state where the accident happened, not the insured's home state, when allocating fault.
atoms.lesson: Roughly a dozen jurisdictions use pure comparative fault, most use modified comparative with a fifty or fifty-one percent bar, and a handful, including Alabama, Maryland, North Carolina, Virginia and the District of Columbia, remain contributory negligence states where any claimant fault defeats recovery entirely. Getting the jurisdiction wrong turns a defensible sixty forty allocation into either an overpayment or a bad-faith exposure.

atoms.obligation: Treat the police report as one piece of evidence rather than the fault determination, and note whether the officer witnessed the crash.
atoms.lesson: Officers usually arrive afterwards and record a narrative from the parties, sometimes with a citation. Citations are admissible in some states and excluded in others, and a dismissed or amended citation carries little weight. Read the diagram, the roadway measurements and the stated contributing factors, but be prepared to reach a different allocation supported by statements, scene photographs and vehicle damage.

atoms.obligation: Document the presumption you relied on and the specific facts that confirm or rebut it in the liability evaluation.
atoms.lesson: Rear-end, backing, unprotected left turn and lane-change scenarios each carry a rebuttable presumption against one driver. Rebuttal facts matter: a brake check, a non-functioning brake lamp, an unsignalled lane entry, a vehicle stopped in a live lane without hazards. Written evaluations that name the presumption and the rebutting evidence survive supervisor review, claimant challenge and a later bad-faith file audit.

name: repair-estimate-review
description: Reviews a contractor or adjuster repair estimate line by line for scope, pricing and duplication before payment issues. Use when a contractor's estimate is far above the adjuster's, when a supplement arrives mid-repair, when depreciation or overhead and profit is disputed, or when checking that the written scope matches the loss photographs.
expansions: contractor estimate is triple our adjuster figure
supplement request came in after demolition
is overhead and profit owed here
estimate calls for full roof replacement
check line items against the loss photos
homeowner disputes the depreciation applied
matching siding on a partial loss
estimate has duplicate labour lines

atoms.obligation: Compare the estimate scope against the documented damage photographs before challenging any unit prices.
atoms.lesson: Most estimate disputes are scope disputes wearing a price mask. Confirm each line ties to visible damage or to a necessary consequential item such as tear-off, disposal, containment, drying or a code-required upgrade. A line for full slope replacement needs test-square evidence of widespread damage or a genuine matching problem. Arguing unit price on a line that should not exist at all wastes cycle time and concedes the scope.

atoms.obligation: Apply depreciation only to items with recoverable wear, and hold back only what the policy and the state permit.
atoms.lesson: Actual cash value is replacement cost less depreciation. Labour depreciation is prohibited or restricted in several states and permitted in others, so the practice must follow the loss state and the policy language. Depreciation should reflect the age, expected life and observed condition of the specific component; a fifteen-year-old three-tab roof on a twenty-five-year life is treated differently from vinyl siding. Record age, life and percentage basis per line.

atoms.obligation: Include contractor overhead and profit when the repair genuinely requires coordinating three or more separate trades.
atoms.lesson: The working test is whether a general contractor is reasonably necessary given the number and complexity of trades, not whether one was actually hired. A kitchen fire needing demolition, framing, electrical, plumbing, drywall, cabinetry and paint qualifies; a single-room carpet replacement does not. Several jurisdictions treat systematic withholding on genuinely multi-trade losses as an underpayment practice, so the reasoning belongs in the file, not just the number.

atoms.obligation: Require documented hidden damage or a signed change order before paying any supplement above the agreed scope.
atoms.lesson: Supplements are legitimate when demolition exposes rot, obsolete wiring, missing sheathing or code upgrades invisible at inspection. They are not a second attempt at unit pricing already agreed. Ask for date-stamped progress photographs of the concealed condition, the code section behind any ordinance-driven upgrade, and a delta estimate rather than a rewritten total, so the paid scope stays reconcilable against the original agreement.

name: bodily-injury-reserve-setting
description: Sets and revises indemnity and expense reserves on injury claims so the file carries a defensible number. Use when medical specials jump, when a demand package arrives, when a claim is first flagged as potentially serious, or when a reserve is challenged in a file review or large-loss roundtable.
expansions: demand package landed with eighty thousand specials
claimant now has a surgical recommendation
reserve has not moved in six months
need a reserve for a soft tissue claim
roundtable wants justification for the number
attorney representation letter just came in
medicals doubled after the last imaging
expense reserve for defence counsel spend

atoms.obligation: Reserve to the most likely settlement value on known facts, not to the demand and not to the best defence case.
atoms.lesson: A reserve estimates ultimate cost including future medicals, wage loss and general damages, plus separate allocated expense for counsel, experts and records. Anchoring on the claimant demand inflates the book; anchoring on the defence best case creates stair-step development that regulators and reinsurers read as reserve inadequacy. Value the range, select the most probable point, and name the two or three facts that would move it.

atoms.obligation: Revise the reserve within days of any event that materially changes exposure, and record exactly what changed.
atoms.lesson: Material events include a surgical recommendation, a specialist referral, a permanent impairment rating, a representation letter, a suit filing, a lien notice or a policy-limits demand. Stair-stepping, meaning small repeated increases with no triggering event, signals the file was under-evaluated rather than that facts changed. Each revision note should name the document received, its date, and its effect on specials, general damages or expense.

atoms.obligation: Separate hard medical specials from projected future care and value each on its own supporting evidence.
atoms.lesson: Billed charges are not paid charges. Network repricing, fee schedules and usual-and-customary reductions mean a billed sixty thousand may reprice near twenty-two thousand, and some jurisdictions admit only amounts actually paid while others send the full billed figure to the jury. Future care needs a treating physician plan or a life care plan rather than extrapolation of past visits, and may be reserved at present value where permitted.

atoms.obligation: Escalate to management and to reinsurance reporting once probable exposure crosses the notification threshold.
atoms.lesson: Excess and reinsurance treaties set individual loss notification triggers, often at half of the retention or on defined injury types such as fatality, amputation, spinal cord injury, brain injury or severe burns. Late notice can prejudice the reinsurer and complicate recovery. The same thresholds usually drive internal large-loss committee review, so a single escalation memo covering facts, liability, damages and plan serves both audiences.

name: total-loss-settlement
description: Values and settles a vehicle or property declared a total loss, including salvage and owner-retention scenarios. Use when repair cost approaches the threshold, when an insured disputes the actual cash value offer, when handling a lease or lienholder payoff, or when deciding whether to let the owner keep the salvage.
expansions: repair cost is seventy eight percent of value
insured says our valuation is too low
lienholder payoff exceeds the settlement
owner wants to retain the salvage
need comparable vehicles for the valuation
total loss threshold in this state
gap coverage question on a leased car
sales tax and title fees on settlement

atoms.obligation: Determine total loss status using the loss state's threshold or required formula, and preserve the calculation in the file.
atoms.lesson: Some states set a fixed percentage, often seventy to eighty percent of actual cash value, while others use a formula comparing repair cost plus salvage value against actual cash value. Repair cost for the test should include anticipated supplements from hidden structural damage, not only the visible estimate. Crossing the threshold triggers branded title obligations and disclosure duties, so inputs and arithmetic must both be documented.

atoms.obligation: Build the valuation from recent comparable local sales with condition and option adjustments itemised line by line.
atoms.lesson: A defensible actual cash value uses recent comparable sales within a reasonable radius, adjusted for mileage, trim, drivetrain, options and pre-loss condition, with every adjustment shown. Insureds successfully challenge valuations that present one opaque figure. Prior damage, aftermarket equipment and documented recent maintenance all move the number, and several states require the offer to include sales tax, title and registration fees whether or not a replacement is purchased.

atoms.obligation: Confirm lienholder and lessor payoff figures in writing before issuing any settlement draft to anyone.
atoms.lesson: The loss payee clause obligates payment to the secured party to the extent of its interest. Verbal payoffs go stale because per diem interest, late fees and repossession holds change the figure between quote and issuance. Where payoff exceeds actual cash value the shortfall belongs to the borrower unless gap coverage or a lease residual provision applies, and paying the wrong party creates a second payment obligation.

atoms.obligation: Decide owner retention against salvage recovery and reduce the settlement by the actual retained salvage value.
atoms.lesson: Owner retention reduces the payment by the salvage bid, transfers branded-title and disclosure burdens to the owner, and forfeits the carrier's recovery. It usually suits antique, custom or sentimental vehicles and units with a thin salvage market. Where the vehicle carries flood, fire or structural damage, retention raises re-titling and roadworthiness questions and some states restrict rebuilding, so confirm the loss state rules before agreeing.

name: fraud-indicator-triage
description: Screens a claim for fraud indicators and builds a referral a special investigations unit can act on. Use when the loss facts do not hang together, when a claimant's claim history looks staged, when documentation looks manufactured, or when deciding whether to refer, investigate further or simply pay.
expansions: loss happened days after the policy bound
same claimant on three prior claims
receipts for contents look fabricated
staged accident pattern with four occupants
no police report on a large theft
invoice from a clinic we have flagged
insured pressuring for a fast payout
build the investigations referral for this file

atoms.obligation: Refer on documented indicator patterns, never on a single indicator or on the claimant's personal background.
atoms.lesson: Isolated indicators are common in legitimate claims because people do lose receipts and do have prior claims. Referral strength comes from clusters: recent inception or a coverage increase just before the loss, no independent witness, an unusually rehearsed narrative, cash purchases with sequential receipts, treatment patterns matching a known clinic, and pressure for speed. Referring on ethnicity, neighbourhood, language or income is unlawful and contaminates the file.

atoms.obligation: Keep handling the claim within statutory time limits while the investigation runs, and communicate on schedule in writing.
atoms.lesson: An open investigation does not pause unfair claims practices deadlines. Delay without a documented basis, or a records demand with no plausible relevance, converts a good fraud case into a bad-faith case. Use the cooperation clause and the examination under oath provision deliberately, give written notice of what is required and why, log every extension notice, and issue a written status letter rather than silence when no decision is possible yet.

atoms.obligation: Preserve original documents, image metadata and recorded statements in evidentiary form from the moment suspicion arises.
atoms.lesson: Altered invoices are usually proven by comparison against the vendor's own records, by inconsistent fonts or totals, or by image metadata showing a photograph predates the loss. Once a file is annotated, re-saved or summarised, that proof weakens. Keep originals unaltered, log chain of custody for physical evidence such as a fire scene sample or a failed appliance, and take recorded statements with consent valid in the loss state.

atoms.obligation: File the mandatory report to the state fraud bureau once the threshold of reasonable belief has been met.
atoms.lesson: Most states require carriers to report suspected insurance fraud to a fraud bureau or insurance department, usually on a prescribed form and within a set number of days of forming a reasonable belief. Statutory immunity for good-faith reporting protects the carrier only when the prescribed process is followed. The report is independent of the coverage decision: a claim may be paid while a report stands, and a denial does not substitute for reporting.

name: subrogation-referral
description: Spots recovery potential on a paid or reserved claim and packages it for subrogation before the right to recover is lost. Use when a third party or a product caused the loss, when a contractor's work failed, when deciding whether recovery is economically worth pursuing, or when a limitation period is approaching.
expansions: water loss caused by a failed water heater
third party carrier already accepted liability
plumbing contractor work caused this loss
limitation period runs in four months
worth pursuing a six thousand recovery
need to preserve the failed part
landlord tenant waiver of subrogation question
made whole doctrine in this state

atoms.obligation: Identify the recovery target and preserve the physical evidence before repairs destroy the failure point.
atoms.lesson: Subrogation dies the moment the failed water heater, supply hose, dryer or electrical component goes to the dump. Secure the component, photograph the installation as found, record serial and model numbers and the installer, and place the responsible party on written spoliation notice with a real opportunity to inspect. Courts sanction carriers that destroy evidence before giving that notice, and a product claim without the product is not a claim.

atoms.obligation: Check leases and construction agreements for contractual waivers of subrogation before spending money on pursuit.
atoms.lesson: Standard commercial leases and construction contracts frequently contain mutual waivers of subrogation, and many jurisdictions enforce them even against a negligent party. A tenant treated as an implied co-insured under the lease cannot be pursued in many states. Read the insurance and indemnity clauses and the construction contract waiver article early, because discovering the waiver after retaining an expert turns a recovery file into a pure expense file.

atoms.obligation: Apply the loss state's rules on the insured's deductible and on made-whole before allocating any recovered money.
atoms.lesson: Recovery allocation is not automatically pro rata. Many states require the insured to be made whole before the carrier retains anything, and most require the deductible to be included in the demand and returned first or shared proportionally with pursuit costs. Errors here trigger regulatory complaints and class exposure. Document the allocation formula, the deductible amount and the costs deducted, and send the insured a written accounting.

atoms.obligation: Calendar the limitation period from the correct accrual date and diary the file well ahead of it.
atoms.lesson: The clock varies by theory and jurisdiction: often two to three years for negligence, four for contract or sale of goods, and much shorter notice periods against public entities, sometimes ninety days. Construction defect claims can also face a statute of repose measured from substantial completion. Accrual may run from the date of loss or from discovery. Missing the date extinguishes recovery and creates an errors and omissions exposure for the handler.

name: coverage-position-letter
description: Drafts reservation of rights, denial and coverage-position letters that state the policy basis precisely. Use when a claim raises a coverage question, when defending an insured under a reservation, when denying in whole or in part, or when the insured's counsel challenges the position the carrier has taken.
expansions: need a reservation of rights on this suit
denying this claim for late notice
wear and tear exclusion applies here
draft a partial denial for the mould cap
insured lawyer challenged our reservation letter
which exclusions do we actually cite
duty to defend question on this complaint
business use exclusion on a personal auto

atoms.obligation: Quote the exact policy language relied on and tie each quoted provision to the specific facts of this loss.
atoms.lesson: A letter listing a dozen exclusions without connecting any of them to facts is treated in many jurisdictions as no reservation at all, and can waive the defences it purported to preserve. Quote the insuring agreement, the relevant definition, the exclusion and any exception, identify the form number and edition date, then state the facts bringing the loss inside that language. Generic boilerplate invites waiver and estoppel arguments.

atoms.obligation: Assess the duty to defend against the allegations pleaded, separately from and more broadly than the duty to indemnify.
atoms.lesson: The duty to defend is triggered by any allegation potentially within coverage, judged on the four corners of the complaint against the policy, with a few jurisdictions admitting extrinsic facts. If one count of a ten-count complaint is potentially covered, the entire defence is normally owed. Denying a defence on an indemnity analysis is a classic bad-faith error, and some states strip the insurer of settlement control after a wrongful refusal.

atoms.obligation: State the remaining investigation, the information needed from the insured, and the right to modify the position later.
atoms.lesson: A reservation letter is a live document. It should identify which coverage issues remain unresolved, what documents, statements or examinations are required, that investigation continues without waiver, and that the position may be amended as facts develop. It should also address the insured's right to independent counsel where the reservation creates a conflict, a right that in several jurisdictions the reservation itself gives rise to.

atoms.obligation: Meet the state deadline for a written coverage decision and include the required appeal and regulator notices.
atoms.lesson: Denials commonly must issue in writing within a set period after proof of loss, state the specific reason, and include notice of the right to complain to the insurance department, with some states also requiring notice of any contractual suit limitation period. A denial that is timely but vague draws the same regulatory criticism as a late one. Preserve the mailing date, the method and every address used.

name: business-interruption-loss
description: Quantifies a time-element loss covering lost income, extra expense and the period of restoration. Use when a covered property loss shuts operations down, when an insured's accountant submits a lost profits calculation, when the indemnity period end date is disputed, or when contingent or dependent-property exposure is raised.
expansions: plant shut down for eleven weeks
accountant submitted a lost profits claim
how long is the period of restoration
extra expense to rent temporary space
supplier fire stopped our insured production
payroll continuation during the shutdown
seasonal business income calculation
dispute over the indemnity period end date

atoms.obligation: Fix the period of restoration by the time reasonably required to repair, not by the actual downtime experienced.
atoms.lesson: The standard time-element trigger runs from the date of physical loss to the date the property should be rebuilt, repaired or replaced with reasonable speed and similar quality, regardless of policy expiry. Delays from the insured's financing, an elective upgrade or slow permitting are not covered, though ordinance-driven rebuild requirements may extend it where that time-element extension was purchased. Build a construction timeline with the contractor before arguing about numbers.

atoms.obligation: Project the income the business would have earned using trend and seasonality rather than repeating last year's figures.
atoms.lesson: Business income equals net profit or loss plus continuing normal operating expenses, measured against what would have happened had no loss occurred. That requires adjusting for growth trend, seasonality, a lost or won contract, market conditions and any make-up sales after reopening. A bakery earning forty percent of annual revenue in November and December cannot be valued on a twelve-month average. Use monthly prior-year figures plus documented forward orders.

atoms.obligation: Separate saved expenses from continuing expenses and deduct every cost that did not continue during the shutdown.
atoms.lesson: Raw materials not purchased, hourly wages not paid, utilities not consumed, freight not incurred and commissions not earned are saved and must come out. Rent, salaried staff, insurance, interest, depreciation and contracted services generally continue. Ordinary payroll may be limited or excluded unless an endorsement extends it for a stated number of days, and retaining key staff is a continuing expense only where the policy or extra expense cover permits.

atoms.obligation: Treat extra expense as recoverable to the extent it reduces the income loss the policy would otherwise have paid.
atoms.lesson: Expediting and extra expense cover temporary premises, rented equipment, overtime, air freight on replacement machinery and relocation, but the classic test is whether the spend avoids a greater income loss. A dollar spent to save fifty cents is not fully recoverable unless a separate extra expense limit applies without that offset. Ask the insured to document the counterfactual, meaning the income loss that would have occurred without the spend.

name: catastrophe-response-plan
description: Stands up the claims operation for a declared catastrophe: staffing, coding, reserving, communication and field logistics. Use when a hurricane, wildfire, hail swarm or freeze event is forecast or has landed, when claim volume overwhelms normal capacity, or when setting up an event code and surge handling process.
expansions: hurricane makes landfall in seventy two hours
hail swarm generated four thousand claims
need an event code for this catastrophe
deploying independent adjusters to the region
wildfire evacuation zone claims handling
advance payments for additional living expense
set up mobile claim centres in the county
freeze event burst pipes across the book

atoms.obligation: Open a catastrophe event code before the first claim arrives so every related loss aggregates correctly.
atoms.lesson: A single event code drives reinsurance recovery under the catastrophe treaty hours clause, commonly seventy-two hours for hurricane and one hundred sixty-eight for other perils, plus regulatory data calls, deductible application and internal loss tracking. Losses miscoded into normal handling are the most common reason a carrier under-recovers from its catastrophe programme. Define the geographic scope, the peril and the start and end times of the event window in writing.

atoms.obligation: Apply the correct percentage deductible against the right insured value and confirm the peril trigger was actually met.
atoms.lesson: Hurricane and named-storm deductibles are percentages of the dwelling or building limit rather than of the loss, and trigger only on defined conditions such as a named storm within a stated distance, sustained wind speeds, or a declaration window with fixed start and end times. Wind-driven rain, storm surge and inland flood are treated differently, and surge is generally excluded from wind cover. Verify the trigger against official meteorological data.

atoms.obligation: Issue advance payments for additional living expense and emergency mitigation before full adjustment is complete.
atoms.lesson: Displaced families need lodging money within days, not after inspection. Advances against the eventual settlement reduce complaint volume, prevent further avoidable damage, and are expected by regulators after a declared event. Set a field authority level, require only proof of loss location and displacement, record the advance against the correct coverage part, and state in writing that it is neither a final settlement nor a coverage admission.

atoms.obligation: Match field capacity to inspection demand by severity tier and track cycle time and pending age daily during the surge.
atoms.lesson: Independent adjusters, staff catastrophe teams, aerial imagery review and virtual inspection cost different amounts and suit different severities. Total losses and commercial risks need experienced field handlers, while minor roof and fence claims settle from photographs or a self-service scope. The surge metrics that matter are new claims, inspections completed, files closed, average cycle time and open pending age, because pending age becomes complaints and litigation.

name: workers-comp-claim-handling
description: Manages an injured worker's compensability, benefit payments and return to work. Use when an employee reports a workplace injury, when compensability is questionable, when indemnity benefits must start, change or stop, or when planning modified duty, an impairment evaluation or a full and final settlement.
expansions: employee hurt their back lifting at the warehouse
is this injury compensable or idiopathic
start temporary total disability payments
doctor released the worker to modified duty
employer has no light duty available
impairment rating came back at twelve percent
injury reported three weeks after the fact
settle this as a full and final

atoms.obligation: Decide compensability on whether the injury arose out of and in the course of employment, and document the evidence.
atoms.lesson: Arising out of means a causal connection to the work; in the course of means during the time, place and circumstances of employment. Recurring disputes involve horseplay, intoxication, the going and coming rule, personal deviations, idiopathic falls and degenerative conditions aggravated by work. Most states allow a delayed or investigating status for a set number of days with benefits paid without prejudice, so first report rarely demands an outright accept or deny.

atoms.obligation: Calculate the average weekly wage from the statutory look-back and include every wage component the state requires.
atoms.lesson: The average weekly wage drives every indemnity dollar and errors compound across years of benefits. Most states use a fifty-two week look-back with special rules for short tenure, concurrent employment, seasonal work, overtime, bonuses, tips and employer-provided lodging or meals. The compensation rate is typically two-thirds of that wage subject to annually changing state maximum and minimum. Underpayment triggers penalties and interest, while overpayment is frequently unrecoverable.

atoms.obligation: Drive return to work by matching documented physical restrictions to a written modified duty offer from the employer.
atoms.lesson: Duration of disability rather than medical cost is what makes a claim expensive, and the probability of ever returning falls sharply after twelve weeks away. Obtain specific restrictions such as lifting limits, standing tolerance and no overhead reach, then have the employer put an offer in writing describing actual tasks, hours and pay. A written offer refused usually suspends temporary total benefits; an informal phone conversation does not.

atoms.obligation: Coordinate any settlement with future medical exposure and with the interests of any government benefit programme.
atoms.lesson: Closing future medicals for a claimant who receives or reasonably expects government health benefits raises secondary payer obligations, and larger settlements involving future treatment usually require a set-aside allocation and reporting. Many states also require board or judicial approval of a compromise, with distinct rules for closing versus leaving medicals open. A structured settlement can fund lifetime care at lower present cost, which matters most on younger claimants.

name: litigated-claim-management
description: Runs a claim once suit is filed: counsel assignment, litigation plan, budget control and settlement authority. Use when a complaint is served on an insured, when defence spend runs past budget, when preparing for mediation, or when deciding whether to try a case or resolve it.
expansions: complaint served on our insured yesterday
defence counsel blew through the budget
mediation next month need settlement authority
should we try this case or settle
answer is due in twenty days
expert disclosure deadline is approaching
policy limits demand with a short deadline
evaluate the trial verdict range here

atoms.obligation: Confirm the answer deadline and assign defence counsel immediately on service, before the coverage analysis concludes.
atoms.lesson: A default judgment against the insured is nearly always worse than a coverage dispute. Response deadlines commonly run twenty to thirty days from service and vary by court and by whether service reached a registered agent or a state official. Assign counsel, get an appearance filed or an extension stipulated, and run the coverage analysis in parallel under a reservation, using separate coverage counsel where the reservation creates a conflict.

atoms.obligation: Require a written litigation plan and phased budget covering discovery, experts, motions and trial before authorising spend.
atoms.lesson: Uncontrolled defence spend rather than indemnity is what makes small cases unprofitable. The plan should state the defence theory, the two or three facts that will decide the case, the discovery genuinely needed to establish them, which experts are necessary and when, and a realistic resolution window. Phased budgets with variance reporting let a handler challenge a forty thousand dollar expert on a sixty thousand dollar case before the invoice arrives.

atoms.obligation: Evaluate the case as a range of verdict outcomes weighted by probability, then set settlement authority against that range.
atoms.lesson: A defensible evaluation combines the probability of a defence verdict, the probability of liability findings at various comparative splits, and the damages range supported by medicals and wage evidence, then adds the cost of trying the case and the risk of fee shifting or prejudgment interest. Venue matters enormously, since identical facts resolve very differently in a conservative rural county and a plaintiff-friendly urban one.

atoms.obligation: Respond in writing to a time-limited policy limits demand within its deadline, even when the answer is not yet yes.
atoms.lesson: A limits demand with a short fuse is engineered to create an excess judgment and a bad-faith claim against the carrier. Acknowledge in writing immediately, state exactly what information is needed to evaluate and why, request an extension with a reason, notify the insured of the demand and any excess exposure, and notify excess carriers. Silence or a late counteroffer is the single most expensive mistake in claims.

name: commercial-property-risk-assessment
description: Underwrites a commercial property risk from construction, occupancy, protection and exposure information. Use when a broker submits a warehouse or manufacturing risk, when a survey report returns with recommendations, when setting terms and deductibles, or when judging whether the reported values are credible.
expansions: submission for a plastics manufacturer
survey flagged no sprinkler in storage
insured values look low per square foot
what deductible for this frame apartment
occupancy changed to cannabis processing
review the construction data on this schedule
sprinkler design versus commodity stored
protection class nine rural risk

atoms.obligation: Assess construction, occupancy, protection and external exposure together, because each one changes the meaning of the others.
atoms.lesson: A fully sprinklered building is not automatically good if the sprinkler design density is wrong for the commodity, since rack-stored plastics behave nothing like paper on shelving. Non-combustible construction with a highly combustible occupancy still burns, while joisted masonry with a light occupancy may be fine. External exposure means adjacent hazards, brush, and distance to the responding fire station and hydrants, captured in the public protection classification.

atoms.obligation: Test reported values against an independent cost basis before accepting them and before relying on coinsurance.
atoms.lesson: Undervaluation is the most common and most damaging data error in property underwriting: it understates premium, understates the exposure the reinsurance programme assumes, and produces a coinsurance penalty that lands on the insured at claim time. Compare reported values per square foot against current construction cost by occupancy and region, question values unchanged year over year during inflation, and consider agreed value or a margin clause on unreliable schedules.

atoms.obligation: Convert every survey recommendation into a priced condition, a subjectivity or a documented decision to accept the hazard.
atoms.lesson: A recommendation sitting unactioned in a file is worse than no survey, because it evidences a known hazard with no response. High-value recommendations such as sprinkler upgrades, electrical infrared findings, missing hot-work permits, blocked exits and unmaintained fire pumps should become policy subjectivities with completion dates, protective safeguard warranties, or an explicit written acceptance carrying a rate or deductible load.

atoms.obligation: Set the deductible and any percentage wind or hail deductible against the risk's own loss history and volatility.
atoms.lesson: Deductibles are both a pricing tool and a behaviour tool. Attritional losses such as minor water damage and small hail should sit with an insured whose schedule generates them, while a catastrophe-exposed single location needs a percentage deductible sized so the insured retains real exposure. Consider aggregate deductibles on large schedules with frequency, and check whether a percentage deductible applies per building or per occurrence.

name: catastrophe-accumulation-control
description: Monitors and manages aggregate exposure by peril and geography against appetite and the reinsurance structure. Use when a large risk would concentrate exposure in a zone, when zonal limits are nearly full, when preparing exposure data for reinsurers, or when quoting inside a capacity-constrained territory.
expansions: this risk pushes us over the coastal limit
how much do we have in this county
quake aggregate for the bay area book
prepare exposure data for the treaty renewal
declining a risk on accumulation grounds
wildfire concentration in this postcode
modelled loss versus our retention
tracking aggregate for a named windstorm zone

atoms.obligation: Check the aggregate impact of a risk in its accumulation zone before quoting it, not after it binds.
atoms.lesson: Accumulation control only works upstream. Once a policy binds the exposure sits on the book until renewal, and a portfolio that quietly fills its coastal zone in the second quarter has no capacity for the profitable business arriving in the third. Zone definitions must match how the reinsurance programme and the catastrophe model define them, whether by county, zone code or distance-to-coast band, so internal limits mean something in recovery terms.

atoms.obligation: Report exposure location by location with geocoded coordinates and the construction and occupancy fields models require.
atoms.lesson: Modelled output is only as good as its input. Missing or street-level-only geocoding, unknown construction class, unknown year built, unknown storey count and blank secondary modifiers push the model to conservative defaults that distort probable maximum loss in both directions. Reinsurers price that uncertainty, so a schedule with thirty percent unknown construction pays a data quality load. Track resolution rates and fix the largest insured values first.

atoms.obligation: Compare modelled losses at the return periods that match the reinsurance attachment and exhaustion points.
atoms.lesson: A programme attaching near a one in twenty loss and exhausting near one in two hundred fifty needs the portfolio measured at exactly those points, plus a view of loss above exhaustion falling back to the balance sheet. Use occurrence exceedance probability for single-event capacity and aggregate exceedance probability for a season, and stress results for demand surge, surge inclusion and secondary uncertainty, because model versions shift materially between releases.

atoms.obligation: Track non-modelled and secondary perils as a separate aggregate rather than assuming the main model captures them.
atoms.lesson: Wildfire, severe convective storm, inland flood, freeze and hail frequently produce the worst annual result while the hurricane model absorbs attention. Some are poorly modelled or excluded from the vendor view, and many sit below the treaty attachment where they hit the retention repeatedly. Track them with exposure counts by zone, historic burn perimeters, hail swath frequency and distance-to-water flags, and set explicit appetite limits even without a probabilistic number.

name: underwriting-authority-referral
description: Applies binding authority rules and escalates risks a delegated underwriter cannot write alone. Use when a risk exceeds a limit, class or attachment inside the grant, when an exception is requested for a favoured account, when documenting a referral decision, or when auditing a binder's compliance with its authority.
expansions: risk is above my binding limit
class is not on my authority schedule
requesting an exception for a good account
document the referral decision on file
audit this binder for authority breaches
who signs off a five million limit
coverholder wrote outside the class list
backdated binder needs approval

atoms.obligation: Read authority as the intersection of limit, class, territory, attachment and coverage grant, never as one number.
atoms.lesson: Delegated authority documents constrain several dimensions simultaneously, so a risk within the limit can still breach the class list, a prohibited occupancy schedule, a maximum policy period, a minimum premium, a territorial exclusion or a ban on manuscript wordings. Breaching any single dimension can leave the business unsupported by the treaty. Check every dimension before quoting, and check again whenever terms change during negotiation.

atoms.obligation: Refer with a written recommendation and the supporting facts rather than forwarding the submission unanalysed.
atoms.lesson: A referral is a request for a decision, not a handoff of work, and the referring underwriter should already hold a view. State the risk, why it falls outside authority, the underwriting merits, the loss history, the terms proposed, the price against the technical rate, what the broker is comparing against, and the recommendation with reasons. Referrals without a recommendation take three times as long and produce worse decisions.

atoms.obligation: Record every exception granted with the approver, the date and the reason, and review exceptions as a portfolio.
atoms.lesson: Exceptions are where portfolios drift. One relaxed deductible is a judgement call; two hundred of them is an unpriced change in the book that only appears in the loss ratio eighteen months later. Capture exception type, rate impact, approver and rationale in a form that aggregates, then review quarterly for patterns concentrated in one broker, one class, one underwriter, or a systematic gap between technical and charged price.

atoms.obligation: Audit delegated business against the authority terms on a sample basis and act on breaches promptly.
atoms.lesson: Coverholder audits test whether risks written match the schedule: bound limits, classes, rates against the agreed rating basis, use of approved wordings, timely bordereau reporting and accurate premium accounting. Findings need owners and dates rather than just a report. Persistent out-of-authority writing justifies suspending the binding authority, and the carrier remains liable to the policyholder for a risk bound outside authority even while pursuing the coverholder.

name: reinsurance-treaty-structuring
description: Designs and negotiates a ceded reinsurance programme covering structure, retention, layers and contract terms. Use when planning a treaty renewal, when choosing between quota share and excess of loss, when setting a net retention the balance sheet can carry, or when evaluating reinsurer quotes and wordings.
expansions: renewal structure for the property treaty
quota share versus excess of loss here
what retention can our balance sheet carry
evaluating three reinsurer quotes
reinstatement provisions on the cat layer
sliding scale commission on the quota share
aggregate protection for frequency years
wording differences between slip and treaty

atoms.obligation: Set the net retention against capital, earnings volatility tolerance and the realistic frequency of losses at that level.
atoms.lesson: Retention trades capital efficiency against earnings stability. A retention the balance sheet absorbs once may be unacceptable if the treaty attaches where three or four events a year reach it, because retained frequency plus reinstatement premium destroys the year. Model retained loss distributions rather than single events, and test the retention against a bad but plausible sequence such as two hurricanes plus a severe convective season in one year.

atoms.obligation: Choose proportional or non-proportional structures based on the volatility profile and the capital or commission need.
atoms.lesson: Quota share cedes a fixed proportion of every risk, brings ceding commission that supports the expense ratio and surplus, and suits new or growing books with uncertain experience. Excess of loss protects against severity and catastrophe while retaining the profitable attritional layer, and costs less premium for the same peak protection. Most programmes combine them, with surplus share or facultative handling individual large risks the treaty cannot absorb.

atoms.obligation: Specify the occurrence definition, hours clause, reinstatements and territorial scope explicitly in the contract wording.
atoms.lesson: The hours clause, typically seventy-two hours for windstorm and one hundred sixty-eight for other perils, decides whether a multi-day event is one loss or several, which changes both the recovery and the number of retentions borne. Reinstatement terms determine whether the layer remains available after a first event and at what cost. Ambiguity here is where disputes live, so reconcile the broker slip against the final wording line by line.

atoms.obligation: Assess each reinsurer's security, payment behaviour and panel concentration before allocating any share of the programme.
atoms.lesson: A cheap line from a weak counterparty is a contingent asset that fails exactly when needed. Examine financial strength ratings, the reinsurer's own catastrophe concentration in the same territories, its history of paying disputed claims without argument, and collateral or trust arrangements where it is unauthorised in the ceding company's state.
