Spread the panel so no single failure creates a material recovery gap, and reassess after any major event.

name: facultative-risk-cession
description: Places an individual risk facultatively when it exceeds treaty capacity or falls outside treaty terms. Use when a single account needs capacity above the automatic programme, when an excluded class must still be written, when preparing a facultative submission, or when reconciling facultative recoveries after a large loss.
expansions: need capacity above our treaty limit
class is excluded from the treaty
prepare a facultative submission for this risk
which markets write this occupancy
certificate wording versus policy wording
recovering facultative on a large fire loss
cost of the cession makes it uneconomic
urgent placement before the bind date

atoms.obligation: Present the underwriting file completely, including the loss history and survey findings you would rather leave out.
atoms.lesson: Facultative reinsurers price on the ceding company's file, and the duty of utmost good faith means material non-disclosure can void the cession precisely when a loss occurs. Include full ten-year loss experience, survey reports with outstanding recommendations, the values basis, occupancy detail, the exact wording and endorsements, and the ceding company's own view of the risk. Reinsurers who see complete files price better over time and dispute less.

atoms.obligation: Confirm the certificate follows the underlying policy wording, or list every difference before binding the cession.
atoms.lesson: Certificates are usually written to follow the form and fortunes of the original policy, but reinsurers frequently attach their own exclusions for communicable disease, cyber, terrorism or sanctions, or impose a different territorial scope, retained line or claims control clause. Any gap is retained net, unnoticed, until a claim. Compare wordings at bind time, list every difference, and decide consciously whether to accept, price or place the gap elsewhere.

atoms.obligation: Reconcile the facultative placement against the treaty so the retained net line is what was actually intended.
atoms.lesson: Facultative cessions usually inure to the benefit of the treaty, meaning the treaty applies net of facultative, but some programmes state the opposite. Getting the order of operations wrong changes the net retention on the very risk that was reinsured for being large. Confirm the inurement language, calculate the net line after both cessions, and record the risk in the accumulation system at the correct net figure rather than gross.

atoms.obligation: Notify facultative reinsurers of a loss promptly and follow the claims cooperation terms written into the certificate.
atoms.lesson: Certificates commonly require prompt notice of any loss likely to reach the cession, and many include claims control or cooperation clauses letting the reinsurer participate in defence or settlement. Settling without the required consultation can jeopardise recovery entirely. Track which facultative placements attach to which policy so notice goes out when the reserve moves rather than when the payment is finally made.

name: loss-run-experience-analysis
description: Reads an account's loss runs to judge experience, credibility and pricing adequacy at renewal or new business. Use when a broker sends several years of loss runs, when developing incurred losses to ultimate, when an experience modification is disputed, or when explaining a rate increase from the account's own history.
expansions: five years of loss runs from the broker
loss ratio looks fine until you develop it
one shock loss distorting the whole picture
explain the rate increase to the account
open reserves look understated on this run
frequency trend in the last two years
experience modification calculation seems wrong
compare loss runs from two prior carriers

atoms.obligation: Develop incurred losses to ultimate before comparing experience against premium, especially on long-tail lines.
atoms.lesson: A loss run valued three months after policy expiry shows a fraction of what a liability or compensation year will finally cost. Apply development factors suited to the line and the valuation age, since auto liability and workers compensation still develop meaningfully at thirty-six and sixty months while property is largely settled at twelve. An undeveloped forty-five percent casualty loss ratio can become seventy-five percent at ultimate, changing the renewal decision entirely.

atoms.obligation: Separate frequency from severity and treat a single shock loss differently from a pattern of small repeated losses.
atoms.lesson: Frequency reflects operations and controls such as driver behaviour, housekeeping, maintenance and training, and generally repeats. Severity is partly luck and partly exposure. A schedule producing fifteen small claims a year has a management problem pricing alone will not solve, while one two million dollar loss on an otherwise clean account may be excludable or may reveal an unmanaged hazard. Cap the shock loss for trending, then consider it separately.

atoms.obligation: Verify that the loss runs cover every prior carrier and every year requested before drawing any conclusion.
atoms.lesson: Missing years are rarely accidental, and a broker supplying four of five requested years or omitting one carrier across mid-term rewrites is usually hiding the bad year. Check that each run is on carrier letterhead, valued within the last ninety days, states the policy period and valuation date, shows open and closed claims separately with paid and reserve columns, and reconciles claim counts across successive valuations of the same year.

atoms.obligation: Challenge open case reserves that look inconsistent with the described injury or damage before relying on the totals.
atoms.lesson: Prior carriers reserve to their own philosophy and to whatever they knew when the file went quiet. An open back injury with a surgical recommendation carried at fifteen thousand is understated, while a functionally closed file still showing a forty thousand reserve is stale. Request claim-level detail above a materiality threshold, note how many claims are open and how old they are, and price for the development a thin prior reserve implies.

name: rate-adequacy-and-filing
description: Builds and defends a rate indication and the narrative supporting a filing. Use when preparing a rate change, when a regulator objects to a filing assumption, when explaining the gap between indicated and selected rate, or when checking whether current rates still cover trend, catastrophe load and expense.
expansions: indication says plus fourteen we filed plus eight
regulator objected to our trend selection
build the rate indication for homeowners
loss trend versus premium trend gap
expense provision in the rate calculation
capping increases at renewal for disruption
territory relativities need updating
justify the catastrophe load in the filing

atoms.obligation: Build the indication from developed and trended losses against on-level earned premium, and state every selection made.
atoms.lesson: The standard indication brings historical losses to ultimate with development factors, trends them to the average date of loss in the future policy period, compares them against premium adjusted to current rate level by parallelogram or extension of exposures, then adds provisions for expense, catastrophe and profit. Every step involves a judgement selection, and filings fail objection when the arithmetic is right but the selections are unexplained.

atoms.obligation: Separate the catastrophe and large-loss provision from attritional experience rather than averaging all years together.
atoms.lesson: Twenty years of hurricane experience compressed into a five-year rate review either overstates or understates the load depending on which years fall in the window, because catastrophe losses are not a stable average of recent history. Use a modelled average annual loss for modelled perils and an excess factor for non-catastrophe large claims above a threshold, then remove those actual losses from the attritional data so nothing is counted twice.

atoms.obligation: Explain the gap between the indicated and the selected change and state how the shortfall will be recovered.
atoms.lesson: Regulators and management both accept selecting below indication for disruption, competitive or affordability reasons, but expect documented reasoning and a stated plan: a multi-year path, a capping structure limiting any individual policyholder increase, or an offsetting change in deductibles or eligibility. Undocumented selection below indication compounds, because next year's indication grows and the carrier eventually needs a change large enough to be politically impossible.

atoms.obligation: Check that each rating variable and its relativities are permitted in the filing state before including them.
atoms.lesson: States differ sharply on credit-based insurance scores, prior insurance and coverage gaps, occupation and education, gender, territory definitions and price optimisation, with several prohibiting some outright and others requiring specific disclosure. A model that improves fit but relies on a prohibited or heavily scrutinised variable will not be approved and may attract a market conduct review. Confirm the state position and show the relativity is supported by loss experience rather than elasticity.

name: life-underwriting-medical-review
description: Assesses mortality and morbidity risk on an individual life or disability application. Use when an application discloses medical history, when laboratory results or attending physician records return with findings, when assigning a rating class or substandard table, or when choosing between postponement, exclusion rider and decline.
expansions: applicant disclosed treated hypertension and apnoea
labs came back with elevated liver enzymes
physician statement mentions a prior cardiac event
preferred or standard class for this file
family history of early onset cancer
applicant flies a private aircraft
build to weight ratio outside guidelines
postpone until after the scheduled biopsy

atoms.obligation: Assess each impairment against its own mortality debit table and combine debits and credits into one class.
atoms.lesson: Underwriting manuals express risk as debits and credits: points added for blood pressure above a treated threshold, for body mass index outside a band, or for smoking history, and credits for favourable cholesterol ratios, normal stress testing or sustained control. The combined score maps to preferred, standard or a substandard table with a percentage load. Combining without checking for correlated impairments such as obesity with apnoea and diabetes understates aggregate mortality.

atoms.obligation: Order additional medical evidence only where it can plausibly change the decision, and weigh the delay it causes.
atoms.lesson: An attending physician statement can take weeks and often costs more than the first-year premium, so it belongs where the disclosed history is material and unresolved, such as a recent cardiac event, an abnormal imaging finding or a cancer inside the surveillance window. Routine requisitions on clean applications destroy placement rates because applicants abandon the process. Where a test is imminent, postponement usually beats rating on an unknown.

atoms.obligation: Separate mortality risk from non-medical risk and rate avocation, occupation and travel exposure appropriately.
atoms.lesson: Private aviation, technical diving, motorsport, climbing and certain occupations carry a flat extra per thousand of coverage rather than a table rating, because the hazard is accidental and does not increase with duration. Foreign travel and residence raise both mortality and claim verification difficulty. Aviation and hazardous sport exclusion riders are an alternative where permitted, and the choice between flat extra and exclusion belongs to the applicant with clear disclosure.

atoms.obligation: Check the financial and insurable interest justification for the amount applied for, not only the medical picture.
atoms.lesson: The amount at risk must bear a rational relationship to income, net worth, business value or the loss the beneficiary would genuinely suffer, using earnings multiples that decline with age. Applications far above justification, particularly with unusual ownership, recent stacking of policies across carriers, or a non-family beneficiary, raise anti-selection and stranger-originated concerns. Verify inforce and applied-for amounts across the market and require documentation above the non-financial limit.

name: submission-clearance-triage
description: Clears, triages and responds to incoming broker submissions so underwriting effort goes to business the carrier actually wants. Use when a submission arrives, when two brokers submit the same account, when deciding to quote or decline, or when writing a declination that preserves the broker relationship.
expansions: two brokers submitted the same account
clear this submission against our records
worth quoting or decline politely
submission missing half the underwriting information
broker of record letter arrived mid quote
declination letter for an out of appetite risk
prioritise today's submission queue
incumbent terms attached to the submission

atoms.obligation: Clear the account against open submissions and inforce records before any underwriter begins work on it.
atoms.lesson: Clearance matches named insured, trading names, addresses and identifiers against open submissions, quotes and inforce policies to catch the same account arriving through two brokers. Working a duplicate wastes underwriting time, produces two different prices for one risk, and damages the relationship with whichever broker loses. The first broker with a complete submission normally holds it, and only the insured's own broker of record instruction overrides that.

atoms.obligation: Screen the submission against written appetite and decline out-of-appetite risks the same day rather than sitting on them.
atoms.lesson: Brokers ration submissions by response speed as much as by price, so a fast clear decline preserves the flow of business you do want, while a submission that dies silently teaches the broker to send good risks elsewhere. Screen against class, size, territory, loss history, capacity and any prohibited occupancy list, and say plainly what would have made the risk workable, such as a different attachment or three cleaner years.

atoms.obligation: Ask for the complete information set once, in a single prioritised request, rather than in successive rounds.
atoms.lesson: Incomplete submissions are the normal case: missing loss runs, unsigned applications, no schedule of values, no driver list, no supplemental for a hazardous operation. Each round trip through a broker costs days. Send one consolidated list separating what is needed to quote from what is needed to bind, so the underwriter can indicate on partial information and hold the rest as a subjectivity, and state when the file will be closed.

atoms.obligation: Read the incumbent's expiring terms as information about the risk rather than as a target to undercut.
atoms.lesson: The expiring programme reveals what another underwriter concluded: the deductible chosen, exclusions attached, sublimits imposed, a protective safeguards warranty, a rate that rose sharply. A large increase from an incumbent who knows the account is usually a signal rather than an opportunity. Ask why the account is moving, whether a mid-term cancellation or non-renewal notice is involved, and whether open claims are missing from the loss runs.

name: policy-wording-drafting
description: Drafts and reviews manuscript wordings, endorsements and sublimits so the intent survives a claim. Use when a broker requests a bespoke clause, when tailoring a standard form to a specific exposure, when an endorsement conflicts with the base policy, or when reviewing wording after a coverage dispute exposed an ambiguity.
expansions: broker wants a manuscript cyber endorsement
this endorsement contradicts the base form
sublimit wording is ambiguous on aggregate
add a protective safeguards warranty
define the insured location for this schedule
review wording after the last coverage dispute
carve back to the pollution exclusion
named perils versus all risks wording change

atoms.obligation: Define every operative term you introduce and check the definition against how that term is used elsewhere.
atoms.lesson: Coverage disputes concentrate in undefined or inconsistently used words such as occurrence, damages, property damage, employee, insured location, computer system and period of restoration. A bespoke endorsement introducing an undefined term invites the rule construing ambiguity against the drafter, applied in almost every jurisdiction. Where a defined term already exists in the base form, either use it as defined or state expressly that the endorsement replaces that definition for its own purposes.

atoms.obligation: State how each endorsement interacts with the base form: whether it replaces, adds to, or sits excess of existing coverage.
atoms.lesson: An endorsement is read together with the policy, and silence about precedence creates conflicts a court resolves in the insured's favour. Say explicitly which provisions are amended and which are unchanged, whether a sublimit is part of or in addition to the policy limit, whether it erodes the aggregate, whether the deductible applies before or after the sublimit, and whether the endorsement's exclusions supplement or replace the base exclusions.

atoms.obligation: Write exclusions together with their carve-backs in the same clause and test both against expected loss scenarios.
atoms.lesson: An exclusion that swallows intended coverage is as damaging as one drawn too narrowly. Take three or four realistic loss scenarios for the account and read the clause against each: does the pollution exclusion with a hostile fire carve-back still cover a fuel spill from a covered collision, does the cyber exclusion still permit resulting fire damage, does the faulty workmanship exclusion preserve resultant damage. Wording never tested against a scenario has not been reviewed.

atoms.obligation: Confirm any bespoke wording is permitted by the reinsurance programme and by the filing rules of the state.
atoms.lesson: Treaties commonly restrict manuscript wordings, non-standard forms and coverage broader than the standard market, and writing outside those terms can leave the ceded protection unavailable when it matters. Separately, admitted business generally requires forms filed and approved with the state while surplus lines business is freer. Check both before promising a broker a clause, and log the wording so it can be aggregated, reviewed after losses and reconciled at renewal.

name: complaint-and-conduct-response
description: Responds to a regulator complaint, a market conduct inquiry or a formal grievance about claim handling. Use when an insurance department forwards a policyholder complaint with a deadline, when a pattern of similar complaints appears, when preparing a data call response, or when auditing closed files for handling compliance.
expansions: department forwarded a complaint with a deadline
policyholder says we delayed their claim
market conduct examination notice arrived
third complaint about the same adjuster
prepare the file chronology for the regulator
data call on claim cycle times
audit closed files for handling compliance
respond to an agent complaint about a denial

atoms.obligation: Answer the regulator by the stated deadline with a factual chronology, the policy basis and the documents relied on.
atoms.lesson: Departments typically require a substantive response within fifteen to twenty-one days of forwarding a complaint and treat a missed deadline as a separate violation regardless of merits. Build the response as a dated chronology of contacts, inspections, payments and letters, tie the decision to quoted policy language, attach the letters actually sent, and answer the complainant's specific grievance rather than restating the whole file. State facts, never argue.

atoms.obligation: Review the underlying handling honestly and correct any error before defending the position that was taken.
atoms.lesson: A large share of forwarded complaints reveal a genuine handling problem: a missed callback, an unexplained delay, a payment issued to the wrong party, depreciation applied without explanation. Fixing it and saying so closes the complaint faster and reduces the chance of a market conduct follow-up more than an eloquent defence of an indefensible file. Where the position was right but communication was poor, say so and re-explain the decision directly.

atoms.obligation: Read complaints as a portfolio and look for the pattern behind repeated grievances of the same type.
atoms.lesson: Individual complaints are noise, but three about the same adjuster, vendor, endorsement or automated decision are a finding. Categorise by cause such as delay, denial, unsatisfactory offer or unsatisfactory service, and by product, state and handler, then compare the complaint ratio against premium volume since regulators publish and rank those ratios. Patterns fixed before an examination cost far less than patterns discovered during one.

atoms.obligation: Prepare for a conduct examination by testing your own files against the standards the examiners will apply.
atoms.lesson: Examiners sample files and test timeliness of acknowledgement, investigation, coverage decision and payment; accuracy of settlement calculations; documentation of denials with policy citations; correct application of deductibles and depreciation; interest paid on late payments; and use of licensed adjusters. Run the same tests internally on a random sample using the state's own standards as the checklist, because self-identified and corrected errors are treated far more leniently.

name: hs-code-classification
description: Assigns goods to the correct tariff code and writes down the reasoning so it survives an audit or a customs challenge. Use it when a new SKU needs a code before its first import, when a broker's proposed classification looks wrong, when a customs authority issues a rate-advance or classification notice, or when someone simply asks what code a product falls under.
expansions: new sku needs a tariff code
broker classified this as a toy
customs disputed our hs code
rate advance notice on an entry
what code for a lithium power bank
classify a kit of mixed parts
duty rate looks far too high
prepare a binding ruling request

atoms.obligation: Apply the general interpretive rules in strict order rather than matching a marketing description to a heading that sounds right.
atoms.lesson: Rule 1 governs: the heading texts and the section and chapter notes decide first, and legal notes routinely exclude goods the words appear to cover. Only when a good is prima facie classifiable under two headings do you reach Rule 3, and only there does essential character matter. Jumping straight to essential character because an assortment feels like a set is the single most common finding in classification audits.

atoms.obligation: Record the physical characteristics, materials, function and condition as imported that drove the code, with a source for every fact.
atoms.lesson: A code is only defensible with the evidence behind it: bill of materials with percentage composition, engineering drawings, the technical datasheet, photographs of the retail packing, and lab results where composition decides the heading. Condition as imported matters most - an unassembled machine shipped complete is classified as the machine, while the same parts shipped separately over months are not. File the reasoning with the part master, not in an email thread.

atoms.obligation: Check published rulings and explanatory notes on the same or similar goods before settling on a code.
atoms.lesson: Customs authorities publish their own decisions: the US CROSS database, EU binding tariff information, and national ruling libraries. The World Customs Organization explanatory notes and classification opinions carry weight everywhere the harmonized system is used. If an authority has already ruled that a similar article sits in a particular heading, declaring differently invites a penalty for lack of reasonable care. Where the answer is genuinely ambiguous and the volume is large, request a binding ruling before the first shipment.

atoms.obligation: Flag when a code choice changes duty rate, quota, licensing or trade remedy exposure, and quantify the difference in money.
atoms.lesson: Classification decides far more than the base duty. The same product can fall inside or outside an antidumping order scope, attract a punitive tariff line, trigger a quota, or flag a partner agency requirement such as food, radio or safety approval. National statistical suffixes beyond the six-digit international code carry those flags. Model annual duty at each candidate code and state the exposure if the aggressive code is later overturned with interest and penalties.

name: customs-entry-audit
description: Reviews import declarations before they are filed and reconciles filed entries afterwards against commercial records. Use it when a broker sends a draft entry for approval, when duty paid does not match the commercial invoice, when post-entry corrections are piling up, or when preparing a periodic review of what was declared in your name.
expansions: broker sent a draft entry to approve
duty paid does not match the invoice
entry summary needs a correction
wrong country of origin declared
reconcile entries against purchase orders
importer of record looks wrong
we missed a partner agency flag
monthly entry review before duty payment

atoms.obligation: Verify that the importer of record, ultimate consignee and entry type match the actual commercial transaction and its terms.
atoms.lesson: The importer of record carries the legal liability and the recordkeeping duty, so a mismatch is not clerical. A delivered duty paid sale where the foreign seller has no resident presence leaves nobody properly liable, and brokers often paper over it with the buyer's identifier. Entry type also matters: consumption, warehouse, foreign trade zone and temporary import bond entries carry different duty timing and different exit obligations, and choosing the wrong one is expensive to unwind later.

atoms.obligation: Reconcile declared value, quantity, weight and origin line by line against the commercial invoice and packing list.
atoms.lesson: Brokers key from whatever document reached them first, so short shipments, free-of-charge samples, tooling amortisation and separately invoiced freight routinely land in the wrong field. Check that assists and royalties are included where required and that inland freight in the exporting country is treated per the destination rules. Origin is the field most often copied from the shipper's address rather than the place of manufacture, which quietly misstates preference claims and trade remedy exposure.

atoms.obligation: Confirm every partner government agency requirement is answered before release rather than after the shipment is held.
atoms.lesson: Food, drug, cosmetic, radio, vehicle, plant, wildlife and consumer safety agencies each attach data requirements to specific tariff lines. Missing a prior notice, an establishment registration, a radio equipment declaration or a plant health certificate turns a routine release into days of terminal storage and demurrage. Build the required dataset into the part master so the broker receives it with the shipping instruction, and confirm the agency has actually issued may-proceed before booking the delivery appointment.

atoms.obligation: Correct discovered errors through the formal amendment route and keep a record of what changed and why.
atoms.lesson: Errors do not disappear if the goods have cleared. Most regimes provide a short window for a straightforward correction of the entry summary, a longer window for a protest of a liquidated decision, and a voluntary disclosure route that caps penalties when the error is systemic. Choosing disclosure before the authority opens an inquiry is what preserves the reduced penalty. Keep the underlying documents for the statutory retention period, commonly five years from entry.

name: incoterms-selection
description: Chooses the delivery term for a quotation, purchase order or supply contract and spells out exactly who does what, where risk passes and who pays which leg. Trigger it when negotiating a new supply agreement, when a supplier quotes CIF and you would rather buy FOB, when an insurance gap surfaces after a loss, or when a contract draft needs its delivery clause written.
expansions: supplier quoted cif we want fob
who pays for the ocean leg
risk transfer point unclear after a loss
new contract needs a delivery term
ddp quote for a german customer
which term for containerised cargo
insurance gap on a damaged pallet
ex works but we handle export clearance

atoms.obligation: Match the term to the mode of transport and never use a shipboard term for containerised cargo.
atoms.lesson: The shipboard terms assume the seller controls the goods until loading, which fits bulk and breakbulk. A container is handed to the carrier at a terminal days before loading, so under a shipboard term the seller keeps risk while the box sits in a stack it cannot touch - a real loss when a terminal fire strikes before loading. The multimodal carriage terms pass risk at handover instead. Incoterms 2020 added an on-board bill of lading option under FCA precisely to close the letter of credit objection.

atoms.obligation: State the risk transfer point and the cost transfer point separately, because under several terms they are not the same place.
atoms.lesson: Under the cost-and-freight family the seller pays carriage to the destination port but risk passes at origin, so a loss in mid-ocean is the buyer's even though the seller booked and paid the ship. Contracts that say only delivered destination invite an argument after every casualty. Write both points into the clause in plain words, and say who must claim against the carrier and who holds the insurable interest at each stage.

atoms.obligation: Name the delivery place with street-level precision and cite the Incoterms version year in the contract.
atoms.lesson: A term without a named place is not a term. Delivered at place at a customer plant is a different obligation from delivered at the nearest terminal, and unloading responsibility differs between the two delivered variants. Ambiguity shows up as an argument over a crane, a forklift or two hours of detention. Citing the rules year matters because 2010 and 2020 differ on the insurance level required under CIP and on carrier-arranged own transport.

atoms.obligation: Assign export and import clearance duties explicitly and confirm the named party can lawfully act in that country.
atoms.lesson: Ex works leaves the buyer responsible for export clearance in a country where it may have no legal standing to file, and delivered duty paid leaves the seller importing into a country where it may need local tax registration and a resident representative. Both fail quietly until the first shipment. Check whether the destination allows a non-resident importer, whether local consumption tax can be recovered by that party, and who will hold the customs records for the retention period.

name: dangerous-goods-paperwork
description: Prepares and checks dangerous goods declarations, marks and packaging for air, sea and road movements. Trigger it when a shipment contains lithium batteries, aerosols, paints, solvents or magnets, when an airline or forwarder rejects a declaration, when a driver needs road transport documents, or when someone asks whether a product can move by a given mode at all.
expansions: airline rejected our dg declaration
shipping lithium batteries by air
need a dangerous goods note for a container
forwarder wants the safety data sheet
aerosols on a consolidated pallet
un number and packing group unclear
limited quantity or fully regulated
driver needs road transport paperwork

atoms.obligation: Determine the UN number, proper shipping name, class and packing group from the safety data sheet before quoting or booking.
atoms.lesson: Section 14 of the safety data sheet gives the transport classification, but it is often written for one mode only and sometimes left blank by a supplier who never ships internationally. Flash point, corrosivity and the presence of subsidiary risks drive packing group, and packing group drives permitted packaging and quantity. Never take a classification from a purchase description: paint, adhesive and battery are commercial words that map to several UN numbers with very different limits.

atoms.obligation: Confirm the packing instruction, quantity limits per package and whether the chosen mode permits the substance at all.
atoms.lesson: Air rules are the tightest and forbid outright a set of substances that move freely by sea or road. Lithium batteries are the everyday case: state of charge capped around thirty percent for cells shipped alone by air, different instructions for cells alone, cells packed with equipment and cells inside equipment, and passenger aircraft forbidden for several of them. Limited quantity and excepted quantity provisions cut paperwork but impose their own inner receptacle sizes and marks.

atoms.obligation: Ensure the marks, labels, orientation arrows and any overpack statement on the package match the declaration exactly.
atoms.lesson: Inspectors compare the box to the paper. A declaration listing three packages against two visible, a missing orientation arrow on a liquid, an old-format lithium mark, or an overpack without the word overpack and the repeated marks will hold the freight at the acceptance counter. Packaging must carry a valid UN specification mark and be within its periodic retest date for pressure receptacles. Segregation rules also apply inside a container, so incompatible classes cannot simply share a pallet.

atoms.obligation: Verify the person signing holds current training for that mode and keep the signed declaration on file for the retention period.
atoms.lesson: Signing a dangerous goods declaration is a personal legal act. Air requires formal recurrent training on a fixed cycle, sea requires documented function-specific training, and European road movements require access to a qualified safety adviser. Airlines check the certificate reference on the paperwork. Retain the declaration, the packing certificate and the training records - typically two years for air and sea - because they are the first documents requested after an incident.

name: demurrage-detention-dispute
description: Builds and files disputes against ocean demurrage, detention and per diem invoices, and negotiates the write-off. Use it when a carrier bills a large storage or per diem amount, when a chassis shortage, terminal closure or customs exam caused the delay, when free time appears to have been counted from the wrong date, or when a dispute deadline is approaching.
expansions: carrier billed forty thousand in demurrage
terminal was closed on those days
free time counted from the wrong date
no chassis available for pickup
per diem on containers we already returned
dispute a detention invoice
rail ramp congestion delayed pickup
customs exam caused the storage charge

atoms.obligation: Rebuild the free time clock from documented milestones instead of accepting the carrier's day count.
atoms.lesson: Free time normally starts from discharge or from the date the container is made available, not from vessel arrival, and weekends and terminal holidays may or may not count depending on the tariff. Pull the discharge date, the availability posting, the last free day shown on the terminal system, the customs release timestamp and the actual gate-out. A one-day error at the start compounds across every container on the bill, and carriers rarely recalculate unless shown the timeline.

atoms.obligation: Gather evidence that the container could not actually be retrieved or returned during the days being billed.
atoms.lesson: The strongest disputes are made of screenshots: no appointments offered for that terminal on those dates, gate rejections, a chassis shortage notice, a rail ramp embargo, an empty return restriction naming that container line and depot, or a terminal closure bulletin. Save them at the time, because portals overwrite availability daily and the evidence is gone within a week. Trucker gate receipts showing a turned-away move are worth more than an email describing one.

atoms.obligation: Cite the contractual free time and argue that a charge which could not change behaviour is not a valid incentive.
atoms.lesson: Regulators have converged on the principle that these charges exist to encourage cargo velocity, so billing for days when pickup or return was impossible is not defensible. In the US the rules also require the invoice to carry specified elements - dates, the basis of the charge, the free time allowance, and a dispute contact - and to reach the billed party within a set window, with a minimum period allowed to dispute. A non-conforming invoice is itself grounds to seek elimination of the charge.

atoms.obligation: Escalate on a fixed schedule and protect the deadline for a formal complaint while continuing to negotiate.
atoms.lesson: Carrier dispute queues absorb claims silently. Set a first response deadline of about ten business days, then escalate to the account manager and then to the trade director, restating the same evidence pack rather than a new argument each time. Keep the container release moving separately, paying under written protest where the cargo would otherwise sit, and note the statutory window for filing a complaint with the regulator so leverage does not lapse while emails circulate.

name: freight-rate-benchmark
description: Compares rates actually paid against market indices and comparable lanes to show where the network is overpaying. Trigger it at budget season, when a carrier files a general rate increase, when cost per container or per mile jumps on a lane, or when someone asks whether a quoted rate is market.
expansions: are we paying market on this lane
carrier announced a general rate increase
cost per container jumped this quarter
build budget rates for next year
compare spot against contract rates
benchmark our truckload cost per mile
bunker surcharge looks inflated
justify a rate reduction ask

atoms.obligation: Normalise every rate to an all-in comparable basis before comparing anything to anything else.
atoms.lesson: A headline ocean rate can exclude terminal handling at both ends, bunker adjustment, low sulphur surcharge, peak season surcharge, congestion surcharge and destination delivery order fees, which together often exceed the base. Road rates split between linehaul, fuel and accessorials. Convert to cost per loaded container or per shipped unit door to door, state the unit clearly, and rebuild the same structure for the benchmark. Comparing an all-in quote to a base-only index is the classic error that produces a false saving.

atoms.obligation: Choose an index that matches the actual lane, equipment type and contract structure being examined.
atoms.lesson: Container indices differ by port pair and by whether they track spot or contract; a headline transpacific index tracks a west coast base port and will mislead for an inland point intermodal move to the midwest. Road indices split dry van, reefer and flatbed and split contract from spot, and the spot series moves months ahead of the contract series. Reefer, out-of-gauge and hazardous cargo rarely have a usable public index, so peer lanes and prior awards are the better reference.

atoms.obligation: Separate rate movement from volume, mix and fuel movement when explaining a change in freight cost.
atoms.lesson: A rising cost per unit often has nothing to do with rates. Smaller average order size, a shift from full container loads to consolidation, a new customer in an expensive zone, or a swing from sea to air to protect a launch will each move the average while unit rates hold. Build a simple bridge: prior cost, then the effect of volume, then mix, then fuel index, then residual rate. Only the residual belongs in a carrier conversation.

atoms.obligation: Time the negotiation to contract season and capacity signals rather than to the arrival of a painful invoice.
atoms.lesson: Ocean contract cycles concentrate around fixed annual dates by trade, and going to market off-cycle exposes you to spot. Road markets turn on tender rejection rates and load-to-truck ratios, which lead price by roughly a quarter. Ask for reductions when capacity is loosening and lock length when it is tightening. Bring a data pack that shows your freight is attractive - consistent volume, low dwell, clean detention record - because carriers price predictability as much as distance.

name: carrier-tender-management
description: Runs a freight procurement event end to end: bid package, lane list, evaluation and award. Trigger it for an annual road bid, at ocean contract season, when replacing an underperforming carrier or adding a logistics provider, or when an incumbent demands a mid-term increase and you need a market test.
expansions: annual truckload bid package
ocean contract season is starting
build the lane list for the rfp
evaluate carrier bid responses
award lanes across three carriers
onboard a new logistics provider
incumbent wants a mid year increase
set minimum volume commitments

atoms.obligation: Publish verified lane volumes and shipment characteristics so carriers price the freight that actually exists.
atoms.lesson: A lane list needs origin and destination at postcode-prefix level, annual loads, weekly seasonality, average weight and cube, live load or drop trailer, expected dwell at each end, appointment rules and any accessorial history. Carriers bid a risk premium against vague data, and then reprice or reject tenders once reality appears. Purging cancelled orders and one-off moves from history matters, because a phantom lane wins a cheap bid nobody can serve.

atoms.obligation: Score bids on total landed cost and demonstrated service capability rather than on the lowest linehaul number.
atoms.lesson: Build the score from rate plus expected accessorials plus the cost of failure. Weight tender acceptance history, on-time pickup and delivery, claims ratio, safety scores, insurance limits, equipment availability in the origin market and financial stability. A carrier five percent cheaper that rejects a fifth of tenders costs more once spot coverage is included. Ask for the operating plan on your top lanes, not just a price sheet.

atoms.obligation: Award every meaningful lane with a ranked backup and publish the routing guide order that follows.
atoms.lesson: Single sourcing a lane looks cheapest until the primary rejects during peak. Award primary, secondary and tertiary positions with the price each will honour, define the tender lead time that triggers the next position, and set the point at which the lane goes to spot. Review rejection rates monthly and demote carriers that lean on the backup, because a routing guide that is not enforced degrades into spot pricing within one season.

atoms.obligation: Fix the commercial terms that determine what is actually paid: accessorial schedule, fuel basis, validity and volume commitments.
atoms.lesson: The rate is a fraction of the contract. Pin the fuel table to a published index with a stated base and a stated step, or fuel becomes an uncapped variable. Define every accessorial with a unit, a free allowance and an evidence requirement. Set rate validity dates and the notice period for change. In ocean contracts, name the minimum quantity commitment and read the dead freight and equipment guarantee clauses - they bind both directions and are enforced.

name: bill-of-lading-amendment
description: Handles corrections and reissues of bills of lading, waybills and cargo manifests. Trigger it when a consignee or notify party is wrong, when declared weight or description does not match the entry, when a switch bill or telex release is requested, or when originals have gone missing and cargo needs releasing.
expansions: consignee name misspelled on the bill
need a switch bill of lading
manifest correction before arrival
weight declared wrong on the bill
original bills lost in the post
telex release for the consignee
amend the notify party details
shipper wants to change destination

atoms.obligation: Amend before the destination manifest cutoff, because corrections after filing carry penalties and holds.
atoms.lesson: Advance manifest regimes bind well before arrival: cargo details filed a day before loading at origin, security filings due in advance of that, and European entry summary declarations timed to the voyage. After the filing, the change becomes a formal manifest amendment with a fee and, in several jurisdictions, a fixed penalty per correction, plus a strong chance the container is flagged for examination. Getting the change to the carrier before the documentation cutoff turns a penalty into a keystroke.

atoms.obligation: Account for every original bill in circulation before issuing a replacement or a switch set.
atoms.lesson: A negotiable bill is a document of title, normally issued in a set of three originals, any one of which can claim the cargo. Reissuing without collecting the outstanding set creates two valid claims on one container. Where originals are lost, carriers release against a bank-countersigned letter of indemnity, often for a multiple of cargo value. Switch bills raise the same exposure plus a fraud risk, so only switch against surrender of the first set and with the carrier's written agreement.

atoms.obligation: Keep verified gross mass, package count and cargo description consistent across booking, weight declaration, bill and customs entry.
atoms.lesson: The container weight declared under the international weight verification rule must reach the carrier before the loading cutoff or the box is not loaded, and it must reconcile with the bill and the entry. Mismatched piece counts between the bill, the packing list and the entry are a classic examination trigger and complicate any later claim, because the bill is the evidence of what the carrier received. Fix the source document rather than patching each downstream copy.

atoms.obligation: Obtain written carrier confirmation of any amendment and recheck every downstream document that quotes the bill.
atoms.lesson: A verbal agreement at the counter does not amend a title document. Get the corrected copy, then trace the reference through the customs entry, the insurance certificate, the letter of credit presentation, the delivery order and the arrival notice, because each was built from the earlier version. Where a credit is involved, a corrected bill can breach a presentation deadline, so check the credit calendar before requesting a reissue.

name: letter-of-credit-documents
description: Prepares and checks the document set presented under a documentary credit so the bank pays instead of refusing. Trigger it when a credit arrives for review before shipment, when a bank raises discrepancies on a presentation, when the invoice wording does not match the credit, or when a presentation deadline is close.
expansions: bank flagged discrepancies on our presentation
review the credit before we ship
invoice description differs from the credit
late presentation after the shipment date
need a clean on board bill
amend credit terms with the buyer
insurance certificate percentage is wrong
documents due in five days

atoms.obligation: Read the credit's own terms first and build the document checklist from its text before drafting anything.
atoms.lesson: The credit is the contract for payment and overrides what the sales agreement says. Extract the required documents and copies, the latest shipment date, the expiry date and place, the presentation period after shipment, the permitted ports, and every special condition buried in the free-text field. Where no presentation period is stated the default is twenty-one days after shipment, and it still cannot run past expiry. Build the checklist once, and have the person who packs the shipment work from the same list.

atoms.obligation: Make the goods description on the commercial invoice mirror the credit exactly, while other documents may carry a general description.
atoms.lesson: Banks examine on their face against the credit wording. The invoice must correspond with the description in the credit - including spelling, model numbers and the incoterm and named place - while transport and insurance documents may use a general description not in conflict with it. Amounts, unit prices and quantity tolerances must obey the stated tolerance words. An invoice that adds an unrequested line, such as a separate freight charge under a term where freight is included, creates a discrepancy on its own.

atoms.obligation: Check dates, ports, partial shipment and transhipment permissions against the transport document exactly as issued.
atoms.lesson: The on-board date on the bill is the shipment date, not the booking date, and a dated on-board notation on a received-for-shipment bill overrides the issue date. Where the credit forbids transhipment, a bill that reserves the carrier's right to tranship can still be acceptable for container carriage under the rules, but a routing that names a relay port will not be. Confirm the port of loading and discharge match the credit's named ports, not the terminal names the carrier prints.

atoms.obligation: Resolve any conflict between the credit and reality by amendment before shipping, not by asking for a waiver afterwards.
atoms.lesson: Once documents are discrepant the buyer holds the decision, and in a falling market that becomes a price renegotiation. Amendments need issuing bank and beneficiary agreement and take days, so review the credit within forty-eight hours of receipt and raise every impossible term at once: unachievable shipment dates, documents only the buyer can issue, inspection certificates signed by a named individual, or a required vessel age. Refusing a credit you cannot perform is cheaper than presenting into it.

name: preferential-origin-qualification
description: Determines whether goods qualify for preferential duty under a trade agreement and builds the file that proves it. Trigger it when a customer requests an origin certification, when supplier declarations are missing, when a customs verification letter arrives, or when someone asks whether a part can be claimed duty free under an agreement.
expansions: customer wants an origin certification
supplier declaration missing for preference
does this part meet the tariff shift
regional value content calculation
claim preference retroactively
verification letter from customs
origin rules for a new supplier
origin versus country of manufacture

atoms.obligation: Apply the agreement's product specific rule for the finished good's own tariff code rather than a general origin assumption.
atoms.lesson: Preference is decided rule by rule. Some products qualify by a change of tariff classification at chapter, heading or subheading level for every non-originating input; others require a minimum regional value content computed either on transaction value or on net cost; others demand a specific process such as spinning or chemical reaction. Many rules combine them. A de minimis allowance, commonly around ten percent of value, forgives small non-qualifying inputs but is excluded for certain textile and agricultural lines.

atoms.obligation: Collect supplier declarations and bills of material that prove the rule was met, and refresh them on a schedule.
atoms.lesson: You cannot certify origin on a supplier's word that goods are domestic. You need the input tariff codes, values and origins behind each finished part. Long-term supplier declarations cover a stated period, typically a year, and must be renewed before they lapse; a claim made on an expired declaration is unsupported. Store them against the part and the period, because verification asks for the declaration that was valid on the date of the shipment being questioned.

atoms.obligation: Distinguish preferential origin from non-preferential origin and from country of origin marking, because they can differ for the same good.
atoms.lesson: Preferential origin decides duty under an agreement. Non-preferential origin decides marking, trade remedy scope, quotas and government procurement, and is usually judged on substantial transformation or on a separate rule list. A product can be originating under an agreement while its non-preferential origin, and therefore its marking and its antidumping exposure, remains the country where the core component was made. Answer the question actually being asked before writing any statement on a document.

atoms.obligation: Keep the qualification calculation reproducible so it can be reconstructed on the day a verification arrives.
atoms.lesson: Verification typically demands the bill of materials, costed inputs, supplier declarations, production records and the origin calculation for a period that ended years earlier, with a reply window measured in weeks. Retention obligations commonly run five years. Save the calculation as it stood, with the cost data and the exchange rates used, rather than intending to recompute later from a system that has since been repriced. A failed verification cancels preference for every shipment in the period, with interest.

name: duty-drawback-claim
description: Identifies and files refunds of import duty on goods later exported, destroyed or rejected. Trigger it when a business both imports and exports, when imported goods are returned by a customer or scrapped, when someone asks how far back a refund can reach, or when a drawback programme needs setting up.
expansions: we import and re export the same goods
customer returned imported units
claim refund on destroyed inventory
unused merchandise drawback eligibility
substitution drawback on components
how far back can we claim
proof of export for a claim
apply for drawback privileges

atoms.obligation: Establish which drawback category fits the movement before building any claim file.
atoms.lesson: Unused merchandise drawback covers imported goods exported in essentially the same condition. Manufacturing drawback covers imports consumed in production of an exported article. Rejected merchandise drawback covers goods that did not conform to specification or were shipped without consent, and allows destruction under supervision as well as export. Substitution provisions let commercially interchangeable goods stand in, generally matched at eight-digit tariff level, which is what makes drawback workable for a business that does not track individual units.

atoms.obligation: Trace each claimed unit from its import entry to its export or destruction with an auditable inventory method.
atoms.lesson: The claim must connect a specific import entry line to a specific export or destruction, directly or through an accepted accounting convention such as first in first out applied consistently. Evidence means the entry summary, the export declaration or bill of lading, and for destruction a witnessed certificate. Mixed domestic and imported stock in the same location is the usual obstacle, so agree the inventory method up front and document it, because switching methods mid-period invalidates the trail.

atoms.obligation: Respect the filing windows and the refund ceiling, including which trade remedy duties are refundable at all.
atoms.lesson: Claims generally must be filed within five years of the import date, and the refund is capped just below the full duty paid, with the balance retained as an administrative fee. Not every duty type is recoverable: certain punitive tariff programmes are refundable while national security tariffs and antidumping or countervailing duties are commonly excluded. Confirm eligibility by duty type before promising a number, because the excluded portion is often the largest part of the payment.

atoms.obligation: Apply for accelerated payment and any waiver privileges once claim volume justifies the bond and setup cost.
atoms.lesson: Without accelerated payment, refunds arrive only after the underlying entries liquidate, which can be years. The privilege requires an application, a continuous bond sized to the expected refunds, and demonstrated recordkeeping. Waiver of prior notice of intent to export removes the need to notify before each export, which otherwise makes routine shipping unworkable. Model the bond premium and the compliance effort against annual expected recovery before committing to the programme.

name: customs-valuation-review
description: Determines the value to declare to customs and finds where it is understated or overstated. Trigger it for related-party imports, royalty or licence payments tied to goods, tooling or materials supplied free to a supplier, year-end transfer pricing adjustments, or when customs queries a declared value.
expansions: related party pricing on imports
we supplied tooling to the vendor
royalty payable on imported goods
year end transfer pricing adjustment
assist value was never declared
first sale for export eligibility
should freight sit inside the value
customs questioned our declared value

atoms.obligation: Start from the transaction value and test whether the relationship influenced the price before moving to any alternative method.
atoms.lesson: Related-party sales can still use transaction value if the price is settled in a way consistent with normal industry pricing practice, or if it closely approximates a test value from unrelated sales of identical or similar goods. Evidence means a transfer pricing study aligned to the customs question, or a cost-plus build showing a profit consistent with the firm's overall performance. Only when the test fails do you move down the sequence: identical goods, similar goods, deductive value, computed value, then a reasonable fallback.

atoms.obligation: Identify and apportion assists, royalties and resale proceeds that must be added to the price actually paid.
atoms.lesson: An assist is anything supplied to the producer free or at reduced cost and used in production: tooling, dies, moulds, components, and design or engineering work performed outside the importing country. Its value is added and apportioned across the production run, either on the first shipment or spread evenly. Royalties are added when they relate to the imported goods and are a condition of sale, which turns on the licence wording rather than on who receives the money. Subsequent resale proceeds accruing to the seller are also additions.

atoms.obligation: Deduct only what the destination's rules permit, and only when the amount is separately identified on the invoice.
atoms.lesson: Systems differ at the base. Where value is declared on a delivered basis, international freight and insurance are inside the value; where it is declared on a departure basis, they are excluded but only if shown separately rather than buried in a single delivered price. Post-importation transport, installation, buying commissions and duties are commonly deductible; selling commissions are not. A single all-inclusive delivered price with no breakdown means the whole amount is dutiable.

atoms.obligation: Handle retroactive price adjustments through the formal reconciliation route rather than absorbing them silently.
atoms.lesson: Year-end transfer pricing true-ups, rebates and retrospective discounts change the price paid after entry. Upward adjustments create underpaid duty that must be declared, and downward adjustments can be refunded only if the arrangement was fixed by an objective formula agreed before importation and the entries were flagged as provisional. Register for the reconciliation or provisional value mechanism before the year begins, because retrofitting the claim afterwards usually fails on the pre-existing formula requirement.

name: restricted-party-screening
description: Screens counterparties, vessels, banks and end uses against sanctions and denied party lists, and resolves the hits. Trigger it when onboarding a customer or forwarder, when ownership changes, when a shipment routes through a sensitive jurisdiction, or when a screening tool flags a possible match before booking.
expansions: new customer in a sensitive country
screen this consignee before booking
possible hit on a denied party list
vessel appears on a sanctions list
fifty percent ownership rule question
forwarder in a transshipment hub
stated end use looks military
rescreen the whole customer master

atoms.obligation: Screen every party to the transaction, not only the buyer, and rescreen at each material event.
atoms.lesson: The parties include the ordering customer, the consignee, the notify party, the ultimate end user, the freight forwarder, the trucker, the vessel and its operator, the bank and any intermediary. Screen at onboarding, at order acceptance, at booking, at shipment, and again when any detail changes. Lists move weekly, so a party cleared at order entry can be listed by the time the container loads, and the offence is judged at the moment of the transaction.

atoms.obligation: Resolve a potential match with documented evidence before either releasing or refusing the shipment.
atoms.lesson: Most alerts are false positives generated by common surnames, transliteration variants and shared city names. Clear them with corroborating data - registration number, full address, date of birth, known aliases - and record what was checked and by whom, because that log is the audit trail if the same name recurs. Never clear a hit by lowering the fuzzy match threshold, and never let commercial urgency substitute for the evidence; escalate genuinely ambiguous cases rather than deciding in the booking queue.

atoms.obligation: Apply ownership and control rules that reach entities which are not themselves named on any list.
atoms.lesson: A company owned fifty percent or more by listed persons is treated as listed in several regimes, and the ownership can aggregate across multiple listed shareholders. European rules add a control test that captures dominant influence even below majority ownership. Screening the trading name alone therefore misses the exposure entirely. For counterparties in higher-risk jurisdictions, obtain the shareholder register or a corporate registry extract, and re-check it annually rather than trusting an onboarding snapshot.

atoms.obligation: Stop and escalate on diversion red flags rather than proceeding under commercial pressure.
atoms.lesson: The classic pattern is a customer whose stated business does not match the goods, an order for quantities or specifications inconsistent with local use, a freight forwarder's address as the final destination, a refusal of installation or warranty service, unusual routing through a known transshipment hub, and payment in full up front by an unrelated party. Any two together justify holding the shipment. Document the decision, because knowledge of the red flags is itself the basis of liability if the goods later surface elsewhere.

name: export-license-determination
description: Classifies items for export control and decides whether a licence or exception applies. Trigger it for encryption or security software, aerospace and machine tool parts, sensors and test equipment, a first shipment to a new country, or a foreign national needing access to controlled technology.
expansions: do we need a licence for this part
classification for a new product line
encryption item shipping abroad
deemed export to a foreign national
is a licence exception available
dual use item to a listed country
reexport of foreign origin content
defence article or dual use question

atoms.obligation: Establish jurisdiction before classification, because the wrong regime produces a confidently wrong answer.
atoms.lesson: Defence articles designed or modified for military use fall under the munitions regime, which is licence-first with very few exemptions. Everything else, including items with both civil and military application, sits under the dual-use regime with a graduated control list. The order of review runs munitions first, then the dual-use list, then the catch-all residual category. A part originally designed for a fighter programme stays in the munitions regime even when sold into a civil aftermarket, unless a formal commodity jurisdiction determination says otherwise.

atoms.obligation: Derive the control classification from the item's technical parameters read against the control list text itself.
atoms.lesson: Control entries turn on numbers: composite fibre modulus, machine tool positioning accuracy and number of simultaneously controlled axes, sensor wavelength and frame rate, encryption key length and whether cryptography is the primary function. Get the engineering specification and compare parameter by parameter, including the technical notes and the general technology and software notes that pull design data and source code into the same entry. Supplier statements of no control are common and frequently wrong for the destination in question.

atoms.obligation: Check the destination country matrix and the available exceptions before assuming a licence application is needed.
atoms.lesson: A classification alone does not determine licensability; the reason for control crossed against the destination does. Many shipments move under an exception - low value consignments, shipments to a group of close allies, temporary export for exhibition or repair and return, mass market encryption after notification, or intra-company transfers under a general authorisation. Each exception carries its own conditions and record entries on the export declaration, and using one without meeting its conditions is an unlicensed export.

atoms.obligation: Treat releases of technology and software to foreign persons as exports in their own right, wherever they occur.
atoms.lesson: Showing controlled drawings to a foreign national employee, granting repository access to an offshore contractor, discussing controlled specifications on a call, or hosting the data where a foreign administrator can reach it all count as exports to that person's country of nationality. The controls follow the technology, not the border. Manage it with access controls on the drawing repository, nationality screening for engineering roles, and a licence where the work genuinely requires the release.

name: warehouse-slotting-plan
description: Redesigns pick face assignments and storage locations to cut travel, congestion and replenishment work. Trigger it when pick rates fall, when a new product family arrives, ahead of a seasonal peak, when replenishment cannot keep up, or when pickers are visibly walking too far per order.
expansions: pickers walking too far per order
reslot the fast movers
new product family needs locations
congestion in the same aisle
replenishment cannot keep up
peak season layout change
golden zone assignments
too many faces for slow movers

atoms.obligation: Rank items by pick frequency and by cube moved together, rather than by units sold alone.
atoms.lesson: Two rankings matter: how often a location is visited, which drives travel, and how much volume moves through it, which drives replenishment. A high-hit small item belongs at waist height near the despatch end; a heavy bulky item belongs low and close even if it is picked rarely, because handling risk dominates. The classic error is filling the golden zone by sales value, which parks a slow expensive item in the best real estate while a daily-picked consumable sits on a top shelf.

atoms.obligation: Size each pick face so it holds at least one full replenishment cycle of demand for that item.
atoms.lesson: A face too small for daily demand generates emergency replenishments that block the aisle and stall pickers mid-order. Compute demand per replenishment interval in the pick unit, add safety, and choose the face type - flow rack lanes, case shelving, pallet position - that holds it. Oversizing is the opposite failure: a slow item given a full pallet position creates honeycombing, where partly empty locations consume the cube that fast movers need.

atoms.obligation: Place correlated items to shorten the pick path without pushing multiple pickers into the same aisle.
atoms.lesson: Order affinity analysis shows which items appear together on the same order, and co-locating them collapses two trips into one. Push it too far and the top movers concentrate into a short stretch of one aisle, where pickers queue behind each other and gain nothing. Spread the highest-hit items across the ends of several aisles or across zones sized to balance work, and check the resulting picker density against the aisle width and the equipment used.

atoms.obligation: Phase the moves so picking continues during the reslot and location records stay accurate throughout.
atoms.lesson: Reslotting is inventory movement, and unrecorded movement destroys accuracy faster than any theft. Move in waves outside the pick window, count each item before and after the move, update the system location at the moment of the physical move rather than in a batch afterwards, and keep the old location blocked until it is confirmed empty. Sequence the waves so no wave leaves a top mover unpickable, and measure travel per line before and after to prove the gain.

name: cycle-count-reconciliation
description: Investigates inventory record discrepancies and designs the counting programme that prevents them. Trigger it when a pick comes up short, when book against physical variance is growing, before a financial audit, when a location shows a negative balance, or when one area keeps producing shrink.
expansions: system says forty shelf has twelve
short pick on a customer order
variance grew before the audit
design a cycle count programme
which items to count weekly
negative on hand in a location
recurring shrink in one aisle
adjust inventory after a recount

atoms.obligation: Recount blind before adjusting anything, and count the item across every location rather than the one bin that failed.
atoms.lesson: A blind recount, where the counter does not see the expected figure, is the only count worth trusting; a verification count against a displayed number confirms the number. Stock hides in receiving, staging, quality hold, returns, damaged bins, packing benches and on a trailer at the dock, so a single-bin count usually finds a transfer rather than a loss. Use a second counter for high value items and freeze movement of that item during the count window.

atoms.obligation: Trace the transaction history around the discrepancy to find the process cause before recording an adjustment.
atoms.lesson: Walk the item's movements backwards: receipt without putaway confirmation, a unit of measure error where cases were received as eaches, a putaway to a mistyped location, a pick short-shipped but never adjusted, an unrecorded scrap, a return receipted to the wrong item, or an offsetting mispick that shows as a shortage here and a surplus in a lookalike item. Roughly the majority of variances resolve to a paired transaction error rather than to loss.

atoms.obligation: Set count frequency by value and movement rather than counting every item at the same rate.
atoms.lesson: Classify by annual movement value: the small group carrying most of the value counted monthly or more, the middle group quarterly, the long tail once or twice a year, with high-theft and high-error items promoted regardless of value. Measure accuracy by location and by item within tolerance, not by net currency variance, because offsetting errors net to zero while the operation still ships the wrong things. Count on an event basis too - at zero balance during picking, and after each replenishment.

atoms.obligation: Fix and record the process that produced the error, because the adjustment alone guarantees the same variance returns.
atoms.lesson: Every adjustment should carry a reason code that names a mechanism: receiving error, putaway error, pick error, damage, scrap, system timing, unknown. Review the reason mix monthly, because a rising unknown share means the root cause work is not happening. Then change the process - scan verification at putaway, unit of measure validation at receipt, mandatory short-pick confirmation - and watch the same reason code fall. Auditors weigh the trend in accuracy far more heavily than a single clean count.

name: dock-appointment-planning
description: Builds the dock and yard schedule that matches unloading labour to arriving freight. Trigger it when trailers queue at the gate, when detention charges from carriers climb, when receiving is backed up for days, when the yard fills with unturned trailers, or when a heavy inbound week needs planning.
expansions: trailers queuing at the gate
receiving backed up until thursday
carrier detention charges climbing
set appointment windows for inbound
not enough unloaders on monday
live unload versus drop trailer
yard is full of empty trailers
prioritise a hot inbound container

atoms.obligation: Build the schedule from unload hours required per load rather than from the number of doors available.
atoms.lesson: Doors are rarely the binding constraint; labour is. A floor-loaded container of cartons can take three to four hours to strip by hand, while a slip-sheeted or palletised trailer clears in thirty to forty-five minutes. Convert the day's expected arrivals into unload hours by load type, compare against the crew hours actually rostered by shift, and schedule against the smaller number. Publishing more slots than the crew can absorb simply moves the queue from the gate to the dock.

atoms.obligation: Reserve capacity for arrivals you do not control and keep a buffer of slots for exceptions.
atoms.lesson: Ocean containers arrive on a terminal's clock, rail ramps release in bunches, and small parcel and courier deliveries turn up unannounced. Hold roughly a fifth of the day's capacity unallocated, weighted to the shift where uncontrolled volume lands, and convert live unloads to drop and hook wherever the carrier has spare equipment, because a dropped trailer decouples the carrier's clock from yours. Track no-show rates by carrier and overbook only where the history supports it.

atoms.obligation: Publish the appointment rules and the detention terms so the site and the carriers are judged by the same clock.
atoms.lesson: Detention normally starts after a free period of about two hours from arrival, measured from gate-in, and disputes turn on whose timestamps count. State how arrival is recorded, what counts as on time, how late arrivals are handled, and how a driver requests a reschedule. Give drivers a gate receipt with in and out times, retain the yard log, and reconcile it against detention invoices monthly - most contested charges dissolve when a timestamped gate record exists.

atoms.obligation: Sequence putaway and cross-dock priorities against outbound cut times, not against arrival order.
atoms.lesson: Unloading a trailer is only half the job; product that is not put away or staged in time misses the outbound wave and becomes tomorrow's backorder. Identify the inbound lines that feed today's open orders and today's cross-dock outbounds, and unload those first regardless of when the trailer arrived. Where a receipt must clear customs or quality hold, book it early in the shift so the hold clears before the cut, and keep a marked staging lane so hot freight is not buried.

name: distribution-network-design
description: Evaluates where to hold inventory and site facilities, weighed against service commitments and total cost. Trigger it when considering an additional warehouse, when transit-day coverage is slipping, after a lasting shift in demand geography, when consolidating sites, or when choosing which port to import through.
expansions: should we open a west coast site
two day coverage is slipping
compare three candidate locations
consolidate two warehouses into one
cost to serve by region
port of entry choice for imports
inventory versus transport tradeoff
model service levels by zone

atoms.obligation: Model total cost to serve, including inventory and facility cost, rather than transport cost alone.
atoms.lesson: Adding a site shortens outbound distance but adds inbound transfer legs, fixed facility and management cost, and safety stock. Pooled safety stock rises roughly with the square root of the number of stocking locations, so splitting one site into two adds about forty percent to safety stock for the same service level. Build the comparison as outbound plus inbound plus fixed plus variable handling plus inventory carrying, and state the carrying rate assumed, because it decides the answer for high-value goods.

atoms.obligation: Anchor the analysis in real shipment-level demand geography across a full year, not in regional summaries.
atoms.lesson: Use actual ship-to postcodes, weights, cubes and order dates. Aggregating to region hides the concentration that decides site placement - a single large customer can pull the centre of gravity hundreds of kilometres. A full year captures seasonality and stops a peak-quarter skew from driving a ten-year lease. Strip one-off events and closed accounts, and separate the parcel profile from the pallet profile, because their cost curves respond to distance in completely different ways.

atoms.obligation: Test candidate networks against service commitments measured in transit days, not in distance or radius.
atoms.lesson: Customers experience delivery days, and carrier transit maps are not circles: parcel zone boundaries, ground service day maps and less-than-truckload service areas follow terminal networks and reflect river crossings, mountains and hub locations. Overlay the actual carrier day map on each candidate site, count the demand covered within the promised day, and check the despatch cut-off time that assumes, because moving the cut-off an hour earlier can cost more coverage than moving the building.

atoms.obligation: State the assumptions and switching costs that would reverse the recommendation before presenting it.
atoms.lesson: Network answers are usually close together, and the decision often turns on things outside the cost model: lease length and exit terms, labour availability and wage rates in the local market, the one-time cost of moving inventory and ramping a new crew, customer disruption during cutover, and duty or free-trade-zone consequences of a new port of entry. Give the break-even on the main uncertainty - volume growth or fuel - so the reader knows how much the answer can bend.

name: last-mile-route-design
description: Plans delivery routes, time windows and fleet size for own or contracted vehicles. Trigger it when routes overrun the shift, when stops per hour fall, when a customer demands a narrow window, when adding or removing a vehicle, or when failed deliveries repeat on the same rounds.
expansions: routes overrunning the shift
can four vans cover this area
