Changes that touch analysis populations, the estimand, or the primary timepoint need the statistician to co-sign and usually a matching update to the analysis plan.

name: informed-consent-form-review
description: Reviews and drafts informed consent documents so they are complete, readable and consistent with the protocol. Use it when a consent form comes back from an ethics committee with comments, when new risk information means participants must be re-consented, when a site needs an assent form for adolescents or a short form for a non-English speaker, or when someone asks whether the reading level is acceptable.
expansions: ethics committee sent back consent comments
new risk found, do we need reconsent
consent reading level is too high
need an assent form for teenagers
participant enrolled on an outdated consent version
translating the consent into polish
adding optional genetic sub-study consent
consent for a legally authorised representative

atoms.obligation: Check the consent contains every required element, including foreseeable risks, alternatives, confidentiality limits, compensation for injury and the right to withdraw.
atoms.lesson: The required elements are fixed by regulation and inspectors check them line by line: purpose and duration, description of procedures and which are experimental, reasonably foreseeable risks, expected benefits or a statement that none is expected, alternative treatments, how confidentiality is kept and who may inspect records, whether treatment or compensation exists for research injury, contacts for questions and for injury, and a statement that participation is voluntary and withdrawal carries no penalty.

atoms.obligation: Write at a lay reading level, replacing clinical terms with plain words and keeping sentences short and directly addressed to the participant.
atoms.lesson: Aim for roughly a sixth to eighth grade level. Replace randomised with assigned by chance like flipping a coin, placebo with a dummy treatment that looks the same but has no active drug, and pharmacokinetics with blood tests to see how the drug moves through your body. Keep the second person throughout, avoid nested clauses, and put the number of visits, needle sticks and total blood volume in concrete figures rather than percentages.

atoms.obligation: Decide whether new information requires re-consent of enrolled participants, or only a revised form for future enrolment.
atoms.lesson: Re-consent is required when new information could reasonably affect a participant's willingness to continue: a newly identified serious risk, a change in the treatment schedule, a new procedure, or a shift in the risk-benefit balance. Administrative edits and clarifications need only a new version for future enrolment. When re-consent is needed, define the window, plan how participants who are off treatment but in follow-up will be contacted, and document any participant who declines.

atoms.obligation: Confirm the consent process itself, not just the document, is documented with dates, signatures and evidence of discussion before any study procedure.
atoms.lesson: The signature date must precede every protocol-specific procedure including screening bloods and washout. The person conducting the discussion must be delegated to do so and, where required, must be the investigator. Notes should record that time to ask questions was given, who was present, and that a copy was handed over. When an impartial witness or a legally authorised representative signs, the reason and the local legal basis must be recorded in the participant file.

name: eligibility-screening-check
description: Works through inclusion and exclusion criteria against a candidate's actual history and screening results before enrolment is confirmed. Use it when a coordinator is unsure whether a borderline lab value or a past medication disqualifies someone, when a waiver is being requested, or when screen failure rates are climbing and someone wants to know which criterion is the bottleneck.
expansions: borderline creatinine, is the patient eligible
prior therapy might breach exclusion 7
site is asking for an eligibility waiver
screen failure rate is running at sixty percent
washout period ended two days early
rescreening a candidate who failed on haemoglobin
which criterion is knocking most people out
check this screening log before enrolment

atoms.obligation: Assess each criterion against dated source evidence rather than participant recall, and record where each answer came from.
atoms.lesson: Every criterion needs a traceable source: a laboratory report with the collection date, a pathology report confirming histology, an imaging read, a pharmacy or referral record for prior therapy. Self-reported history is acceptable only where the protocol allows it and must be documented as such in the medical notes. Screening results must fall inside the protocol screening window, and repeat values are only usable if the protocol explicitly permits a retest.

atoms.obligation: Refuse eligibility waivers and treat any enrolment outside the criteria as a deviation requiring immediate reporting.
atoms.lesson: Sponsors cannot grant exemptions from their own protocol; enrolling a participant who does not meet the criteria is an important deviation and, in many jurisdictions, a serious breach if it affects safety. The correct routes are a protocol amendment for a criterion that is systematically too tight, or a screen failure for this individual. If enrolment has already happened, assess whether continuing is safe, notify the ethics committee, and document the medical judgement in writing.

atoms.obligation: Track screen failure reasons by criterion so recruitment problems can be separated from criteria that are simply too restrictive.
atoms.lesson: A screening log recording each candidate, the date, and the specific failing criterion turns anecdote into evidence. When one criterion accounts for a large share of failures, the choice is between an amendment, better pre-screening at referral, or accepting slower enrolment. Distinguish failures on fixed characteristics such as histology or prior lines of therapy, which pre-screening can catch, from failures on transient laboratory values, where rescreening after a defined interval may be permitted.

atoms.obligation: Confirm the investigator has personally signed the eligibility assessment and dated it before the first dose or randomisation.
atoms.lesson: Eligibility confirmation is a delegated medical decision that usually sits with the investigator or a sub-investigator who is a qualified physician. The signed eligibility checklist must be dated before randomisation, since a retrospective signature cannot demonstrate the judgement was made in advance. Where a central review of imaging or pathology gates entry, the confirmation must be received and filed before the participant is randomised, not reconciled afterwards.

name: serious-adverse-event-reporting
description: Handles the workflow when a serious adverse event occurs: seriousness and causality assessment, expedited reporting clocks, and follow-up until resolution. Use it when a site calls about a hospitalisation, when someone asks whether an event is a suspected unexpected serious adverse reaction, when a reporting deadline is at risk, or when a follow-up report needs to be prepared.
expansions: participant hospitalised over the weekend
is this event expected per the brochure
susar clock started, when is it due
death on study, what do we report first
site reported an sae five days late
need a follow-up report on the liver injury
does an elective admission count as serious
who tells the ethics committee about this event

atoms.obligation: Apply the seriousness definition strictly rather than judging by how severe the event feels clinically.
atoms.lesson: Serious means the event resulted in death, was life-threatening, required or prolonged inpatient hospitalisation, caused persistent or significant disability or incapacity, was a congenital anomaly or birth defect, or was an important medical event requiring intervention to prevent one of these. Severity and seriousness are separate: severe headache may be non-serious, while a mild rash needing hospitalisation is serious. Elective admissions for a pre-existing condition planned before enrolment are usually not serious.

atoms.obligation: Start the reporting clock from the moment any study staff member first became aware of the minimum criteria, not from the event date.
atoms.lesson: The clock starts on day zero at first awareness by any person acting for the sponsor, once an identifiable participant, an identifiable reporter, a suspect product and an event are known. Fatal or life-threatening suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions go to authorities within seven calendar days with follow-up within eight further days; other such reactions go within fifteen days. Late site notification does not reset the sponsor clock, so escalation paths must work on weekends.

atoms.obligation: Record the investigator causality assessment separately from the sponsor assessment and never downgrade the investigator opinion.
atoms.lesson: Causality is assessed by the investigator and independently by the sponsor's medical monitor. If either considers a reasonable possibility of relationship, the event is treated as related for expedited reporting purposes. Upgrading is allowed, downgrading is not. Expectedness is judged only against the reference safety information in the current investigator brochure, not against general drug class knowledge or the label of a marketed comparator.

atoms.obligation: Reconcile safety database entries against the clinical database and chase follow-up until every event reaches a final outcome.
atoms.lesson: Divergence between the safety database and the clinical data is a standing inspection finding: an event closed as resolved in one and ongoing in the other, or an outcome date missing. Reconcile at defined intervals and before every data cut, interim analysis and database lock. Follow-up reports should capture the final diagnosis where a syndrome was initially reported as separate symptoms, treatment given, action taken with the investigational product, and whether rechallenge occurred.

name: adverse-event-coding
description: Codes verbatim adverse event and medical history terms to a standard dictionary and codes concomitant medications to a drug dictionary. Use it when a coding batch needs review, when a verbatim term is ambiguous or reports a diagnosis plus symptoms together, when an uncoded backlog is blocking a data cut, or when a coding decision needs a documented rationale before lock.
expansions: batch of uncoded verbatim terms to review
verbatim says chest pain query mi
auto-coder failed on this medication name
need a coding convention for splitting terms
dictionary upversion before database lock
concomitant medication has no active ingredient listed
why did this term map to that system organ class
medical monitor disagrees with the coded term

atoms.obligation: Code the diagnosis when one is reported and code signs and symptoms separately only when no unifying diagnosis exists.
atoms.lesson: If a site reports cough, fever and an infiltrate on imaging with a diagnosis of pneumonia, code pneumonia alone; coding the symptoms as well inflates event counts and splits the safety signal. When a verbatim term contains a provisional diagnosis and a symptom, such as chest pain query myocardial infarction, query the site rather than guessing, because the choice determines whether the event lands under cardiac disorders or general disorders and changes how the signal reads in the summary tables.

atoms.obligation: Query the site for clarification instead of interpreting an ambiguous verbatim term, and never edit the verbatim text yourself.
atoms.lesson: The verbatim term is source-linked data and must stay exactly as the investigator wrote it, including misspellings. Where the term is uninterpretable, abbreviations are local, or several events are bundled in one entry, raise a data query asking the site to split or clarify. Coders may create a synonym mapping for a corrected spelling, but that mapping is a coding artefact recorded in the coding log, not a change to the reported term.

atoms.obligation: Fix the dictionary version for the study, plan the upversion deliberately, and re-review affected terms after any change.
atoms.lesson: Medical and drug dictionaries release new versions twice a year, and terms are added, demoted or reassigned between organ classes. Decide in the data management plan whether the study codes against a fixed version through to lock or upversions at defined points. After an upversion, run an impact report on changed terms and re-review anything whose primary organ class or preferred term moved, because safety tables and any cumulative pooled analysis will shift with it.

atoms.obligation: Keep a written coding convention document and record the reasoning for every non-obvious decision so choices are reproducible.
atoms.lesson: Conventions should state how to handle procedural terms, worsening of pre-existing conditions, laboratory abnormalities reported as events, device-related terms, and combination medications. For drugs, record whether coding is by trade name, ingredient, or a reported class when the ingredient is unknown. An auditor asking why two similar verbatim terms coded differently should find the answer in the log, and the medical monitor should sign off the final coded listing before lock.

name: protocol-deviation-handling
description: Classifies, documents and escalates protocol deviations, and decides which rise to serious breaches. Use it when a visit falls outside its window, when a dose is given wrongly, when a site reports a missed assessment, when the deviation log needs review before a data cut, or when someone asks whether an ethics committee has to be told.
expansions: visit happened eleven days outside the window
wrong dose dispensed at the last visit
missed the pharmacokinetic sample entirely
is this a serious breach we must notify
deviation log review before database lock
site keeps repeating the same deviation
participant took a prohibited medication
sample stored at the wrong temperature overnight

atoms.obligation: Classify each deviation as important or minor using pre-defined criteria written before the trial rather than judged case by case.
atoms.lesson: Important deviations are those that affect participant rights, safety or wellbeing, or the reliability of the trial results: enrolment of an ineligible participant, missed safety assessments, dosing errors, consent taken late, or use of prohibited medication that interacts with the study drug. A visit two days outside a wide window with all assessments done is usually minor. Defining the categories in advance, with visit-window tolerances and dose-deviation thresholds, stops classification drifting between sites and monitors.

atoms.obligation: Record the deviation, the root cause and the corrective action taken, not just the fact that a rule was broken.
atoms.lesson: A log entry saying visit out of window is useless for prevention. Capture whether the cause was scheduling capacity, participant travel, a missed reminder, a training gap or an ambiguous protocol instruction. Repeated deviations of the same type at one site point to a training or process fix; the same type across many sites points to a protocol that is impractical and may justify an amendment. Corrective actions belong to the site with monitor verification at the next visit.

atoms.obligation: Escalate as a serious breach when the deviation significantly affects participant safety or the scientific value of the trial.
atoms.lesson: A serious breach must be notified to the competent authority within a short statutory window, commonly seven days of the sponsor becoming aware in the European framework. Examples include systematic falsification of data, repeated failure to report serious events, dispensing unblinded product to a blinded participant, or enrolling participants without valid consent. This is a separate and higher obligation than the routine deviation log and requires the sponsor, not the site, to make the notification decision.

atoms.obligation: Reconcile the deviation log with the clinical database and confirm every important deviation before the analysis populations are fixed.
atoms.lesson: Important deviations drive exclusion from the per-protocol population, so the log must be final and medically reviewed before the blind is broken and populations are assigned. Reconcile deviations recorded in visit reports, the database and the site's own log, since the three commonly disagree. Any deviation identified after lock has to be handled through a documented post-lock process, which is far more disruptive than closing the log properly in the pre-lock review.

name: site-feasibility-assessment
description: Evaluates whether a proposed investigator site can realistically deliver a study, using a feasibility questionnaire, patient population evidence and site capability checks. Use it when a country list is being built, when a site claims an enrolment number that looks optimistic, when competing trials are suspected, or when a decision is needed on whether to qualify or drop a site.
expansions: site claims twenty patients a year
building the country and site list
competing trial at the same centre
does the site have a minus eighty freezer
feasibility questionnaire responses to review
site has no experience with this indication
should we qualify this hospital or drop it
how many sites do we need for this enrolment

atoms.obligation: Challenge claimed enrolment numbers against documented patient flow rather than accepting the figure on the questionnaire.
atoms.lesson: Sites routinely overestimate by a factor of two to five. Ask how many patients with the indication were seen in the last twelve months, then apply the eligibility funnel: what fraction meets the key criteria such as prior lines of therapy, organ function or biomarker status, what fraction consents, and what fraction survives screening. A site seeing sixty patients a year with a fifteen percent eligible rate and half consenting will deliver four or five, not twenty.

atoms.obligation: Map the competing studies at the site that draw on the same patient population and the same coordinator time.
atoms.lesson: Competition is the single most common cause of enrolment shortfall at otherwise strong sites. Ask which open trials recruit the same indication and line of therapy, how patients are allocated between them, and which studies the principal investigator personally favours. Coordinator capacity matters as much as patient numbers: a site with one coordinator running nine studies cannot absorb an intensive protocol with weekly visits and complex sampling regardless of its patient volume.

atoms.obligation: Verify the physical and procedural capabilities the protocol demands, including storage, processing, imaging and pharmacy conditions.
atoms.lesson: Check specifics against the protocol: temperature-controlled storage with continuous monitoring and alarm callout, a centrifuge with the required speed and a refrigerated option, dry ice supply and courier access for time-critical shipments, the imaging modality with the exact sequence or contrast protocol, and a pharmacy able to prepare blinded infusions with the required hood and hours. Weekend and out-of-hours coverage matters where the schedule includes dosing days outside normal hours.

atoms.obligation: Record the feasibility decision and its rationale so site selection can be defended and later performance can be compared against the prediction.
atoms.lesson: Keep the questionnaire, the visit report and the decision memo in the trial file; regulators expect documented justification for selecting each investigator. Just as important, record the enrolment prediction so the actual figure can be compared later. Building that comparison across studies produces a site-level correction factor, and it identifies which questions in the feasibility questionnaire actually predicted performance and which were noise.

name: recruitment-enrollment-planning
description: Builds and rescues enrolment plans: recruitment channels, materials that need ethics approval, referral pathways and enrolment curves. Use it when enrolment is behind the projection, when a rescue plan is needed, when advertising material has to be reviewed before submission, or when someone asks whether to add sites or extend the recruitment window.
expansions: enrolment is forty percent behind projection
need a recruitment rescue plan
drafting a patient-facing advert for review
should we open more sites or wait
referral pathway from community clinics
half the sites have never randomised anyone
recruitment window ends in three months
screen failures are eating the enrolment funnel

atoms.obligation: Diagnose whether the shortfall sits in referral, screening or consent before proposing any remedy.
atoms.lesson: The three failure modes need opposite fixes. Too few candidates identified means a referral and awareness problem, addressed by outreach, chart review support or new sites. Many screened but failing means eligibility criteria or pre-screening are wrong, addressed by an amendment or better pre-screen filters. Many eligible but declining means the burden or the consent conversation is the barrier, addressed by visit-schedule relief, travel reimbursement or coordinator training. Enrolment funnel numbers per site tell you which one it is.

atoms.obligation: Submit every participant-facing recruitment material for ethics approval before use and keep approved versions under version control.
atoms.lesson: Adverts, posters, social posts, radio scripts, screening scripts, referral letters and websites all count as recruitment material and need approval in most jurisdictions. They must not promise benefit, must not describe the investigational product as safe or effective, must not overstate compensation, and must not use language that could coerce. Sites using a locally made flyer that never went to the committee is a routine and avoidable finding at monitoring visits.

atoms.obligation: Model enrolment with a realistic site activation curve rather than assuming all sites start on the same day at full rate.
atoms.lesson: Sites activate over months, and each has a ramp period before it randomises steadily. A credible model uses per-site monthly rates after ramp, a staggered activation schedule based on regulatory and contract timelines by country, and a discount for the roughly quarter of sites that will never enrol anyone. Compare the projection against actuals monthly, and set decision triggers in advance for adding sites, adding countries, or extending the window.

atoms.obligation: Weigh adding sites against activating them in time, since a site opened late may never contribute before the window closes.
atoms.lesson: From selection to first participant a new site typically needs three to six months for contracts, ethics and authority approval, initiation and supply. If the recruitment window has four months left, new sites add cost and oversight burden without patients. In that situation the better levers are targeted support to mid-performing existing sites, a protocol amendment easing the criterion driving screen failures, or a formal extension agreed with the steering committee.

name: monitoring-visit-report
description: Prepares for and writes up an on-site or remote monitoring visit, including the follow-up letter and action items. Use it when a visit report is due, when findings from the last visit are still open, when a site needs a confirmation letter before a visit, or when repeated findings across visits need to be escalated into an oversight issue.
expansions: monitoring visit report due in five days
action items from the last visit still open
writing the follow-up letter to the site
same finding at three consecutive visits
remote monitoring visit instead of on-site
close-out visit checklist for this site
what to check at the interim monitoring visit
escalating a non-responsive site

atoms.obligation: Write findings with the specific participant, document and date involved rather than a general statement of the problem.
atoms.lesson: A finding reading consent documentation issues gives the site nothing to act on. Write that for participant zero zero four the consent version two dated ten March was signed after the screening blood draw on nine March, and state the required action and the due date. Specific findings can be verified as closed at the next visit; general ones recur indefinitely. Keep participant identifiers to the study code, never names or hospital numbers, in any report leaving the site.

atoms.obligation: Issue the report and follow-up letter inside the timeline in the monitoring plan and track each action to documented closure.
atoms.lesson: Monitoring plans usually require the report within a set number of business days and the site letter shortly after, because a finding communicated a month later has already been repeated. Every action item needs an owner, a due date and evidence of closure recorded at the next visit. Open items carried across three or more visits are an oversight failure on the sponsor side as much as a site failure and should trigger escalation, not another repetition.

atoms.obligation: Follow the risk-based monitoring plan for what to review, and document any deviation from the planned sampling with its reason.
atoms.lesson: Contemporary monitoring targets critical data and processes rather than verifying everything. The plan defines which variables are critical, the verification percentage, and the triggers that increase intensity: a safety signal, high deviation rates, staff turnover, or key data lagging. If a monitor reviews more or fewer records than planned, the report must say why, since the plan is the evidence that oversight was systematic rather than improvised.

atoms.obligation: Verify investigational product accountability, consent, safety reporting and eligibility at every visit regardless of the risk-based sampling.
atoms.lesson: Some checks are non-negotiable at every visit because failures are unrecoverable. Confirm consent for every newly enrolled participant, including version and date order. Reconcile product received, dispensed, returned and destroyed against the log. Check that every serious event in the notes was reported and reported on time. Confirm eligibility was signed before randomisation. These four account for the majority of critical inspection findings and cost little to check when done routinely.

name: source-data-verification
description: Compares reported study data against the underlying medical record and resolves discrepancies. Use it when a monitor is planning what to verify, when a site's notes do not support a recorded value, when data was entered directly without a paper source, or when someone asks what counts as source and how corrections should be made.
expansions: case report form value has no source
which fields do we verify at this site
site entered data with no paper notes
source note contradicts the reported date
correcting an error in the medical record
defining the source data location list
electronic record has no audit trail
sampling plan for source verification

atoms.obligation: Agree a source data location list per site before the first visit, naming where each key variable originates.
atoms.lesson: For every critical variable the list states the origin: the hospital record system, the paper progress note, the laboratory report, the device printout, the participant diary, or direct entry into the study database. Ambiguity here creates arguments mid-study about whether a transcribed value is source. Where data is entered directly with no prior record, the study database is the source and that must be declared in advance, with an audit trail available for review.

atoms.obligation: Require that source records be attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original and accurate, and check corrections preserve the original entry.
atoms.lesson: Corrections in paper records are made with a single line through the error, the correct value beside it, and the initials and date of the person correcting, never overwritten or obscured with correction fluid. Backdating is falsification. In electronic records the audit trail must capture who changed what, when and why, and must not be disabled. A late note is acceptable if dated the day it was written and marked as a late entry describing the earlier event.

atoms.obligation: Focus verification on the variables that determine safety conclusions and the primary endpoint rather than verifying uniformly.
atoms.lesson: Full verification of every field consumes most of the monitoring budget and detects few errors that change conclusions. Concentrate on eligibility criteria, consent, primary and key secondary endpoint values, serious events, dosing records and randomisation. Non-critical fields can be checked by sampling or handled through centralised statistical checks that detect outliers, digit preference, impossible values and unusual variability, which find data problems that a site visit never would.

atoms.obligation: Raise a query rather than instructing the site what value to enter, and never enter or correct study data yourself.
atoms.lesson: The monitor identifies the discrepancy; the site resolves it. Telling a coordinator that the date should be the fourteenth compromises the independence of the record and the audit trail will show the sequence. Write the query against the specific field with the observed discrepancy, let site staff investigate the source, and verify the resolution at the next visit. If a site cannot explain a discrepancy from source, that is itself a finding requiring escalation rather than a value to be settled by agreement.

name: data-query-resolution
description: Manages the discrepancy and query cycle in the clinical database: writing clear queries, chasing ageing ones, and clearing the backlog toward lock. Use it when the open query count is rising, when sites are answering without fixing anything, when a query is unclear enough to bounce back repeatedly, or when a data cut is coming and the aged query list needs triage.
expansions: open queries piling up before the data cut
site keeps answering without changing the value
query has been open for ninety days
writing a clearer query for this discrepancy
too many auto-fired edit checks
manual query for an inconsistent stop date
triage the aged query list for lock
reconciling lab data against the database

atoms.obligation: Write each query naming the field, the observed value, why it is questioned, and the action needed, without suggesting the answer.
atoms.lesson: A query saying please check date is answered with checked and closes nothing. Write that the event stop date precedes the start date for event three, and ask the site to review the source and correct whichever is wrong. Avoid leading text that supplies the expected value, since that invites the site to enter what the query implies rather than what the record says. One issue per query keeps the answer unambiguous and the audit trail readable.

atoms.obligation: Tune automated edit checks during testing so implausible firing rates are fixed before sites drown in noise.
atoms.lesson: Over-broad range checks and cross-form checks that ignore legitimate clinical situations generate thousands of queries that sites learn to dismiss, which then hides the real discrepancies. Review firing rates in user acceptance testing against realistic test data, and again after the first weeks of live enrolment. A check firing on a large share of records is almost always mis-specified rather than evidence of widespread site error, and should be widened or moved to manual review.

atoms.obligation: Monitor query ageing by site and escalate when responses stall, rather than measuring only the total open count.
atoms.lesson: Total open queries hides the pattern. Track median days to response and the count over thirty and sixty days by site, because a small number of unresponsive sites usually drives most of the aged backlog. Escalation runs from the monitor to the site coordinator, then the principal investigator, and finally to a formal letter. Old queries are also the ones least likely to be resolvable from source, since staff turn over and memory fades.

atoms.obligation: Reconcile externally sourced data such as laboratory results and safety events against the clinical database before every data cut.
atoms.lesson: Central laboratory results, imaging reads, electrocardiogram overreads and the safety database arrive on separate schedules with their own identifiers. Reconciliation checks that every participant and visit present in one is present in the other, that dates align, and that events flagged serious in the safety database match the clinical forms. Mismatched participant identifiers and visits recorded under the wrong number are the two most frequent findings, and both take longer to fix than teams expect.

name: randomization-and-unblinding
description: Covers randomisation design and the handling of the blind: allocation schemes, stratification, emergency code break procedures and unblinding for reporting. Use it when a randomisation scheme is being specified, when a site calls needing an urgent code break, when an accidental unblinding is reported, or when a decision is needed about who may be unblinded for a safety report or interim analysis.
expansions: site needs an emergency code break tonight
designing the block size and stratification
pharmacist saw the treatment allocation
who can be unblinded for the susar report
accidental unblinding of a coordinator
randomisation failed at the last visit
stratifying by region and disease severity
unblinding plan for the interim analysis

atoms.obligation: Keep block sizes non-obvious and undisclosed to sites so allocation cannot be predicted from previous assignments.
atoms.lesson: Fixed small blocks let an unblinded observer at a site predict the last allocations in each block, which biases who gets enrolled next. Use randomly varying block sizes and keep the block structure out of the protocol and site-facing documents, restricting it to the randomisation specification held by the statistician. Stratify only on factors genuinely prognostic and known at randomisation, since too many strata with small sites produce imbalance rather than preventing it.

atoms.obligation: Make emergency unblinding available at any hour but only when knowing the treatment changes immediate clinical management.
atoms.lesson: The investigator decides, and the participant's safety comes first, so no approval from the sponsor may be required before breaking the code. But most situations do not require it: managing an adverse event usually proceeds identically either way, and the question to ask is what would be done differently knowing the assignment. When the code is broken, record who, when, why, and what was decided, notify the sponsor promptly, and keep the participant in the trial and in the analysis unless the protocol says otherwise.

atoms.obligation: Unblind the minimum number of people for regulatory reporting and keep the trial team and investigators blinded.
atoms.lesson: Expedited reports of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions are submitted unblinded to authorities, but the sites and the operational team stay blind. A small designated group, typically pharmacovigilance and a medical reviewer outside the study team, handles the unblinded assessment under a documented procedure. Sending an unblinded report back to investigators as a safety notification is a classic error; the site letter must carry the blinded event description only.

atoms.obligation: Investigate every unintentional unblinding as a deviation and assess its effect on the analysis populations.
atoms.lesson: Common causes are a distinguishable formulation, a laboratory value that reveals treatment, a shipment label showing the arm, or a system access error. Record who became aware, when, for which participants, and what containment followed, such as replacing an unblinded assessor. If unblinding affected an endpoint assessor rather than a coordinator, the risk to the endpoint is materially higher and the statistician should judge whether a sensitivity analysis excluding those participants is warranted.

name: investigational-product-accountability
description: Tracks investigational product from receipt through dispensing, return and destruction, and handles storage excursions and supply forecasting. Use it when an accountability log will not reconcile, when a fridge alarm reports a temperature excursion, when a site is running low before a shipment arrives, or when expiry dates need relabelling.
expansions: accountability log does not reconcile
fridge went out of range overnight
site is running low before the next shipment
expiry date extension and relabelling
participant returned empty blister packs
destroying unused product at the site
kit dispensed to the wrong participant
temperature excursion during courier transit

atoms.obligation: Reconcile quantity received, dispensed, returned, destroyed and remaining at every monitoring visit and resolve differences before the visit closes.
atoms.lesson: Reconcile at three levels: the site total, the per-participant dispensing record, and the physical count in storage. Discrepancies usually come from units dispensed but not logged, kits returned and reshelved without an entry, or a damaged kit removed without documentation. An unreconciled log means dosing compliance cannot be demonstrated and, for a controlled substance, may be a regulatory offence in its own right. Never resolve a difference by adjusting the log to match the count.

atoms.obligation: Quarantine product immediately after any temperature excursion and do not use it until the sponsor confirms it remains acceptable.
atoms.lesson: Move the product to a labelled quarantine area, keep it under the correct conditions, and send the full excursion record: minimum and maximum temperature, duration, the monitoring device readout, and the cumulative history of prior excursions for that batch. Stability assessment is made by the manufacturer against the batch data, not by the site or the monitor. Continued use of excursion product without written release is one of the most serious product handling findings.

atoms.obligation: Store product securely under controlled access with continuous temperature monitoring, an alarm, and a documented out-of-hours response.
atoms.lesson: Requirements are a locked area limited to delegated staff, a calibrated continuous monitoring device with a current calibration certificate, minimum and maximum readings recorded on defined working days, and an alarm that reaches a named person outside working hours. Keep a written contingency for power failure with a designated backup unit. Calibration certificates and the temperature log are essential documents and must be filed for the retention period, not discarded when the study closes.

atoms.obligation: Forecast resupply against enrolment and dosing rather than reordering when stock runs visibly low.
atoms.lesson: Supply planning must account for the randomisation ratio, weight-based or titrated dosing, the number of visits per participant, expiry dates and courier lead times including customs clearance where shipments cross borders. Automated resupply triggers set on stock thresholds fail at fast-enrolling sites with long lead times. Expiring stock at slow sites should be recovered or relabelled under an approved extension rather than destroyed, and any relabelling needs documented authorisation and reconciliation.

name: trial-master-file-management
description: Maintains the trial master file and its investigator site counterpart so the conduct of the trial can be reconstructed. Use it when filing is behind, when a completeness review is due before an inspection or a close-out, when someone asks whether a particular document is essential, or when certified copies and retention periods need to be decided.
expansions: filing is three months behind
completeness review before inspection
is this document essential or not
missing signed delegation log for site 12
scanning paper originals as certified copies
how long must we retain these records
investigator file versus sponsor file split
reconstructing the file at close-out

atoms.obligation: File essential documents contemporaneously rather than assembling the file at the end of the trial.
atoms.lesson: The file must be complete before the trial starts for the documents required at that point, maintained during conduct, and completed at close-out. Reconstruction at the end never reproduces the true sequence and inspectors detect it easily through metadata, missing intermediate versions and implausibly clustered filing dates. Set a filing service level, commonly within days of a document being finalised, and run periodic completeness checks rather than one panic review before an inspection.

atoms.obligation: Keep the sponsor file and the investigator file distinct, with each holding the documents required of that party.
atoms.lesson: Some documents live in both, such as the signed protocol and the approved consent versions. Others belong to one only: the investigator holds the participant identification code list and signed consent forms, which must never leave the site; the sponsor holds the monitoring visit reports, the randomisation code list and vendor contracts. Financial disclosure forms, delegation logs, curricula vitae and current medical licences for delegated staff belong in both files.

atoms.obligation: Confirm scanned copies are certified, with a documented process showing the copy is complete and faithful before any original is destroyed.
atoms.lesson: A certified copy carries a dated signature or a validated automated process attesting it reproduces the original including handwritten entries and their context. Destroying source originals after an uncertified scan removes the ability to demonstrate authenticity. Where wet-ink signatures matter, such as consent forms and the investigator statement, many organisations retain the paper regardless. Retention typically runs at least twenty-five years for the sponsor file in the European framework, and local law can require longer.

atoms.obligation: Run structured completeness checks against an expected document list per site and per country, not by browsing folders.
atoms.lesson: Build an expectation list keyed to milestones: for each site, the approval letters, the signed agreement, the delegation log, the training records, the laboratory certification and normal ranges valid for the period, and the product receipt records. Check that expiring documents such as licences, accreditations and normal ranges have successor versions covering the whole conduct period without gaps, since a lapsed range or an expired certificate leaves data unsupported for that window.

name: ethics-committee-submission
description: Assembles and tracks submissions to research ethics committees and institutional review boards, including initial applications, amendments, annual reports and responses to conditions. Use it when a first submission package is being built, when a committee raises conditions that need answering, when an annual progress report falls due, or when a local site needs its own approval alongside a central one.
expansions: building the initial ethics submission package
committee raised six conditions to answer
annual progress report is due next month
local approval needed on top of central
which documents go in the amendment submission
notifying the committee of a safety issue
meeting deadline is friday, what do we need
committee asked about the compensation arrangement

atoms.obligation: Build the package against the committee's own current checklist and submission deadline rather than a generic template.
atoms.lesson: Committees differ in what they demand and in format: some require a specific application form version, wet signatures, a set number of paper copies, or an insurance certificate translated locally. Meeting agendas close one to three weeks before the meeting, and a package arriving a day late waits a full cycle. Confirm the meeting calendar, the cut-off, and the exact document list including consent versions, participant materials, investigator credentials, the brochure and the indemnity evidence.

atoms.obligation: Answer every condition point by point, showing the changed text and the version it now sits in.
atoms.lesson: Respond in the committee's numbering with the original point quoted, the response, and a reference to the revised document, section and version. Where you disagree, say so with a scientific or regulatory justification rather than silently not making the change, since an unanswered point delays another cycle. Provide both a clean and a tracked version of every revised document, and keep an internal mapping of which condition drove which edit for the file.

atoms.obligation: Do not implement any change or start any activity at a site until that site's own approval is in hand.
atoms.lesson: Central or coordinating approval does not authorise local conduct where a local institutional review or governance sign-off is also required. Screening, consenting or shipping product before local approval is a serious breach. Keep a per-site tracker of submission date, approval date, approved document versions and any local conditions, because sites frequently operate under different consent versions during the weeks after an amendment approval rolls out.

atoms.obligation: Report to the committee on the schedule it sets, including annual progress, safety updates, early termination and end of trial.
atoms.lesson: Standing obligations usually include an annual report on the anniversary of favourable opinion, the periodic development safety update report, prompt notification of urgent safety measures and serious breaches, notification of temporary halt or early termination with reasons, declaration of end of trial within ninety days, and a summary of results within a year. Missing an annual report can suspend the favourable opinion, which stops enrolment until it is reinstated.

name: regulatory-authority-submission
description: Prepares clinical trial applications and their lifecycle with national competent authorities and drug regulators, including initial applications, amendments, safety reporting obligations and responses to requests for information. Use it when a first-in-human application is being assembled, when an authority sends questions with a short clock, when a new country is being added, or when a clinical hold or halt has to be handled.
expansions: assembling the first-in-human application
authority sent a request for information
adding two new countries to the trial
clinical hold placed on the study
which safety reports go to the regulator
annual safety update deadline approaching
notifying a temporary halt of enrolment
does this change need authority approval

atoms.obligation: Confirm the exact application content and clock for each jurisdiction before assembling, since requirements and review timelines differ.
atoms.lesson: A European application under the harmonised framework runs a validation phase then an assessment split into a scientific part shared across member states and a national part covering consent, recruitment, indemnity and data protection. A United States application relies on a thirty day waiting period before dosing may start, with no approval letter issued if no hold is placed. Assembling one dossier and assuming it satisfies both leads to validation failure and a lost cycle.

atoms.obligation: Answer requests for information within the stated clock and treat a missed deadline as a lapse of the application.
atoms.lesson: Clocks are short, often twelve days for a consolidated response in the European framework, and the clock is suspended only for the stated period. A missed response usually means the application lapses and must be resubmitted from the start with a new fee and a new queue position. Coordinate the medical, non-clinical, manufacturing and operational answers in parallel from the moment questions arrive, and use the full window for quality review rather than for waiting on one contributor.

atoms.obligation: Do not dose the first participant until the waiting period has expired or approval is granted, whichever the jurisdiction requires.
atoms.lesson: Dosing during a waiting period or before authorisation is a serious regulatory violation regardless of ethics approval being in place. Track approval, ethics opinion, site contract, site initiation and product release as five separate gates for each site, since all five must be closed before first dose. Where an authority issues a hold, no new participants may be enrolled and dosing of enrolled participants stops unless the authority explicitly permits continuation for safety reasons.

atoms.obligation: Maintain the ongoing safety obligations to the authority, including expedited reactions, the annual safety report and urgent safety measures.
atoms.lesson: Beyond the application, the sponsor owes expedited reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions on seven and fifteen day clocks, an annual development safety update report timed to the international birth date of the product, and immediate notification of any urgent safety measure taken to protect participants, followed by a written report within days. Failure to keep these current is treated as a compliance issue affecting the whole development programme, not just this trial.

name: statistical-analysis-plan
description: Drafts and reviews the statistical analysis plan: estimands, analysis populations, handling of missing data, multiplicity control and the table shells. Use it when a plan must be finalised before unblinding, when an endpoint definition is ambiguous, when someone proposes a new analysis after seeing data, or when the handling of intercurrent events needs to be pinned down.
expansions: finalise the analysis plan before unblinding
how do we handle treatment discontinuation
defining the estimand for the primary endpoint
multiplicity across three secondary endpoints
missing data at the week 24 visit
which population for the safety analysis
someone wants a new subgroup after the data cut
drafting the table shells for the report

atoms.obligation: Finalise and sign the plan before any unblinding or access to comparative results, and date the approval.
atoms.lesson: The credibility of the analysis rests on it being specified before anyone sees treatment differences. Any change after that point must be documented as a post-hoc amendment with the reason and the date, and reported as such. This applies to apparently minor choices: switching a transformation, changing a covariate set, or redefining a window can move a borderline result. Where an interim analysis occurs, the plan for the final analysis must be locked before the interim results circulate.

atoms.obligation: Define the estimand explicitly, naming the population, the endpoint, how intercurrent events are handled, and the summary measure.
atoms.lesson: Intercurrent events such as treatment discontinuation, rescue medication, surgery or death change the meaning of the estimate. A treatment policy strategy counts outcomes regardless of what happened afterwards; a hypothetical strategy asks what would have happened without rescue; a composite strategy folds the event into the endpoint as a failure. Stating simply that the intention-to-treat population will be analysed is no longer sufficient, because it does not say how these events are handled.

atoms.obligation: Specify the multiplicity strategy and the testing order in advance when more than one hypothesis can drive a claim.
atoms.lesson: Multiple primary endpoints, several dose arms, interim looks and key secondary endpoints intended to support labelling all inflate the false positive rate. Pre-specify a hierarchy where later tests proceed only if earlier ones succeed, or a formal procedure allocating alpha across the family. Endpoints outside the controlled family must be labelled as exploratory and described without inferential claims. Deciding the order after seeing the data invalidates the control entirely.

atoms.obligation: State the primary approach to missing data and pre-specify sensitivity analyses under different assumptions about why data is missing.
atoms.lesson: Single imputation with the last observation carried forward is generally unacceptable for a primary analysis because it assumes a participant's condition froze at withdrawal. Mixed models for repeated measures or multiple imputation under a missing at random assumption are the usual primary choices. Sensitivity analyses should test departures from that assumption, for example imputing withdrawn participants as if they followed the control arm trajectory, and the pattern of missingness by arm should be reported.

name: sample-size-justification
description: Calculates and defends trial sample size: effect size assumptions, power, dropout inflation, and the case for non-inferiority margins. Use it when a protocol needs its sample size section written, when a reviewer challenges the assumed event rate, when recruitment is short and someone asks about re-estimation, or when a feasibility ceiling on numbers forces a rethink of the endpoint.
expansions: write the sample size section for the protocol
reviewer challenged our assumed event rate
we can only recruit 180, is that enough
justify the non-inferiority margin
adjust for twenty percent dropout
sample size for a cluster randomised design
blinded sample size re-estimation mid-study
power for the key secondary endpoint

atoms.obligation: Base the assumed effect size on the smallest clinically meaningful difference rather than the effect seen in a small earlier study.
atoms.lesson: Early-phase estimates are inflated by selection and small samples, so powering on them systematically underpowers the confirmatory trial. Anchor the target difference on what would change practice: a difference patients notice, a threshold used by guidelines, or an established minimal clinically important difference for the instrument. State the source of the control arm rate or mean separately, since a wrong control assumption distorts the calculation as much as a wrong effect size.

atoms.obligation: Inflate the calculated number for expected dropout and non-adherence, and state each assumption with its source.
atoms.lesson: The calculation gives evaluable participants; the protocol needs randomised participants. Inflate for withdrawal and loss to follow-up, and consider whether non-adherence or crossover dilutes the observed effect under an intention-to-treat analysis, which needs a larger sample than a per-protocol view suggests. Quote a dropout figure from comparable trials in the same population and setting, and say plainly what happens to power if the actual rate exceeds it.

atoms.obligation: Justify a non-inferiority margin on clinical and historical grounds, not on what makes the trial affordable.
atoms.lesson: The margin must preserve a meaningful fraction of the active control's established effect over placebo, which requires a defensible estimate of that historical effect and evidence that it still applies in the current population and standard of care. Regulators expect a stated fraction retained, often around half, and a margin chosen before the trial. Non-inferiority trials also demand strict adherence and complete follow-up, because sloppy conduct pushes results toward apparent equivalence.

atoms.obligation: Pre-specify any adaptive re-estimation of sample size and keep it blinded unless the design formally controls the error rate.
atoms.lesson: Blinded re-estimation using the pooled variance or the pooled event rate does not compromise the type one error rate and is the safer route when the nuisance parameter was uncertain. Unblinded re-estimation based on the observed treatment effect requires a pre-specified adaptive design with a formal method to preserve the error rate and an independent group performing the look. Increasing enrolment after glimpsing an unblinded interim result without such a design invalidates the analysis.

name: dsmb-interim-review
description: Supports independent data monitoring committee work: charter drafting, closed and open session packages, stopping rules and the handling of recommendations. Use it when a committee is being constituted, when a scheduled safety review is approaching, when an imbalance in events prompts an unscheduled meeting, or when a recommendation to modify or stop the trial has to be acted on.
expansions: setting up the independent monitoring committee
charter needs stopping rules defined
preparing the closed session package
imbalance in deaths between the arms
committee recommended stopping for futility
unscheduled safety review requested
who sits on the committee and who cannot
minutes and recommendation handling after the meeting

atoms.obligation: Constitute the committee from members independent of the sponsor and the sites, with no financial or intellectual stake in the outcome.
atoms.lesson: Members should include clinicians experienced in the indication and at least one statistician, none of whom is an investigator on the trial, employed by the sponsor, or holding equity or a competing product interest. Conflicts are declared in writing and refreshed annually. The independent statistician preparing the unblinded reports must sit outside the trial team so that the operational statistician stays blinded and the final analysis remains untainted by knowledge of interim results.

atoms.obligation: Write the charter before the first participant is enrolled, defining meeting timing, the data to be reviewed, and the decision rules.
atoms.lesson: The charter fixes review frequency or event-driven triggers, the closed and open session structure, quorum, voting, how recommendations are communicated and to whom, and how confidentiality is maintained. It states the statistical stopping guidance for harm, benefit and futility, whether those are formal boundaries or advisory, and who may see unblinded data. Writing it after enrolment starts invites the appearance that rules were shaped by early observations.

atoms.obligation: Keep interim unblinded results inside the committee and the independent statistician, releasing only the recommendation to the sponsor.
atoms.lesson: Knowledge of an emerging treatment difference changes sponsor behaviour, site behaviour and investor conduct, and can bias enrolment and endpoint assessment. The sponsor receives a recommendation such as continue as planned, continue with modification, or stop, with reasoning that avoids conveying the direction or size of the effect. Closed session minutes and unblinded outputs are stored separately from the trial file and released only after the database is locked and the final analysis is complete.

atoms.obligation: Act on a recommendation with a documented sponsor decision and inform authorities, ethics committees and investigators as required.
atoms.lesson: The committee advises; the sponsor decides and owns the consequence. Record the decision, the rationale for accepting or departing from the advice, and who made it. A recommendation to stop for harm usually requires an urgent safety measure, immediate notification to authorities and ethics committees, a plan for participants already on treatment, and a letter to investigators. Departing from a stopping recommendation without compelling justification is very difficult to defend afterwards.

name: clinical-study-report-writing
description: Writes the clinical study report and its narratives: efficacy and safety sections, participant disposition, deviations, and individual case narratives for deaths and serious events. Use it when a report outline is needed after database lock, when narratives are being drafted, when an inconsistency appears between text and tables, or when a synopsis and lay summary are required.
expansions: outline the study report after lock
drafting narratives for the deaths
text says 214 but the table says 213
writing the safety results section
lay summary of results for participants
disposition and analysis population counts
how to describe an unexpected negative result
integrating the deviation list into the report

atoms.obligation: Report every randomised participant through to a documented disposition so the accounting reconciles at each stage.
atoms.lesson: The flow runs from screened to screen failed, randomised, treated, completed and discontinued with reasons. Every number in the text must reconcile with the disposition figure and the analysis population definitions, and each analysis population must state exactly who was excluded and why. Participants lost to follow-up are distinguished from those who withdrew consent, since withdrawal of consent limits what further data may be used and that limitation belongs in the report.

atoms.obligation: Write narratives for deaths, other serious events and discontinuations due to adverse events in a consistent chronological structure.
atoms.lesson: Each narrative gives age, sex, relevant history and concomitant medication, the study treatment with start date and dose, the event with onset in study day terms, the clinical course including investigations and treatments, the action taken with study drug, the outcome with dates, and the investigator causality assessment with reasoning. Keep the participant identifier as the study code alone. Consistency of structure across narratives is what lets a reviewer read fifty of them and spot a pattern.

atoms.obligation: Present results that contradict the hypothesis as plainly as those that support it, without selective emphasis.
atoms.lesson: Report the pre-specified primary analysis first and give its result whatever it shows, before any secondary or subgroup material. Do not promote a favourable secondary endpoint into the position of the primary, and label post-hoc analyses explicitly with the point at which they were conceived. Subgroup findings are described as hypothesis-generating with the interaction test result given. Reviewers weigh the discussion of limitations heavily, and an absent limitations section reads as an attempt to conceal.

atoms.obligation: Reconcile every number in the narrative text against the source tables and listings before the report is circulated.
atoms.lesson: The most common quality failure is text that no longer matches regenerated outputs after a data correction or an analysis rerun. Maintain a traceable link from each stated figure to the table, listing or figure number that produced it, and repeat the check after any rerun rather than only at the first draft. Percentages must state their denominator explicitly, since safety percentages usually use the treated population while efficacy uses a different one.

name: capa-quality-management
description: Handles quality issues, root cause analysis and corrective and preventive action plans across sites and vendors. Use it when an audit or inspection raises findings, when the same deviation keeps recurring, when a quality issue needs classifying as critical or major, or when a plan needs an effectiveness check before it can be closed.
expansions: audit report came back with major findings
same deviation at the site for the fourth time
writing a corrective action plan
is this finding critical or major
root cause analysis for the dosing errors
effectiveness check before closing the action
quality issue escalation to the sponsor
vendor keeps missing the reporting deadline

atoms.obligation: Find the true root cause by asking why repeatedly rather than accepting human error as an explanation.
atoms.lesson: Human error is a symptom, not a cause. A coordinator missing a sampling window is usually caused by an assessment schedule that is ambiguous, a reminder system nobody owns, a workload that exceeds capacity, or training delivered once at initiation and never repeated after staff turnover. Distinguish causes that sit with the site, the protocol design, the vendor, or the sponsor's own oversight, because a plan aimed at the wrong layer will not prevent recurrence.

atoms.obligation: Separate correction, corrective action and preventive action, and make sure the plan contains all three where warranted.
atoms.lesson: Correction fixes the instance: retrain that coordinator, retrieve the missing document, correct the record. Corrective action removes the cause so it does not recur at that site: rewrite the ambiguous instruction, add a second reviewer, change the scheduling process. Preventive action extends the fix where the same cause could occur but has not yet: circulate the clarification to all sites, update the training material, adjust the monitoring plan. Plans that stop at correction guarantee recurrence.

atoms.obligation: Grade each finding by its actual effect on participant safety, rights or data reliability, and escalate critical findings immediately.
atoms.lesson: Critical findings are those where participants were or could have been harmed, consent was invalid, or the data underpinning the conclusions cannot be trusted, and they need immediate containment such as suspending enrolment at the site, not a ninety day plan. Major findings compromise a process without immediate harm. Minor findings are isolated lapses. Consistent grading criteria written in advance prevent the drift where uncomfortable findings quietly become minor.

atoms.obligation: Define the effectiveness check and its evidence at the time the plan is written, and close only when that evidence exists.
atoms.lesson: State what will be measured, over what period, and what result counts as success: no recurrence of that deviation type across the next twenty participant visits, or a monitoring review of ten consecutive records showing the corrected process. Closing a plan on the strength of a completed retraining record is the most frequent weakness, because training completion is an activity, not evidence that the outcome changed. Reopen rather than re-close when the check fails.

name: cro-vendor-oversight
description: Manages oversight of contract research organisations and specialist vendors: transfer of responsibilities, performance metrics, governance meetings and issue escalation. Use it when responsibilities are being allocated in a new outsourcing arrangement, when a vendor is missing timelines, when quality signals appear in delegated work, or when a governance meeting or vendor audit needs preparing.
expansions: who owns which task in this outsourcing
vendor missed the reporting timeline again
preparing for the governance meeting
quality signals in the delegated monitoring
auditing the central laboratory vendor
escalation path when the study manager stalls
metrics to track vendor performance monthly
transitioning the study to a new provider

atoms.obligation: Document every transferred responsibility explicitly, since the sponsor keeps ultimate accountability for the trial regardless of delegation.
atoms.lesson: A transfer of obligations schedule should name each task, who performs it, who reviews it and who approves it, with nothing left ambiguous. Common gaps sit at the seams: who reconciles the safety database against the clinical data, who chases sites on aged queries, who signs the study report sections, who releases product. Regulators hold the sponsor responsible for the quality of delegated work, so oversight evidence must exist even where execution sits entirely with a provider.

atoms.obligation: Oversee through quality indicators and sampled review of the work itself, not through status reports written by the vendor.
atoms.lesson: Meaningful indicators include days from visit to report issue, aged action items, protocol deviation detection rates by monitor, safety report timeliness against the clock, query ageing and data entry lag. Sample the underlying work directly: read a set of visit reports for specificity, verify a subset of the monitoring the provider claims to have performed, and attend site visits periodically. A dashboard that is always green usually reflects the reporting design rather than the conduct.

atoms.obligation: Agree an escalation path with named roles and time limits before problems arise, and use it rather than waiting for the next meeting.
atoms.lesson: Define who is contacted at each level, from study manager to programme lead to executive sponsor, and how long an issue may sit at each level before rising. Record issues in a joint log with owner, target date and status reviewed at every governance meeting. Contractual levers such as staff replacement, withheld payment on unmet performance criteria and a rectification period should exist in the agreement rather than being negotiated during a crisis.

atoms.obligation: Qualify vendors before contracting and requalify periodically, keeping the assessment evidence in the trial file.
atoms.lesson: Qualification covers regulatory inspection history, quality system maturity, validated systems where applicable, staff turnover, experience in the therapeutic area and geography, business continuity and data protection arrangements. For laboratories and imaging providers it extends to accreditation, method validation and proficiency testing. Requalification on a defined cycle catches deterioration after acquisitions or mass staff departures, both of which change delivery quality faster than any contractual metric will show.

name: central-lab-sample-logistics
description: Covers biological sample handling from collection to central laboratory receipt and long-term storage, including kits, processing windows, shipping conditions and chain of custody. Use it when samples arrive compromised, when a site is unsure about processing or the collection window, when a shipment is stuck in customs, or when biobanking consent and sample destruction need sorting out.
expansions: samples arrived thawed at the lab
shipment stuck in customs over the weekend
site missed the two hour processing window
kits are expiring before the visit
chain of custody gap on the courier record
consent for long term biobank storage
which tube for the biomarker assay
destroying remaining samples at study end

atoms.obligation: Specify collection tube, volume, processing steps, time window and storage temperature for every sample type in a site-facing manual.
atoms.lesson: Analyte stability drives everything: some markers degrade within thirty minutes at room temperature, some need chilled centrifugation within a fixed window, some need a stabiliser tube or immediate acidification. The manual must give the tube type by additive and colour, fill volume with a minimum, inversion count, spin speed, time and temperature, aliquot number and volume, and the label format. Vague instructions to process promptly generate unusable samples that cannot be recollected once the visit has passed.

atoms.obligation: Ship under validated conditions with temperature monitoring and confirm receipt, quarantining any shipment whose readout shows an excursion.
atoms.lesson: Frozen shipments need sufficient dry ice for the worst-case transit including customs delay, and a monitoring device inside the shipper. Ambient shipments still need a temperature record. Do not dispatch frozen material late in the week where a weekend hold is possible unless the courier guarantees replenishment. On receipt the laboratory records condition, and any shipment arriving warm or partially thawed is quarantined pending an assessment of whether the specific analytes are still valid, which differs by assay.

atoms.obligation: Maintain an unbroken chain of custody with dated handovers, and label samples with coded identifiers only.
atoms.lesson: Record collection date and time, who processed and when, freezer location, who packed the shipment, courier consignment number, dispatch and receipt times, and receiving condition. Labels carry the study code, participant number, visit and sample type, never a name or hospital number, because samples leave the site and cross borders. A gap in custody means the result cannot be tied with confidence to the participant and visit, which can invalidate an endpoint measurement.

atoms.obligation: Track what consent permits for each stored sample, including future research use, retention period and the effect of withdrawal.
atoms.lesson: Optional biobanking consent is usually separate from the main trial consent and must be recorded per participant, since using a sample beyond the consented scope is a serious breach. Cross-border transfer of identifiable or pseudonymised samples engages data protection rules and may need specific consent and a legal transfer mechanism. Define what happens when a participant withdraws: samples already analysed and in the data set generally stay, but unanalysed samples are usually destroyed with the destruction documented.

name: public-records-request
description: Handles incoming public records and freedom-of-information requests from intake through release or denial. Use when a resident, reporter, or attorney asks for emails, contracts, body-worn camera footage, or inspection files, when a request is too broad to answer as written, or when a record may need redaction under a statutory exemption. Also covers tracking the statutory response clock and writing a denial letter that cites the exemption relied on.
expansions: reporter asked for two years of emails
records request due friday
can we redact this personnel file
request is too broad to search
resident wants police body camera footage
how much can we charge for copies
attorney demand letter for contract records
need to write a denial citing exemption

atoms.obligation: Acknowledge the request in writing within the statutory window and start a tracked clock even when the response will be partial.
atoms.lesson: Most state public records acts run a short clock, five business days in California and Florida practice, three in Texas, starting the first business day after receipt regardless of which department received it. The clock runs against the municipality, not the custodian, so a request emailed to a council member still counts. Acknowledgment is not production: statutes allow a written extension for unusual circumstances such as volume, off-site records, or consultation with counsel, but only if invoked before the original deadline lapses.

atoms.obligation: Narrow an overbroad request by offering the requester specific search terms, date ranges, and custodians rather than refusing outright.
atoms.lesson: 'All emails about the new development' is not a proper request in most jurisdictions because it asks the clerk to judge relevance, but flat refusal invites an attorney general opinion or a mandamus action. The defensible move is a documented clarification: propose named custodians such as the planning director and city manager, a date range tied to project milestones, and three to five search terms, then confirm in writing. If the requester declines to narrow, the file shows good faith.

atoms.obligation: Redact only the specific exempt content, cite an exemption for each withholding, and release the remainder of the record.
atoms.lesson: Segregability is the rule nearly everywhere: an email containing one line of attorney-client advice is not wholly exempt. Common municipal exemptions cover attorney-client and work product, personnel evaluations and medical files, ongoing law enforcement investigations, security and critical infrastructure plans, and identifiers like social security numbers. Home addresses of police and judges are protected by name in many states. A withholding log listing record, date, exemption, and reason survives appeal; blanket confidential stamps do not.

atoms.obligation: Charge only the fees the statute authorizes and give a written estimate before doing work that exceeds the free threshold.
atoms.lesson: Fee rules are narrow: direct duplication cost, often capped per page at ten to twenty-five cents, plus programming or redaction labor only where the statute names it. Staff search time is not chargeable in many states, including California for paper records, and electronic delivery of records already in electronic form usually carries no fee. Overcharging is the most common way a routine request becomes a complaint, so issue a written estimate and require a deposit only where the ordinance allows.

name: council-agenda-packet
description: Prepares and reviews the material that goes to a governing body before a public meeting: agenda item descriptions, staff recommendations, fiscal impact statements, and supporting exhibits. Use when someone says the packet closes Thursday, when an item needs a staff report written or tightened, when deciding whether a matter belongs on consent or the regular calendar, or when a late item raises open-meeting-law posting questions.
expansions: packet closes thursday and i have nothing
write the staff report for this item
should this go on consent calendar
item added after agenda was posted
fiscal impact section is missing
council asked for options not a recommendation
need the recommended motion language
is this item properly noticed for hearing

atoms.obligation: Post the agenda by the statutory deadline with enough detail that a member of the public can tell what will be decided.
atoms.lesson: Open meeting laws require a brief general description of each item, twenty words being the Brown Act benchmark, posted seventy-two hours before a regular meeting and twenty-four before a special one, in a location freely accessible at all hours plus the municipality's website. 'Personnel matter' or 'contract award' alone is too vague; name the position or the vendor and dollar amount. A defective description voids the action taken, which means re-noticing and re-hearing the item.

atoms.obligation: State the recommended action as a motion the body can adopt verbatim, and name the vote threshold it requires.
atoms.lesson: Clerks record what was moved, so a staff report should end with language like: adopt Resolution 2026-14 awarding a contract in an amount not to exceed $412,000 and authorizing the manager to execute. Thresholds vary by charter: simple majority of the quorum for most business, two readings for ordinances, four-fifths for urgency ordinances and many budget amendments, and a separate roll call for anything creating debt.

atoms.obligation: Place routine items on the consent calendar and keep anything contested, quasi-judicial, or newly funded off it.
atoms.lesson: Consent exists so a body can adopt twenty routine items in one vote: minutes, warrant registers, routine renewals, second readings without changes. Quasi-judicial matters such as variances, appeals, and revocations require testimony and findings, so they can never be consented. Any item a member or a member of the public asks to discuss must be pulled on request without a vote. Placing a controversial contract on consent is the fastest route to a rescission demand.

atoms.obligation: Include a fiscal impact statement naming the fund, the appropriation status, and the recurring cost, not just the contract total.
