atoms.lesson: Elected bodies approve one-time numbers and inherit ongoing costs. A usable statement names the fund, whether general, enterprise, gas tax, or impact fee, states whether the amount is in the adopted budget or needs an amendment, gives the unencumbered balance, and shows annualized future cost including maintenance and staffing. Grant-funded items must state the local match, its source, and what happens when the grant ends, since a position funded three years is a permanent liability otherwise.

name: ordinance-drafting-review
description: Drafts and reviews local ordinances and resolutions, including amendments to the municipal code. Use when the council directs staff to bring back an ordinance, when a proposed regulation needs enforcement teeth and penalty provisions, when checking whether the city has authority to regulate a subject at all, or when an existing code section conflicts with a new one.
expansions: council directed staff to bring back an ordinance
do we have authority to regulate this
new section conflicts with existing code
what penalty should this violation carry
need first and second reading dates
is this a resolution or an ordinance
state law may preempt our draft
add severability and effective date clauses

atoms.obligation: Confirm the municipality has authority over the subject before drafting, and identify any state preemption of the field.
atoms.lesson: Home rule charters grant broad police power over municipal affairs, while Dillon's Rule states limit cities to powers expressly granted. Even in home rule states, legislatures preempt whole fields: firearms regulation, short-term rental bans, tobacco and vaping in some states, oil and gas siting, minimum wage, and rent control under statutes like Costa-Hawkins. Preemption can be express, implied by a comprehensive scheme, or conflict-based. Drafting into a preempted field yields an unenforceable ordinance and a fee-shifting lawsuit.

atoms.obligation: Write the penalty, enforcement mechanism, and responsible party into the ordinance rather than leaving enforcement implied.
atoms.lesson: An ordinance without a stated enforcement path is aspirational. Specify whether a violation is an infraction, a misdemeanor, or an administrative citation, the escalating fine schedule, commonly one hundred, two hundred, and five hundred dollars for repeats within twelve months, whether each day is a separate violation, and which officers may cite. Add administrative abatement and cost recovery with lien authority for property conditions. Criminal penalties need a culpable mental state and the charter's jail maximum, usually six months.

atoms.obligation: Amend the code by showing the exact section with insertions and deletions marked, rather than describing the change in prose.
atoms.lesson: Codified text is what a judge reads, so amendments must be surgical: 'Section 8.24.030(B) is amended to read as follows,' with new language underlined and removed language struck. Renumbering cascades, since amending one subsection often orphans cross-references elsewhere, so search the whole title for citations to the section being changed. Include a codifier's note for the publisher and confirm whether the change alters definitions relied on by other titles of the code.

atoms.obligation: Include effective date, severability, and required findings, and calendar both readings with the publication step between them.
atoms.lesson: Most charters require two readings at separate meetings, publication of the ordinance or a summary in a newspaper of general circulation, and an effective date thirty days after adoption. Urgency ordinances compress this but need express findings of immediate threat to health, safety, or welfare, usually a four-fifths vote, and a short life unless extended. Severability preserves the remainder if a provision falls. Zoning ordinances add a planning commission recommendation and a separately noticed hearing.

name: zoning-variance-hearing
description: Works up land use entitlement applications heading to a planning commission or board of adjustment: variances, conditional use permits, and appeals. Use when an applicant wants to build closer to a property line than the setback allows, when a proposed use needs a conditional use permit, when neighbors have organized against a project, or when the decision needs written findings that will survive an appeal.
expansions: applicant wants a setback variance
neighbors are organizing against this project
need findings for the commission decision
is this use permitted or conditional
hardship claim looks self created
what conditions of approval should we attach
appeal filed on the commission decision
how do we notice the public hearing

atoms.obligation: Test each variance request against every statutory finding and recommend denial when any single finding cannot be made.
atoms.lesson: Variance findings are conjunctive, not a balancing test. The standard set: a special circumstance of the property in size, shape, topography, or surroundings not shared by others in the zone; strict application deprives the owner of privileges neighbors enjoy; the variance grants no special privilege; it is consistent with the general plan; and it is not detrimental to health or safety. Economic hardship and self-created hardship, such as a lot the applicant subdivided, never satisfy the special circumstance finding.

atoms.obligation: Write findings that connect each conclusion to specific evidence in the record rather than restating the legal standard.
atoms.lesson: Courts review entitlement decisions for whether findings bridge the analytic gap between evidence and decision, the Topanga standard. 'The site has unusual topography' fails; 'the rear third slopes at thirty-two percent per the March 3 survey, leaving a buildable envelope of 1,400 square feet, about half the zone median' survives. Cite the traffic study, the staff site visit, and testimony by name. Denials need findings too, and must address the applicant's strongest evidence.

atoms.obligation: Attach conditions of approval that address identified impacts, are enforceable, and stay within nexus and proportionality limits.
atoms.lesson: Conditions must relate to impacts the project actually causes and be roughly proportional to them under Nollan and Dolan, with Sheetz extending that scrutiny to legislatively imposed fees. Workable conditions are measurable and tied to a trigger: install the left-turn pocket before certificate of occupancy, limit deliveries to seven in the morning through seven at night, maintain landscape screening in perpetuity. Vague conditions like 'minimize noise' cannot be enforced by a code officer and collapse at the first complaint.

atoms.obligation: Notice the hearing by mail to the statutory radius, by publication, and by site posting, documenting each method in the file.
atoms.lesson: Typical requirements are mailed notice to owners within three hundred to five hundred feet drawn from the latest assessment roll, publication ten days before the hearing, and a posted sign on the site. Defective notice is the most common reason an approval is overturned, and the fix is re-noticing months later. Keep the radius map, mailing list, affidavit of publication, and a dated photograph of the sign. Where the applicant supplies the list, staff still verifies it against the current roll.

name: building-permit-intake
description: Screens building permit applications for completeness and routes them through plan review and inspection. Use when a contractor submits drawings and wants to know what is missing, when a permit has been in review too long and the applicant is escalating, when deciding whether work is exempt or eligible over the counter, or when unpermitted work has to be legalized after the fact.
expansions: contractor says the plans are complete
how long can we take on review
is a permit required for this work
applicant escalating a stalled review
unpermitted work needs legalizing
what triggers a fire sprinkler requirement
third correction cycle on the same sheets
can we issue a partial foundation permit

atoms.obligation: Screen submittals against a published completeness checklist at intake and reject incomplete packages the same day.
atoms.lesson: The permit clock generally starts when an application is deemed complete, and in states with permit streamlining acts the municipality has a fixed window, often thirty days, to notify the applicant of incompleteness or the application is deemed complete by operation of law. Publish the checklist by project type: site plan with setbacks, structural calculations stamped by a licensed engineer, energy compliance forms, soils report where required, contractor license and workers compensation on file.

atoms.obligation: Consolidate every reviewing discipline's comments into one correction letter per cycle and hold later cycles to prior issues.
atoms.lesson: Applicants lose faith when building, fire, planning, and engineering send comments serially over weeks, and when cycle three raises an issue that existed on cycle one. Route disciplines concurrently, set an internal due date shorter than the statutory one, and have a plan check coordinator merge comments with the code section cited for each. Restrict later cycles to unresolved items and genuinely new conditions the applicant's revisions created, which also protects staff when a project stalls.

atoms.obligation: Confirm whether the scope is exempt, eligible for over-the-counter issuance, or requires full review before quoting any timeline.
atoms.lesson: Most codes exempt one-story detached accessory structures under one hundred twenty square feet, fences under six or seven feet, painting, and flooring, while a like-for-like water heater swap still needs a plumbing permit. Over-the-counter typically covers reroofs, service upgrades, in-kind window replacement, and small remodels without structural change. Full review is triggered by changes to shear walls or bearing elements, flood zone or hillside overlays, historic resources, and additions crossing sprinkler or septic thresholds.

atoms.obligation: Legalize existing unpermitted work through a retroactive permit with exposure of concealed elements rather than ignoring it.
atoms.lesson: Retroactive permits apply the code in effect at issuance unless the owner proves the earlier construction date. The path is an as-built drawing set, a structural evaluation by a licensed engineer for anything load bearing, and selective demolition exposing framing, wiring, and connections for inspection. Investigation fees, often double the standard permit fee, must be in the adopted fee schedule to be charged. Egress windows, smoke alarms, and unsafe wiring are non-negotiable; some nonconformities can be legalized as legal nonconforming.

name: code-enforcement-abatement
description: Runs property maintenance and nuisance cases from complaint through compliance, citation, or abatement. Use when a property has accumulated junk, weeds, or an inoperable vehicle, when a notice of violation has expired with no compliance, when an owner requests an administrative hearing, or when the city must abate a condition itself and recover the cost.
expansions: weeds and junk complaint on a rental
notice of violation expired no compliance
owner requested an administrative hearing
inoperable vehicle in the front yard
vacant building is attracting trespassers
how do we recover abatement costs
repeat offender same address third time
neighbor says enforcement is selective

atoms.obligation: Serve the notice of violation on the record owner and any occupant, citing the section, the condition, and a compliance deadline.
atoms.lesson: Service defects sink more cases than the merits. Pull the owner of record from the current assessment roll, not the utility account, and serve by personal delivery or certified mail with posting on the property as backup, since many codes require both. The notice must identify the parcel by address and assessor number, cite the section violated, describe the condition factually, state what compliance looks like, give a reasonable time, ten to thirty days for maintenance and hours for hazards, and state appeal rights.

atoms.obligation: Document the condition with dated photographs and inspector observations at every visit, including visits that find compliance.
atoms.lesson: The city carries the burden at an administrative hearing and in cost recovery. Each entry should record date, time, weather where relevant, the vantage point whether public right of way or consented entry, and photographs oriented to a fixed landmark so before-and-after images are comparable. Never enter a fenced yard or structure without consent, an administrative warrant, or an exigent condition. A clean record of the abatement scope also determines which costs may be lien recovered.

atoms.obligation: Offer a documented compliance path with milestones before escalating, and escalate on a schedule applied to every case alike.
atoms.lesson: Selective enforcement claims are built from the file, not from intent. Set escalation tiers: courtesy notice, notice of violation, administrative citation with escalating fines, then abatement or criminal referral. For owners in genuine hardship, elderly, disabled, or on fixed income, a written compliance agreement with dated milestones works better than fines and is defensible when extended to similarly situated owners. Track cases by violation type so response times stay consistent across neighborhoods.

atoms.obligation: Follow the statutory abatement sequence of hearing, order, opportunity to abate, city abatement, and cost hearing before recording a lien.
atoms.lesson: Cost recovery fails when a step is skipped. The pattern is notice and opportunity to abate, an appeal hearing before a hearing officer or the council, a written order declaring the nuisance, a final period for the owner to act, then contracted abatement with itemized invoices. A separate noticed hearing confirms the cost report before it becomes a special assessment or lien. Emergency abatement of an imminent hazard may precede the hearing but still requires a prompt post-deprivation hearing on cost.

name: business-license-compliance
description: Handles business tax certificates and regulatory licenses, covering new applications, renewals, and revocations. Use when an applicant's use needs zoning clearance before a license can issue, when a business is operating without a license, when a regulated activity like massage, cannabis, or towing needs background clearance, or when a renewal is held for unpaid taxes or open code cases.
expansions: business operating without a license
renewal held for unpaid occupancy tax
does this use need zoning clearance first
massage establishment background check
home occupation with customer traffic
mobile vendor wants to park downtown
license revocation hearing notice
contractor working outside city limits

atoms.obligation: Verify zoning clearance and any required health, fire, or state licenses before issuing, recording each clearance in the file.
atoms.lesson: A business tax certificate is a revenue instrument, not a land use approval, but issuing one for a prohibited use creates a reliance argument. The clearance chain runs zoning conformance including parking and hours, fire inspection for assembly or hazardous materials, county health for food handling, state license for contractors, cosmetology, alcohol, or firearms dealers, and a conditional use permit where required. Print on the certificate that it confers no right to operate contrary to other law.

atoms.obligation: Classify the business correctly for tax purposes and apply the rate basis the ordinance names, not the applicant's self-description.
atoms.lesson: Tax bases differ sharply: gross receipts, employee count, square footage, flat rate by category, or rental unit count for landlords. Misclassification compounds because it repeats every renewal. Watch the edge cases: a contractor headquartered elsewhere still owes for work performed in the city, an online seller with a local warehouse is a wholesaler rather than a retailer, and a firm with several locations may owe per location. Apportionment rules matter for businesses operating across jurisdictions.

atoms.obligation: Give written notice with hearing rights before suspending or revoking a license, stating the specific grounds relied on.
atoms.lesson: A license, once issued, is a property interest, so revocation demands due process: written notice of grounds, reasonable time to prepare, a hearing before a neutral officer, the chance to present and cross-examine evidence, and a written decision with findings. Grounds must appear in the ordinance, such as fraud in the application, operating outside the permitted scope, a pattern of nuisance violations, or failure to remit taxes. Summary suspension is reserved for immediate threats and needs a prompt hearing after.

atoms.obligation: Pursue unlicensed operators with a compliance-first sequence and reserve penalties for those who continue after notice.
atoms.lesson: Most unlicensed businesses are new, small, or unaware, and a courtesy letter with an application and a short amnesty window converts them at far higher rates than a citation. Reserve penalties, commonly the tax owed for up to three prior years plus interest and a twenty-five to fifty percent penalty, for operators who continue after notice or concealed activity. Discovery sources that work include state sales tax permit lists, contractor permit pulls, signage surveys, and short-term rental listings.

name: capital-improvement-prioritization
description: Builds and defends the multi-year capital improvement program: which streets, pipes, and facilities get funded in which year and from which source. Use when the program is being updated, when a council member wants a project moved up, when a pavement or asset condition report needs turning into a funding recommendation, or when a project's costs have escalated past its appropriation.
expansions: capital program update due before budget
council member wants their street moved up
pavement condition report just landed
project came in over the appropriation
which fund can legally pay for this
do we have operating cost to run it
grant match deadline forces a reorder
deferred maintenance backlog keeps growing

atoms.obligation: Score every candidate project against published criteria and publish the scores rather than ranking by request order.
atoms.lesson: A defensible rubric weights condition or risk of failure, safety and liability exposure, regulatory mandate, cost of deferral, leverage of outside funding, geographic equity, and readiness to construct. Pavement management systems give a condition index from zero to one hundred, and the well-established curve shows a road dropping from seventy to fifty costs roughly six times more per lane mile than preventive work at eighty, which is why worst-first resurfacing bankrupts a program. Published scores let a council override a rank knowingly.

atoms.obligation: Match each project to a fund whose revenue may legally pay for it and state that restriction in the program.
atoms.lesson: Municipal money is layered and mostly restricted. Gas tax and highway user revenue generally fund streets only; water and sewer enterprise revenues fund their own systems and cannot subsidize the general fund; impact and development fees must fund capacity expansion rather than maintenance and carry accounting and refund deadlines; assessment district proceeds serve the district's parcels; and bond proceeds are limited to the stated purpose with arbitrage rules on spending pace. Mismatches surface as audit findings.

atoms.obligation: State each project's ongoing operating and maintenance cost and the year it begins, not only its construction cost.
atoms.lesson: A new park, pool, fire station, or roundabout hands the operating budget a permanent bill for staffing, utilities, insurance, and replacement reserve. Common planning factors run two to four percent of replacement value per year for building maintenance, plus full lifecycle replacement funding for vehicles and equipment. A splash pad funded by a grant with no maintenance appropriation is a closed splash pad in three summers. Show operating impact per project per year so the tradeoff is explicit.

atoms.obligation: Carry a contingency and escalation assumption on each project and rebaseline the program when a bid exceeds appropriation.
atoms.lesson: Concept-level estimates carry wide error, so program design contingency near twenty to thirty percent early, tightening toward ten percent at bid, plus construction escalation tied to a construction cost index rather than general inflation. When a bid comes in over, the options are additive alternates, rescoping, a supplemental appropriation with an identified source, or rejecting bids and rebidding at a better time of year, since rebidding late in a season usually costs more.

name: annual-budget-adoption
description: Runs the annual operating budget cycle from department requests through public hearing and adoption. Use when departments are submitting requests over target, when revenue projections shift mid-cycle, when the proposed budget does not balance, when a mid-year amendment or appropriation transfer is needed, or when preparing the required budget hearing and notices.
expansions: departments submitted requests over target
revenue forecast came in short
budget does not balance this year
need a mid year appropriation transfer
what goes in the hearing notice
one time money proposed for ongoing costs
reserve policy says we are below target
new position request with no funding source

atoms.obligation: Build revenue projections from named assumptions and show sensitivity rather than presenting a single point estimate.
atoms.lesson: Municipal revenue behaves differently by source: property tax lags the market by a year or more because of assessment cycles and caps such as the two percent annual limit under Proposition 13; sales tax swings quickly and concentrates in a handful of point-of-sale generators; transient occupancy tax tracks travel and events; and permit and development revenue is the most volatile of all and should never fund ongoing positions. State each assumption so a variance can be diagnosed.

atoms.obligation: Fund ongoing commitments with ongoing revenue and restrict one-time money to one-time uses, stating the distinction plainly.
atoms.lesson: Structural deficits hide inside balanced budgets when reserves, fund balance, asset sales, or a one-time state allocation cover recurring payroll. A new position costs its salary plus roughly forty to seventy percent in benefits, retirement contribution, and workers compensation, and pension costs rise with the actuarially determined contribution regardless of headcount. Show a two or three year forecast alongside the adopted year so the council sees the out-year gap a one-time-funded decision creates.

atoms.obligation: Hold the budget hearing with the notice the statute requires and record the adopting action separately from the tax levy.
atoms.lesson: State budget acts specify a sequence: publish the proposed budget for public inspection for a set period, publish a hearing notice in a newspaper of general circulation with the required lead time, hold the hearing before adoption, and adopt by resolution before the fiscal year begins, commonly by June 30. Truth-in-taxation states add advertised hearings when the levy exceeds the rolled-back rate. The levy is usually a separate action, certified to the county on a fixed date.

atoms.obligation: Route any change to total appropriations through a formal amendment and keep transfers within the limit policy sets.
atoms.lesson: Appropriation authority is legal, not advisory: spending beyond an adopted appropriation at the control level is a budget violation reported in the audit. A typical structure lets a manager move money between line items inside a department, requires manager approval between departments in one fund, and requires council action for any increase in a fund total or use of reserves. Record the funding source in the amendment, because 'absorbed within existing resources' hides the cost until year-end.

name: property-assessment-appeal
description: Supports the assessor's office and the clerk of the appeals board when property owners contest assessed value. Use when an owner files an appeal on a valuation, when a comparable sales or income analysis is needed to defend a value, when an exemption or homestead classification is in question, or when a supplemental or escape assessment is disputed.
expansions: owner appealed the new assessed value
need comparables to defend a value
income approach on an apartment building
homestead exemption denied and disputed
supplemental assessment after a sale
board hearing is next month
decline in value request from a homeowner
new construction assessed mid year

atoms.obligation: Confirm the appeal was filed within the statutory window and on the correct form before scheduling it for hearing.
atoms.lesson: Appeal windows are short and jurisdictional: regular assessment appeals often run July 2 to September 15 or November 30 depending on whether the county mails value notices, while supplemental and escape assessments run sixty days from the notice date. A late filing generally cannot be cured by the board however meritorious. Check that the applicant is the owner or an agent with signed authorization, that the parcel number matches, and that an opinion of value was stated, since a blank opinion is a common defect.

atoms.obligation: Support the value with adjusted comparable sales or with the valuation approach the property type actually demands.
atoms.lesson: Single-family and small residential property defends on sales comparison, with adjustments for time, size, condition, and location documented line by line from sales within the lien date window. Income-producing property defends on the income approach using market rent rather than contract rent, vacancy and collection loss, operating expenses excluding debt service and depreciation, and a capitalization rate supported by sales or a band-of-investment build-up. Special-purpose property falls back to cost less depreciation, and unreconciled approaches invite the board to pick the owner's number.

atoms.obligation: Apply the correct lien date and reassessment triggers, and explain to the owner in plain terms what caused the change.
atoms.lesson: Value is set as of a fixed lien date, January 1 in many states, and in acquisition-value states the base year changes only on a change in ownership or new construction, then grows by a capped inflation factor. Exclusions are frequently missed: transfers between spouses, parent-child transfers where still available, and adding a co-owner without changing beneficial interest. Repairs and normal maintenance are not new construction; adding conditioned square footage is. Decline-in-value relief is temporary and reverts as the market recovers.

atoms.obligation: Present the board an organized evidence package exchanged in advance and state which party carries the burden of proof.
atoms.lesson: The burden generally sits with the applicant but shifts to the assessor for owner-occupied single-family homes in some states and for escape assessments. Where an exchange of information is properly requested, both sides produce comparables and data before the hearing and are limited at hearing to what they exchanged plus rebuttal. Board decisions must state the value found and the basis, since a decision without findings, when findings were requested, is vulnerable on appeal to superior court on the record.

name: utility-billing-adjustment
description: Resolves water, sewer, and refuse billing disputes and account problems. Use when a customer receives a bill several times their normal usage, when a leak adjustment is requested, when service is scheduled for shutoff over nonpayment, when a landlord-tenant account transfer goes wrong, or when a meter reading looks implausible.
expansions: bill is four times the normal amount
customer requesting a leak adjustment
shutoff scheduled and customer called
meter read looks wrong on this account
tenant moved out with a balance
broken irrigation line ran all month
customer wants a payment arrangement
estimated reads for three months straight

atoms.obligation: Verify the meter reading and test the meter before adjusting a bill or telling the customer they have a leak.
atoms.lesson: High-bill investigations follow a fixed order: re-read the meter, compare against the prior twelve months and the same month last year, check whether an estimated read under-billed and then trued up, then run a leak test by closing the customer valve and watching the low-flow indicator. Meters almost always slow with age rather than over-register, so a genuine spike is usually a running toilet at roughly two hundred gallons a day, a stuck irrigation valve, or a filled pool. Document the test first.

atoms.obligation: Apply the leak adjustment policy as written, requiring the same proof and repair evidence from every customer.
atoms.lesson: A workable policy fixes its elements: eligibility once in a defined period, a leak on the customer side that was not visible or reasonably discoverable, repair documented by a plumber invoice or inspection, and relief computed as a percentage of the excess above average usage, commonly fifty percent and often only the volumetric portion. Sewer charges based on winter water use are usually credited fully for an outdoor leak, since that water never entered the sewer. Ad hoc forgiveness creates the next customer's discrimination claim.

atoms.obligation: Give the notice, hearing opportunity, and medical or hardship protections required before shutting off service for nonpayment.
atoms.lesson: Shutoff rules have tightened in many states: written notice in the customer's language at a set number of days, a second notice or door hanger before the crew arrives, a published policy posted online, an amortization plan of at least twelve months, and a bar on shutoff where a household member's health depends on service and a physician certifies it. Seasonal moratoria during extreme heat or cold are common, reconnection fees are often capped, and restoration must follow payment promptly.

atoms.obligation: Close and transfer accounts on actual service dates with a final read, pursuing the correct responsible party for the balance.
atoms.lesson: Landlord-tenant transitions cause most write-offs. Bill to the date of the final read rather than the lease date, and where the ordinance makes charges a lien on the property, notify the owner of tenant delinquency within the statutory timeframe or the lien right is lost. Owner-of-record liability differs by state and often depends on whether the owner requested notification. Apply deposits to the final bill before referral, and write off small residual balances under a policy threshold rather than sending them to collections.

name: formal-bid-solicitation
description: Runs competitive procurement: invitations to bid, requests for proposals, and the award recommendation. Use when a purchase crosses the formal bid threshold, when writing specifications that must not favor one vendor, when a bidder protests an award, when a bid contains an irregularity, or when deciding between low-bid and qualifications-based selection.
expansions: purchase is over the formal bid threshold
bidder protested the award
low bidder forgot the bid bond
spec looks written for one vendor
can we piggyback another agency contract
sole source justification needed
prevailing wage applies to this project
evaluation committee disagrees on scoring

atoms.obligation: Select the procurement method by dollar threshold and type of work, and document the choice before soliciting.
atoms.lesson: Thresholds are set by charter, ordinance, and state code, and public works usually carries a lower one than supplies. A common structure is informal quotes under a first tier, three written quotes at a second, and formal sealed bids above it. Public works is awarded to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder without negotiation, while professional services such as engineering, architecture, and surveying must be selected on qualifications with price negotiated after, under the Brooks Act and its state analogues.

atoms.obligation: Write specifications by performance and function, and where a brand is named, state that equivalents are acceptable with criteria.
atoms.lesson: Specifications drafted from one manufacturer's cut sheet, matching a unique dimension, proprietary connector, or model-specific feature, are the most common basis for a protest and for audit findings. Where standardization is genuinely required for parts, training, or interoperability, adopt a sole-source or standardization finding before soliciting. 'Or approved equal' needs a substitution deadline before bid opening and objective criteria, otherwise the reviewer is deciding equivalence after prices are already known.

atoms.obligation: Evaluate bids for responsiveness first, then responsibility, distinguishing a waivable irregularity from a material one.
atoms.lesson: Responsiveness concerns the bid: did it conform to the solicitation. Responsibility concerns the bidder: capacity, experience, license, past performance, bonding. Material deviations that cannot be waived are those giving a competitive advantage or an option to walk, such as a missing bid bond or signature, a conditional bid, or an omitted unit price. Minor irregularities like a missing page number may be waived if documented and applied consistently. Finding a bidder non-responsible requires notice and a chance to be heard.

atoms.obligation: Publish the protest procedure with deadlines and decide protests in writing before the award becomes final.
atoms.lesson: A protest process protects the award as much as the bidder. Standard terms: protest filed within five business days of bid opening or of notice of intent to award, stating specific grounds and relief sought; a written staff response; an appeal to the manager or council; and no contract execution until resolution. Protests of the specifications must be filed before bid opening, since a bidder cannot bid, lose, then attack the spec. Keep evaluators' individual score sheets, because they become the record.

name: grant-subrecipient-compliance
description: Manages federal and state grant awards after acceptance: the reporting, procurement, and audit obligations that attach to the money. Use when accepting an award and reading its terms, when a drawdown or reimbursement request is due, when a monitoring visit or single audit is scheduled, when a cost may be unallowable, or when passing funds through to a nonprofit subrecipient.
expansions: award letter arrived with terms attached
reimbursement request due this quarter
monitoring visit scheduled next month
is this cost allowable under the award
single audit threshold question
subrecipient has not reported in months
performance period ends with funds left
match documentation is thin

atoms.obligation: Read the award terms and build a compliance calendar of every report, drawdown, and closeout date before spending funds.
atoms.lesson: Federal awards carry the notice of award terms, the program regulations, and the Uniform Guidance in 2 CFR Part 200 simultaneously, and the strictest applies. Extract the period of performance, pre-award cost eligibility date, financial and performance report frequencies, drawdown method, match type and amount, prior-approval triggers such as budget shifts beyond ten percent or new equipment, and closeout deadlines, usually ninety to one hundred twenty days after the end date. A missed report can suspend payments across every award held.

atoms.obligation: Test each cost against allowability, allocability, and reasonableness, keeping documentation that proves the connection.
atoms.lesson: A cost must be necessary and reasonable for the award, allocable in proportion to benefit, consistent with how the municipality treats the same cost on non-federal work, and not excluded by the cost principles. Personnel charges need after-the-fact time and effort records tied to actual activity rather than budget estimates. Common disallowances include entertainment, lobbying, fines and penalties, bad debt, and equipment outside the approved budget. Indirect costs come through a negotiated rate or the ten percent de minimis rate, claimed consistently.

atoms.obligation: Follow federal procurement standards on grant-funded purchases even when local rules are looser, and check exclusion status.
atoms.lesson: Uniform Guidance procurement adds requirements local codes often lack: full and open competition, written procurement procedures, cost or price analysis above the simplified acquisition threshold, affirmative steps to solicit minority, women's, and small businesses, and a prohibition on geographic preference except where state licensing applies. Verify the contractor is not suspended or debarred before award and document the check. Construction awards trigger Davis-Bacon wage determinations and bonding requirements on larger contracts.

atoms.obligation: Monitor pass-through subrecipients with a risk assessment, written agreements, and documented review of reports and audits.
atoms.lesson: A pass-through entity answers for what its subrecipients do with the money. The agreement must carry the federal award identification number, the assistance listing number, the indirect rate, and all applicable terms. Assess risk from prior experience, audit findings, personnel turnover, and program complexity, then match monitoring intensity to it, with desk review of invoices at minimum and site visits for higher risk. Where a subrecipient expends a million dollars or more in federal funds, obtain and follow up on its single audit.

name: service-request-triage
description: Handles resident service requests arriving by phone, app, or walk-in: routing them, setting expectations, and closing the loop. Use when a request queue is backing up, when a resident says nobody called them back, when deciding which department owns an issue that crosses boundaries, or when setting or reporting on response time targets.
expansions: resident says nobody called them back
pothole reported three weeks ago
which department owns this issue
request queue is backing up
caller escalating to the mayor's office
streetlight out on a utility pole
duplicate reports for the same location
what response times should we promise

atoms.obligation: Route by asset ownership and jurisdiction first, and tell the resident who owns the problem when the city does not.
atoms.lesson: A large share of municipal service requests belong to someone else: streetlights on utility-owned poles, state highways running through town as a main street, county-maintained roads inside city limits, school district property, and sidewalk maintenance many codes assign to the adjacent property owner. Maintain a routing reference by asset type and location with the correct external contact and expected turnaround. Handing a resident a phone number without transferring the request is the most common source of a second, angrier call.

atoms.obligation: Set the response commitment by request type at intake, distinguishing acknowledgment time from resolution time.
atoms.lesson: Residents accept long timelines and reject silence. Publish tiered targets: same-day for hazards such as a downed sign, water main break, or signal outage; forty-eight to seventy-two hours for acknowledgment of routine requests; and seasonal windows for work that batches, such as pothole patching waiting on the asphalt plant or tree trimming on a grid cycle. Say which tier applies at intake, so a pothole call ends with the resident knowing it is on the next patch route.

atoms.obligation: Merge duplicate reports of one condition into a single case and notify every reporter when the work is done.
atoms.lesson: One failed streetlight can generate a dozen reports from one block, and closing eleven silently produces eleven residents who believe the city ignored them. Deduplicate on location and asset identifier, keep every reporter attached to the parent case, and send closure notice to all of them describing what was done. Duplicate volume is also a useful priority signal, since five reports at one intersection usually indicates a genuinely worse condition than a single report elsewhere.

atoms.obligation: Close a request only after verifying the work, recording what was done, and reopen rather than re-create on a callback.
atoms.lesson: Closure quality is what audits and council inquiries examine. A useful closure records the crew or contractor, the date, and the action, such as patched a four by six foot area with cold mix, temporary until the June overlay, rather than merely completed. Flag temporary fixes so a follow-up is scheduled instead of a new complaint arriving. Reopening the original case preserves true elapsed time, while creating a new one resets the clock and flatters the performance report.

name: special-event-permit
description: Reviews applications for parades, street fairs, races, farmers markets, and other events using public streets or parks. Use when an organizer applies close to the event date, when a route needs police and traffic control, when alcohol or amplified sound is involved, when insurance and indemnification are being negotiated, or when event cost recovery is in question.
expansions: parade route needs traffic control
organizer applied two weeks out
alcohol service in a public park
amplified sound near residences
insurance certificate names wrong entity
road race wants to close a highway
food booths need health clearance
neighbors complained about last year's event

atoms.obligation: Enforce the application deadline tied to event size and complexity and state what an incomplete late application forfeits.
atoms.lesson: Lead time exists because other agencies need it: transit reroutes typically need thirty days, state highway encroachment for a route on a state road sixty or more, and state alcohol licenses thirty to forty-five days. Common tiers run thirty days for a block party and sixty to ninety for events over a few thousand attendees or involving closures. First Amendment activity is the exception, since spontaneous demonstrations responding to breaking events cannot be barred for missing a deadline, so include a waiver path.

atoms.obligation: Base conditions and fees on the event's operational impact, applying content-neutral standards to expressive events.
atoms.lesson: Permit schemes touching speech must be content neutral, narrowly tailored, leave open alternative channels, and give officials no unbridled discretion. Charge for measurable services actually provided, such as traffic control officers at loaded hourly rates, barricade delivery, refuse and restroom service, and park staffing, never for anticipated crowd hostility, which is an unconstitutional heckler's veto. Fee waiver policies need written criteria, and access concerns are handled by conditioning on a twenty-foot fire lane rather than denying the route.

atoms.obligation: Require insurance naming the municipality as additional insured at limits matched to the risk, with indemnification in the permit.
atoms.lesson: Typical requirements are one million per occurrence and two million aggregate in general liability for a standard event, rising for races, carnival rides, fireworks, or alcohol, plus liquor liability where alcohol is served and auto liability where vehicles are in a parade. The certificate must name the municipality, its officials, and employees as additional insured by endorsement rather than a checked box, and be primary and non-contributory. Vendors and inflatable operators carry their own coverage, verified before issuance.

atoms.obligation: Convene the reviewing departments together for events above a complexity threshold and issue one conditioned permit.
atoms.lesson: Police, fire, public works, parks, risk management, and county health each hold a practical veto, and serial review turns a sixty-day lead into a twenty-day scramble. A standing event review meeting produces one permit with the site plan attached showing route, closure points, staging, emergency vehicle access lanes, restroom and refuse placement, and fire department occupancy limits for tents and cooking. Post-event debriefs on complaints and cleanup should carry into next year's conditions rather than being relitigated.

name: encroachment-permit-review
description: Controls work in the public right of way: utility cuts, driveway approaches, sidewalk closures, dumpsters, and construction staging. Use when a contractor wants to trench a street, when a newly paved street is under moratorium, when a sidewalk closure needs a pedestrian detour, when restoration has failed, or when a franchise utility claims it does not need a permit.
expansions: contractor wants to trench a new street
pavement moratorium on that block
sidewalk closure with no pedestrian detour
trench patch already failing after a year
utility says they do not need a permit
dumpster sitting in the parking lane
driveway approach cut without approval
who inspects the backfill compaction

atoms.obligation: Require a permit with traffic control and restoration details before any work in the right of way, franchise utilities included.
atoms.lesson: Franchise agreements grant utilities the right to occupy the right of way, not to skip municipal permits and standards for how and when they work. The submittal should carry limits of work, a traffic control plan conforming to the national traffic control manual with the applicable typical application, the trench section and backfill specification, restoration limits, dates and hours, and evidence of insurance and bond. Emergency work is the exception, permitted after the fact within twenty-four to forty-eight hours.

atoms.obligation: Apply the pavement cut moratorium on recently surfaced streets and require enhanced restoration when an exception is granted.
atoms.lesson: A trench cut in new asphalt materially shortens remaining pavement life, so most cities impose a moratorium, typically five years after reconstruction and three after an overlay, with exceptions only for emergencies and service connections with no alternative. Price the exception into the restoration standard: half-width or full-width grind and overlay across the block rather than a T-patch, an extended warranty, or a degradation fee scaled to remaining life. Publish the paving schedule a year ahead so utilities can consolidate.

atoms.obligation: Maintain an accessible pedestrian route past the work zone or provide a compliant detour, never merely a closed sign.
atoms.lesson: Federal access rules require a route past construction that is stable, firm, and slip resistant, at least forty-eight inches wide and sixty where the route is long, with detectable edging traversable by a cane, ramps at grade changes, and signage placed at the last point where crossing is possible rather than at the closure. Closing a sidewalk and pushing pedestrians into a travel lane is both a liability exposure and a complaint magnet, and a wheelchair user backtracking a block will file formally.

atoms.obligation: Hold a restoration bond or deposit and inspect compaction and final surface before release, with a warranty period after acceptance.
atoms.lesson: Failed trench patches are the most visible sign of weak right-of-way control. The controls that work are inspection at open trench for bedding and pipe zone, compaction testing at specified lifts to a stated relative compaction, a temporary patch within twenty-four to seventy-two hours, permanent restoration within a set number of days, and a warranty of one to two years covering settlement. Release the bond only after a warranty inspection; blanket bonds for annual permittees still run warranty per location.

name: stormwater-permit-compliance
description: Keeps the municipality's stormwater discharge permit obligations on track: inspections, illicit discharge investigations, construction site oversight, and the annual report. Use when a discharge is spotted at an outfall or creek, when a construction site is tracking sediment into the street, when the annual report is due to the state board, or when a permit renewal adds new requirements.
expansions: oily sheen at the outfall
sediment tracking off a construction site
annual report due to the state board
someone dumped paint in a storm drain
new permit term added requirements
restaurant washing mats into the gutter
inspection frequency for treatment facilities
illicit connection found during a camera run

atoms.obligation: Investigate a suspected illicit discharge promptly, trace it to the source, and document the finding and correction.
atoms.lesson: A municipal separate storm sewer permit requires a program to detect and eliminate non-stormwater discharges, with written procedures and response timeframes. Field triage notes color, odor, turbidity, floatables, and flow during dry weather, samples where the discharge may be hazardous, then works upstream manhole by manhole with dye or smoke testing. Exempted flows generally include firefighting, uncontaminated groundwater, irrigation runoff, and residential car washing, while sewage, mobile wash water, and chlorinated pool discharges are enforcement matters.

atoms.obligation: Inspect construction sites at the permit frequency and require correction of sediment controls before the next rain event.
atoms.lesson: Sites disturbing one acre or more need coverage under the state construction general permit with a pollution prevention plan kept on site, though municipal ordinances routinely reach smaller sites. What actually fails: stabilized construction entrances too short to shake mud off tires, inlet protection installed but never cleaned, silt fence trenched too shallow or run across concentrated flow where only a check dam works, and stockpiles left uncovered before a forecast storm. Track corrections to closure with dated photographs.

atoms.obligation: Verify post-construction treatment facilities are maintained by the owner under a recorded maintenance agreement.
atoms.lesson: Bioretention cells, permeable pavement, and detention basins fail silently as they clog. Permits require a mechanism ensuring long-term maintenance, usually a covenant recorded against the land plus municipal verification inspection every one to five years. Look for ponding beyond the design drawdown time of forty-eight to seventy-two hours, sediment accumulation at the forebay, mulch and vegetation loss, and permeable pavement never vacuumed. Keep the facility inventory current at occupancy, since an unrecorded system is one nobody inspects.

atoms.obligation: Compile the annual report from records kept through the year, reporting shortfalls honestly with a corrective schedule.
atoms.lesson: The report typically covers inspections performed against those required, illicit discharge cases opened and closed, outreach and public participation, training delivered, monitoring results, and progress against any total maximum daily load waste load allocation the receiving water carries. Regulators respond far better to a reported gap with a dated corrective plan than to a clean report contradicted at the next audit. Retain inspection records for the permit period, commonly three to five years, and make them publicly available where required.

name: winter-operations-readiness
description: Plans and runs snow and ice control: route priorities, material stockpiles, crew callout, and public communication. Use when preparing the seasonal plan, when a forecast triggers a pretreatment decision, when residents complain about a plowed-in driveway or an unplowed street, or when reviewing material use and overtime after a storm.
expansions: storm forecast tomorrow do we pretreat
residents complaining about plowed in driveways
salt stockpile running low mid season
which routes get plowed first
overtime blew past the storm budget
school district asking about morning routes
brine versus rock salt in this temperature
unplowed cul de sac third day

atoms.obligation: Publish route priority tiers before the season and hold to them during a storm rather than chasing individual calls.
atoms.lesson: Standard tiering puts emergency routes, arterials, hospital and fire station approaches, and main hills first; collectors, school zones, and transit routes second; and residential streets and cul-de-sacs third, often not started until snowfall ends and primaries are stable. Publishing the map with an honest statement that residential streets may take twenty-four to forty-eight hours after a storm ends converts most complaints into understanding. Diverting a plow off route costs more time than the single pass saves.

atoms.obligation: Choose material and application rate from pavement temperature and precipitation type rather than air temperature or habit.
atoms.lesson: Rock salt loses effectiveness sharply as pavement temperature drops, with a practical working range down to about fifteen to twenty degrees Fahrenheit and treated salt or a magnesium or calcium chloride blend needed below that. Anti-icing with brine before a storm at roughly twenty to forty gallons per lane mile prevents bonding and uses far less chloride than deicing afterward. Do not apply brine ahead of freezing rain or onto wet pavement that dilutes it, and prewet at the spinner to cut bounce loss.

atoms.obligation: Set callout triggers, shift rotation, and hours-of-service limits in advance of the storm rather than during it.
atoms.lesson: Fatigue drives plow crashes late in long events. Build twelve-hour shifts with a defined relief plan, name who authorizes callout and at what forecast trigger, commonly one inch predicted or any freezing rain, and identify mechanic and fuel access at three in the morning. Track overtime against the storm reserve as the event runs, since a heavy December drains a budget built for an average season. Confirm before the season that operators hold current commercial licenses and have driven their route in daylight.

atoms.obligation: Communicate before, during, and after the storm with specific expectations, parking rules, and residents' own obligations.
atoms.lesson: The messages that reduce call volume are concrete: when the snow emergency parking ban starts and where towing applies, which route tier is running now, that plows will push snow across driveway aprons and clearing the apron is the resident's job, and the ordinance deadline for clearing an abutting sidewalk, often twenty-four hours after snowfall ends. Publish route status at fixed intervals during long events and include the mailbox damage claim process, the highest-volume post-storm complaint.

name: local-emergency-declaration
description: Guides the steps a municipality takes when an incident exceeds routine response: declaring a local emergency, activating the emergency operations center, and preparing for state and federal reimbursement. Use when a flood, wildfire, storm, or major utility failure hits, when the council must ratify a proclamation, when mutual aid is requested, or when disaster cost documentation must begin.
expansions: flooding overwhelmed our own crews
do we need to declare a local emergency
council has to ratify the proclamation
requesting mutual aid from the county
how do we track disaster costs
opening a shelter tonight
damage assessment needed for the state
debris contractor without a bid process

atoms.obligation: Declare the local emergency promptly with findings of conditions beyond local capacity and ratify it within the statutory window.
atoms.lesson: A proclamation is the legal hinge: it activates emergency powers such as suspending competitive bidding, authorizing emergency expenditures, imposing curfews, and ordering evacuations, and it is a prerequisite for requesting county, state, and eventual federal assistance. Where an official proclaims outside a council meeting, most statutes require the governing body to ratify within seven days and to review continuation at intervals until terminated. State the specific conditions and geography covered, since a generic proclamation complicates later reimbursement.

atoms.obligation: Stand up the operations center with a clear command structure and separate policy decisions from tactical incident command.
atoms.lesson: Under incident command structure the field incident commander runs tactics while the operations center supports with resources, information, and policy, staffed by section chiefs for operations, planning, logistics, and finance and administration. Elected officials belong in a policy group deciding evacuation orders, curfews, resource commitments, and public messaging, not in the operations room directing crews. Set operational periods, usually twelve hours, with a written incident action plan for each, because reimbursement and after-action review depend on that record.

atoms.obligation: Begin disaster cost documentation from the first hour with separate cost coding for labor, equipment, materials, and contracts.
atoms.lesson: Federal public assistance generally reimburses seventy-five percent of eligible costs, and eligibility turns on documentation quality. Track force account labor by employee, hours, and task with the regular and overtime split, since for emergency protective measures straight time for permanent employees is often ineligible while overtime is eligible; equipment hours at published federal rates by type; materials drawn from stock with invoices; and mutual aid under a written agreement. Photograph damage with location and date before repairs.

atoms.obligation: Use emergency procurement only for the immediate life-safety window and return to competitive process for recovery work.
atoms.lesson: Emergency proclamations relax bidding rules, but auditors later disallow costs that were not truly urgent. Time-and-materials contracts are acceptable only for a short initial period, generally up to seventy hours, and must convert to fixed unit price or lump sum. Avoid cost-plus-percentage-of-cost structures entirely, since they are prohibited in federally funded work. Debris removal should ride a pre-positioned contract competitively bid before the season, with a separate monitoring firm, because a hauler cannot verify its own volumes.

name: ada-transition-plan
description: Manages the municipality's accessibility obligations for programs and public facilities: self-evaluation, the transition plan, curb ramps, and complaint handling. Use when a resident reports an inaccessible facility or meeting, when a paving project triggers curb ramp obligations, when a grievance is filed, or when the transition plan needs updating with priorities and a schedule.
expansions: resident cannot access the counter
paving project triggers curb ramps
grievance filed about a public meeting
transition plan has not been updated
captioning for council meetings
park path is not accessible
who is our accessibility coordinator
accessible parking count at the library

atoms.obligation: Designate a coordinator, publish a grievance procedure, and respond to accessibility complaints within a stated timeframe.
atoms.lesson: Public entities with fifty or more employees must designate a responsible employee and adopt a grievance procedure providing prompt and equitable resolution, and publish notice of accessibility rights where the public can find it. A workable procedure names how to file including alternate formats, a response deadline of fifteen to thirty days, an appeal path, and record retention. Track complaints by facility and program, since they surface systemic gaps. A procedure existing only in a binder is treated by investigators as absent.

atoms.obligation: Rebuild curb ramps to current standards whenever a street is altered, using the resurfacing trigger as the schedule driver.
atoms.lesson: Federal guidance treats resurfacing, including overlays and mill and fill work that extends pavement life, as an alteration requiring compliant curb ramps at every affected crossing, while crack sealing and pothole patching are maintenance and do not trigger it. Current standards call for running slope no steeper than 8.33 percent, cross slope at or under two percent, a level landing, and a detectable warning surface with truncated domes. Budget ramps inside the paving project, since retrofitting afterward costs far more.

atoms.obligation: Build the transition plan with a facility inventory, identified barriers, a dated removal schedule, and the responsible official.
atoms.lesson: A compliant transition plan has four required elements and most municipal plans fail the last two. Inventory every facility and program location, list each physical barrier with its location, set a schedule showing what is removed in which year, and name the official responsible for implementation. Prioritize by public contact, so entrances, counters, restrooms, and connecting paths come before back-of-house areas, and routes to transit and schools before low-traffic paths. Update annually and keep it publicly available.

atoms.obligation: Provide program access through auxiliary aids and, where a facility cannot be made accessible, by relocating or redesigning the program.
atoms.lesson: The obligation runs to the program, not only the building. A historic city hall with no elevator can meet program access by moving the meeting to an accessible room, and a permit counter by serving a resident at an accessible table. Effective communication requires auxiliary aids with primary consideration given to the requester's preference, including interpreters, real-time captioning for meetings, large print, and accessible electronic formats. Publish the request notice period, commonly forty-eight to seventy-two hours, with every meeting notice.

name: vital-records-issuance
description: Handles the clerk's records counter: birth and death certificate copies, marriage licenses, and related filings. Use when an applicant's identification does not meet the requirement, when someone requests a record they may not be entitled to, when a record contains an error needing amendment, or when a marriage license raises residency, waiting period, or confidential license questions.
expansions: applicant identification does not match
who is entitled to a certified copy
name misspelled on a death certificate
confidential marriage license question
out of state couple wants to marry here
request has fraud red flags
amend a record after an adoption
funeral home filing a death record late

atoms.obligation: Verify entitlement to a certified copy against the statutory list of authorized persons before issuing, offering an informational copy otherwise.
atoms.lesson: Certified copies of birth and death records are restricted in most states to the registrant, a parent or legal guardian, a spouse or domestic partner, a child, grandparent, grandchild or sibling, a party entitled by court order, and law enforcement or attorneys acting in a matter. Requesters sign a sworn statement of relationship under penalty of perjury. Where an informational copy exists, it carries a legend that it cannot establish identity, which is the right answer for a genealogist rather than refusing service.

atoms.obligation: Check the identification presented against the accepted list and reject expired or mismatched documents without exception.
atoms.lesson: Identity fraud at the records counter feeds downstream identity theft, so the accepted list is fixed: unexpired government-issued photo identification, with secondary document combinations allowed in some states when no photo document exists. The name on the identification must match the stated relationship path, and a maiden name change needs supporting documentation. Red flags worth supervisor review include a requester who cannot state the registrant's date of birth or parents' names, several unrelated requests at once, and pressure to hurry.

atoms.obligation: Route corrections and amendments through the state registrar's affidavit or petition process rather than altering a record at the counter.
atoms.lesson: A local office cannot edit a vital record. Minor typographic corrections within a defined window after filing may go on an affidavit with supporting documents predating the event, while later or substantive changes to parentage, sex designation, or a name require a court order or the state's amendment petition and produce an amended record with the amendment noted. Adoption and paternity actions generate a new record with the original sealed. Set expectations on state processing time, often several weeks to months.

atoms.obligation: Apply marriage license rules on residency, waiting period, expiration, and confidential licenses before collecting the fee.
atoms.lesson: Most states impose no residency requirement for a license, but the license is valid only for ceremonies within the issuing state and expires, commonly in thirty to ninety days, with some states imposing a waiting period between issuance and ceremony. Confidential licenses, where they exist, require the couple to be living together, are not public record, and are searchable only by court order. Both parties must appear with identification, minors need court and parental consent, and the officiant must return the license within the statutory window.

name: municipal-election-administration
description: Covers the clerk's election duties: calling the election, candidate filing and qualification, ballot measures, campaign finance filings, and the canvass. Use when candidate nomination papers are being taken, when a measure must be placed on the ballot with impartial analysis and arguments, when a campaign statement is late, or when a recount or contest is threatened.
expansions: candidate nomination papers due friday
signature check on nomination petitions
placing a measure on the ballot
impartial analysis and rebuttal deadlines
campaign statement filed late
write in candidate qualification
recount request after certification
consolidating with the county election

atoms.obligation: Publish the election calendar working backward from election day and treat every filing deadline as jurisdictional.
atoms.lesson: The calendar is a chain of fixed intervals: the resolution calling the election and requesting consolidation with the county, a nomination period typically opening one hundred thirteen days and closing eighty-eight days before the election, a five-day extension when an incumbent does not file, ballot measure submission with argument and rebuttal deadlines, the random alphabet drawing for ballot order, and the canvass and certification window. Miss the consolidation request and the city funds a standalone election at many times the cost.

atoms.obligation: Review nomination papers for form and signature sufficiency during the filing period and give the candidate time to cure.
atoms.lesson: Verification is ministerial but exacting: signers must be registered voters in the district as of signing, the required count typically runs twenty to thirty signatures with candidates encouraged to gather extra, signatures must fall inside the nomination period, and the candidate must be a registered voter residing in the jurisdiction. Check the ballot designation against rules limiting it to a principal profession or an incumbent title rather than a slogan. Once accepted, most states bar withdrawal, so say so before the candidate signs.

atoms.obligation: Prepare the impartial analysis and manage arguments and rebuttals within statutory word limits and the priority order.
atoms.lesson: The attorney's impartial analysis, commonly capped at five hundred words, explains what a yes and a no vote mean and the measure's legal effect without advocating. Arguments run to three hundred words with rebuttals at two hundred fifty, and where competing arguments are submitted, statutory priority favors the governing body or its members, then bona fide associations, then individual voters. All are subject to a public examination period during which a court can order corrections, and public funds may not be spent on advocacy.

atoms.obligation: Track campaign finance filings against their deadlines and notify late filers of the accruing penalty in writing.
atoms.lesson: Filing obligations attach as soon as a candidate raises or spends above the threshold, often two thousand dollars, with semiannual statements, preelection statements at fixed intervals, and twenty-four-hour reports for large late contributions in the final stretch. Late filing penalties commonly accrue at ten dollars per day. The clerk receives filings, makes them available for public inspection, and refers rather than adjudicates, since enforcement sits with the state ethics body. Keep written notification records, because penalties are challenged for lack of notice.

name: traffic-calming-petition
description: Evaluates neighborhood requests for speed humps, all-way stops, crosswalks, and other traffic control on residential streets. Use when residents petition about speeding, when someone demands a stop sign to slow traffic, when a school crossing is requested, or when a speed study contradicts what neighbors report.
expansions: neighbors petitioning for speed humps
demand for a stop sign to slow traffic
speed study contradicts what residents say
school crossing guard request
crosswalk where a pedestrian was hit
cut through traffic from the new development
fire department objects to speed humps
how many signatures does the petition need

atoms.obligation: Collect speed, volume, and collision data before recommending any device, and share the results with the petitioners.
atoms.lesson: A seven-day tube or radar count gives the numbers that matter: the eighty-fifth percentile speed, average daily volume, and the directional and hourly pattern, plus three to five years of collision history from the state database. Most neighborhood speeding complaints measure within a few miles per hour of the posted limit, and the real issue is volume or a handful of repeat drivers, often residents. Sharing data early converts a confrontation into a joint problem and usually points toward enforcement rather than construction.

atoms.obligation: Refuse stop signs and posted limit reductions as speed control devices and explain the engineering basis to requesters.
atoms.lesson: Stop control is warranted by intersection sight distance, volume, and collision patterns, not by mid-block speeding, and unwarranted stops produce high noncompliance, rolling stops, added noise and emissions, and speeding between intersections to make up time. Speed limits on most streets are set by an engineering and traffic survey near the eighty-fifth percentile, and in many states an unjustified posted limit is unenforceable by radar. Say this plainly with alternatives before the council promises a sign.

atoms.obligation: Select devices by street classification, emergency response route status, and grade, consulting the fire department before committing.
atoms.lesson: Vertical deflection belongs on local residential streets carrying roughly five hundred to four thousand vehicles daily, with speeds at or above thirty in a twenty-five zone, grades under eight percent, and no transit or primary emergency route. Each speed hump costs a fire apparatus several seconds and jars patients, so departments often accept speed cushions with wheel gaps that let apparatus straddle, or lateral treatments such as chicanes, medians, curb extensions, and mini roundabouts instead. Get the chief's position in writing first.

atoms.obligation: Require documented neighborhood support and notify every affected household, including parallel streets traffic may shift onto.
atoms.lesson: Programs commonly require a petition from sixty to seventy percent of households fronting the affected segment, with a confirmation vote after a trial installation. Notify the whole affected area rather than only signers, and include streets that may receive diverted traffic, since the most bitter disputes arise when one block's calming pushes cut-through traffic onto the next. Publish the removal path too, because a stated period after which residents may petition for removal makes trial installations politically possible.

name: shot-list-breakdown
description: Turns a script, treatment or storyboard into a shootable shot list organised by location and setup. Use when a director hands over a draft and asks what needs covering, when a producer wants to know how many setups realistically fit in a day, or when a read-through exposes a scene with no coverage.
expansions: director sent a script to break down
how many setups fit in a day
need a shot list for tomorrow
no coverage for the interview scene
turn the storyboard into setups
scene list for the schedule
which lens for each scene
b-roll list for the shoot day

atoms.obligation: Group shots by location and lighting setup rather than script order so the day is shot with the fewest moves.
atoms.lesson: A company move eats sixty to ninety minutes and a full relight of an interior around forty-five. Ordering by unit, shooting every wide on one axis then working tighter before turning around, keeps the key light in place. Scene twelve and scene thirty-four shoot back to back if they share the kitchen. Flag in the list where costume or time-of-day continuity forbids that regrouping.

atoms.obligation: State frame size, lens, movement and camera support for every listed shot instead of a prose description of the action.
atoms.lesson: A shot list the crew can act on reads: 2 of 3, MCU Sarah, 50mm, slow push on slider, camera left of the eyeline. Grip needs slider versus dolly versus handheld to pre-rig; the focus puller needs the lens to lay out the prime set and matte box. Entries like cover the conversation produce a missing size that only surfaces in the assembly.

atoms.obligation: Mark which shots the sequence cannot be cut without and which can be dropped if the day runs behind.
atoms.lesson: Carry a priority column: A for shots without which the scene will not cut, B for coverage giving the editor options, C for texture and cutaways. When the first assistant director says at four o'clock that two setups are gone, the director drops C then B without an argument on the floor. A normally means a clean master or two-shot plus a matched single on each speaker.

atoms.obligation: Estimate setup time per shot and total it against the hours actually available after rigging, travel and meal breaks.
atoms.lesson: Budget twenty to thirty minutes per setup for interior dialogue and forty-five or more for anything needing a relight, track or crowd. From a twelve-hour day subtract the pre-call rig, an hour for lunch and a wrap window, leaving roughly eight productive hours, so sixteen to twenty setups. Listing more than that on paper is how overtime gets booked.

name: call-sheet-assembly
description: Builds and reissues the daily call sheet for a shoot: per-department call times, locations, schedule, contacts and safety information. Use when tomorrow's shoot needs paperwork out tonight, when a location or time changes mid-prep, or when crew are asking where unit base is and what time they are needed.
expansions: call sheet for tomorrow's shoot
crew asking where unit base is
need call times per department
sunset time for the shoot day
nearest hospital details for the sheet
who is on set at seven
location changed, reissue the sheet
talent travel and pickup times

atoms.obligation: Give each department its own call time counted backwards from the first shot rather than one blanket crew call.
atoms.lesson: Lighting and grip normally pre-call sixty to ninety minutes before the crew to rig and run distro. Hair and makeup are counted back from the talent's on-set time, roughly forty-five minutes per contributor, and costume before that. A single blanket call means twenty people standing in a car park on the clock while three of them work, and it burns hours off the back of the day.

atoms.obligation: Put unit base, parking, nearest emergency department and the on-site first aider on the front page of every sheet.
atoms.lesson: The front page is what someone reads on their phone during an incident, so it carries the site address with a what3words or grid reference for ambulance access, the nearest accident and emergency with its postcode and drive time, the named first aider and their mobile, plus the fire assembly point. Bury this on page three and nobody finds it when a sparks falls off a ladder.

atoms.obligation: Publish sunrise, sunset and forecast conditions and mark which scheduled scenes depend on daylight or dry weather.
atoms.lesson: Exterior scenes shot for daylight need to be inside the golden window, and magic hour is genuinely twenty to thirty minutes, not an hour. Print first light, sunrise, sunset and last light with the forecast and, near water, the tide times. Flag the daylight-dependent items on the schedule so the assistant director knows which scenes get bumped first and which cover set is on standby.

atoms.obligation: Reissue a clearly versioned sheet whenever times or locations change and confirm receipt from every head of department.
atoms.lesson: Amended sheets go out as version two with the changes marked at the top, never as a silent replacement of the same file, because half the crew have already screenshotted version one. Send after the recce or wrap meeting locks the change, chase a thumbs-up from each head of department, and telephone anyone travelling that night. Drivers and talent are the ones who turn up at the old address.

name: location-recce-report
description: Structures a technical recce and writes up the report the crew will shoot from. Use before committing to a venue, when you need to know whether there is power and how loud the room is, when access or parking looks tight, or when a venue asks what permissions and insurance you need in place.
expansions: recce next week for the interview venue
is there enough power at the site
traffic noise in that room
can the van park near the door
permission to film in the lobby
how dark can we get the room
check ceiling height for a rig
write up notes from the site visit

atoms.obligation: Record available power, socket positions and circuit limits, and calculate whether the planned rig exceeds them.
atoms.lesson: A standard thirteen-amp domestic ring gives you about three kilowatts before the breaker goes, which two older tungsten heads will eat on their own. Note where the consumer unit is, who holds the key, whether there is a sixteen or thirty-two amp supply, and how far the nearest socket is from the set so the gaffer knows the cable run. If the sums do not work, the report calls for a generator and a genny driver.

atoms.obligation: Survey ambient noise across the times you intend to shoot and note what can be switched off and by whom.
atoms.lesson: Listen with headphones on, not just with your ears. Air conditioning, fridge compressors, fluorescent ballast hum, lifts, and a flight path or school playground on a cycle all wreck dialogue. Establish who can silence the air handling and for how long before the building overheats, and whether the plant restarts automatically.
