atoms.obligation: Program bass and kick as one rhythmic unit, deciding which of them owns each shared attack.
atoms.lesson: When kick and bass land on the same beat, one has to lead. A bass note starting ten to twenty milliseconds after the kick lets the kick transient speak while the bass sustain follows, which is why that pairing sounds tight in most modern productions. Note length matters as much as position: shortening a bass note so it releases before the next kick clears the low end better than any equalizer move.

name: synth-patch-design
description: Builds a synthesizer sound from oscillators, filters and modulation to fit one specific part in one specific arrangement. Use when a preset almost works but sits in the wrong place, when a pad is static and lifeless, or when a bass loses power on small speakers. Also use when a lead is shrill rather than cutting.
expansions: preset almost works but sits wrong
pad sounds static and lifeless
bass disappears on phone speakers
lead is shrill instead of cutting
need movement in a sustained sound
pluck has no attack character
detuned stack sounds smeared
filter sweep sounds harsh at the top

atoms.obligation: Shape the amplitude envelope to the role of the part before touching filters, effects or oscillator choice.
atoms.lesson: Attack and release define whether a sound reads as a pluck, a pad or a stab far more than raw timbre does. A pad with a 400 to 800 millisecond attack sits under a vocal without competing for the transient, while the same patch with a two millisecond attack fights the snare. Release should relate to tempo, roughly one beat for legato parts and shorter in dense arrangements so notes clear before the next chord.

atoms.obligation: Add continuous modulation to any sustained sound so it evolves instead of sitting still under the arrangement.
atoms.lesson: Static waveforms fatigue the ear within seconds. Slow modulation of filter cutoff, oscillator detune or pulse width at 0.1 to 0.5 Hz gives motion without obvious wobble, and keying modulation depth to velocity or a wheel makes it playable. A few cents of pitch drift between oscillators mimics analogue instability. Two layers modulating at different rates produce a shimmer that a single layer cannot achieve.

atoms.obligation: Keep sub bass content mono and narrow while widening only the harmonics above roughly one hundred and twenty hertz.
atoms.lesson: Wide detuned low frequencies cancel when a club system or a phone sums to mono, which is exactly where the bass matters most. Split the patch: a mono sine or triangle for weight below 120 Hz, and the wide detuned layer bandpassed above it. Saturating the harmonics above 200 Hz makes the note audible on small speakers through the missing fundamental effect, where the ear infers pitch from the harmonic series.

atoms.obligation: Tame filter resonance and harsh harmonics with saturation and dynamic control rather than by removing brightness.
atoms.lesson: A resonant sweep creates a narrow peak that can jump 15 dB above the rest of the patch as it crosses harmonics. Saturation before the filter thickens the source so that peak sits in more content, and a dynamic equalizer band between 3 and 8 kHz catches it only when it appears. Simply lowering the cutoff instead makes the part dull, and it then stops cutting through the arrangement at all.

name: sample-clearance-licensing
description: Handles the paperwork and risk assessment when a track uses someone else recording, loop or melody. Use when a demo contains an uncleared sample, when a label asks for clearance status before a release date, or when someone asks whether a library loop is safe to use. Also use when a replayed melody needs a publishing split agreed.
expansions: demo has an uncleared sample
label wants clearance status
is this library loop safe to use
replayed a melody instead of sampling
who owns the master versus the song
splits sheet for a co written track
sample fee quote seems too high
release is blocked pending clearance

atoms.obligation: Clear both the sound recording and the underlying composition separately, since two different owners control them.
atoms.lesson: A sampled record carries two rights: the master, usually owned by a label, and the composition, owned by writers and publishers. Permission from one does not cover the other and either can block a release. Master clearance is typically a fee or a buyout, while composition clearance is usually a share of publishing plus sometimes an advance. Get both in writing before any release date is announced, because retroactive negotiation always costs more.

atoms.obligation: Record the exact source, timestamp and length of every sample at the moment it enters the session.
atoms.lesson: Six months later nobody remembers which pressing or which upload a two bar loop came from, yet clearance requires naming the specific recording, its release and where in it the sample sits. A running list with title, artist, release year, timecode in and out, and how the sample is used, plus the raw source file kept in the project folder, turns a week of detective work into a form you can send the same day.

atoms.obligation: Consider replaying a part with session musicians when master clearance is refused or priced out of reach.
atoms.lesson: Re-recording an interpolation removes the master owner from the negotiation entirely, leaving only the publishing side to license. It must be a genuine new performance rather than a filtered or pitched copy, and any distinctive production sound that identifies the original recording is still risky. Budget for players and studio time, and expect the publisher to still demand a large share of a song built around a recognisable melody.

atoms.obligation: Treat royalty free library terms as binding limits and read carefully what each licence excludes.
atoms.lesson: Most sample libraries permit use inside a new musical work but forbid redistributing the sounds as a sample pack, and some restrict production music, advertising or standalone loop use. Subscription libraries often revoke rights for material downloaded after a subscription lapses. Keep the licence text and the download receipt with the project, because a distributor content claim on a widely used loop is resolved by producing exactly that documentation.

name: arrangement-song-structure
description: Diagnoses why a track drags or fails to lift and rearranges parts to fix it. Use when a chorus does not feel bigger than the verse, when the second verse repeats the first exactly, or when an intro takes too long to arrive. Also use when a client says the song loses them halfway through.
expansions: chorus does not feel bigger
second verse identical to the first
intro takes too long to get going
song loses people halfway through
too much happening all the time
bridge feels tacked on
drop needs to land harder
outro just stops awkwardly

atoms.obligation: Create lift by removing elements before a chorus rather than by piling more instruments inside it.
atoms.lesson: Perceived size is relative. If the verse already carries full drums, wide guitars and a pad, the chorus has nowhere left to go. Thinning the last two bars before it, dropping the low end, narrowing the stereo image or muting the hats makes the same chorus feel twice as large. Filtering through the pre chorus and releasing the filter on the downbeat is the same trick applied to spectrum instead of instrumentation.

atoms.obligation: Give each section a new event within its first two bars so the listener registers that something changed.
atoms.lesson: Attention resets on change. A new instrument entry, a rhythm shift, an octave move in the bass, or the removal of a familiar part all read as an event. A second verse identical to the first tells the listener nothing has progressed, which is exactly where skip rates rise. The change need not be large: an added tambourine, a doubled vocal line or a different hi hat pattern can carry a whole section.

atoms.obligation: Assign every element a register and a rhythmic role, then cut whatever duplicates a role already taken.
atoms.lesson: Two parts occupying the same octave with the same rhythm cancel each other identity no matter how they are mixed. Map the arrangement as a grid of frequency ranges against rhythmic function: low sustain, low rhythm, mid sustain, mid rhythm, high sustain, high rhythm. Empty cells show what the track still needs and doubled cells show what to mute. Most crowded mixes are arrangement problems that equalization cannot solve.

atoms.obligation: Test the arrangement against the clock, checking that the first hook arrives early and the track ends deliberately.
atoms.lesson: Streaming listening punishes slow starts, so a recognisable hook or vocal within the first fifteen to thirty seconds keeps skip rates down. Sections that run four bars past their idea lose momentum, and an outro that stops mid phrase feels like an error rather than an ending. Marking the timeline with section start times and reading those against reference tracks in the same genre exposes both problems within minutes.

name: low-end-phase-management
description: Sorts out the bottom two octaves so kick, bass and low instruments coexist and translate across systems. Use when a mix is boomy on monitors and thin in the car, when kick and bass mask each other, or when the low end disappears in mono. Also use when a mastering engineer flags uncontrolled sub energy.
expansions: boomy on monitors thin in the car
kick and bass are fighting
low end vanishes in mono
mastering says the sub is uncontrolled
808 masking the kick drum
muddy buildup around two hundred hertz
bass level jumps note to note
room is lying about the bass

atoms.obligation: Decide which source owns the sub range and which owns the punch range, then carve the other around it.
atoms.lesson: Below about 60 Hz there is room for one dominant element. If the kick owns the sub, filter the bass around 40 to 50 Hz and let it lead from 80 to 200 Hz; if the bass owns the sub, the kick becomes a 60 to 120 Hz punch with a click on top. Ducking the bass two to three decibels for 80 to 150 milliseconds under each kick clears the overlap without audible pumping.

atoms.obligation: Check mono compatibility and polarity for every low frequency source before calling the mix finished.
atoms.lesson: Club systems, phones and many broadcast paths sum to mono, and wide or out of phase bass largely disappears there. Collapse the mix to mono and listen for level drops, and watch a correlation meter for negative readings below 200 Hz. Multi source bass rigs, direct plus amplifier, are the usual culprit, and a polarity flip or a few samples of alignment restores the fundamental. Keep everything below roughly 120 Hz centred.

atoms.obligation: Control note to note level swings in the bass with compression and dynamic equalization rather than one static curve.
atoms.lesson: A bass jumping 6 dB between notes is usually exciting a room mode or a resonant instrument note rather than showing a mix fault. A compressor with a slow attack near 10 to 30 milliseconds and a release matched to tempo evens the performance, while a dynamic equalizer on the one or two offending frequencies catches specific notes without dulling the rest. Fixing this before mastering stops the limiter reacting differently every bar.

atoms.obligation: Verify low end decisions on a second system and against a reference, never on one pair of monitors alone.
atoms.lesson: Small rooms show modal peaks and nulls of 10 to 20 dB below 300 Hz, so the bass heard at the desk may not exist. Standing elsewhere in the room, checking on headphones, and reading a slow averaging spectrum against a reference track all give independent evidence. Sub content that looks reasonable on an analyser but sounds absent in the room is almost always the room rather than the mix.

name: reverb-space-design
description: Places elements in a believable space with reverb and delay, and rescues mixes that sound either pasted together or washed out. Use when a vocal sits on top of the track like a sticker, when the mix sounds like a cave, or when someone asks which reverb suits a snare. Also use when tails are eating the low mids.
expansions: vocal sits on top like a sticker
mix sounds washed out and distant
which reverb for this snare
reverb tails are muddying the mix
want depth without losing clarity
delay throws cluttering the phrases
drums sound like two different rooms
reverb disappears when the mix is loud

atoms.obligation: Use pre delay and early reflections to set distance while keeping the direct sound in front of the tail.
atoms.lesson: The ear judges distance from the ratio of direct to reflected sound and from the gap before the first reflections arrive. A pre delay of 20 to 60 milliseconds keeps a vocal forward because dry consonants land before any wash, whereas zero pre delay glues the source into the room and pushes it back. Timing pre delay to a sixteenth or eighth note at the song tempo makes the tail breathe with the groove.

atoms.obligation: Filter reverb and delay returns so tails do not compete with their sources in the low mids and the highs.
atoms.lesson: A full range tail adds energy everywhere, and the 200 to 500 Hz region turns to mud fastest. High passing the return around 250 to 400 Hz and low passing between 6 and 10 kHz leaves a tail that is felt rather than heard as clutter. Darker tails also read as more distant, matching how air absorbs high frequencies over distance. De-essing a vocal send stops sibilance splashing across the whole tail.

atoms.obligation: Share one or two main spaces across the whole mix instead of giving every track its own reverb.
atoms.lesson: Elements sound like they occupy the same room when they share reflections. One short space, roughly 0.6 to 1.2 seconds for cohesion, plus one longer space for effect, covers most productions, and instruments are then placed by how much they are sent rather than by owning a unique reverb. Drum room mics already supply a real space, so extra drum reverb should match the decay of those mics.

atoms.obligation: Duck or gate effect returns against the dry signal so words and hits stay intelligible.
atoms.lesson: A tail is most useful in the gaps rather than under the source. Compressing the reverb return with the dry vocal as the trigger, giving three to six decibels of ducking with a fast release, lets the tail bloom between phrases. Gated or short plate treatments on a snare give size without ringing into the next hit. A delay throw on the last word of a line beats a delay running under every word.

name: mix-automation-moves
description: Uses level, effect and tonal automation to keep a mix moving and every word audible. Use when a static balance works in the verse but collapses in the chorus, when a few vocal words keep disappearing, or when a solo needs to come forward for eight bars. Also use when a mix feels flat despite good individual sounds.
expansions: balance works in verse not chorus
a few vocal words keep disappearing
solo needs to come forward
mix feels flat despite good sounds
automating reverb into the chorus
riding the vocal instead of crushing it
fader moves are audible as jumps
section changes need level bumps

atoms.obligation: Ride the vocal level word by word and phrase by phrase before adding any more compression.
atoms.lesson: A compressor reacts to level rather than to intelligibility, so it will duck a loud consonant and still leave a swallowed word buried. Manual rides of one to three decibels on individual words place the performance where you want it and hand the compressor a more even signal, so 3 to 6 dB of gain reduction does the job instead of 10. Riding first also removes the pumping heavy compression causes on a dynamic vocal.

atoms.obligation: Automate section changes with small level and effect moves rather than trusting one static balance all song.
atoms.lesson: Choruses usually want the vocal a decibel down and the band up, because the arrangement is denser and the singer is already louder. Half decibel to one decibel moves on buses at section boundaries are inaudible as moves yet change how a section feels. Reverb sends commonly rise into a chorus and fall for verses. Writing these moves on the last beat before the downbeat hides the transition completely.

atoms.obligation: Shape automation curves and hide move points where the music masks them.
atoms.lesson: A vertical step in a fader move clicks or jumps, while a ramp over 50 to 200 milliseconds does not. Move points placed under a snare hit, a cymbal crash or a breath vanish entirely, which is why bus moves belong on downbeats. For sends and filters, longer curves of one to four bars read as a build rather than as an edit. Always audition automation in context rather than soloed.

atoms.obligation: Keep automation editable on channels and buses rather than baking level changes into rendered audio.
atoms.lesson: Rendering a level change into a file forecloses revisions, and revision rounds always arrive. Level automation on the channel plus separate automation on the send lets a request to lift the backing vocals in the last chorus be answered in minutes. Where a plugin parameter must move, automating that parameter beats printing the result. Snapshots at section starts make it easy to reset a section that has drifted.

name: mix-bus-glue
description: Sets up processing on the mix bus so a record moves as one piece and still survives mastering. Use when a mix sounds like separate stacked tracks, when the bus chain is squashing transients, or when someone asks whether to mix into a compressor. Also use when a mastering engineer requests a version with less bus processing.
expansions: mix sounds like stacked separate tracks
bus compressor is killing the drums
should i mix into the compressor
mastering wants less bus processing
parallel compression on the whole mix
master chain sounds smaller not bigger
gluing a mix without losing punch
how much gain reduction on the bus

atoms.obligation: Insert bus processing early and build the balance into it rather than adding it to a finished mix.
atoms.lesson: A bus compressor changes the internal balance, pulling down whatever is loudest, usually drums and vocal, and letting quieter parts rise. Adding it at the end undoes decisions made without it. Setting a gentle two to three decibels of gain reduction from the start means every balance choice already accounts for it. If the chain arrives late, expect to revisit vocal and drum levels rather than trusting the old balance.

atoms.obligation: Choose bus attack and release times that let transients through and recover in time with the tempo.
atoms.lesson: An attack faster than about 10 milliseconds flattens drum transients and shrinks the mix, while 10 to 30 milliseconds lets the stick hit pass before gain reduction bites. Release should recover between beats, so an automatic setting or something near 0.1 to 0.3 seconds at common tempos keeps any pumping musical. Watching the gain reduction meter return to zero on every backbeat is a better check than any published number.

atoms.obligation: Keep the bus chain modest and deliver a mix the mastering stage can still shape.
atoms.lesson: A mix limited to near zero leaves nothing to adjust and turns mastering into an argument rather than a refinement. Deliver a mix peaking around minus 6 dBFS with any bus limiter bypassed, alongside a reference version with the chain engaged so the intent is clear. Broad tonal moves of one to two decibels on the bus are welcome, whereas aggressive multiband work usually signals a problem better fixed on individual channels.

atoms.obligation: Compare the processed bus against bypass at matched loudness before keeping any part of the chain.
atoms.lesson: Every glue chain adds level, and the louder version wins by default. Trim the output so bypassed and engaged match within a few tenths of a decibel, then switch between them. If the processed version loses depth, punch or width, the chain is doing harm that loudness was hiding. Checking on a small speaker and in mono exposes stereo width tricks that fall apart outside the control room.

name: reference-track-matching
description: Uses commercial references to calibrate tonal balance, loudness and arrangement decisions while mixing. Use when a mix does not sound like its genre, when a client sends a track and says make it sound like this, or when comparing tonal balance against a finished master. Also use when the low end reads differently at home and in the studio.
expansions: client sent a track to match
mix does not sound like the genre
comparing tonal balance to a master
our mix is duller than the reference
reference is louder so it sounds better
picking the right reference track
matching stereo width to a reference
reference sounds bigger in the chorus

atoms.obligation: Level match the reference to the working mix before making any comparison or judgement.
atoms.lesson: Commercial references are mastered and can sit 6 to 10 dB louder than a mix in progress, which biases every judgement toward the reference. Match short term loudness first, then compare. Comparing an unmastered mix with a finished master also exaggerates differences in top end and density, so either allow mentally for what mastering will add or listen through a rough limiter set to a similar loudness.

atoms.obligation: Choose references with similar instrumentation and production era, not merely a similar mood.
atoms.lesson: A sparse acoustic reference says nothing useful about a dense synth production, because spectral balance is driven by arrangement. Match instrumentation, tempo range, vocal register and roughly the decade, since low end extension and top end brightness have shifted noticeably over time. Two or three references covering different aspects, one for low end, one for vocal placement, one for width, beat a single supposedly perfect track.

atoms.obligation: Compare one specific attribute at a time instead of judging the whole picture in a single pass.
atoms.lesson: The ear cannot hold a whole mix in memory. Pick one question, such as how much energy sits between 100 and 250 Hz or how far back the snare sits, and switch quickly between the two tracks on that question alone. Switching within a second preserves the comparison, while longer gaps let auditory memory decay. Note the answer, fix it, then move on rather than adjusting everything at once.

atoms.obligation: Treat a reference spectrum as a guide for spotting gross departures, not as a curve to match exactly.
atoms.lesson: Matching a spectrum shape exactly imposes another song arrangement onto yours. A track with a baritone vocal and one with a soprano legitimately differ around 200 to 400 Hz. Use the reference to catch large errors, such as four decibels too much upper mid or a missing 40 to 60 Hz region, and correct those. Automatic matching curves are useful as a diagnostic display and dangerous as a finished decision.

name: mastering-loudness-targets
description: Prepares a final master for a given destination at the right loudness and dynamics, and sequences a release. Use when a track has to reach streaming loudness without pumping, when a master sounds smaller than its references, or when distortion appears only after encoding. Also use when someone asks what loudness figure to aim at.
expansions: what loudness should this master be
master pumps when pushed louder
distortion appears after encoding
master sounds smaller than references
limiter is squashing the drums
true peak keeps going over
club version needs to be louder
streaming turned my track down

atoms.obligation: Set loudness by what the material can hold, then check the result against the destination normalization.
atoms.lesson: Streaming services normalize playback, commonly near minus 14 LUFS integrated, so a master pushed to minus 7 is simply turned down and arrives with less dynamic range than a quieter one would. Dense electronic material tolerates minus 8 to minus 10, while acoustic and orchestral material usually sounds best around minus 14 to minus 16. Judge the ceiling by where transients begin to flatten rather than by hitting a number.

atoms.obligation: Keep true peak below a ceiling that survives lossy encoding, not merely below the sample peak limit.
atoms.lesson: Sample peak meters miss intersample overs, and lossy encoders reconstruct waveforms that can exceed the original peaks by one to two decibels. A true peak ceiling of minus 1.0 dBTP, or nearer minus 1.5 dBTP for heavily limited material, keeps the encoded file clean. Distortion that appears only after encoding, and only in the loudest sections, is almost always this. Always audition an encoded copy rather than only the master file.

atoms.obligation: Return to the mix rather than the limiter whenever extra loudness starts costing punch.
atoms.lesson: A limiter can only take away. If two decibels of gain flatten the drums, the cause is usually low mid buildup, one uncontrolled bass note or wide sub energy eating headroom, and fixing that in the mix buys the same loudness for free. Multiband or dynamic equalization on one or two problem regions ahead of the limiter often recovers several decibels of apparent loudness with no audible processing at all.

atoms.obligation: Sequence and top and tail the whole release, matching level and tone across every track.
atoms.lesson: A record is judged as a sequence, so a track sitting a decibel and a half above its neighbours breaks the listen even when each master is fine alone. Match by loudness rather than by peak, allow deliberate contrast where the music asks for it, set fades that begin and end in silence without truncating tails, and choose gaps by feel, often two to four seconds, auditioning across every transition.

name: stem-delivery-package
description: Prepares stems, multitracks and alternate versions for another engineer, a licensing request or a live show. Use when a mastering engineer or remixer asks for stems, when a sync request needs an instrumental and a television mix, or when a mix must be handed to another mixer. Also use when delivered stems fail to line up on import.
expansions: mastering engineer needs stems
sync request wants an instrumental
remixer asked for multitracks
stems do not line up on import
need a tv mix without lead vocals
handing the project to another mixer
backing tracks for the live show
what naming convention for files

atoms.obligation: Print every stem from the same start point across the full song length so files align on import.
atoms.lesson: Stems that begin at each part first note force the recipient to guess offsets, and one misplaced file ruins the session. Export from bar one, or from timecode zero, out to the end of the longest tail including reverb decay, so silence carries the alignment. Keep the session sample rate and bit depth, deliver at 24 bit or higher, and never normalize individual stems because that destroys the balance you built.

atoms.obligation: Print stems with their channel processing but without the mix bus chain, and state clearly which choice was made.
atoms.lesson: A remixer wants stems that already sound like the record, which means channel equalization, compression and effects are baked in. Applying the mix bus compressor to each stem separately multiplies its effect, so those stems will never sum back to the mix. The safe delivery is stems that sum to a bus free mix, plus the finished mixdown for reference, with a written note saying the bus chain is excluded.

atoms.obligation: Deliver the alternate versions the destination actually needs, including instrumental and vocal free variants.
atoms.lesson: Sync and broadcast requests routinely need a full mix, an instrumental with no lead or backing vocals, a television mix keeping backing vocals and gang chants, and sometimes an a cappella. Live playback needs a click and a guide on separate channels. Producing them all while the session is open costs minutes, whereas recalling the session months later costs hours and risks plugins having changed underneath you.

atoms.obligation: Name files consistently and include a manifest listing tempo, key, sample rate and version.
atoms.lesson: File names should carry song title, version, stem name and date in a fixed order, avoid spaces and special characters, and stay inside the length limits of the receiving system. A short text list of the files, plus tempo map, key, sample rate, bit depth, whether the bus chain is included, and contact details, prevents almost every follow up email. Add a checksum or archive so truncated transfers are caught.

name: immersive-atmos-mix
description: Mixes and delivers object based immersive audio alongside an approved stereo version. Use when a label requests a spatial mix, when bed and object assignments need deciding, or when a binaural fold down sounds worse than the stereo. Also use when an immersive deliverable has been rejected on level or format grounds.
expansions: label requested a spatial version
what goes in the bed versus objects
binaural fold down sounds worse
immersive deliverable was rejected
vocal placement in the height channels
stereo and spatial versions do not match
how loud should the spatial mix be
monitoring immersive without a full rig

atoms.obligation: Anchor low frequencies and the lead vocal in the bed and centre rather than spreading them into moving objects.
atoms.lesson: Bass placement in immersive playback collapses unpredictably across speaker layouts and headphones, so low content belongs in the bed where it is handled consistently. Lead vocals pushed into a height object lose intelligibility and shift position as listeners move or switch to headphones. Reserve objects for elements that gain from motion or separation: effects, doubles, percussion, pads and reverb returns.

atoms.obligation: Check the binaural and stereo fold downs regularly, since most listeners will only ever hear those.
atoms.lesson: Immersive music reaches most people through headphone virtualization or a downmix rather than a speaker array. Elements that read as spacious over speakers can turn phasey or distant binaurally, and hard panned height objects often vanish in a fold down. Auditioning the binaural render throughout, and comparing balance and loudness against the approved stereo mix, catches problems that a speaker only workflow hides until delivery day.

atoms.obligation: Meet the destination loudness and format specification exactly before submitting any immersive deliverable.
atoms.lesson: Immersive music deliverables are typically specified around minus 18 LUFS integrated with a true peak ceiling near minus 1 dBTP, supplied as the authoring interchange file with the correct frame rate, sample rate and bed configuration. A louder mix is rejected or normalized down, which breaks its relationship with the stereo master. Confirm the current specification for that destination first, since these requirements get revised.

atoms.obligation: Build the immersive mix from the same balance decisions as the stereo instead of treating it as a separate version.
atoms.lesson: Listeners switch between formats, so a spatial mix with a different vocal level or a different arrangement reads as a mistake rather than a choice. Start from the relative levels and tonal decisions of the stereo mix, then use the extra space to unmask rather than to reinvent. Moving reverb and doubles out of the front image usually lets centre elements sit a decibel lower while sounding clearer, which is the real gain.

name: audio-restoration-noise
description: Cleans up problem recordings carrying hum, hiss, clicks, rumble, traffic or mismatched room tone. Use when an interview has air conditioning under it, when a location recording has traffic beneath the dialogue, or when a transfer crackles. Also use when a chair squeak or mouth click sits inside the best phrase of a take.
expansions: air conditioning hum under interview
traffic noise under location dialogue
vinyl transfer full of crackle
chair squeak in the best take
clipped recording sounds distorted
hiss from an old tape transfer
mouth clicks between words
room tone changes between edits

atoms.obligation: Remove noise in small stages using several processes rather than one aggressive pass.
atoms.lesson: A single strong reduction pass produces the watery metallic artefacts that give restoration away. Three light passes of six to eight decibels each, using different processes, sound cleaner than one pass of twenty. Order matters: fix clicks and crackle first, then hum and its harmonics, then broadband hiss, then rumble, because each stage makes the next detector more accurate. Compare constantly against the untreated file at matched level.

atoms.obligation: Capture a clean profile of the noise from a passage containing no wanted sound.
atoms.lesson: Broadband reduction needs a fingerprint of the noise alone, ideally one to two seconds of room tone from the same take, the same position and the same gain setting. A profile grabbed from a different scene or after a gain change will not match and will chew into the dialogue. Ask for thirty seconds of room tone on every location shoot, and when none exists hunt for gaps before the first word or after the last.

atoms.obligation: Attack mains hum at its fundamental and each harmonic instead of with one wide low frequency cut.
atoms.lesson: Mains hum sits at 50 or 60 Hz depending on the region and carries strong harmonics up through 300 Hz and beyond, while lighting buzz reaches higher still. Narrow notches at the fundamental and each harmonic, or a comb based remover, preserve the material between them. A wide low cut instead strips the warmth out of the voice. Check whether the hum is steady or drifting, since drifting hum needs a tracking process.

atoms.obligation: Judge every repair in context at conversational listening level rather than soloed and loud.
atoms.lesson: Restoration auditioned soloed under headphones at high level tempts over processing of noise nobody will hear once music and effects sit underneath. Play the repaired section inside the full mix at the level the audience will use. Equally, an artefact hidden by a busy mix will be exposed in a quiet passage, so check both extremes. Keep the untreated file, since a director may prefer honest noise to a processed voice.

name: adr-dialogue-edit
description: Records replacement dialogue and edits production dialogue against picture. Use when a line is unusable because of location noise, when an actor is being cued for replacement lines, or when replacement dialogue does not match the original perspective. Also use when dialogue edits sound bumpy and need smoothing before the mix.
expansions: line unusable from location noise
cueing an actor for replacement lines
adr does not match the room
dialogue edits sound bumpy
syncing replacement lines to picture
actor performance flat in the booth
perspective change between angles
fitting a new line to lip movement

atoms.obligation: Match the replacement microphone, distance and perspective to the original production recording before rolling.
atoms.lesson: A booth recording made with a large diaphragm condenser at six inches will never cut against a boom mounted shotgun at three feet. Use the same or a similar boom microphone at a similar distance and height, off axis if the original was, and let the actor stand or move as they did on set. Perspective is distance plus room reflection, and matching it first makes the later equalization and reverb work almost invisible.

atoms.obligation: Cue performers with a consistent countdown and let them hear the original guide take.
atoms.lesson: Actors deliver in sync far more reliably when they hear their guide track plus a three beep countdown with the line starting one beat after the third beep, though some prefer a streamer across picture instead. Keep the room quiet, the picture large enough to read mouth shapes, and record several passes without stopping, because the second and third passes usually carry both sync and performance together.

atoms.obligation: Edit dialogue so continuous room tone runs under every cut and fills every gap.
atoms.lesson: A cut between two camera angles changes background level and colour, which reads as a click or a hole even when the words are fine. Filling gaps with room tone from the same setup, overlapping tone under each transition, and crossfading between eight and forty milliseconds makes a scene continuous. Splitting dialogue onto separate tracks by character and by microphone lets the mixer treat each consistently instead of automating every line.

atoms.obligation: Fit replacement lines to picture syllable by syllable rather than stretching a whole line to length.
atoms.lesson: A whole line time stretch drifts against lip movement, and stretching beyond a few percent audibly changes the voice. Cut the line into words or syllables, place strong consonants against the visible mouth closures, especially plosives, and absorb the remaining difference inside the silences. Watch at speed against picture first, then check frame by frame at the plosives, because those are what the eye catches first.

name: room-acoustics-monitoring
description: Improves what a room and its monitors actually tell you, through placement, treatment and calibration. Use when mixes do not translate to the car, when bass changes as you move your head, or when setting up a new control room. Also use when someone asks whether to buy correction software or acoustic panels first.
expansions: mixes do not translate to the car
bass changes as i move my head
setting up a new control room
panels or correction software first
monitors sound harsh at the desk
flutter echo when i clap
where to place the speakers
checking monitor level calibration

atoms.obligation: Set speaker and listening positions first, since geometry fixes more problems than treatment or correction can.
atoms.lesson: An equilateral triangle with tweeters at ear height, the listening position around 38 percent of the room length from the front wall, and symmetrical side distances removes most imaging and comb filtering problems for free. Speakers pushed against a wall gain 3 to 6 dB of low end plus a boundary null higher up. Desk and console surfaces cause a reflection that notches the 1 to 3 kHz region, which moving the speakers forward relieves.

atoms.obligation: Treat low frequencies with absorption of real depth before covering walls with thin panels.
atoms.lesson: Bass problems come from room modes, and controlling a 60 Hz mode needs absorber depth on the order of a quarter wavelength, roughly a metre of porous material or a tuned membrane, placed where pressure is highest, in the corners. Two inch foam absorbs above about 500 Hz and does nothing below, so a room covered in it becomes dead and bright while the bass stays uneven. Treat corners first, then first reflection points.

atoms.obligation: Use measurement to diagnose the room and correction only to finish, never as a substitute for treatment.
atoms.lesson: A measurement microphone and a sweep reveal modal peaks, nulls and decay times that hearing alone cannot separate from the mix. Correction filters can lower a peak but cannot fill a null, because that energy is cancelling in the air rather than missing from the signal. Correcting broadly above the transition frequency also fights the room own reflections. Fix decay and geometry physically, then correct gently below roughly 300 Hz.

atoms.obligation: Calibrate monitor level to a repeatable reference and check work at more than one listening loudness.
atoms.lesson: Perceived tonal balance changes with level, so a mix judged loud will sound thin and bright when played quietly. Setting a repeatable reference, commonly 79 to 83 dB SPL per speaker with pink noise in larger rooms and lower in small ones, makes decisions consistent from day to day. Working mostly at a moderate level and checking at both a whisper and a loud pass exposes vocal level and low end weight problems.

name: daw-latency-troubleshooting
description: Diagnoses clicks, dropouts, timing offsets and delay compensation faults inside a session. Use when playback crackles under plugin load, when a printed track lands early or late, or when external hardware inserts drift out of sync. Also use when the buffer has to be raised so far that recording becomes unplayable.
expansions: playback crackles under plugin load
printed track lands late
hardware insert is out of sync
buffer too high to record with
clicks and pops during playback
some tracks sound flammed together
delay compensation seems wrong
session slows down as it grows

atoms.obligation: Separate a timing offset from a performance dropout before changing any audio setting.
atoms.lesson: Crackles, pops and stuttering under load are a processing problem, solved by buffer size, freezing tracks or reducing plugin count. A track that is consistently early or late by a fixed amount is a compensation problem that no buffer change will ever fix. Measuring the offset in samples on a clear transient tells you which you have: a constant offset points at compensation while random glitches point at load.

atoms.obligation: Track at a small buffer with heavy processing disabled and raise the buffer only for mixing.
atoms.lesson: Buffer size trades latency against processing safety. Sixty four or 128 samples keeps monitoring comfortable while recording, whereas 512 or 1024 gives the headroom a full mix needs. Lookahead limiters, linear phase equalizers and some pitch and amp modelling plugins each add tens of milliseconds that compensation resolves on playback but cannot remove from live monitoring. Disabling them, or bypassing the whole bus chain, restores a playable feel.

atoms.obligation: Measure and compensate the round trip delay of any external hardware placed in the signal path.
atoms.lesson: A hardware insert leaves and returns through converters, adding a fixed delay of typically one to three milliseconds each way plus whatever processing latency the unit itself carries. Send a transient through the loop, measure the sample offset of the return against the source, and enter that as compensation. Digital units with internal buffering add more, and some vary by preset, so re-measure whenever their settings change.

atoms.obligation: Reduce the live processing load by committing finished parts to audio instead of tuning driver settings.
atoms.lesson: Freezing or printing a track together with its instrument and plugins removes that processing from the real time load entirely, which helps far more than any driver tweak. Commit virtual instruments once a part is final, keeping the source track disabled but present so it can be revived. Large sessions also slow from thousands of small edits and from streaming many files at once, so consolidating edited playlists helps.

name: session-archive-backup
description: Consolidates, backs up and archives finished projects so they can be reopened years later. Use when a client asks for a recall on an old song, when a session opens with missing files or missing plugins, or when a drive is filling with old projects. Also use when setting up a backup routine for a studio.
expansions: client wants a recall on an old song
session opens with missing files
plugin discontinued and wont load
drive is full of old projects
setting up a studio backup routine
archiving a finished album
moved a session and lost audio
restoring a project from two years ago

atoms.obligation: Consolidate every referenced audio file into the project folder before archiving anything.
atoms.lesson: Sessions routinely reference files living outside their folder: a sample from a library, a bounce left on a desktop, an imported stem from a shared drive. Copying every referenced file into the project audio folder is what makes an archive self contained. Then open the consolidated copy from a different location and confirm nothing is missing, because an incomplete archive only ever reveals itself at the moment it is needed.

atoms.obligation: Print flat audio versions of every track and every mix alongside the editable session.
atoms.lesson: Plugins are discontinued, licences expire and formats change, so a session may not reload sounding as it did. Printing each track with its processing, plus the final mix, the instrumental and the stems, guarantees the record can be rebuilt or remixed whatever software survives. Those prints also answer most recall requests without opening the session at all. Store them at the session sample rate and bit depth.

atoms.obligation: Keep at least three copies on two kinds of media with one copy held off site.
atoms.lesson: Working drives fail, and a single backup sitting in the same room is lost to the same flood, theft or power event. A local working copy, a local backup on separate media, and an off site or cloud copy is the accepted minimum. Verify restores periodically rather than assuming the routine ran, and refresh archive media every few years since drives left unpowered for years can fail to mount.

atoms.obligation: Write a short session note recording tempo, key, tunings, notable settings and who played what.
atoms.lesson: A recall a year later fails on details nobody wrote down: the guitar tuned down a semitone, the tempo map with a ritardando, which preamp and which microphone, the singer preferred headphone balance, and credits and contact details for the players. A plain text note in the project folder covering tempo and key, a track list with sources, notable settings and personnel turns an archaeology exercise into a quick reopen.

name: anesthesia-risk-plan
description: Builds a pre-anaesthetic risk assessment and a written anaesthetic protocol for one named patient, from physical status grade through premedication, monitoring thresholds and recovery. Use when a dog or cat is booked for a procedure and someone asks what to premedicate with, when a murmur or an abnormal pre-anaesthetic blood result turns up the morning of surgery, or when a brachycephalic, geriatric or unstable patient needs the standard house protocol reworked.
expansions: murmur found at the pre-op exam
bulldog booked for a neuter tomorrow
premed choice for a 14 year old cat
what asa status is this patient
pre-anaesthetic bloods came back abnormal
anaesthetic plan for an emergency c-section
what to use in a dog with kidney disease
monitoring plan for a three hour dental

atoms.obligation: Assign a physical status grade before choosing any drug, and record the specific finding that justifies that grade.
atoms.lesson: Grade I is healthy; II mild systemic disease such as obesity or controlled hypothyroidism; III severe but compensated disease such as stable IRIS stage 2 kidney disease or a grade III of VI murmur without signs; IV a constant threat to life such as gastric dilatation-volvulus or uroabdomen; V moribund. The grade drives monitoring depth and drug choice, not the procedure name. Record the finding itself, because a reviewer must see why a routine dental became a grade III.

atoms.obligation: Choose premedication that matches this patient's cardiovascular reserve instead of defaulting to a single house combination.
atoms.lesson: Acepromazine causes vasodilation and has no reversal, so avoid it in hypovolaemia, in aortic stenosis and in boxers. Dexmedetomidine gives excellent sedation and spares other agents but raises afterload and drops heart rate, so reserve it for young stable patients and reverse with atipamezole. Opioid-based premedication such as methadone with midazolam suits sick, geriatric and cardiac cases. Midazolam alone disinhibits a healthy excitable dog rather than sedating it.

atoms.obligation: Write the monitoring parameters and their action thresholds for this procedure before the patient is induced.
atoms.lesson: Record electrocardiogram, pulse oximetry, capnography, non-invasive blood pressure and temperature every five minutes. Treat a mean arterial pressure under 60 mmHg as hypotension: reduce the vaporiser first, then give a 5 ml/kg crystalloid bolus, then add ephedrine or a dopamine infusion. End-tidal carbon dioxide over 55 mmHg means start ventilating. A temperature under 36.5 C prolongs recovery and impairs clotting, so active warming begins at induction rather than in recovery.

atoms.obligation: Plan the recovery and airway separately for brachycephalic patients and keep the tube in until swallowing is strong.
atoms.lesson: French bulldogs, pugs and Persians have stenotic nares, elongated soft palates and often hypoplastic tracheas, and most of their deaths happen in the first three hours after extubation rather than on the table. Keep them sternal with the head elevated on oxygen, extubate late and repeatedly test swallowing. Keep an induction dose and a smaller tube at the kennel. Anticipate regurgitation from hiatal disease and consider maropitant and omeprazole before the procedure.

name: dental-chart-workup
description: Turns an oral examination and full-mouth radiographs into a completed dental chart, a staged extraction plan and an explanation the owner will accept. Use when a dental procedure is booked, when someone asks which teeth have to come out today, when radiographs show resorptive lesions or periapical lucency, or when an owner wants to know why a scale and polish turned into eight extractions.
expansions: cat with resorptive lesions on radiographs
which teeth need extracting today
grading periodontal disease on this chart
fractured carnassial with pulp exposure
owner asking why cleaning became extractions
dental x-rays show a retained root
charting a feline stomatitis mouth
estimate for full mouth extractions

atoms.obligation: Probe and chart every tooth with pocket depths, mobility and furcation grades before deciding what to extract.
atoms.lesson: Normal sulcus depth is up to 3 mm in dogs and 0.5 to 1 mm in cats. Stage periodontal disease by attachment loss: stage one is gingivitis only, stage two under twenty-five percent, stage three twenty-five to fifty percent, and stage four over fifty percent, which is an extraction call unless the owner commits to advanced periodontal therapy and daily home care. Record furcation and mobility separately, because a two-rooted tooth with grade three furcation is lost despite shallow pockets.

atoms.obligation: Take full-mouth radiographs before extraction decisions and re-image every site after the tooth comes out.
atoms.lesson: About a quarter of clinically normal cat mouths and a fifth of dog mouths hide pathology visible only on radiographs: tooth resorption, periapical lucency, retained roots and unerupted mandibular first premolars with dentigerous cysts. Type one resorption keeps a visible periodontal ligament and needs complete extraction, while type two shows root replacement by bone where crown amputation is acceptable in the absence of stomatitis. Post-extraction views are the only proof no root tip remains.

atoms.obligation: Block the surgical site with local anaesthetic and record the nerve, the drug volume and the time given.
atoms.lesson: Infraorbital, caudal maxillary, middle mental and inferior alveolar blocks with 0.5 percent bupivacaine, keeping the total under 2 mg/kg, give six to eight hours of analgesia and cut inhalant requirement sharply. Aspirate before injecting and keep volumes under 0.5 ml per site in cats to avoid pressure on the globe. Never block both inferior alveolar nerves in a cat going home the same day, because tongue self-trauma follows.

atoms.obligation: Explain the findings to the owner using the chart and the images, describing what was found rather than what was billed.
atoms.lesson: Owners consent to a cleaning and hear about extractions afterwards, and the trust break is surprise rather than money. Take a contact number for intraoperative consent and agree a ceiling beforehand. Show the radiograph of the resorptive lesion beside a normal tooth. Explain the pain the tooth was causing, since cats with resorption usually keep eating, and give the two-week soft food instruction and the recheck date in writing before they leave.

name: euthanasia-visit-planning
description: Prepares a euthanasia appointment end to end: the quality of life conversation, sedation, technique, aftercare choices and the bereavement follow-up. Use when an owner asks whether it is time, when a hospitalised patient will not recover, when a home visit is being scheduled, or when the team needs wording for the phone call nobody wants to make.
expansions: owner asking whether it is time yet
scheduling a home euthanasia visit
quality of life scoring for this dog
sedation before the final injection
aftercare and cremation options
wording for a difficult phone call
euthanasia in a fractious cat
children present during the appointment

atoms.obligation: Anchor the timing conversation in observable daily behaviours rather than in a diagnosis or a survival statistic.
atoms.lesson: Ask which five things this animal loved and how many are still possible, then score hurt, hunger, hydration, hygiene, happiness, mobility and whether good days outnumber bad. A dog that no longer greets at the door, cannot settle at night or needs help to toilet is saying something no creatinine value says. Give the owner permission language: the decision is best made a week early rather than a day late.

atoms.obligation: Sedate the patient to unconsciousness before giving the euthanasia solution and let the owner watch it settle.
atoms.lesson: Intramuscular or subcutaneous premedication, such as alfaxalone with butorphanol in cats or acepromazine with methadone in dogs, takes ten to twenty minutes and removes the struggle owners replay for years afterwards. Place an intravenous catheter after sedation, taped and flushed, so the final injection needs no restraint. Warn beforehand about agonal breaths, muscle twitching, eyes staying open and bladder release, because explaining them afterwards sounds like an excuse.

atoms.obligation: Document consent, aftercare choice and body handling in writing before the appointment starts.
atoms.lesson: Confirm on the form whether the owner wants private cremation with ashes returned, communal cremation or home burial where local rules allow it. Record who is authorising, because a co-owner dispute afterwards is unrecoverable. Offer a paw print or fur clipping. For any animal with a recent bite to a person or a rabies suspicion the head must be preserved and submitted, which rules out cremation, so check the bite history first.

atoms.obligation: Close the record with a bereavement follow-up and cancel every automated reminder the same day.
atoms.lesson: A handwritten card or a call at three to five days lands better than one made the same afternoon. Cancel vaccine reminders, insurance direct debits and repeat prescriptions immediately, because an automated booster reminder to a grieving owner is the complaint you will receive. Offer guidance on the surviving pet, which may search, vocalise and refuse food for one to two weeks, and name a pet bereavement support line for owners living alone.

name: treatment-estimate-builder
description: Produces an itemised treatment estimate with a low to high range, plus the informed financial consent conversation that goes with it. Use when a client asks what a work-up will cost, when a hospitalised patient's spend is approaching the authorised figure, when insurance pre-authorisation is needed, or when options have to be presented at more than one price point.
expansions: how much will the workup cost
estimate for a gdv surgery tonight
client cannot afford the gold standard
we are past the approved amount
low and high range for hospitalisation
quoting a cruciate ligament repair
insurance pre-authorisation for this claim
options at three different price points

atoms.obligation: Give every estimate as a low to high range with the assumptions and the exclusions written on the same page.
atoms.lesson: Set the low end at an uncomplicated course and the high end at the realistic complicated one: for a pyometra that is a straightforward ovariohysterectomy against one with sepsis and two extra hospital days. Name what is excluded, such as histopathology, culture, referral or a second surgery. Practices under-quote by omitting the out-of-hours fee, the recheck and the take-home medication, and every omission reads to the client as a hidden charge.

atoms.obligation: Present at least two clinically defensible options rather than one plan and an implied refusal.
atoms.lesson: When money is short there is almost always a gold, silver and bronze path: full staging with advanced imaging, in-house bloods with radiographs, or symptomatic treatment with a strict recheck trigger. State honestly what each option risks missing. Offering only the top plan pushes owners toward economic euthanasia or toward another practice, and documenting the declined option protects the practice while keeping the medicine transparent.

atoms.obligation: Reauthorise before spending past the approved figure and record who approved what amount and when.
atoms.lesson: Set an internal trigger at seventy-five percent of the estimate so there is time to reach the owner before the ceiling. Log the call in the clinical record with the time, the person, the amount authorised and the plan agreed, not on a sticky note. For a patient in intensive care, a morning update carrying the running total and the projected day three figure keeps discharge a clinical conversation rather than an argument.

atoms.obligation: Settle payment and insurance mechanics before the patient is admitted rather than at discharge.
atoms.lesson: A fifty percent deposit at admission is normal for surgical and emergency cases. Most pet insurance reimburses the owner rather than paying the practice directly, excludes pre-existing conditions and caps by condition or by policy year, so check the wording rather than the client's summary. Third-party medical credit and charity funds must be applied for while the client is still in the building. The first mention of money must never happen at collection.

name: controlled-drug-reconciliation
description: Runs a controlled drug audit: reconciling the register against physical stock, recording wastage, tightening storage and access, and escalating discrepancies. Use at month end, when the ketamine bottle does not match the log, before an inspection visit, when someone asks how to record a part-used vial, or when diversion is suspected.
expansions: ketamine count does not match the log
monthly controlled drug reconciliation
recording wastage from a part vial
who holds keys to the cd cabinet
preparing for an inspection visit
methadone log missing a signature
disposing of expired schedule two drugs
suspected diversion by a staff member

atoms.obligation: Reconcile each controlled drug by physical count against the running register balance and sign the result with a witness.
atoms.lesson: Count weekly for the highest schedule drugs, including ketamine, methadone, hydromorphone, phenobarbital and pentobarbital euthanasia solution, and at every month end for the rest. Two people count, both sign, and the balance carries forward. Measure liquid volumes rather than eyeballing the bottle: a ten millilitre ketamine vial reading six when the register says seven point four is a finding to write up the same day, not a rounding error.

atoms.obligation: Record wastage at the moment it happens, witnessed, with the volume discarded and the reason.
atoms.lesson: A fifty milligram per millilitre methadone vial drawn for a four kilogram cat leaves a discard, and that discard is the commonest diversion route because it is the least witnessed. The entry names the patient, the drug, the amount given, the amount wasted, the destruction method and two signatures. Waste into an approved denaturing kit rather than a sink. Never pre-sign or backfill a register, because uniform handwriting across a page discredits the whole book.

atoms.obligation: Keep controlled drugs in a fixed locked store with a named key holder per shift and a short access list.
atoms.lesson: The standard is a double-locked cabinet bolted to a masonry wall inside a locked room, not a drawer in the preparation area. Hold the key on a named person each shift rather than on a hook, and log handovers. Limit access to veterinarians and one or two senior nurses. Purchasing patterns matter as much as storage: a practice buying ketamine at three times its surgical caseload is exactly the pattern inspectors look for.

atoms.obligation: Escalate any unexplained discrepancy the same day through a written process instead of a quiet recount.
atoms.lesson: Freeze the register page, photograph the vial, quarantine the stock and inform the practice principal and the named responsible person. Repeated small shortfalls clustering in one person's shifts is the classic diversion pattern, and an impaired colleague needs occupational support alongside the reporting duty. Requirements differ by jurisdiction and some demand notifying the drug regulator within a fixed window, so the practice policy must name the authority, the form and the deadline.

name: vaccine-protocol-tailoring
description: Builds a vaccination plan for an individual animal from species, age, lifestyle and local disease pressure, and handles overdue, unknown-history and previously reactive patients. Use at a puppy or kitten visit, when an owner questions whether a booster is really needed, when a dog is going into kennels or travelling, or after a vaccine reaction.
expansions: puppy series timing for a new litter
does my indoor cat need this booster
dog is two years overdue for vaccines
vaccine reaction last time facial swelling
kennel requirements before boarding
titre test instead of a booster
leptospirosis risk in this area
rescue dog with no vaccine history

atoms.obligation: Separate core from non-core vaccines and justify each non-core product by a named lifestyle exposure.
atoms.lesson: Core for dogs is distemper, adenovirus, parvovirus and rabies where endemic or required by law; core for cats is panleukopenia, herpesvirus type one, calicivirus and rabies. Non-core must be earned: leptospirosis for dogs with standing water, rodent or livestock contact; Bordetella and parainfluenza for boarding, daycare, grooming and shows; Lyme in tick-endemic areas; feline leukaemia for every cat with outdoor access and for all kittens, since lifestyle changes later.

atoms.obligation: Time the primary series around maternal antibody decline and finish it no earlier than sixteen weeks of age.
atoms.lesson: Maternally derived antibody blocks vaccination and wanes unpredictably between eight and sixteen weeks, creating a window of susceptibility. Give doses every two to four weeks from six to eight weeks with a final dose at sixteen weeks or later, because a puppy finishing at twelve weeks is under-protected regardless of how many doses it had. Booster at six or twelve months and then triennially for core modified live products. Rabies intervals are statutory.

atoms.obligation: Record the vaccine site, serial number and route, and use consistent anatomical sites in cats.
atoms.lesson: Injection-site sarcoma risk means using a distal limb or the tail rather than the interscapular space, one product per site, recorded so any later mass traces back to a product. Apply the three-two-one rule: biopsy a post-vaccination lump that is still present three months later, larger than two centimetres, or still growing one month after injection. Serial numbers matter for adverse event reporting and for proving an efficacy failure to a manufacturer.

atoms.obligation: Plan in advance for reactions and for the animal whose vaccine history is unknown or lapsed.
atoms.lesson: Facial angioedema and urticaria appear within hours, so premedicate a known reactor with an antihistamine, split the visit so only one product is given per day and observe for thirty minutes. Anaphylaxis needs adrenaline first, not a corticosteroid. Treat an adult with no records as naive, with two core doses three to four weeks apart in dogs. Titre testing is a defensible alternative for distemper and parvovirus but not for leptospirosis or rabies.

name: parasite-prevention-planning
description: Sets a year-round internal and external parasite plan based on region, lifestyle and household composition, including the testing that has to happen before preventives start. Use when a client asks which flea product to buy, when a heartworm test is positive, when fleas keep coming back after treatment, or when a household includes young children or an immunocompromised adult.
expansions: fleas came back after treatment
heartworm test came up positive
puppy deworming schedule from the shelter
tick prevention for a hunting dog
safe product for a herding breed
child in the house with a new puppy
cat that hunts and brings in mice
giardia keeps recurring in the kennel

atoms.obligation: Test before starting or restarting heartworm prevention and confirm any positive result by a second method.
atoms.lesson: Run an antigen test alongside a microfilariae check, because antigen tests miss immature and all-male infections and antigen-antibody complexes can mask a true positive until the sample is heat treated. Test annually even on year-round prevention, since compliance gaps are common and macrocyclic lactone resistance exists in the Mississippi delta. Starting a preventive in a microfilaraemic dog risks an anaphylactoid reaction, so use a staged protocol with doxycycline and steroid cover.

atoms.obligation: Treat the environment and every animal in the household rather than only the presenting pet.
atoms.lesson: Adult fleas on the animal represent roughly five percent of the burden, while eggs, larvae and pupae in carpet and bedding are the rest, and pupae survive months before hatching in response to vibration. Expect apparent product failure for eight to twelve weeks even with perfect compliance. Wash bedding at sixty degrees, vacuum daily and discard the bag, and treat every cat and dog on the same day, using species-appropriate products for rabbits and ferrets.

atoms.obligation: Match the drug class to the species and breed, and check for the multidrug resistance gene risk.
atoms.lesson: Permethrin at canine spot-on concentrations is lethal to cats, and a cat can be poisoned simply by grooming a treated dog, which is a common and entirely preventable emergency. Collies, Australian shepherds, Shelties and long-haired whippets may carry the MDR1 mutation, where label-dose macrocyclic lactones are safe but the high doses used for demodicosis are not. Isoxazolines carry a labelled neurological warning for animals with a seizure history.

atoms.obligation: Cover the zoonotic risks explicitly with households containing children or immunocompromised adults.
atoms.lesson: Toxocara eggs need two to four weeks in the environment to become infective, so daily faecal pickup breaks the cycle, and larva migrans in children is why puppies are wormed fortnightly from two to twelve weeks then monthly to six months. Advice for a pregnant owner is gloves, daily litter changing by someone else and no raw meat, not rehoming the cat. Echinococcus and hookworm pressure shape intervals in hunting and coastal populations.

name: lab-result-client-summary
description: Interprets in-house or reference laboratory results into a clinical picture, a next test that changes the plan, and a short client-ready explanation. Use when a chemistry panel returns with abnormalities, when blood and urine results seem to disagree, when a client calls for their results, or when a sick animal has a panel that looks normal.
expansions: chemistry panel back with high alt
explain these results to the owner
azotaemia but the urine is concentrated
mild anaemia on the cbc what next
thyroid value borderline in an old cat
urine protein creatinine ratio elevated
which confirmatory test do we run
results normal but the dog is sick

atoms.obligation: Interpret every abnormal value against signalment, hydration and the medication list before calling it disease.
atoms.lesson: Greyhounds run higher haematocrits and lower total protein, puppies have high alkaline phosphatase from bone growth, lipaemia falsely raises haemoglobin and phosphorus, and haemolysis falsely raises potassium in Akitas and Shiba Inus with high-potassium red cells. Phenobarbital and corticosteroids induce alkaline phosphatase without liver disease. A single mildly abnormal value in a well animal is usually a reference interval artefact, since about one test in twenty falls outside by definition.

atoms.obligation: Pair the blood results with a urine sample collected at the same time before drawing any renal conclusion.
atoms.lesson: Azotaemia is renal only when the urine is inadequately concentrated, meaning below 1.030 in dogs and 1.035 in cats. Concentrated urine with a high urea points prerenal, to dehydration or gastrointestinal bleeding. Isosthenuria around 1.008 to 1.012 with azotaemia stages as renal disease. Add SDMA, which rises at roughly forty percent nephron loss against seventy-five percent for creatinine, plus a protein-creatinine ratio on an inactive sediment, and stage on two stable samples.

atoms.obligation: Name the single next test that would change the plan rather than repeating the whole panel.
atoms.lesson: A raised alanine aminotransferase with normal bilirubin needs bile acid stimulation or abdominal ultrasound, not a repeated panel. A borderline total thyroxine in an older cat needs free thyroxine by equilibrium dialysis with a TSH, because non-thyroidal illness suppresses total thyroxine. A non-regenerative anaemia needs a reticulocyte count first and then a marrow aspirate. State what each result would rule in or out, and what it costs, before ordering.

atoms.obligation: Write the client explanation as a number, a meaning and an action in plain language.
atoms.lesson: Say that the kidney value is 3.2 where normal ends at 1.6 and the urine is dilute, meaning roughly two thirds of kidney function is gone, rather than describing azotaemia with isosthenuria. Give three lines: what was found, what it means for this animal, and what happens next and when. Flag urgency honestly, since a potassium of 7.8 is a today problem while a marginally raised alkaline phosphatase in a well dog is a three-month recheck.

name: surgery-discharge-instructions
description: Writes post-operative discharge instructions and the verbal handover that accompanies them, covering medication, activity restriction, wound care and the exact signs that should bring the animal straight back. Use after any surgical procedure, when an owner phones worried about the incision, or when a patient goes home with a drain, a cast or a feeding tube.
expansions: discharge notes after a spay today
incision looks red owner is worried
how long is cage rest after tplo
dog keeps licking the wound
sending home with a drain
pain medication schedule for the owner
when can the stitches come out
post op feeding tube instructions

atoms.obligation: State activity restriction as a duration with concrete permitted and forbidden activities rather than as rest.
atoms.lesson: Write lead walks only, five minutes, four times daily for fourteen days after a routine spay, with no stairs, no jumping onto furniture, no off-lead running and no play with other dogs. Orthopaedic cases differ sharply: a cruciate repair needs eight to twelve weeks of controlled loading with a written weekly progression and a radiographic recheck at six to eight weeks before any return to free exercise. Vague instructions produce dehiscence and implant failure.

atoms.obligation: Give each medication with its dose, timing, food requirement and the one interaction warning that matters.
atoms.lesson: Write one and a half tablets by mouth every twelve hours with food for five days and finish the course, rather than relying on the dispensing label. Never send a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory home alongside a corticosteroid, and explain that switching between anti-inflammatories needs a washout. Tell owners gabapentin causes expected wobbliness, that trazodone with an opioid deepens sedation, and that vomiting, black stools or appetite loss on an anti-inflammatory means stop and call today.

atoms.obligation: Describe the normal incision appearance and the exact abnormal findings that require a same-day call.
atoms.lesson: Normal is a thin dry line with mild bruising and slight swelling for two to three days, and a small amount of clear serous discharge in the first forty-eight hours is acceptable. Call the same day for gaping, purulent or bloody discharge, swelling that grows after day three, self-trauma, heat and pain, or a temperature above 39.5 C. Book a recheck at three days and suture removal at ten to fourteen days before they leave the building.

atoms.obligation: Insist on a protective collar or garment and give a written plan for the animal that removes it.
atoms.lesson: One licked incision costs more than the entire prophylaxis. A correctly fitted Elizabethan collar extends past the nose and stays on twenty-four hours a day, including sleeping and eating; inflatable collars do not stop a determined dog reaching a flank or a hindlimb. Offer surgical suits for cats and abdominal wounds. Tell owners to raise food and water bowls, and to ring for a different device rather than removing it just at night.

name: phone-triage-protocol
description: Guides reception and nursing staff through telephone triage: what must be seen immediately, what can wait until a routine appointment, and what is safe to advise at home. Use when a client rings describing symptoms, when the day is fully booked and someone must be squeezed in, or when a poisoning, trauma or collapse call comes through.
expansions: caller says the dog ate chocolate
cat straining in the litter box
is this an emergency or can it wait
deep chested dog retching and bloated
book is full who gets squeezed in
puppy vomiting since this morning
hit by a car on the way in
seizure lasting a few minutes

atoms.obligation: Screen every call first against the short list of presentations that are emergencies regardless of other detail.
atoms.lesson: See immediately: unproductive retching with a distended abdomen in a deep-chested dog, a male cat straining without producing urine, open-mouth breathing in a cat, a seizure lasting over five minutes or clustering, uncontrolled bleeding, collapse, pale or blue gums, thirty minutes of strong straining in whelping, prolapsed organs, snake bite and any road or height trauma. These need no further questions, only an instruction to come now and a warned team.

atoms.obligation: Handle exposure calls quantitatively by asking what, how much, how long ago and the animal's weight.
atoms.lesson: Dose per kilogram decides everything. Dark chocolate carries roughly ten times the theobromine of milk chocolate, xylitol causes hypoglycaemia from around 0.1 g/kg and liver failure from 0.5 g/kg, grapes and raisins have no established safe dose, lilies of the Lilium and Hemerocallis genera cause anuric renal failure in cats from petal or pollen contact, and paracetamol kills cats at doses dogs tolerate. Never advise home emesis with salt or peroxide.

atoms.obligation: Never diagnose over the phone; describe what cannot be assessed remotely and give a clear time frame.
atoms.lesson: The caller wants reassurance and both the clinical and legal risk lie in giving it. Say the signs described fit several causes, some serious, and none can be excluded without an examination. Offer only three outcomes: come now, take an appointment today, or monitor against named red flags with a stated call-back time. Record the call, the advice given and the caller's decision in the patient record, because that entry is the defence.

atoms.obligation: Prepare the hospital before the emergency arrives and get the caller travelling safely.
atoms.lesson: Confirm the expected arrival time and route, advise towel or muzzle restraint for a painful animal, and instruct them to withhold food, water and any human medication. Alert the team so oxygen, the crash trolley and a catheter kit are ready and someone meets the car. For a suspected gastric dilatation-volvulus or a road traffic case, a nurse waiting at the door with a trolley saves minutes and keeps the scene out of the waiting room.

name: fluid-therapy-planning
description: Calculates and writes a fluid plan covering deficit, maintenance and ongoing losses, with fluid type, rate, additives and monitoring for one patient. Use when a dehydrated or shocked animal is admitted, when an anaesthetised patient becomes hypotensive, when potassium needs supplementing, or when cardiac or renal disease makes standard rates unsafe.
expansions: dehydrated vomiting dog admitted overnight
shock bolus for a collapsed patient
how much potassium to add
fluid rate for a cat in heart failure
hypotension under anaesthesia what now
estimating percent dehydration from skin turgor
diabetic ketoacidosis fluid plan
when to stop the drip and reassess

atoms.obligation: Estimate the deficit from physical signs and replace it over hours, separately from maintenance and ongoing losses.
atoms.lesson: Five percent dehydration shows as barely tacky mucous membranes, seven percent adds a mild skin tent and dry gums, ten percent gives obvious tenting with sunken eyes and prolonged capillary refill, and twelve percent is shock. Deficit in millilitres is percent multiplied by body weight in kilograms multiplied by ten. Replace over six to twenty-four hours as tolerated, add maintenance at around 2 ml/kg/hour, then add measured vomit, diarrhoea and urine losses rather than guessing them.

atoms.obligation: Treat shock with titrated boluses and reassess perfusion after each one instead of running a fixed volume.
atoms.lesson: Give a quarter-shock isotonic crystalloid bolus of 10 to 20 ml/kg in dogs and 5 to 10 ml/kg in cats over fifteen minutes, then recheck heart rate, pulse quality, mucous membrane colour, capillary refill time, lactate and blood pressure. Cats decompensate into bradycardia and hypothermia rather than tachycardia. Stop and reconsider a cardiac or haemorrhagic cause after two boluses without improvement, and never bolus a patient with a murmur and a gallop rhythm.

atoms.obligation: Choose the fluid and its additives for the electrolyte problem in front of you rather than by habit.
atoms.lesson: A balanced isotonic crystalloid such as lactated Ringer's is the default. Use 0.9 percent saline for hypercalcaemia, for post-obstructive hyperkalaemia and where hyponatraemia risk matters. Supplement potassium on the sliding scale, from 20 mmol per litre at a serum of 3.5 to 4.5 up to 80 mmol per litre below 2.0, and never exceed 0.5 mmol/kg/hour. Correct chronic hyponatraemia no faster than 0.5 mmol per litre per hour.

atoms.obligation: Weigh the patient twice daily and set explicit stop rules for fluid overload before starting.
atoms.lesson: One kilogram of acute weight gain equals one litre of retained fluid, and the scale is more sensitive than any other bedside measure. Watch for serous nasal discharge, chemosis, a rising respiratory rate and effort, new crackles and jugular distension. Cats and patients with cardiac, renal or hypoalbuminaemic disease overload at rates dogs tolerate easily.
