Record inputs and outputs, and cut back to maintenance as soon as the patient is drinking voluntarily.

name: pain-management-protocol
description: Builds a multimodal analgesia plan for acute or chronic pain, covering drug selection, intervals, non-drug measures and how the team will score whether it is working. Use post-operatively, for an arthritic dog whose owner says the tablets have stopped helping, for feline pain that is easy to miss, or when non-steroidals are contraindicated.
expansions: old dog struggling to get up
nsaid not enough after surgery
cat hiding and not grooming
kidney disease so cannot use nsaids
adding gabapentin to the plan
pain scoring for the hospital sheet
long term osteoarthritis management plan
how do we tell if it still hurts

atoms.obligation: Score pain with a validated scale at set intervals and treat the score rather than the impression.
atoms.lesson: Use the Glasgow composite measure short form in dogs, intervening at six out of twenty-four or five out of twenty when mobility cannot be assessed, and the Feline Grimace Scale, where four out of ten triggers analgesia. Score on admission, hourly for four hours after surgery, then every four hours. Cats express pain as stillness, a hunched posture, ears rotated outward and a tightened muzzle, so the quiet cat at the back of the kennel is often the painful one.

atoms.obligation: Combine drug classes acting at different points in the pathway rather than escalating a single agent.
atoms.lesson: Multimodal analgesia means an opioid for acute pain, an anti-inflammatory where organ function allows, a local block at the surgical site, and ketamine or a lidocaine infusion for wind-up in severe cases. Adding a second class beats doubling the first. For chronic osteoarthritis, an anti-inflammatory plus weight loss plus controlled exercise plus an anti-nerve-growth-factor antibody where licensed outperforms any single agent, and paracetamol can be added in dogs but never in cats.

atoms.obligation: Screen for anti-inflammatory contraindications and have a defined plan for the patients who cannot receive them.
atoms.lesson: Avoid non-steroidals in hypotension, dehydration, active gastrointestinal ulceration, concurrent corticosteroid use and uncontrolled renal or hepatic disease, and around a hypovolaemic anaesthetic. When excluded, build the plan from paracetamol in dogs, gabapentin at 10 to 20 mg/kg two or three times daily titrated against sedation, amantadine at 3 to 5 mg/kg daily for central sensitisation, and grapiprant where licensed. Recheck renal values and blood pressure before restarting anything.

atoms.obligation: Prescribe the non-pharmacological half of the plan with the same specificity as the drugs.
atoms.lesson: In osteoarthritis a ten percent reduction in body weight can improve lameness scores as much as an anti-inflammatory. Specify non-slip runners over laminate flooring, a ramp instead of jumping into the car, a raised food bowl, a firm orthopaedic bed away from draughts, five short walks instead of one long one, and hydrotherapy twice weekly. For cats add low-entry litter trays, steps to the favoured windowsill and elevated feeding stations.

name: weight-and-nutrition-plan
description: Assesses body and muscle condition, calculates a calorie target and writes a staged weight loss or therapeutic diet plan with scheduled weigh-ins. Use when an owner asks what to feed, when a pet is obese or losing weight unexpectedly, when a disease calls for a prescription diet, or when a multi-pet household free-feeds.
expansions: cat is nine kilos and needs to slim
body condition score for this dog
which renal diet for a fussy cat
raw feeding question from a client
large breed puppy growth food
losing weight but eating well
multi cat household free feeding
how many calories per day exactly

atoms.obligation: Score body condition and muscle condition separately and record both alongside the weight at every visit.
atoms.lesson: Body condition uses a nine-point scale where five is ideal and each point above is roughly ten percent over target weight, with ribs palpable under thin fat, a waist visible from above and an abdominal tuck from the side. Muscle condition is scored independently over the spine, scapulae, skull and wings of the ilium, because a cachectic cancer or cardiac patient can carry a body score of six with severe muscle loss. Photograph and weigh consistently.

atoms.obligation: Calculate the calorie target from ideal weight and express it in grams of the named food, never in cups.
atoms.lesson: Resting energy requirement is seventy multiplied by ideal body weight in kilograms to the power of 0.75. For weight loss feed about eighty percent of that resting requirement for the ideal weight, aiming for one to two percent of body weight lost weekly in dogs and 0.5 to one percent in cats. Convert to grams using the food's kilocalories per kilogram and send the owner home with a kitchen scale, since cup measurement varies by up to fifty percent between people.

atoms.obligation: Recheck at two-week intervals and adjust the ration on measured progress rather than reissuing the same plan.
atoms.lesson: Weight loss plateaus as metabolic rate falls, so if a dog loses nothing over three weeks reduce by a further ten percent and audit the treats first, because one rich tea biscuit is significant for a five kilogram dog. Allocate ten percent of calories to treats openly so they are not banned and then smuggled. Nurse-run clinics with a fixed weigh day, a wall chart and a target date complete far more often than opportunistic advice in consultations.

atoms.obligation: Match therapeutic diets to the specific disease and check which competing condition currently threatens life.
atoms.lesson: Renal diets restrict phosphorus and moderate protein and are the only intervention proven to extend survival in feline chronic kidney disease. Struvite dissolution diets acidify the urine and are wrong for a calcium oxalate former, so identify the stone type first. Hepatic and cardiac diets conflict with renal ones, so decide the priority. Warn about raw diets in immunocompromised households and about grain-free legume-heavy foods and dilated cardiomyopathy.

name: behavior-consult-intake
description: Structures a behaviour consultation: history taking, ruling out medical drivers, functional assessment and an immediate management plan. Use when a client reports aggression, house soiling, separation distress or noise phobia, when a cat suddenly stops using the tray, or when a patient is too fearful to be examined in the consulting room.
expansions: dog bit a visitor last week
cat urinating outside the litter box
destroys the house when left alone
terrified of fireworks every year
puppy biting the children
too fractious to examine in clinic
growling over the food bowl
new baby coming and dog unsettled

atoms.obligation: Rule out medical drivers before labelling any change in behaviour as behavioural.
atoms.lesson: House soiling in cats needs urinalysis and imaging for cystitis and crystals, plus assessment of arthritis making a high-sided tray unusable. New aggression in an older dog can be pain, hypothyroidism, hepatic encephalopathy, failing vision or cognitive dysfunction. Sudden noise sensitivity in an older dog is frequently musculoskeletal pain. Run a full physical examination, a blood panel, urinalysis, blood pressure and where indicated a two-week analgesia trial before writing any training plan.

atoms.obligation: Take the history as an antecedent, behaviour and consequence sequence for specific incidents, supported by video.
atoms.lesson: Ask for three recent episodes in detail: where it happened, who was present, what occurred in the ten seconds before, exactly what the animal did, and what happened next. Owners describe unprovoked bites that video reveals were preceded by lip licking, a head turn, a freeze and a low growl. Ask for home video of the empty house, because separation distress beginning within five minutes looks nothing like boredom chewing three hours in.

atoms.obligation: Give management that prevents rehearsal of the behaviour before any training protocol begins.
atoms.lesson: Every repetition strengthens the response, so first make the trigger impossible: a baby gate with no unsupervised child contact, window film for the door-barking dog, and a second litter tray in a separate room following the one-per-cat-plus-one rule with unscented clumping litter. Walk a reactive dog at quiet times or on a different route. Management is not failure; it buys the weeks that desensitisation and counter-conditioning need to work.

atoms.obligation: State the bite risk and the safety plan plainly in writing, and refer beyond your own competence.
atoms.lesson: Record bite history on a severity scale: level one is an air snap, level two skin contact without puncture, level three punctures shallower than the canine length, and level four deep punctures with bruising or shaking. A level four bite to a child turns the conversation from training into containment, safety and honest prognosis. Refer aggression cases to a veterinary behaviourist, and state that punishment-based methods increase bite risk in the published evidence.

name: specialist-referral-letter
description: Prepares a referral to a specialist: the clinical summary, the specific question being asked, the raw data to send, and the expectations set with the owner. Use when a case exceeds in-house capability, when an owner requests a second opinion, when a critical patient is being transferred tonight, or when the specialist's report comes back and care returns to you.
expansions: referring for a cruciate repair
needs an mri for neuro signs
owner wants a second opinion
transferring a critical patient tonight
what to send with the referral
specialist report back what now
oncology referral for a mast cell tumour
cardiology echo before anaesthesia

atoms.obligation: Ask the specialist one specific question rather than sending the animal for general assessment.
atoms.lesson: A request to please assess wastes a consultation slot. Write instead whether this thoracolumbar myelopathy is surgical and what the prognosis for ambulation is given fourteen hours without deep pain sensation. A defined question shapes which imaging is done first and lets the specialist quote accurately. State whether you want an opinion, a procedure or a full transfer of care, and whether the owner has a financial ceiling or active insurance.

atoms.obligation: Send the raw diagnostic data with the letter instead of only your interpretation of it.
atoms.lesson: Radiographs travel as complete DICOM studies with every view and the acquisition date, not photographs of a monitor. Include the full laboratory history so trends are visible, cytology and histopathology slides or block numbers, electrocardiogram traces, and a precise drug list with doses and last administration times. A dog given a corticosteroid within seventy-two hours cannot yield a meaningful lymph node aspirate or adrenal function test, and discovering that on the day wastes the appointment.

atoms.obligation: Set the owner's expectations on cost, timing and what referral can and cannot achieve.
atoms.lesson: Tell them the consultation fee, that imaging under anaesthesia often happens the same day, and give a realistic total range for the likely procedure. Say whether the referral is diagnostic or curative, and warn that the specialist may advise against surgery. Confirm insurance pre-authorisation and who holds the clinical notes. Owners expecting a modest opinion who meet a four-figure imaging and surgery quote frequently decline out of shock rather than budget.

atoms.obligation: Close the loop when the case returns by reconciling the specialist plan into your records and owning the follow-up.
atoms.lesson: Read the discharge summary before the recheck, transcribe new medications and monitoring into your own record, and diary the specific checks: neutrophil counts seven days after chemotherapy, ciclosporin blood levels, orthopaedic radiographs at six weeks. Tell the owner explicitly who does what and who to call out of hours. The commonest post-referral failure is a patient falling between two practices with neither running the promised bloods.

name: pharmacy-inventory-review
description: Reviews practice pharmacy and consumable stock: par levels, expiry management, cold chain, backorders and dispensing accuracy. Use at a stock take, when a drug runs out mid-procedure, when the fridge alarm has gone off overnight, when short-dated stock needs a decision, or when drug spend looks wrong against turnover.
expansions: ran out of cefazolin mid surgery
fridge temperature alarm overnight
short dated vaccines on the shelf
setting par levels for the crash box
backorder on a key anaesthetic
stock take before year end
expired drugs disposal process
why is our drug spend so high

atoms.obligation: Set par levels from measured usage and supplier lead time rather than from how the shelf looks.
atoms.lesson: The reorder point is average daily usage multiplied by supplier lead time plus a safety stock covering the longest recent delay. A drug used twice weekly with a five-day lead time from an unreliable wholesaler needs a very different level from a daily item delivered overnight. Review quarterly against actual dispensing figures. Emergency drugs are the exception: crash box contents are held as a full set regardless of turnover and checked weekly against a written list.

atoms.obligation: Manage expiry with first-expired-first-out rotation and a monthly short-date sweep of every shelf.
atoms.lesson: Date-check monthly and move anything within ninety days to a marked short-date shelf at the front. Opened multidose vials carry their own in-use dates: many are twenty-eight days after broaching, unpreserved propofol is discarded within six hours, and reconstituted vaccines within an hour. Write the broach date on the vial. Expired stock cannot be used or dispensed, and a client-facing bottle with a past date is both a complaint and an inspection finding.

atoms.obligation: Monitor the cold chain continuously and write the excursion procedure before an alarm ever sounds.
atoms.lesson: Vaccines, insulin and biologicals need 2 to 8 C with a data logger recording minimum and maximum, checked and signed daily; a domestic fridge holding staff lunches is not compliant. On an excursion, quarantine the stock, record the duration and the temperature reached, and ask the manufacturer for a stability ruling rather than deciding locally. Frozen vaccine is destroyed even when it thaws looking normal, and adjuvanted products are the most sensitive.

atoms.obligation: Reconcile dispensing against purchasing on high-value lines to find leakage and lost margin.
atoms.lesson: Compare units purchased against units billed for a sample of expensive lines each quarter. The usual gaps are undercharging on part-used vials, in-hospital use never entered on the invoice, and staff pet dispensing without a record. A twenty percent discrepancy on a wormer line is almost always a billing habit rather than theft. Fix it by making dispensing a billed action inside the workflow, not by circulating another policy memo.

name: isolation-biosecurity-protocol
description: Sets the isolation, barrier nursing and disinfection plan for a suspected or confirmed infectious case, and manages the clinic-wide response afterwards. Use when a parvovirus suspect arrives in the car park, when kennel cough spreads through boarding, when ringworm or leptospirosis is admitted, or when contacts need tracing after an outbreak.
expansions: parvo suspect in the car park
kennel cough spreading through boarding
ringworm in a rescue kitten litter
lepto suspect and staff exposure
which disinfectant kills this virus
how long to keep the ward closed
cat flu outbreak in the cattery
cleaning after an infectious case

atoms.obligation: Admit suspected infectious cases straight into isolation from the vehicle without crossing the waiting area.
atoms.lesson: Meet the car, carry the patient through a dedicated door, and keep a stethoscope, thermometer and clippers permanently inside isolation. Parvovirus sheds before clinical signs appear and survives months in the environment, so a parvo puppy walked across reception contaminates the busiest square metres in the building. Log everyone who enters, restrict nursing to one dedicated person per shift, and place isolation last on the daily treatment round.

atoms.obligation: Match the disinfectant to the organism and give it the contact time the label states on a pre-cleaned surface.
atoms.lesson: Non-enveloped viruses such as parvovirus, calicivirus and panleukopenia resist quaternary ammonium compounds and alcohol. Use accelerated hydrogen peroxide, potassium peroxymonosulfate or sodium hypochlorite at one in thirty-two with ten minutes of wet contact. Every disinfectant is inactivated by organic matter, so detergent washing and rinsing must come first. Ringworm spores need mechanical removal plus twice-weekly bleach or enilconazole, while leptospires die readily but the urine still needs gloves.

atoms.obligation: Define barrier nursing as a numbered sequence of steps and post it on the isolation door.
atoms.lesson: Dedicated gown, gloves, shoe covers or a footbath, and hair covering for ringworm; put on outside the room and remove inside it, and wash hands with soap and water rather than alcohol gel for parvovirus and fungal spores. Materials leave in sealed clinical waste and food bowls stay in the room. Pregnant or immunocompromised staff should not nurse ringworm, leptospirosis or toxoplasma-risk cases, and every technique breach must be reportable without blame.

atoms.obligation: Trace contacts and communicate to owners and staff, including the zoonotic risk where one exists.
atoms.lesson: List every animal that shared airspace or a corridor within the incubation window, which is three to fourteen days for parvovirus and two to ten days for canine infectious respiratory disease and panleukopenia, and call those owners with a watch list and a temperature threshold. For leptospirosis, warn about urine handling and send exposed staff and household members to a doctor. For ringworm, tell owners to check their own skin. Record the outbreak and its closure date.

name: herd-health-visit-plan
description: Plans and runs a routine herd or flock health visit for a farm client, covering the pre-visit data review, the on-farm scoring and a written action list with review dates. Use before a quarterly dairy visit, when a client reports rising cell counts or lameness, when calf mortality climbs, or when the annual herd health plan is due an update.
expansions: quarterly dairy visit next week
cell count climbing on the bulk tank
mobility score the milking herd
calf scour losses this spring
not in calf rate is terrible
annual herd health plan update
youngstock pneumonia keeps recurring
reviewing the farm antibiotic use figures

atoms.obligation: Review the herd's own recorded data before the visit and arrive with the three questions it raises.
atoms.lesson: Pull the bulk milk somatic cell count trend, individual cow counts and the new infection rate, the twenty-one day pregnancy rate and calving interval, mortality by age group, and the medicine book. A rising bulk count with a stable new infection rate means chronic cows to segregate or cull, while a rising new infection rate points at the parlour and the environment. Arriving without the numbers turns a health visit into another fire call.

atoms.obligation: Score a representative sample of animals objectively instead of examining only the ones brought to you.
atoms.lesson: Mobility score the whole milking herd on flat non-slip ground as they leave the parlour using the four-point scale, and treat more than ten percent at score two or three as an action threshold. Body condition score at drying off, at calving and mid-lactation against target curves. Use lying times, hock lesion scores and cleanliness scores to separate a cubicle design problem from an underfoot hygiene problem before recommending spending.

atoms.obligation: Sample and culture before changing any treatment protocol, and tie the change to the medicine records.
atoms.lesson: Culture mastitis milk before selecting a tube, because a herd dominated by environmental Streptococcus uberis and Escherichia coli needs bedding, cubicle and pre-milking hygiene work rather than a new intramammary. Record antimicrobial use as milligrams per population-corrected unit or as defined daily doses, and remove highest-priority critically important antibiotics from first-line use. Selective dry cow therapy needs individual cell count histories and a clean dry environment before it is safe.

atoms.obligation: Leave a written action list with named people, deadlines and a review date at the next visit.
atoms.lesson: Three to five actions is the workable number, for example calibrate the parlour vacuum and change liners every 2,500 milkings, move dry cows to the far shed with 1.2 metres of feed space each, and start colostrum testing with a refractometer targeting over 22 percent Brix given within two hours of birth. Name the person on the farm responsible for each item, and open the following visit by reviewing that list.

name: equine-lameness-workup
description: Structures a lameness examination in the horse from history and static assessment through dynamic evaluation, flexion tests and diagnostic analgesia, and into imaging choices. Use for a horse that is short in front, a lameness after competition, a pre-purchase soundness concern, a poor performance complaint, or when a nerve block has localised the pain and the next step is unclear.
expansions: horse short striding on the right fore
lame after jumping at the weekend
which block do we do next
flexion test positive on the hock
pre purchase exam soundness concern
swollen hot foot suspect abscess
poor performance but not obviously lame
when to image after the block

atoms.obligation: Grade and localise the lameness in a repeatable way before reaching for a needle.
atoms.lesson: Use the five-point grading scale and watch in hand on a straight hard surface, then on the lunge on both reins on hard and soft ground, then ridden when performance is the complaint. Forelimb lameness gives a head nod down onto the sound limb, while hindlimb lameness gives pelvic hike and reduced hip drop on the affected side. Watch for the compensatory contralateral forelimb nod that accompanies hindlimb lameness and misdirects blocking.

atoms.obligation: Examine the foot thoroughly with hoof testers and a shoeing history before assuming soft tissue injury.
atoms.lesson: Around ninety percent of forelimb lameness arises at or below the fetlock and most of that lies within the foot. Check digital pulses, hoof wall temperature, sole depth and mediolateral balance, and ask when the horse was last shod, because a horse lame two days after shoeing is a close nail or nail bind until proven otherwise. Subsolar abscess is the commonest severe acute lameness and presents looking like a fracture.

atoms.obligation: Work diagnostic analgesia from distal to proximal, confirming the effect of each block before moving upward.
atoms.lesson: Begin with a palmar digital block, then abaxial sesamoid, then low four-point, then lateral palmar and higher. Allow five to ten minutes for a low perineural block and twenty to thirty for a high or intra-articular one, and re-trot on the same surface each time, recording the percentage improvement. Local anaesthetic diffuses proximally, so a horse eighty percent better to a palmar digital block may still have a proximal sesamoidean lesion.

atoms.obligation: Choose imaging by the tissue the block implicates and interpret findings against the clinical picture.
atoms.lesson: Radiography answers bone questions such as navicular flexor cortex change, distal phalanx fracture and osteoarthritis; ultrasound answers tendon and ligament questions in the pastern, flexor tendons and suspensory branches; magnetic resonance imaging is the only reliable way to see the navicular bursa, deep digital flexor lesions and collateral ligaments inside the hoof capsule. Radiographic navicular change is common in sound horses, so image the blocked region rather than treating an incidental finding.

name: exotic-husbandry-review
description: Reviews husbandry for reptiles, birds and small mammals as the first step of any exotic consultation, and converts the findings into a corrected setup plan. Use when a bearded dragon stops eating, when a rabbit stops passing droppings, when a parrot is plucking, when a snake refuses food, or when a new owner asks whether their enclosure is right.
expansions: bearded dragon not eating for a week
rabbit stopped eating and passing faeces
parrot plucking its chest feathers
tortoise setup check for a new owner
guinea pig with overgrown teeth
snake refusing food this winter
chinchilla kept in a hot conservatory
which uvb bulb and what distance

atoms.obligation: Take a complete husbandry history first, because most exotic presentations are husbandry failures in disguise.
atoms.lesson: Ask for enclosure dimensions, actual hot and cool end temperatures measured with a probe rather than a stick-on dial, ultraviolet lamp type, age and distance, humidity, substrate, diet by item and frequency, supplementation, water source, cage mates and the date anything last changed. A bearded dragon under an ultraviolet tube older than nine months is developing metabolic bone disease even though the lamp still visibly lights the vivarium.

atoms.obligation: Treat a rabbit or guinea pig that has stopped eating as an emergency rather than a diet question.
atoms.lesson: Gastrointestinal stasis in a rabbit progresses to hepatic lipidosis and death within days, and the trigger is usually pain elsewhere, such as dental spurs, a fractured incisor or urolithiasis, combined with a low-fibre diet. Give analgesia, warmed fluids, four-hourly syringe feeding of a fibre-based recovery formula and prokinetics once radiographs have excluded obstruction. Guinea pigs also need vitamin C, and both species need over eighty percent hay rather than selective-feeding muesli mixes.

atoms.obligation: Set temperature, lighting and humidity as species-specific ranges with a measured gradient and a thermostat.
atoms.lesson: A bearded dragon needs a basking spot of 38 to 42 C, a cool end near 24 C and a ten to twelve percent ultraviolet B tube replaced every six to twelve months at the manufacturer's stated distance with no glass in between. A corn snake needs 28 to 30 C warm and 21 to 24 C cool. Ball pythons need 55 to 60 percent humidity and refuse food when it drops. Every unregulated heat mat eventually causes thermal burns.

atoms.obligation: Correct the diet toward the species' natural intake and stage the transition over several weeks.
atoms.lesson: A seed-fed parrot is deficient in vitamin A, calcium and protein; convert to a formulated pellet over four to six weeks by mixing gradually while weighing the bird daily, because a psittacine will starve rather than accept unfamiliar food. Juvenile bearded dragons need roughly seventy percent gut-loaded insects dusted with calcium and vitamin D3, while adults need mostly greens. Mediterranean tortoises need high-fibre low-protein weeds and no fruit at all.

name: hospital-rounds-handover
description: Runs the structured handover of hospitalised patients between shifts, producing a per-patient plan, monitoring frequency and named overnight escalation triggers. Use at morning and evening rounds, when handing critical cases to the overnight team, when a locum picks up a caseload, or after a patient deteriorated and nobody was sure who owned the decision.
expansions: handing over to the night nurse
morning rounds on six inpatients
who is the vet on this case tonight
what do we call about overnight
locum taking over tomorrow
patient deteriorated and nobody was told
writing the treatment sheet for today
critical case handover to the referral centre

atoms.obligation: Hand over each patient in a fixed structure so that nothing depends on somebody's memory.
atoms.lesson: Situation, background, assessment and recommendation works well: signalment and presenting problem, what has happened so far including surgery and drugs given, current status with the latest vital signs and pain score, then the plan with its timings. Include the details people forget, such as when the animal last urinated, when the intravenous catheter was placed, whether it has bitten anyone, and the owner's stated resuscitation decision.

atoms.obligation: Set explicit numeric escalation triggers for each patient and name the person who gets called.
atoms.lesson: Write, for this patient, to call the on-call veterinarian if the heart rate exceeds 160, the respiratory rate exceeds 40, systolic pressure falls below 90 mmHg, temperature falls below 37 C, blood glucose falls below 4 mmol per litre, or there has been no urination in six hours. Generic instructions to call if worried fail overnight when one nurse must judge alone. Name a first and second on call with numbers and confirm the second knows.

atoms.obligation: Write the treatment sheet as timed tasks with a signature box and reconcile it at every shift change.
atoms.lesson: Every fluid rate, drug, dose, route, time and monitoring parameter goes on the sheet with an initial when completed and a note when omitted with the reason. Reconcile the sheet against the clinical record at each handover, because drug omissions cluster at shift changes and in patients whose plan changed mid-day. Highlight anything altered in the last twelve hours so the incoming clinician sees what is new rather than rereading the history.

atoms.obligation: Assign one named clinician who owns each case and who speaks to the owner.
atoms.lesson: Shared ownership produces the case nobody chases. Name the responsible veterinarian for every inpatient on the whiteboard and in the record, including who will phone the owner and at what time. When ownership transfers to the night team, to a colleague's day off or to a referral centre, make it an explicit verbal handover that both parties acknowledge rather than an entry someone might read, and tell the owner the name has changed.

name: antimicrobial-stewardship-review
description: Reviews antibiotic decisions against culture results, guidelines and the practice's protected-drug policy, producing either a defensible prescription or a documented no-antibiotic plan. Use when a culture and sensitivity report arrives, when a case has failed first-line treatment, when someone wants a fluoroquinolone or a long-acting injectable, or when prescribing is being audited.
expansions: culture and sensitivity report back
third course of antibiotics not working
want a long acting injectable for this cat
does this even need antibiotics
resistant staph on the swab result
auditing our prescribing this quarter
duration for a simple bladder infection
pyoderma keeps coming back

atoms.obligation: Decide first whether an antibiotic is indicated at all, and record the reasoning when it is not.
atoms.lesson: Sporadic bacterial cystitis, uncomplicated feline upper respiratory disease, most acute diarrhoea and clean post-operative wounds do not need antibiotics. Feline lower urinary tract signs are idiopathic cystitis in the large majority and respond to analgesia, increased water intake and stress reduction. Canine infectious respiratory disease is usually viral and self-limiting within two weeks. Writing why antibiotics were not indicated is what makes the decision defensible when the owner rings the next day.

atoms.obligation: Culture before prescribing in any recurrent, deep or previously treated infection.
atoms.lesson: Sample properly: cystocentesis urine rather than a free catch, a deep tissue biopsy rather than a superficial swab in wounds, and an intact pustule for pyoderma. Meticillin-resistant Staphylococcus pseudintermedius is now common in dogs treated repeatedly for skin disease and cannot be predicted from appearance. Interpret sensitivity reports against the target site, because a drug reported sensitive that never reaches urinary or skin concentrations is false reassurance.

atoms.obligation: Choose the narrowest effective agent and reserve the highest-priority classes for culture-proven need.
atoms.lesson: Amoxicillin, amoxicillin-clavulanate and first-generation cephalosporins cover most first-line indications. Fluoroquinolones, third-generation cephalosporins including long-acting injectables, and any human last-line class should require a culture result plus a documented reason no lower tier works. A fourteen-day injectable cannot be withdrawn when the culture disagrees, and its convenience is what drives overuse. Topical chlorhexidine often removes the need for systemic treatment in superficial pyoderma entirely.

atoms.obligation: Prescribe an evidence-based duration and audit practice prescribing every quarter.
atoms.lesson: Sporadic cystitis needs three to five days rather than fourteen, superficial pyoderma is treated to one week past clinical resolution, and surgical prophylaxis is a dose at induction repeated every ninety minutes during surgery and stopped at closure. Audit by courses per hundred consultations, the proportion using protected classes, and the proportion supported by culture. Feeding anonymised figures back by clinician changes prescribing far faster than another guideline circular.

name: rabies-exposure-casework
description: Manages an animal bite or rabies exposure case: verifying vaccination status, deciding the observation or quarantine requirement, meeting the reporting duty and submitting samples where needed. Use when a dog bites a person, when a pet tangles with a bat or wildlife, when a bite victim's doctor calls for records, or when an unvaccinated animal has been exposed.
expansions: dog bit the postman this morning
cat caught a bat in the bedroom
unvaccinated dog fought with a raccoon
ten day observation period rules
doctor calling about a bite victim
sending a head for rabies testing
overdue rabies vaccine after exposure
quarantine requirements for this case

atoms.obligation: Establish and verify vaccination status from the certificate rather than from the owner's recollection.
atoms.lesson: The certificate carrying the date, product, serial number and administering veterinarian decides the entire pathway. A currently vaccinated animal exposed to a rabid animal typically needs an immediate booster and a shorter observation period, while an unvaccinated one may face months of strict quarantine or euthanasia. An overdue animal with documented prior vaccination is often handled as currently vaccinated at the health officer's discretion, and only the paper record makes that argument possible.

atoms.obligation: Confine and observe any animal that has bitten a person for the statutory period regardless of vaccination status.
atoms.lesson: Ten days is the standard observation window for dogs, cats and ferrets, because an animal shedding rabies virus in saliva will show signs and die within that time. Many jurisdictions forbid vaccinating during the observation period, since a vaccine reaction confuses the picture. Examine and document on day zero, day five and day ten. Never euthanise a biting animal before checking the reporting rules, because that destroys the observation evidence.

atoms.obligation: Report bites and suspected exposures to the public health authority within the required window.
atoms.lesson: Most jurisdictions require any animal bite to a person to be reported within twenty-four hours, by the veterinarian as well as the physician. Keep the local health department and animal control numbers by the phone. Record the victim's name and contact details, the circumstances, the wound site and the animal's details. Provide the vaccination history to the treating doctor promptly, because the human post-exposure prophylaxis decision depends on it.

atoms.obligation: Handle suspect samples and human contact risk with barrier precautions and correct submission.
atoms.lesson: Rabies testing requires post-mortem brain tissue, so the head is removed by trained staff wearing gloves, gown and eye protection, then chilled, never frozen and never placed in formalin, which destroys the direct fluorescent antibody test, and shipped to the designated laboratory with the completed form. Log every staff member who contacted saliva or nervous tissue. A bat found in a room with a sleeping person or a young child counts as a potential human exposure.

name: purchase-agreement-review
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Reviews a residential purchase and sale contract before signature, flagging contingency deadlines, financing terms, and clauses that shift risk. Use when a buyer or seller sends over a signed offer, a counteroffer, or an addendum and asks what they are agreeing to. Also triggers when someone asks whether a deadline has already run or what happens if a contingency is not removed in time.
expansions: review this purchase contract before we sign
buyer sent a counteroffer, what changed
when does the financing contingency expire
seller slipped in an addendum overnight
can we back out and keep the deposit
offer has an escalation clause in it
check the closing date and possession terms
as-is clause in this contract worries me

atoms.obligation: Build a dated timeline of every contingency, notice, and performance deadline from the effective date before commenting on any other term.
atoms.lesson: Contract clocks run from the effective date, the day the last party signs and delivery is confirmed, not from the offer date. Inspection periods commonly run seven to seventeen days, loan contingencies twenty-one to thirty, and appraisal contingencies may run separately. Most forms count calendar days and roll a deadline landing on a weekend to the next business day. Deadlines are rarely self-executing: the buyer must deliver written removal, or the seller must serve a notice to perform, before cancellation rights ripen.

atoms.obligation: Confirm the earnest money amount, who holds it, and the exact conditions under which each party can claim it.
atoms.lesson: Earnest money is typically one to three percent residential, larger and often partly non-refundable in commercial deals. The holder matters: a neutral escrow will not release funds without mutual written instruction or a court order, so a refundable deposit still freezes if the seller refuses to sign a cancellation. Check whether the deposit goes hard at contingency removal, whether it applies to the price at closing, and whether a liquidated damages clause caps the seller's remedy.

atoms.obligation: Identify every item of personal property, fixture, and system included or excluded, and put it in writing rather than assuming.
atoms.lesson: Walkthrough disputes almost always involve arguable fixtures: mounted televisions and brackets, washer and dryer, refrigerator, window coverings, video doorbells, above-ground spas, and mini-split heads. The general test is attachment, adaptation, and intent, but the contract's inclusion list overrides it. Photograph anything the buyer expects to remain at the time of offer, and list model-level detail for appliances so a cheaper substitute cannot be swapped in before closing.

atoms.obligation: Read the financing and appraisal sections together to determine what actually happens if the loan or the value falls short.
atoms.lesson: A loan contingency protects the buyer only for the described loan type, rate cap, and amount, so a buyer approved for conventional financing who later switches products may lose that protection. If the appraisal contingency was waived but the loan contingency survives, a low value that still keeps loan-to-value inside guidelines is not a financing failure, and the buyer must bring cash. Confirm whether an assumption or seller carryback raises due-on-sale exposure.

name: title-commitment-review
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Works through a title commitment or preliminary report and explains what each exception means for the buyer, lender, or landlord. Use when the title company sends Schedule A and B, when an easement or old lien surfaces, or when someone asks whether a title issue will actually stop the closing. Also use when deciding what to demand removed, insured over, or endorsed.
expansions: title report came back with exceptions
there is a mechanics lien on schedule b
old easement runs through the driveway
will this cloud stop us closing friday
seller has a deceased co-owner on title
association recorded a lien for unpaid dues
need an endorsement for the survey issue
vesting does not match the seller name

atoms.obligation: Separate the exceptions into monetary liens, use restrictions, and survey matters, and give each category its own cure path.
atoms.lesson: Monetary items such as mortgages, judgments, tax liens, association assessments, and mechanics liens are ordinarily paid or released at closing from seller proceeds and cause little trouble once a payoff demand exists. Use restrictions like recorded covenants and easements rarely get removed and instead force a decision about whether the buyer can live with them. Survey matters such as encroachments and boundary gaps usually need a current survey plus an endorsement rather than a release.

atoms.obligation: Compare the vesting shown on the commitment against who is actually signing, and resolve any mismatch before the signing appointment.
atoms.lesson: Frequent mismatches include a deceased joint tenant needing an affidavit of death, a trust whose trustee has changed, a party divorced since acquisition whose former spouse remains in vesting, a dissolved entity, or a name variation needing a scrivener's affidavit. Probate, guardianship, and powers of attorney each add days or weeks and usually need underwriter approval of the specific instrument. Raising this early is the difference between a one-day fix and a postponed closing.

atoms.obligation: Ask which exceptions the underwriter will delete and which it will merely insure over, and get that answer in writing.
atoms.lesson: Title agents often say an item is no problem when they mean the underwriter will insure over it, which protects the insured against loss but leaves the encumbrance on the land. For a buyer who keeps the property, an insured-over encroachment still limits building and resurfaces at resale. Standard exceptions for parties in possession, unrecorded liens, and survey matters are deleted only on extended coverage supported by a current survey and an owner's affidavit.

atoms.obligation: Check that the legal description, recorded access, and appurtenant rights match what the buyer believes they are purchasing.
atoms.lesson: Compare the legal description against the survey and the tax parcel, because a lot split, a vacated alley, or a metes-and-bounds call that fails to close can mean the parcel is smaller or landlocked. Confirm recorded legal access to a public right of way rather than an assumed driveway over a neighbor. For condominiums, verify unit number, parking and storage assignments, and percentage interest against the declaration, since parking is often limited common element rather than deeded.

name: trust-account-reconciliation
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Keeps broker trust and client escrow accounts compliant through three-way reconciliation, timely deposit, and correct handling of funds belonging to owners, tenants, or buyers. Use at month end, when the bank balance will not match the ledgers, when an audit notice arrives, or when someone asks whether money can be moved between accounts.
expansions: trust account will not reconcile this month
auditor asked for three-way reconciliation
can we pay a vendor from deposits
owner draw overdrew their ledger
earnest money check arrived friday afternoon
rent check bounced after we paid the owner
negative balance on one owner ledger
commission still sitting in the trust account

atoms.obligation: Reconcile the bank statement, the checkbook register, and the sum of all individual beneficiary ledgers to the same figure monthly.
atoms.lesson: Three-way reconciliation is the standard most real estate commissions audit against. The adjusted bank balance must equal the book balance and must equal the total of every owner, tenant, and transaction sub-ledger. A gap between book and ledger totals almost always means a posting to the wrong ledger, an unallocated disbursement, or interest credited without allocation. Sign and date the reconciliation within the required window, often by the tenth to fifteenth of the following month, and retain it.

atoms.obligation: Deposit received funds into the designated trust account within the deadline your jurisdiction sets, never into an operating account.
atoms.lesson: Deposit windows are short and specific, often the next business day or up to three business days from receipt or from contract acceptance depending on the state. Holding an uncashed earnest money check at a party's direction is permitted in some states only when the contract discloses it. Commingling includes leaving earned commissions or management fees in trust beyond the allowed period and paying any company expense from trust funds even temporarily.

atoms.obligation: Keep every owner and tenant ledger non-negative, funding shortfalls from that owner rather than from other beneficiaries' money.
atoms.lesson: A negative owner ledger means one client's money paid another client's bill, the most commonly cited trust violation. It happens when a large repair, an insurance premium, or an eviction cost is paid before rent arrives, or when a draw is issued and the rent check later bounces. Hold a stated reserve per owner in the management agreement, delay draws until funds clear, and get written owner authorization before work exceeding the reserve.

atoms.obligation: Release disputed deposit funds only on mutual written instruction, a court deposit, or the specific statutory notice process.
atoms.lesson: When buyer and seller both claim earnest money, the escrow holder is a stakeholder with no authority to decide. The options are a signed mutual release, interpleader into court, or in several states a notice procedure paying one party if the other does not object within a set period. Some states impose penalties, including treble damages, on a broker who releases unilaterally. Document every demand and response and stay visibly neutral in writing.

name: inspection-repair-negotiation
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Turns an inspection report into a defensible repair or credit request, and prepares the response to one. Use when the general inspection, sewer scope, roof, or pest report lands, when a seller pushes back on a repair list, or when someone asks how much to ask for. Also use to choose between repairs, credits, and a price reduction before the contingency deadline.
expansions: inspection report came back with forty items
how much credit should we ask for
seller refuses to fix the roof
sewer scope found a belly in the line
buyer's repair request is unreasonable
knob and tube wiring flagged by inspector
two days from removing the contingency
take a credit or make them repair

atoms.obligation: Sort inspection findings into safety and habitability, deferred maintenance, and cosmetic items before naming any dollar figure.
atoms.lesson: Sellers respond to categories, not lists. Safety and system items such as active leaks, failed heat, exposed wiring, gas leaks, structural movement, sewer failure, and moisture behind finishes carry weight because they reappear for the next buyer and often trigger disclosure duties. Deferred maintenance like an aging water heater is usually priced into the market already. Cosmetic items reset the tone against you and invite a blanket refusal, so drop them entirely.

atoms.obligation: Obtain at least one written contractor bid for any item you intend to price above a few thousand dollars.
atoms.lesson: Inspectors write recommend evaluation by a licensed contractor precisely because they do not price work. A request built on inspector language alone is easy to dismiss, while a bid turns the conversation into a number. Specialist scopes matter: a structural engineer's letter for foundation movement, a plumber's camera report with footage marks for sewer, a roofer's remaining-life estimate. Expect bids high and confirm whether permits and finish restoration are included.

atoms.obligation: Prefer a closing credit over seller-performed repairs unless the lender or the condition requires the work completed first.
atoms.lesson: Repairs done under deadline pressure are usually the cheapest legal fix, with unknown contractors and no warranty running to the buyer, while a credit lets the buyer control scope and choose the contractor. The limits are real: lenders cap seller concessions by loan type and occupancy, government-backed loans may require peeling paint, missing handrails, or active leaks cured before funding, and a credit cannot exceed actual closing costs, so large asks become price reductions.

atoms.obligation: Deliver the request and any contingency removal in the contract's required written form before the deadline, not verbally.
atoms.lesson: Most forms require a written repair request and a separate written contingency removal, with a defined delivery method and time. A seller's verbal promise to fix something is unenforceable and never appears on the settlement statement. If negotiation is unfinished as the deadline nears, ask for a written extension rather than trusting goodwill: silence deems the buyer to have accepted the condition under some forms, and gives the seller a cancellation right after a notice to perform under others.

name: appraisal-gap-strategy
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Handles a valuation that lands below contract price, deciding whether to challenge it, renegotiate, cover the gap, or walk. Use when the appraisal comes in low, when the lender opens a reconsideration of value, or when a buyer asks how much cash they now need. Also use in advance when writing an offer on a property that may not appraise.
expansions: appraisal came in forty thousand under contract
how do we file a reconsideration of value
buyer does not have cash for the gap
appraiser used comps from another neighborhood
seller will not drop to appraised value
should we include an appraisal gap clause
second appraisal on the same case number
value came in low on the refinance

atoms.obligation: Recompute the buyer's total cash requirement at the appraised value before recommending any response to a low appraisal.
atoms.lesson: The lender lends against the lesser of price or appraised value, so the shortfall is cash on top of the existing down payment. On a five hundred thousand purchase with five percent down and a four hundred eighty thousand appraisal, the buyer needs the original twenty-five thousand plus the full twenty thousand gap, and the changed loan-to-value may cross a mortgage insurance tier and move the payment. Confirm whether gap funds can be gifted and whether reserves still qualify.

atoms.obligation: Challenge an appraisal only with specific factual errors and better comparable sales, submitted through the lender's formal process.
atoms.lesson: A reconsideration of value succeeds on facts, not disappointment: wrong gross living area, a missed bedroom, a comparable in a different attendance area or across a physical barrier, a distressed or non-arm's-length sale used as a comp, or closed sales after the effective date the appraiser lacked. Submit three or four closed sales with addresses, dates, and adjustments plus supporting listing data. Appraiser independence rules bar direct contact, so route everything through the lender.

atoms.obligation: Treat the appraisal contingency and the loan contingency as separate protections and determine which one the buyer still holds.
atoms.lesson: A waived appraisal contingency does not force the buyer to close if financing itself collapses, but a low value usually does not break the loan, it simply shifts cash to the buyer. Many forms permit cancellation only if value falls below a stated floor, so an appraisal gap clause promising to cover up to a set amount is an enforceable obligation to that number. Confirm how a government case number attaching to the property affects the next buyer.

atoms.obligation: Present the seller with the arithmetic of relisting rather than an appeal to fairness when requesting a price reduction.
atoms.lesson: The persuasive argument is that value follows the property, not the buyer: a government case number stays with the address for a period, and a conventional low value will likely repeat with any financed buyer. Quantify carrying costs per month covering mortgage, taxes, insurance, and utilities, plus renewed marketing time and the risk of another inspection round. Most of these settle in the middle, with the buyer covering part of the gap in cash.

name: closing-statement-reconciliation
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Checks the settlement statement or closing disclosure line by line against the contract, the payoff, and the prior estimate. Use when figures arrive before signing, when a number moves unexpectedly, or when someone asks why cash to close changed. Also use after closing when a proration or fee looks wrong and needs correcting.
expansions: cash to close jumped since the estimate
check this settlement statement before signing
tax proration looks wrong on the disclosure
commission split does not match the agreement
association dues charged for the wrong month
why is there a second title fee
payoff on the seller side seems high
closing tomorrow, review these figures

atoms.obligation: Trace every contract-driven figure, including price, credits, deposits, and prorations, from the agreement and addenda onto the statement.
atoms.lesson: The usual break points are a repair credit negotiated by addendum that never reached the closer, an earnest money amount understated because a second deposit was wired separately, and a rent credit or security deposit transfer on a tenant-occupied sale. Send the closer a short reconciliation naming each contract-based line and its source document. Anything the closer cannot tie to a signed document should be removed rather than explained away at the signing table.

atoms.obligation: Verify prorations by confirming the method, the through-date, and whether the underlying charge is billed in arrears or advance.
atoms.lesson: Property taxes are billed in arrears in some states and in advance in others, with varying installment dates, so an identical closing date can produce a credit to either party. Confirm whether the deal prorates on a three hundred sixty-five or three hundred sixty day basis and whether the seller pays through the closing day or the day before. Also sensitive: association dues, prepaid rent, master-metered utilities, fuel left in a tank, and supplemental tax bills.

atoms.obligation: Compare fees against the last loan estimate and challenge any increase exceeding the tolerance allowed for that category.
atoms.lesson: Lender charges, points, and fees for services the borrower could not shop are generally held to zero tolerance. Recording fees and services shopped from the lender's written provider list carry a ten percent aggregate tolerance. Prepaid interest, escrow deposits, insurance, and services shopped off-list may move freely. A changed circumstance such as a rate lock, product change, or value revision permits a revised estimate, but the lender must actually issue one. Excesses are cured by lender credit.

atoms.obligation: Confirm the payoff covers the correct through-date, per-diem interest, and any junior lien or credit line requiring closure.
atoms.lesson: Payoffs are good only through a stated date with daily interest accrual, so delayed funding leaves a shortage and an unreleased lien. Home equity lines must be frozen and formally closed, not merely paid to zero, or the lender can refuse to reconvey. Watch for prepayment penalties on portfolio and commercial loans, escrow refunds mailed to the seller instead of reducing the payoff, and unrecorded judgments or support liens attaching to the seller personally.

name: seller-disclosure-drafting
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Prepares or reviews a seller's property condition disclosures so known defects are stated accurately and nothing material is omitted. Use when listing a property, when a seller asks whether a past leak or a death must be mentioned, or when a buyer's attorney claims the disclosure was incomplete. Also covers lead paint, flood, and other mandatory supplements.
expansions: what must we disclose about the flood
seller fixed the leak, still disclose it
buyer claims we hid the foundation repair
lead paint pamphlet for a 1962 house
inherited property, seller never lived there
do we disclose the neighbor boundary dispute
prior insurance claim on the roof
filling out the condition report today

atoms.obligation: Disclose known material defects and past repairs even when the problem appears fixed, and attach the supporting paperwork.
atoms.lesson: The standard is knowledge, not current condition. A repaired foundation, a remediated mold event, a past sewer backup, or a roof replaced under an insurance claim all remain disclosable because they affect value and because claims history follows the address through insurance databases. Attaching the engineer's letter, the permit, the warranty, and the paid invoice converts a frightening line item into a documented fix and is the strongest defense against a later concealment claim.

atoms.obligation: Answer every question, using a truthful unknown only where the seller genuinely lacks knowledge, and never leaving blanks.
atoms.lesson: Blanks read as evasion and in many states leave the form legally incomplete, which can restart a buyer's rescission window. An estate, trustee, or investor seller who never occupied the property may qualify for an exemption from the standard form, but no exemption covers fraud or active concealment, and an as-is sale never waives disclosure of known latent defects. Where an exemption applies, state it on the form rather than answering questions the seller cannot answer.

atoms.obligation: Apply the federal lead-based paint requirements to any dwelling built before 1978, including the pamphlet and testing period.
atoms.lesson: For pre-1978 housing the seller must disclose known lead-based paint and hazards, hand over any reports, provide the required pamphlet, and give the buyer a ten-day opportunity to test unless waived in writing. The disclosure must be signed and attached to the contract and records kept three years. Penalties run per violation and can include treble damages. Rentals carry a parallel duty at lease signing, and renovation work triggers certified renovator rules.

atoms.obligation: Separate physical condition facts from opinions about neighbors, stigma, and off-site conditions, and check the local rule first.
atoms.lesson: States differ sharply. Several expressly relieve a seller of any duty to disclose a death on the property, including homicide or suicide, and some bar the question. Off-site conditions such as a planned highway, a nearby facility, or an airport noise contour are sometimes handled by a separate statutory notice. Neighbor disputes are usually disclosable where they involve boundary, easement, or shared-cost claims, because those run with the land and will bind the buyer.

name: commercial-lease-abstract
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Reduces a commercial lease and its amendments to a usable abstract of dates, money, options, and obligations. Use when a new lease is executed, when leases arrive during an acquisition, or when someone asks what a tenant is actually responsible for. Also use before a renewal or assignment when the operative terms are buried across amendments.
expansions: abstract this lease and three amendments
when does the tenant's option notice expire
who pays for the rooftop hvac unit
need key terms for the acquisition file
does the tenant have exclusive use rights
what is the base year for this tenant
assignment clause for a franchise transfer
percentage rent breakpoint on this retail lease

atoms.obligation: Read the original lease together with every amendment, side letter, and assignment before recording any term as current.
atoms.lesson: Amendments routinely reset expiration, restate the premises after an expansion or give-back, change the base year, add or delete options, and grant abatements a later assignee never sees. A side letter or commencement date agreement often fixes the real rent start, which can differ from the stated date by months of free rent or delayed delivery. Abstract by term rather than by document, citing document and section for each entry so a reviewer can verify without rereading.

atoms.obligation: Capture each option's exercise window, notice method, and preconditions, then calendar the earliest and latest permissible dates.
atoms.lesson: Renewal, expansion, termination, and purchase options usually require written notice in a window such as nine to twelve months before expiration, delivered by a stated method, with the tenant not in default. Missing the window by a day forfeits the right in most jurisdictions. Rights of first refusal and first offer carry short fuses, often five to fifteen business days. Record whether renewal rent is fixed, indexed, or set at fair market with an arbitration mechanism.

atoms.obligation: State the expense structure precisely: what base rent includes, what the tenant reimburses, and which caps or exclusions apply.
atoms.lesson: Labels mislead. A triple-net lease may still exclude roof, structure, and capital replacement, while a modified gross lease may pass through everything above a base year. Note the base year or expense stop, the pro rata share and its denominator, gross-up provisions for partial occupancy, caps that may be cumulative or compounding, and audit rights with deadlines. Record who carries which insurance, whether waivers of subrogation exist, and how taxes handle a reassessment triggered by sale.

atoms.obligation: Record the tenant's use clause, exclusives, co-tenancy rights, and any restriction the landlord owes other tenants in the property.
atoms.lesson: In retail, an exclusive granted to one tenant limits what the landlord may lease to anyone else, and breaching it can trigger reduced rent or termination. Co-tenancy clauses let a tenant cut rent or leave when an anchor goes dark or occupancy drops below a threshold. Radius restrictions bar nearby openings. Continuous operation and go-dark rights decide whether the landlord can force a store to stay open. These clauses drive acquisition value more than base rent does.

name: lease-renewal-negotiation
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Prepares and runs a renewal negotiation with an existing tenant, on either side of the table. Use when a term is ending, when a tenant demands a rent reduction to stay, or when deciding whether to renew, restructure, or send the space back to market. Also use to build the concession package or a blend-and-extend alternative.
expansions: tenant's lease expires in eight months
anchor wants a rent reduction to stay
should we renew or remarket this suite
build a blend and extend proposal
what improvement allowance is market right now
tenant threatening to relocate downtown
renewal at fair market rent, how set
holdover rent if they never sign

atoms.obligation: Quantify the true cost of losing the tenant, including downtime, concessions, commissions, and improvement dollars, before setting a position.
atoms.lesson: A renewal avoids a re-tenanting cycle that in most office and industrial markets runs six to twelve months of vacancy plus free rent, an improvement allowance often several times the renewal allowance, and full commissions on both sides. Convert both scenarios to net effective rent over the same term and discount them, rather than comparing face rents. That number typically justifies renewing several dollars under asking and shows precisely where conceding must stop.

atoms.obligation: Open the renewal conversation early enough that both the option deadline and a real marketing timeline remain available.
atoms.lesson: Start twelve to eighteen months out for spaces above roughly ten thousand square feet, six to nine months for small suites, and a full year for anchor or single-tenant assets. Starting late hands the tenant leverage because the landlord can no longer credibly market, and it can blow the notice date needed to regain possession. Track the option window separately, since an unexercised option often converts the tenancy to month-to-month at a premium rather than ending it.

atoms.obligation: Price concessions in whatever form the tenant values most while protecting face rent and any loan covenant tied to it.
atoms.lesson: Free rent, improvement allowance, moving money, a termination right, extra parking, and signage all cost real dollars, but face rent drives appraised value, loan covenants, and any future sale price. Landlords will usually trade a month or two of abatement or a larger allowance before cutting stated rent. Amortizing an allowance into rent at a stated interest rate preserves face rent and creates a recapture if the tenant defaults or terminates early.

atoms.obligation: Define any fair market rent mechanism concretely, naming the comparable set, adjustments, timing, and the tiebreaker.
atoms.lesson: An open fair-market renewal without a mechanism becomes a dispute. Specify the geography and building class of comparables, whether comps are adjusted to net effective terms, and whether the tenant's own improvements are excluded from value. The standard tiebreaker is three-appraiser baseball arbitration, where each side submits a number and the neutral must pick one, which pushes both sides toward reasonable positions. Set a floor at the expiring rent when the landlord needs downside protection.

name: cam-reconciliation-review
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Prepares or audits the annual operating expense and common area maintenance reconciliation for a commercial property. Use at year end when statements go out, when a tenant disputes a charge, or when a tenant's auditor sends a document request. Also use when a capital project or an insurance spike lands in the pool and someone asks whether it can be passed through.
expansions: tenant disputing the operating expense true-up
year end reconciliation statements are due
can we pass through the parking lot resurfacing
gross up expenses at sixty-eight percent occupancy
tenant's auditor requested the ledger detail
insurance premium doubled this year
admin fee on top of management fee
cap on controllable expenses was exceeded

atoms.obligation: Test every expense line against that specific lease's inclusions, exclusions, and caps rather than against the pool as a whole.
atoms.lesson: Reconciliations fail tenant by tenant because each lease negotiated different carve-outs. Common exclusions are capital expenditures except amortized savings items, roof and structural repair, leasing commissions and marketing, costs reimbursed by insurance or another tenant, income taxes and financing costs, repairs caused by landlord negligence, and above-market related-party contracts. Caps may be annual or cumulative, compounding or not, and frequently apply only to controllable expenses, leaving taxes, insurance, snow, and utilities uncapped.

atoms.obligation: Gross up only the occupancy-driven variable expenses to the level the lease states, then allocate.
atoms.lesson: Gross-up exists so a base-year tenant is not overcharged as the building fills. Gross up only costs that vary with occupancy, such as janitorial, interior utilities, and some management fee components, never fixed costs like taxes, insurance, landscaping, or security. The stated level is commonly ninety-five or one hundred percent. If the base year was not grossed up but the comparison year was, the tenant absorbs a phantom increase, which is among the most frequently recovered lease audit items.

atoms.obligation: Amortize any permitted capital item over its useful life at the rate the lease allows instead of expensing it immediately.
atoms.lesson: Most leases allow pass-through only for capital items required by a law enacted after the lease date or expected to reduce operating costs, and then only the annual amortized share. Use defensible lives: roof membrane fifteen to twenty years, asphalt overlay eight to ten, rooftop HVAC units fifteen, lighting retrofits ten. Include whatever interest factor the lease permits. Expensing an entire parking lot replacement in one year is the single most common trigger for a tenant audit and refund.

atoms.obligation: Issue the statement with line-item comparison and supporting detail inside the lease deadline, and answer audit requests promptly.
atoms.lesson: Many leases require delivery within ninety to one hundred twenty days of year end, and some bar recovery entirely when the landlord is late. Send prior year actual, current year budget, current year actual, the tenant's share percentage with its calculation, amounts already billed, and the resulting credit or invoice. Audit rights typically run sixty to one hundred eighty days from the statement and require the tenant to be current, and obstructing a proper audit often shifts its cost to the landlord.

name: rent-roll-audit
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Validates a rent roll against the underlying leases and the accounting ledger so the numbers can be trusted for a sale, a loan, or a budget. Use when a lender or buyer requests a certified rent roll, when reported income does not match deposits, or when preparing an offering package. Also use to expose expirations, concessions, and delinquency hidden inside a summary figure.
expansions: lender wants a certified rent roll
rent roll does not tie to the ledger
check these unit rents against the leases
concessions not showing in reported income
how much of this roll expires next year
delinquency looks understated to me
model and employee units on the roll
buyer's analyst questioning our occupancy

atoms.obligation: Tie the rent roll total to deposited cash and to the general ledger for the same period before circulating it.
atoms.lesson: Three figures should reconcile: scheduled rent on the roll, billed charges on the ledger, and cash actually received net of prepayments and delinquency. Gaps usually mean concessions granted outside the system, units marked occupied that are down or used as models or employee housing, or rent recorded at the lease amount while the resident pays a discounted rate. A roll that cannot be tied is the first thing a buyer's analyst finds, and it costs credibility on every other number.

atoms.obligation: Verify a sample of lease files against the roll, testing rent, term dates, deposit, and any concession or rider.
atoms.lesson: For a small property test every file; for a large one test twenty to thirty units weighted toward recent move-ins, renewals, and the highest rents. Check the signed lease, all riders, and the ledger for one-time credits. Recent leases at above-market face rent hiding a two-month concession are the classic way a roll gets dressed up before a sale, because the face rent supports a higher valuation while net effective rent is far lower.

atoms.obligation: Break the roll down by expiration month and flag any period where an unusual share of income rolls at once.
atoms.lesson: Lease expiration exposure is a metric lenders underwrite directly. In multifamily, clustering expirations into winter months in a seasonal market guarantees weak renewal pricing, and staggering them is worth real money. In commercial, a single tenant above fifteen to twenty percent of income expiring inside the loan term triggers a cash flow sweep or holdback. Show remaining term weighted by rent rather than by unit count, and note options that could extend or terminate.

atoms.obligation: Present delinquency by aging bucket and by tenant rather than as one blended total or percentage.
atoms.lesson: Two percent delinquency spread across many residents is collection friction; the same total concentrated in two tenants ninety days out is a credit problem and probably an eviction. Age receivables at thirty, sixty, and ninety-plus days, separate rent from late fees, utility billbacks, and damage charges, and identify balances already in court or on payment plans. A balance under a repayment agreement behaves very differently from ordinary arrears in underwriting.

name: tenant-screening-policy
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Builds and applies written screening criteria for rental applicants that are consistent, defensible, and fair-housing compliant. Use when setting criteria for a property, when an application is borderline, when a denied applicant asks why, or when a reasonable accommodation request arrives. Also use to handle criminal history and source-of-income rules correctly.
expansions: write screening criteria for this building
applicant has an eviction from 2019
denied applicant asking for a reason
do we have to take a housing voucher
cosigner for a student applicant
assistance animal request with no pet policy
credit score is low, income is strong
how far back can we check criminal records

atoms.obligation: Publish objective written criteria before advertising, and apply them identically to every applicant in order of receipt.
atoms.lesson: Written criteria are the defense against a discrimination claim because they let you show the same rule produced the same outcome for everyone. Set thresholds explicitly: an income multiple, commonly two and a half to three times rent, a minimum credit score, verifiable rental history length, and specific disqualifying records with lookback periods. Disclose the screening fee, what it buys, and the criteria at application. Bending the rule once for a favored applicant undermines every prior denial.

atoms.obligation: Send an adverse action notice naming the reporting agency whenever a report contributes to a denial or a stricter term.
atoms.lesson: Under fair credit reporting rules, a denial, a higher deposit, or a cosigner requirement based even partly on a consumer report requires notice with the agency's name, address, and phone, a statement that the agency did not make the decision, and the applicant's right to a free copy and to dispute. Eviction and criminal databases mismatch names frequently, so applicants must be able to correct errors. Keep the notice and the file for your stated retention period.

atoms.obligation: Evaluate criminal history individually by offense, recency, and relevance instead of applying a blanket exclusion.
atoms.lesson: Fair housing guidance treats blanket criminal bans as likely to create disparate impact, since arrests prove nothing and conviction rates differ by protected class. Weigh the nature of the offense, how long ago it occurred, evidence of rehabilitation, and whether it bears on resident safety or the property. Many states and cities now cap lookback windows, bar consideration of arrests, sealed, expunged, or juvenile records, and some require a conditional offer before any criminal check occurs.

atoms.obligation: Treat assistance animal and accommodation requests as disability matters governed by rules separate from pet policy.
atoms.lesson: A service or documented assistance animal is not a pet: no pet rent, no pet deposit, and no breed or weight limit, even in a no-pets building. Where the disability is not obvious you may ask whether the person has a disability-related need and for reliable documentation of that need, but not for a diagnosis or medical records. Requests may also cover a reserved parking space, a unit transfer, or a policy exception, and must be granted absent undue burden or fundamental alteration.

name: security-deposit-disposition
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Runs the move-out accounting: what can be charged, how it must be documented, and when the itemized statement and refund must go out. Use at move-out, when a resident disputes charges, when a deposit deadline is close, or when a demand letter arrives. Also use to set up move-in documentation that makes later charges defensible.
expansions: move out inspection is tomorrow morning
can we charge for carpet replacement
deposit deadline is in three days
resident disputing the cleaning charges
damage exceeds the deposit amount
tenant left without notice, what now
wording for the itemized deduction statement
roommate wants their share of the deposit

atoms.obligation: Send the itemized statement and any refund within the statutory deadline, counted from the correct triggering event.
atoms.lesson: Deadlines commonly run fourteen to thirty days, but the trigger differs by state: possession returned, the tenancy ending, or receipt of a forwarding address. Missing it is the most expensive routine mistake in property management, because many statutes forfeit all deductions and award double or treble damages plus the resident's attorney fees no matter how real the damage was. Where final repair cost is unknown, several states allow a good-faith estimate followed by receipts within a further period.

atoms.obligation: Charge only for damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, and depreciate replaced items rather than billing full replacement cost.
atoms.lesson: Wear and tear is what normal use produces: traffic-lane carpet wear, small nail holes, faded paint, worn counter finish. Damage is burns, pet stains through to the pad, large holes, broken fixtures, and missing items. Even for real damage most jurisdictions require depreciating to remaining useful life, and carpet typically runs five to seven years with interior paint two to three, so a four-year-old carpet destroyed in year four supports little charge. Cleaning is chargeable only back to move-in condition.

atoms.obligation: Document condition at move-in and move-out with a signed checklist and dated photographs of the same locations.
atoms.lesson: Without a move-in record every charge becomes the landlord's word against the resident's, and most adjudicators resolve that against the party who controlled the documentation. Photograph each room wide plus close-ups of floors, walls, appliances, and every existing defect, preserve the metadata, and have the resident sign the checklist within the first days. Many states additionally require offering a pre-move-out inspection with a written list of curable items so the resident can fix them.

atoms.obligation: Itemize each deduction with the specific location, the work performed, and either an invoice or a documented labor rate.
