atoms.lesson: Cleaning three hundred fifty dollars invites a dispute; kitchen degrease range hood and oven, two and a half hours at forty-five per hour, invoice attached, survives one. Charge from actual invoices where a vendor did the work and from a published, consistently applied rate where staff did it, and never mark up a vendor invoice unless the lease and local law permit. Show unpaid rent, utility billbacks, and late fees on separate lines, with any required deposit interest stated.

name: eviction-notice-preparation
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Prepares the correct pre-filing notice for a lease breach or nonpayment and maps the steps and timing that follow. Use when rent is unpaid past the grace period, when a violation needs a cure notice, when a tenancy must end, or when someone asks whether a notice already served is valid. Never treats self-help as an option.
expansions: rent unpaid for three weeks now
serve a notice to pay or quit
unauthorized occupant living in the unit
tenant holding over past the term
tenant says our notice is defective
repeat noise complaints from neighbors
can we change the locks
notice period to end a month-to-month

atoms.obligation: Match the notice type, cure period, and required content to the specific breach and the local statute before serving.
atoms.lesson: Nonpayment notices commonly run three to fourteen days, curable violation notices ten to thirty, incurable notices for serious conduct shorter, and no-cause terminations thirty to ninety days depending on tenancy length and local just-cause rules. Content requirements are strict: the exact amount owed with no late fees or utility charges bundled in where the statute forbids it, the periods covered, where and how payment may be delivered, and a signature. A defective notice is dismissed and the clock restarts.

atoms.obligation: Serve the notice by a method the statute authorizes and record precisely how, when, and on whom it was served.
atoms.lesson: Personal service is strongest. Substituted service on a suitable occupant usually requires a mailed copy as well, and posting and mailing is generally permitted only after documented attempts at the other methods, often adding days to the period. Record who served it, the date and time, the address, and photograph any posted notice. Count the period correctly: most statutes exclude the day of service and extend a deadline that falls on a weekend or holiday.

atoms.obligation: Never use lockouts, utility shutoffs, or removal of belongings, however clear the breach appears.
atoms.lesson: Self-help eviction is illegal in essentially every jurisdiction and carries statutory penalties, often a multiple of monthly rent or a fixed per-day amount, plus actual damages, the resident's attorney fees, and immediate restoration of possession. Changing locks, removing a door, shutting off water or power, and removing possessions all qualify, and doing any of it after a valid judgment but before the sheriff executes still qualifies. Abandonment has its own statutory notice and storage procedure.

atoms.obligation: Check for retaliation, habitability, and protected-status defenses before filing, and assemble the timeline that answers them.
atoms.lesson: Many statutes presume retaliation when action follows within a set window, often six months or a year, of a repair request, code complaint, or organizing activity, which shifts the burden onto the landlord. Unrepaired habitability defects can support rent withholding or repair-and-deduct and defeat a nonpayment case outright. Accepting rent after serving a notice frequently waives it. Gather the maintenance history, prior notices, and a ledger showing consistent enforcement before filing rather than afterward.

name: maintenance-request-triage
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Classifies incoming maintenance and repair requests by urgency and habitability exposure, then sets the response, the access notice, and the follow-up. Use when a work order arrives, when a resident reports no heat or a leak, when after-hours calls need routing, or when a backlog needs prioritizing. Also use to decide when to dispatch, schedule, or escalate.
expansions: no heat call at eleven at night
water coming through the ceiling
prioritize this week's work order backlog
resident says the cooling has been out
smell of gas reported in a unit
mold complaint from a second floor unit
tenant refusing entry for the repair
which of these count as emergencies

atoms.obligation: Classify every request on intake as emergency, urgent, or routine using habitability and damage exposure, not caller tone.
atoms.lesson: Immediate dispatch belongs to gas odor, no heat in cold weather, no water or a sewage backup, active flooding, arcing or exposed wiring, dead smoke or carbon monoxide alarms, a broken exterior lock or window on an accessible unit, and elevator entrapment. Urgent within roughly twenty-four to seventy-two hours covers refrigerator failure, no hot water, no cooling in extreme heat, and a dead outlet circuit. Everything else is routine inside a stated window, usually a week to ten days.

atoms.obligation: Give proper written notice of entry and honor a reasonable time window unless the situation is a genuine emergency.
atoms.lesson: Most states require twenty-four to forty-eight hours notice and entry at reasonable hours, with the notice stating purpose and date. Emergencies involving fire, flood, gas, or a threat to life or property permit entry without notice, but document the condition, who entered, when, and what was found. Entering without notice for routine work is a privacy violation that resurfaces later as a defense in every dispute with that resident and, in some places, as statutory damages.

atoms.obligation: Photograph the condition on arrival and on completion, and record cause, parts, and labor against that unit's history.
atoms.lesson: The photo pair settles the two arguments that follow every repair: whether the work was actually done, and whether the damage was resident-caused and therefore chargeable. Cause coding also feeds capital planning, since three drain backups in one stack in a year is a line problem rather than three clogs, and repeated compressor failures point to a specification error. A unit-level history is what supports a deposit charge, an insurance claim, and a habitability defense.

atoms.obligation: Escalate water intrusion and suspected mold on a defined clock, treating drying time as the controlling constraint.
atoms.lesson: Microbial growth generally begins within twenty-four to forty-eight hours of wetting, so the first action is stopping the source and getting extraction and drying equipment running, not scheduling an inspection. Document moisture readings inside affected assemblies rather than trusting surface appearance, because wet insulation and wall cavities dry far more slowly than finishes. Small areas may be handled in-house, while larger areas call for a remediation contractor and, in several states, an independent assessor barred from doing the remediation.

name: capital-reserve-planning
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Builds and updates the multi-year capital plan and reserve funding for a property or an owners association. Use when preparing next year's budget, when a major component nears end of life, when an association weighs a special assessment, or when a lender asks for a replacement reserve schedule. Also use to sequence projects against available cash.
expansions: roof is at year eighteen of twenty
association considering a special assessment
build a ten year capital plan
how much should we fund reserves monthly
lender wants a replacement reserve schedule
boiler replacement versus another repair year
reserve study came back underfunded
sequence these projects against cash flow

atoms.obligation: Inventory every major component with installed year, expected life, and current replacement cost before setting any funding number.
atoms.lesson: The component list drives everything: roof covering by section, exterior paint, asphalt and concrete, HVAC equipment by unit, boilers and water heaters, elevators with controllers listed separately from cabs, plumbing risers, electrical panels, windows, decks and balconies, pool equipment, and fire and life safety systems. Use observed condition rather than age alone, since a twenty-year roof at year twelve with ponding and failed flashing is nearer term than the schedule claims. Escalate costs annually instead of carrying stale figures.

atoms.obligation: State the funding target as both a percent funded and a required annual contribution, and show the consequence of underfunding.
atoms.lesson: Percent funded compares the reserve balance to the accrued deterioration of all components. Below roughly thirty percent, special assessments become likely and lenders in condominium markets begin declining loans on the units, which suppresses resale prices. Give the board three lines: current contributions, the fully funded contribution, and a threshold plan keeping the balance above zero at every point, with the special assessment each implies. Several states now mandate studies and minimum funding after structural failures.

atoms.obligation: Distinguish capital replacement from repair and maintenance, and keep operating and reserve spending in separate accounts.
atoms.lesson: Reserves fund replacing a component at the end of its life while operating budgets fund the repairs that keep it running, so patching a roof section is operating and replacing the membrane is reserve. The distinction drives tax treatment, what can be passed through under commercial leases, association rules that usually bar borrowing from reserves without notice and a repayment plan, and lender-held replacement reserve accounts that release funds only against invoices for scheduled items.

atoms.obligation: Sequence projects so work that exposes or damages another component happens first, and bundle mobilization wherever possible.
atoms.lesson: Do not paint before the roof and windows are replaced, do not resurface a parking lot before trenching for utilities or drainage, and do not refinish balconies before the structural scope is known. Bundling matters because mobilization, scaffolding, crane time, and permits are often a large share of a small project, so combining facade sealant work with window replacement on one swing stage saves meaningfully. Carry ten to twenty percent contingency on anything that opens an existing assembly.

name: vendor-service-contracts
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Sets up and manages recurring vendor agreements for landscaping, janitorial, snow, elevator, HVAC, and security, covering scope, insurance, and performance terms. Use when bidding out a service, when an auto-renewing contract is coming up, when a vendor's insurance certificate lapses, or when service quality has slipped. Also use to compare bids written to different scopes.
expansions: three landscaping bids, none comparable
vendor's insurance certificate expired
elevator contract auto renews next month
snow contract per push or seasonal
janitorial quality complaints from tenants
need a scope of work for hvac service
vendor wants to add a fuel surcharge
terminate this contract without a penalty

atoms.obligation: Write the scope of work with frequencies, standards, and measurable outputs before soliciting any bid.
atoms.lesson: Bids are comparable only against a common scope. Specify frequency and season, such as mowing weekly in growing season and biweekly otherwise, janitorial nights per week with trash, restroom, vacuum, and periodic detail broken out, and HVAC quarterly filters with annual coil cleaning and belt replacement listed. State who supplies consumables, what response time applies to call-backs, and what triggers extra billing. Without this the low bid wins by omitting work that becomes a change order.

atoms.obligation: Require a certificate of insurance naming you as additional insured before granting access, and track expiration dates automatically.
atoms.lesson: Verify general liability commonly at one to two million per occurrence, auto liability, workers compensation at statutory limits, and umbrella coverage sized to the property. The certificate must name the correct legal entity as additional insured, ideally on a form covering ongoing and completed operations, and include a waiver of subrogation. A lapsed certificate means an uninsured worker injury or a vendor-caused fire lands on your policy and your loss history. Elevator, roofing, and tree work warrant higher limits.

atoms.obligation: Diary every automatic renewal and its notice deadline, and decide well before the window rather than inside it.
atoms.lesson: Elevator maintenance, fire alarm monitoring, and waste hauling contracts are notorious for five-year terms that renew automatically unless cancelled sixty to one hundred twenty days ahead, sometimes with liquidated damages for early termination. Read the escalation clause, which may tie increases to an index or leave them to the vendor's discretion. Where the contract is called full service, confirm the exclusions, because obsolete parts, controller modernization, and damage from misuse are the usual carve-outs.

atoms.obligation: Tie payment to documented performance with a records requirement and a defined cure process for deficiencies.
atoms.lesson: Require dated service tickets or logs signed on site, and for snow require per-event records showing times, accumulation, and materials applied, which are also your defense in a slip and fall claim. Build in a written cure period, commonly ten to thirty days, with the right to hire a substitute and back-charge on failure. Hold retainage on project work until punch list completion and collect lien waivers with each payment on anything that could support a mechanics lien.

name: property-casualty-claim
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Manages a property insurance claim after a fire, water, wind, or liability event, from first notice through settlement. Use when damage occurs, when an adjuster's estimate comes in low, when someone asks what the policy actually covers, or when a resident's belongings are involved. Also use to preserve evidence and document lost rent.
expansions: burst pipe flooded three units
adjuster's estimate is far below our bid
hail damage on the roof last week
does the policy cover loss of rents
tenant claiming their furniture was ruined
deductible per occurrence or per building
fire damage, need to document everything
wind claim denied as wear and tear

atoms.obligation: Give notice to the carrier immediately, take emergency mitigation steps, and keep every mitigation invoice separate.
atoms.lesson: Policies impose a duty to protect the property from further damage, and reasonable mitigation costs such as board-up, extraction, drying, temporary fencing, and tarping are usually reimbursable and often paid faster than the main claim. Late notice is a common denial ground, especially for wind and hail where the date of loss is contested. Document the loss before mitigation changes the scene, using wide and close photographs, a video walkthrough, moisture readings, and retained damaged components.

atoms.obligation: Read the policy's valuation basis, sublimits, and exclusions before accepting any figure the adjuster proposes.
atoms.lesson: Replacement cost policies commonly pay actual cash value first and release recoverable depreciation only after the work is completed and invoiced, so a settlement number is not cash in hand. Watch sublimits and separate wind, hail, and named storm deductibles, which are often a percentage of insured value rather than a flat sum. Exclusions that drive disputes include long-term seepage, wear and tear, faulty workmanship, flood and surface water, and ordinance or law upgrades unless purchased.

atoms.obligation: Document lost rent and extra expense contemporaneously against the period of restoration, unit by unit.
atoms.lesson: Business income or loss of rents coverage pays for the time reasonably required to repair, not the time actually taken when the delay is the owner's, and typically begins after a waiting period of forty-eight to seventy-two hours. Build support from the rent roll at the date of loss, the leases, vacated unit ledgers, and concessions given to residents who stayed. Extra expense covers relocation, temporary equipment, and expediting. Keep abated rent visible in the ledger rather than netting it away.

atoms.obligation: Keep resident contents and liability exposure separate from the building claim, and check the lease's insurance clauses.
atoms.lesson: The building policy does not cover a resident's belongings; renter's insurance does, which is why most leases require it and name the landlord as an interested party. Where the landlord may be at fault, notify the liability carrier separately and avoid admissions or promises of payment. Check for a mutual waiver of subrogation in the lease, which bars each party's insurer from pursuing the other and can eliminate a recovery you were counting on. Commercial tenants often insure their own improvements.

name: association-resale-package
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Assembles or reviews the association documents a condominium or homeowners association closing needs: the estoppel or demand letter, governing documents, budget, reserve status, and insurance. Use when a unit goes under contract, when the closer requests the demand, when a buyer asks what the rules and fees really are, or when a lender questions project eligibility.
expansions: closer needs the association estoppel letter
condo documents for the buyer review period
what does the monthly assessment include
lender questioning the project's eligibility
special assessment pending at the association
rental cap in the bylaws for investors
association will not respond before closing
pet and parking rules for this unit

atoms.obligation: Order the estoppel or demand letter as early as the contract allows, confirming the association's turnaround time and fee.
atoms.lesson: Associations and their managers commonly take ten to thirty days and charge statutory or contractual fees plus a rush charge. The letter states current assessments, arrears, approved or pending special assessments, transfer and capital contribution fees, recorded violations against the unit, and any right of first refusal the association claims. It is generally binding on the association for a stated period, so a delayed closing may need it reissued, and unpaid assessments follow the unit as a lien in most states.

atoms.obligation: Read the declaration and rules for restrictions that would defeat the buyer's intended use before the review period ends.
atoms.lesson: The usual deal-killers are rental caps and minimum lease terms that block an investor or short-term rental plan, pet weight and breed limits, age restrictions in a fifty-five-plus community with its occupancy percentage requirement, parking assigned as limited common element rather than deeded, flooring and window treatment rules, and alteration approval requirements. Many states give a purchaser a statutory cancellation right running from receipt of complete documents, so incomplete delivery can leave that right open indefinitely.

atoms.obligation: Assess association financial health from the budget, reserve study, delinquency rate, and pending litigation, not from the fee alone.
atoms.lesson: A low assessment usually signals underfunded reserves and a coming special assessment rather than good management. Examine the reserve balance against the study's fully funded figure, the share of owners more than sixty days delinquent, the proportion of investor-owned units, and whether one owner controls a large block. Litigation over construction defects or structural repair is a warning sign and separately disclosable. Several states now mandate milestone inspections and forbid waiving reserve funding.

atoms.obligation: Confirm the association meets the buyer's loan program requirements, including insurance and project eligibility, well before funding.
atoms.lesson: Conventional condominium lending tests owner-occupancy ratios, the share of commercial space, delinquency above a threshold, single-entity ownership concentration, adequate reserve contributions, and the absence of structural safety issues or unfunded critical repairs, which now land projects on ineligibility lists. Insurance requirements include a master policy on the right form, fidelity or crime coverage sized to funds held, and flood coverage where applicable. Whether the master policy is bare-walls or all-in dictates what the unit policy must cover.

name: property-tax-appeal
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Evaluates and pursues an assessment appeal when a property's taxable value looks overstated. Use when the assessment notice arrives, when taxes jump after a sale or a permit, when a tenant asks why the tax pass-through rose, or when deciding whether an appeal is worth the cost. Also use to build the evidence file and hit the filing deadline.
expansions: assessment notice arrived, value looks high
taxes doubled after we bought it
is an appeal worth filing this year
gather comps for the assessor hearing
income approach for our apartment building
deadline to protest is next friday
tenant asking why the tax charge rose
assessor picked up our permit work

atoms.obligation: Confirm the filing deadline and the statutory valuation date first, since both are jurisdictional and rarely extended.
atoms.lesson: Appeal windows are often thirty to sixty days from the notice, or a fixed annual date, and missing one usually means waiting a full year no matter how wrong the value is. Value is set as of a statutory lien or valuation date that may fall months before the notice, so evidence must speak to conditions on that date rather than today. Some jurisdictions require paying the tax under protest to preserve the appeal, and some require informal review before a formal petition.

atoms.obligation: Verify the assessor's physical record card before arguing value, because factual errors are the easiest wins.
atoms.lesson: Assessors work from records that go stale. Check square footage, bedroom and bath count, year built, lot size, construction class, basement finish, and whether a permit was closed for work never done or counted twice. A garage recorded as finished living space or a demolished outbuilding still on the card can often be corrected administratively without a hearing. Also confirm exemptions are applied, since a missing homestead, senior, veteran, agricultural, or nonprofit exemption is a clerical fix.

atoms.obligation: Argue within the valuation approach the assessor uses for that property class rather than mixing approaches.
atoms.lesson: Single-family assessments respond to closed comparable sales near the valuation date, adjusted for size, condition, and location, and a recent arm's-length purchase below assessed value is powerful evidence, though some states then reassess to that price. Income property is argued on the income approach: actual and market rents, vacancy and collection loss, operating expenses excluding depreciation and debt service, and a capitalization rate supported by published surveys and local trades.

atoms.obligation: Weigh the expected tax saving against fees and the risk that the board raises the value before filing.
atoms.lesson: Estimate the saving as the value reduction times the total millage, then compare it against appraisal costs, filing fees, and any contingency fee, typically a share of the first year or of a multi-year saving. Some boards can increase a value on appeal, so a property already assessed below market should be left alone. Check whether a granted reduction carries forward or must be refiled annually, and remember that commercial reductions flow through to tenants who paid the higher pass-through.

name: rent-increase-notice
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Sets and communicates a rent increase that is legally valid and unlikely to trigger avoidable turnover. Use at renewal time, when planning a portfolio-wide increase, when local rent regulation or a statewide cap applies, or when a resident pushes back. Also use to decide when holding rent flat beats raising it.
expansions: raising rents across the portfolio in march
how much notice for a twelve percent increase
rent cap applies to this building
resident says the increase is illegal
renewal offer for a long term resident
market rent is two hundred above theirs
increase on a month to month tenancy
should we hold rent flat to keep them

atoms.obligation: Confirm the required notice period and delivery method for the size of increase and the tenancy type before sending.
atoms.lesson: Notice for a month-to-month increase is commonly thirty days, but many jurisdictions require sixty or ninety once the increase crosses a threshold such as ten percent, and some require the notice to state the current rent, the new rent, the effective date, and the resident's rights. A fixed-term lease cannot be increased mid-term unless it says so. Improper service, such as email where mail is required or a short count, makes the increase unenforceable.

atoms.obligation: Check whether the unit falls under rent regulation or a statewide cap, including which exemptions genuinely apply.
atoms.lesson: Statewide caps commonly limit annual increases to a formula such as a fixed percentage plus inflation with an overall ceiling, and many exempt newer construction under a rolling age test, single-family homes unless corporate-owned, and small owner-occupied properties, usually only where a specific notice was given at tenancy start. Local ordinances can be stricter, requiring unit registration, one increase per year, banking rules for unused increases, and relocation payments for certain no-fault terminations.

atoms.obligation: Compare the proposed increase against the full cost of turning that specific unit before finalizing the number.
atoms.lesson: Turnover in most multifamily markets costs a month or more of lost rent plus make-ready work covering paint, cleaning, flooring, and minor repairs, plus leasing and marketing cost. A ninety dollar monthly increase that pushes out a good resident can take a year or more to recover. Segment the roll: long-tenured residents far below market with clean payment history usually warrant a smaller step, while units near market can move with the comps. Staged increases across two renewals often net more.

atoms.obligation: Deliver the increase with market evidence and a renewal choice rather than as a bare new number.
atoms.lesson: Retention improves markedly when the notice offers options, such as a smaller increase for a longer term or a higher one for month-to-month flexibility, and cites what comparable nearby units actually rent for. Send it early enough that the resident can decide inside their own notice period, typically sixty to ninety days ahead. Never time an increase to follow a complaint, a repair request, or organizing activity, because in most states that sequence creates a presumption of retaliation.

name: comparative-market-analysis
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Produces a defensible pricing opinion for a listing, an offer, or an owner's valuation question. Use when preparing a listing presentation, when an owner asks what their property is worth, when an offer needs support, or when a property has sat without activity. Also use for a broker price opinion requested by a lender or an investor.
expansions: owner wants a price opinion this week
price this listing before we go live
no showings after three weeks
justify our offer to the seller
which comps support this number
unique property with no direct comps
should we do a price reduction now
price opinion requested by the lender

atoms.obligation: Select comparables by physical and market similarity first, then adjust only for the differences that remain.
atoms.lesson: Prefer closed sales from the last three to six months in the same school attendance area and subdivision, within roughly ten to twenty percent of gross living area, of similar age, style, and condition, and on the same side of any physical or perceived boundary. Verify each comp actually closed and was arm's length, excluding foreclosures, family transfers, and portfolio trades. Adjust for concessions first, because a full-price sale carrying a large seller credit is not a full-price comparable.

atoms.obligation: Use active, pending, and expired listings to read the current market rather than to set the value.
atoms.lesson: Closed sales are historical, pendings show what buyers are accepting right now and lead closings by thirty to sixty days, actives are the competition a new listing must beat, and expired or withdrawn listings mark the ceiling the market refused. Compute months of supply from active inventory over monthly absorption to place the property on the buyer's or seller's side, and track the median ratio of sale price to original list price to see how the market punishes overpricing.

atoms.obligation: Value income property on its income stream rather than on comparable price per unit alone.
atoms.lesson: Build net operating income from actual rents with a market vacancy factor and real operating expenses including management, excluding debt service and depreciation, then apply a capitalization rate drawn from recent local trades of similar assets. Test the result against price per unit and price per square foot as sanity checks. Below-market rents create upside a buyer will pay part of, while above-market rents propped up by concessions or expiring leases are risk that pushes the required rate higher.

atoms.obligation: State the recommendation as a supported range with an explicit pricing strategy, not a single number.
atoms.lesson: Give the range, the position within it you recommend, and why: a price at the top of a search bracket loses every buyer searching just beneath it, so a home worth five hundred two thousand usually lists at four hundred ninety-nine. Anticipate the appraisal by naming the comps an appraiser would use. Set expectations for days on market at that price and define the reduction trigger in advance, such as too few showings in two weeks or no offer by day twenty-one.

name: acquisition-due-diligence
domain: real estate transactions and property management
description: Runs the diligence period on an income property purchase: what to request, what to verify, and what must be resolved before the deposit goes hard. Use when a deal goes under contract, when the seller's document delivery slips, when diligence turns up something that changes the price, or when deciding whether to extend or terminate.
expansions: sixty day diligence period starts monday
seller has not delivered the leases yet
what should we request from the seller
deposit goes hard in ten days
environmental report recommends a second phase
zoning says legal nonconforming use
estoppels coming back with discrepancies
found deferred maintenance, retrade or walk

atoms.obligation: Issue a complete document request on day one and tie the diligence clock to delivery rather than to signing.
atoms.lesson: The standard request covers leases with all amendments, the rent roll, two to three years of operating statements and ledgers, tax bills and appeal history, service contracts, five years of insurance loss runs, utility bills, capital expenditure history, permits and certificates of occupancy, environmental and structural reports, litigation, payroll records, and warranties. Negotiate that the period begins on delivery of the last required item, because a slow seller otherwise consumes the buyer's time while the deposit sits exposed.

atoms.obligation: Verify income by tying leases to the rent roll and ledger, then confirm terms through tenant estoppel certificates.
atoms.lesson: Estoppels are the tenant's own confirmation of rent, term, deposit, options, arrears, landlord defaults, and side agreements, and they bind the tenant against later contrary claims. Send the form early because responses take weeks and major tenants negotiate the language. Discrepancies matter more than they look, since an undisclosed free rent period, an unrecorded expansion option, or a claimed landlord duty to replace a roof can move value materially. A seller estoppel is a weak substitute.

atoms.obligation: Commission physical and environmental assessments early enough that a recommended second phase still fits the period.
atoms.lesson: A property condition assessment produces immediate repairs plus a twelve-year capital table, while an environmental first phase is a records and site review that either closes out or recommends sampling, which adds weeks and needs seller access consent. Historic dry cleaners, gas stations, auto repair, and manufacturing are the common triggers, along with underground tanks and vapor intrusion on redevelopment sites. The first phase supports the innocent landowner defense only if completed inside its validity window before closing.

atoms.obligation: Confirm the current use, occupancy, and improvements are legally permitted, including parking counts and nonconforming status.
atoms.lesson: Order a zoning report and a certificate of occupancy for each space, then check the survey against setbacks and parking requirements. A legal nonconforming use may not be rebuildable after a casualty above a damage threshold, which both insurers and lenders price. Unpermitted improvements such as an enclosed patio, a converted basement unit, or an added mezzanine can force removal or an expensive retroactive permit, and they usually show up as a gap between the tax record area and the measured area.

name: mel-deferral-decision
description: Decides whether a reported defect can be carried under the minimum equipment list, which category and rectification interval apply, and what operational and maintenance procedures must be completed first. Use it when a defect is found at the gate or on turnaround and dispatch is asking whether the aircraft can go, when a deferral is approaching expiry, or when someone asks for a rectification interval extension. It also covers the boundary cases where the item belongs on the configuration deviation list or the non-essential equipment programme instead.
expansions: can we dispatch with this defect
one pack inoperative before departure
mel category b expires tomorrow
need a rectification interval extension
is there an o procedure for this
apu unserviceable for the whole rotation
defer the galley oven to next check
cdl or mel for a missing panel

atoms.obligation: Confirm the defect is listed in the operator's approved deferral list before releasing the aircraft, and never dispatch outside it.
atoms.lesson: The operator list derives from the manufacturer master list and may be more restrictive, never less. If the item is not listed, no deferral exists and the aircraft is unairworthy until the defect is rectified. Missing external panels and fairings belong on the configuration deviation list instead, which carries its own performance and speed penalties. Cabin items such as galley inserts are handled under an approved non-essential equipment procedure, not the deferral list.

atoms.obligation: Apply the rectification interval that matches the item category and count the days from the day after the defect was recorded.
atoms.lesson: Category A carries an interval stated in the item remarks, often expressed in flight cycles or a fixed number of sectors. Category B allows three consecutive calendar days, C allows ten and D allows one hundred and twenty. The day of discovery is day zero and is excluded from the count. Starting the clock one day early or late is the single most common finding in a deferral audit and can put the aircraft over expiry.

atoms.obligation: Carry out and record both the operational and the maintenance procedures called by the item before the aircraft is released.
atoms.lesson: An item flagged for an operational procedure needs a crew action such as a placard, an amended checklist item or a performance penalty. An item flagged for a maintenance procedure needs physical work such as deactivating a system, pinning a thrust reverser or capping a line. Both must be complete and signed before release. A pack deferral, for example, drives a maximum flight level restriction that dispatch must feed into the flight plan and the fuel figure.

atoms.obligation: Escalate to the technical authority for a one-time extension only where approved, and never extend the same defect twice.
atoms.lesson: Extensions are normally limited to one additional interval of the same length for category B and C items, granted under the approved procedure and notified to the regulator where required. They need evidence that parts or a hangar slot are genuinely unavailable and that the aircraft condition is unchanged. Chaining extensions, or clearing a defect and immediately re-raising it to reset the clock, is a serious airworthiness finding and shows up quickly in the log page history.

name: aog-recovery-coordination
description: Runs the recovery of an aircraft grounded away from base: identifying the right part, deciding between repair, loan, tail swap or cancellation, and getting people, tooling and paperwork to the aircraft. Trigger it when a tail is stuck at an outstation, when a part has to be sourced overnight, when another operator is being asked for a loan, or when a ferry flight is being considered. It also covers shipping constraints and the removal paperwork that follows.
expansions: aircraft grounded at an outstation
source a spare igniter overnight
borrow a part from another operator
arrange a ferry flight permit
engineer needs to travel with the part
customs holding our rotable shipment
should we swap the aircraft instead
aog desk escalation on a wheel

atoms.obligation: Establish the exact part number, serial effectivity and interchangeability direction before starting any search for a replacement.
atoms.lesson: Alternate and superseding part numbers matter far more than the description. A wheel or actuator may carry several dash numbers with one-way interchangeability, where the later part fits the earlier position but not the reverse. Confirm effectivity against the aircraft build standard and modification status, and check whether a service bulletin has already changed the installed configuration. Sourcing the wrong dash number burns the entire logistics window and usually the night stop with it.

atoms.obligation: Compare repair, part loan, aircraft swap and cancellation against the realistic recovery time before committing crews and passengers.
atoms.lesson: An outstation with no hangar, no ground power, no steps and no certifying staff turns a two-hour task into a twelve-hour one. Weigh flying an engineer and a part out against rotating a spare aircraft in, and check crew duty limits, night curfews at both ends and the departure slot before choosing. The decision taken in the first hour usually saves more time than any amount of chasing a faster part afterwards.

atoms.obligation: Ship the part with its release certificate and settle any dangerous goods classification before it leaves the stores.
atoms.lesson: A rotable arriving without its authorised release certificate cannot be fitted, however fast it got there. Many grounding items are themselves dangerous goods: lithium batteries, chemical oxygen generators, escape slide inflation cylinders, oxygen bottles and flammable adhesives all need correct packing, marking and a shipper's declaration. Hand-carry by an engineer does not exempt the shipment from those rules and normally makes acceptance at the security checkpoint harder, not easier.

atoms.obligation: Record the removed part's observed symptoms and operating history on the removal tag before it goes for repair.
atoms.lesson: Repair shops report no fault found on a large share of returns and the cost lands on the operator. A tag that states the observed symptom, the fault message, the phase of flight, the ambient conditions and the troubleshooting already carried out gives the shop something specific to test against. Add hours and cycles since new and since overhaul so warranty entitlement and later reliability analysis can both use the record.

name: turnaround-transit-check
description: Covers the transit or pre-flight check performed between sectors, including the walkaround scope, fluid servicing, who may certify the release, and the conditions attached to fuelling with passengers aboard. Use it on a short turn when there is pressure to shorten the check, when an arriving crew reports a defect, when oil or hydraulic uplift is needed at the stand, or when it is unclear whether the licensed engineer on shift can sign for the work done.
expansions: transit check on a 35 minute turn
walkaround before the next sector
oil uplift during a quick turn
refuelling with passengers on board
pilot reported a defect on arrival
who can sign the release here
brake wear pin looks short
tyre pressure check between sectors

atoms.obligation: Complete the inspection items in the scope and sequence the maintenance manual sets, not the sequence that fits the clock.
atoms.lesson: A transit check covers a defined external walkaround, fluid levels, tyre and brake wear, obvious damage and leaks, and a review of the technical log. Skipping the underside or the far wing because the airbridge or a loader blocks access is exactly how ground damage and slow leaks are missed. If the available window will not allow the full check, the aircraft is delayed. The check is never shortened to protect the departure time.

atoms.obligation: Check that the person signing the release holds the right licence category and a current type approval for the tasks performed.
atoms.lesson: Line certifying staff hold a category for simple scheduled line tasks and minor defect rectification, another for mechanical and powerplant work and another for avionics, each with a type rating on the specific aircraft variant. The holder of the simple-task category cannot certify a component change outside the defined task list. Releasing outside scope invalidates the certificate of release to service even when the work itself was carried out perfectly correctly.

atoms.obligation: Record fluid uplifts with quantities and apply the consumption limits before accepting the aircraft for the next sector.
atoms.lesson: Engine oil consumption is a leading indicator of seal and bearing distress and is trended in quarts or litres per hour per engine, where a step change matters more than an absolute figure. Log the quantity, engine position and hours since the last uplift. Overservicing pushes oil out of the breather and generates false leak reports. Hydraulic uplift needs the same discipline, because a rising rate usually points at an actuator seal or a line fitting.

atoms.obligation: Allow fuelling with passengers on board only with the agreed safety conditions in place and the flight crew informed.
atoms.lesson: Fuelling while passengers are aboard, boarding or disembarking requires two-way communication between the fuelling operative and a qualified person at the flight deck, seat belt signs off, aisles and exit paths clear, cabin crew at stations and an unobstructed escape route on the side away from the fuelling point. Confirm the airport fire cover requirement and any local prohibition, and stop fuelling immediately if fuel is spilled or vapour is detected in the cabin.

name: hard-landing-inspection
description: Handles the conditional inspection after a reported hard, overweight or abnormal landing: grounding the aircraft, obtaining the recorded touchdown parameters, choosing the level of inspection and dispositioning findings. Trigger it when a crew writes up a heavy landing, when an aircraft lands above maximum landing weight after a return, when someone asks whether the aircraft can fly the next sector while the data is pulled, or when structural distortion is found near the gear or wing root.
expansions: crew reported a hard landing
overweight landing after an air turnback
need the flight data readout first
basic or extended inspection required
gear shock strut looks over compressed
wing to body fairing wrinkled after landing
how long will the conditional check take
landed above max landing weight

atoms.obligation: Ground the aircraft as soon as a hard or overweight landing is reported and before any further sector is flown.
atoms.lesson: The crew report alone triggers the conditional inspection; it is not a judgement call for the duty engineer or the station manager. Damage from a heavy landing is frequently invisible from outside and appears as sheared or migrated fasteners at the gear attach fittings, wrinkled skin near the wing-to-body join, a distorted engine pylon or a compressed shock strut. Continuing on the assumption that the landing felt normal in the cabin is the classic failure in these events.

atoms.obligation: Obtain the recorded landing parameters from the flight data before choosing which level of inspection applies.
atoms.lesson: The branch between the basic and the extended inspection depends on recorded vertical acceleration at touchdown, sink rate, pitch attitude, roll angle and gross weight, read from the flight data or quick access recorder. Typical thresholds sit near one point eight g at maximum landing weight and lower at higher weights, with separate branches for landing above maximum landing weight, a nose-first touchdown or a significant roll. Crew perception correlates poorly with the recorded values in both directions.

atoms.obligation: Inspect the structural zones the manual lists for the applicable level, and release only when every finding is dispositioned.
atoms.lesson: The basic inspection covers the landing gear, gear attach structure, wheel wells, gear doors, nacelles and pylons and the lower fuselage skin. Any finding within that scope escalates to the extended inspection covering wing structure, empennage attachment and the pressure bulkheads. Damage beyond the structural repair manual allowable limits needs a repair approved by the design organisation, so raise the query early with photographs, dent depth and diameter and exact station coordinates.

atoms.obligation: Record the event, the recorded parameters and the inspection outcome so the airframe history carries the occurrence forward.
atoms.lesson: A hard landing becomes part of the airframe damage history and affects later fatigue and damage tolerance assessments, lease redelivery records and any subsequent structural query in the same zone. Log the date, flight number, recorded acceleration and weight, the inspection level performed, findings and repairs with drawing references. The event also goes into the safety reporting system, and repeated hard landings on a fleet or at a base feed the flight data monitoring programme.

name: bird-strike-response
description: Covers what to do after a bird or wildlife strike: inspecting the whole impact path, preserving remains for species identification, filing the mandatory report and judging engine damage against blend limits. Use it when a crew reports a strike on departure or approach, when blood or feathers are found on a walkaround, when an engine has ingested something, or when a station wants to understand its wildlife hazard trend.
expansions: bird strike on departure this morning
blood and feathers on the radome
engine ingested a bird on rollout
who do we file the strike report with
collect the remains for identification
leading edge dented after a wildlife strike
do we need a borescope after ingestion
wildlife hazard trend at this station

atoms.obligation: Inspect every surface downstream of the impact point, not only the area where the crew felt or saw the strike.
atoms.lesson: A single bird can strike the radome and shed into the wing root, an engine inlet or the horizontal stabiliser. Inspect radome, windshield and frames, leading edges of wing and tail, pitot and static ports, angle of attack vanes, antennas, landing gear and the engine inlet and fan. Tissue in an inlet requires an engine inspection even when the fan looks undamaged, because a soft body strike can distort or shift blades without leaving a visible nick.

atoms.obligation: Preserve the remains for species identification before the aircraft is washed or the stand is swept.
atoms.lesson: Species identification drives the aerodrome wildlife management response: gull, raptor, goose and small passerine each imply different mitigations, from grass length and drainage to scaring patterns and control of nearby landfill or water. Where feathers and tissue are unusable, a swab of the residue can be sent for genetic identification. Once the ramp crew hoses the stand the evidence is gone, so collect and bag it first and note the exact airframe location.

atoms.obligation: File the strike report through the national reporting channel within the required time even when no damage is found.
atoms.lesson: Reporting is mandatory in most jurisdictions regardless of damage, and the value of the national database depends on no-damage reports as much as damaging ones. The report needs aerodrome, runway, phase of flight, height above ground, time and light conditions, species where known, parts struck, damage description and operational effect such as a rejected takeoff, air turnback or engine shutdown. Under-reporting distorts the risk picture for every operator using that field.

atoms.obligation: Assess engine damage against the published blend and serviceability limits before returning the engine to service.
atoms.lesson: Fan blade leading edge damage is measured for depth, length and spanwise position, then compared against the manual's allowable limits. Damage within limits can be blended by an approved technician to a defined radius and surface finish, after which the blade set may need a moment weight and balance check. Damage beyond limits, or any sign that debris entered the core, requires borescope inspection of the compressor and turbine before the engine flies again.

name: borescope-inspection-planning
description: Plans and interprets engine borescope inspections: what triggers one, how to record findings so they can be compared over time, how to apply serviceable limits, and how the result feeds the shop visit plan. Trigger it when performance trend data shows margin erosion, when a repetitive inspection interval is coming due, when a technician asks whether a crack or coating loss is within limits, or when deciding between another few hundred cycles on wing and an immediate removal.
expansions: exhaust gas temperature margin has dropped
schedule a borescope at the next night stop
turbine blade coating loss found
is this crack within serviceable limits
engine due a repetitive borescope
plan the shop visit or keep flying
compressor blade tip curl in the image
sulfidation on the turbine nozzle

atoms.obligation: Trigger the inspection from condition indicators and event history, not from the calendar interval alone.
atoms.lesson: On-condition engines are inspected when the evidence calls for it: exhaust gas temperature margin erosion, rising fuel flow or vibration at a fixed power setting, an oil consumption step change, a magnetic chip indication, foreign object ingestion, a surge or a hot start. Repetitive intervals imposed by a directive or bulletin run alongside those triggers. A margin trend projecting to zero before the planned removal date is what drives the shop visit date, not the calendar.

atoms.obligation: Record every finding with its stage, blade position, distress type and measured size so the next inspection can compare growth.
atoms.lesson: The value of a borescope record lies in the delta. A nick on a turbine blade platform means little except against its previous measurement, so log the stage, the blade or vane count from the reference mark, the distress type — coating loss, burn-through, tip curl, creep, cracking, sulfidation, erosion — and the dimensions taken with a measuring probe. Save the images with a scale so a different technician at another base can repeat the same assessment.

atoms.obligation: Compare each finding against the published serviceable limits and record the disposition with the limit reference used.
atoms.lesson: Manuals give limits by stage and distress type, usually in three bands: serviceable, serviceable with a reduced repeat interval, and unserviceable. A crack length acceptable on one turbine stage is often rejectable on the next. When a finding falls into the middle band the reduced interval becomes a hard control that must go into the maintenance plan the same day, with the remaining flight hours or cycles stated on the release paperwork.

atoms.obligation: Plan the removal so the engine build matches the remaining life on its limited parts and the operating environment.
atoms.lesson: A shop visit is scheduled around the lowest remaining cycles among the life limited parts in the module set, because building an engine that returns to the shop for one disk wastes a whole visit and its removal downtime. Harsh environments with high dust, sand or airborne sulphur accelerate coating loss and hot section distress and shorten intervals materially. Match the build specification and thrust rating to the sectors the aircraft actually flies rather than the fleet average.

name: airworthiness-directive-compliance
description: Assesses new and existing mandatory continuing airworthiness instructions against the fleet, converts compliance times into planning controls, chooses between repetitive inspection and terminating action, and handles requests to comply by an alternative means. Use it when a new directive is issued, when preparing a compliance status report for an audit or a lease transaction, when a due date is approaching, or when someone asks whether a specific serial number is affected.
expansions: new directive issued on our fleet
compliance due in 500 flight cycles
apply for an alternative method of compliance
directive status report before the audit
repetitive inspection interval tracking
terminating action at the next heavy check
does this apply to our serial numbers
supplier bulletin referenced by the directive

atoms.obligation: Assess applicability against serial numbers, modification status and installed component part numbers before assuming the fleet is affected.
atoms.lesson: Directives are written against a type with an effectivity list that may exclude airframes already embodying a modification, or may bite on an installed component regardless of the airframe type it is fitted to. Work through the applicability paragraph line by line against the real build standard, including parts held as spares, and record any not-applicable determination with its supporting evidence. An unassessed directive is treated as non-compliant in an audit, however irrelevant it turns out to be.

atoms.obligation: Convert the stated compliance time into a hard planning control on the day the directive becomes effective.
atoms.lesson: Compliance times arrive as calendar time from the effective date, flight hours, flight cycles, time since new or time since last inspection, often combined as whichever occurs first or later. Translate that into a due value against current utilisation, add the repeat interval where the action recurs, and set an alert margin covering parts lead time and hangar slot availability. The effective date, not the issue date, starts the clock, and the gap between them is frequently two weeks.

atoms.obligation: Prefer the terminating action wherever one exists and can be planned into an existing ground opportunity.
atoms.lesson: Many directives offer a choice between a repetitive inspection and a modification that ends the requirement. Repetitive inspections consume hangar slots, man-hours and dispatch reliability for the remaining life of the aircraft, so the modification usually wins even at a higher one-off cost, particularly when a heavy check is already scheduled. Check whether the terminating action needs a long lead kit and whether embodiment changes the configuration relied on by other directives.

atoms.obligation: Route any request to comply by a different means through the approved channel and never apply it before approval is issued.
atoms.lesson: An alternative method of compliance must be approved by the authority that issued the directive, or by an approved design organisation holding that privilege, and the approval is specific to the operator, the airframes named and the conditions stated. Common cases are a different inspection technique, a longer interval justified by fleet data, or a repair already embodied. Flying against an unapproved alternative means the aircraft is simply not airworthy.

name: heavy-check-workpackage
description: Builds and sizes the work package for a base maintenance visit: assembling scheduled tasks, directives, modifications and deferred work, estimating man-hours and ground time with a realistic non-routine allowance, kitting materials and tooling, and controlling interval escalation. Use it when planning a letter check input, when a provider's quoted turnaround looks optimistic, when findings are running above plan mid-check, or when someone proposes deferring tasks at the aircraft.
expansions: build the work package for the c check
estimate man hours and ground time
non routine findings are running high
kitting materials for the hangar input
which tasks can we escalate
check input has slipped two days
capacity plan for the maintenance visit
bundle the modifications into this check

atoms.obligation: Build the package from the scheduled task source first, then add directives, modifications, deferred defects and commercial work as separate blocks.
atoms.lesson: The scheduled backbone comes from the maintenance planning document as adopted in the operator's approved programme: systems, structural, zonal and lubrication tasks at their check intervals. On top sit directives due in the window, chosen service bulletins, deferred defects best cleared with access open, cabin refurbishment and anything needed for a lease return or a new equipment mandate. Keeping the blocks separate is what makes cost recovery, warranty claims and later audit reconstruction possible.

atoms.obligation: Size the ground time from planned man-hours plus a non-routine allowance drawn from your own fleet history.
atoms.lesson: Non-routine cards raised from findings typically add thirty to fifty per cent on top of routine man-hours for a mid-life narrowbody, and far more on an older airframe with corrosion history or deep structural access. Use your own last three checks on the same type and age band rather than the provider's optimistic figure. Build in the shift pattern, the critical path through paint, weighing and functional tests, and a decision gate for late findings.

atoms.obligation: Kit and stage long lead materials, consumables and special tooling against the task cards before the aircraft arrives.
atoms.lesson: The commonest cause of overrun is not labour but a missing seal, a life limited part, a bonded stores item past shelf life or a special tool booked to another line. Explode the bill of materials for every routine card, add a consumable allowance, confirm shelf life will still be valid on the planned fitment day, and reserve calibrated tooling, jacks and weighing equipment with dates. Long lead structural parts need ordering weeks before input.

atoms.obligation: Control interval escalation through the approved programme revision process rather than by deferring tasks at the aircraft.
atoms.lesson: Extending a task interval needs evidence — sampling results, reliability data, manufacturer approval of the revised interval — and a change to the approved maintenance programme accepted by the authority. A one-off deviation at the aircraft is a different instrument with tight limits, usually a small percentage of the interval, applied once and recorded with justification. Confusing the two is a frequent audit finding, and an unapproved escalation invalidates the release for every affected task.

name: tech-log-review
description: Audits technical log entries for quality and legal validity: whether defect close-outs describe what was actually found and done, whether the release names the right approval holder and scope, how corrections must be made, and whether carried forward defects reconcile with the deferral register. Use it for a monthly log audit, when preparing for a regulator or lessor inspection, or when a vague entry blocks investigation of a repeat defect.
expansions: audit last month's technical log pages
defect closed with no rectification detail
pilot report wording is too vague
carried forward defect not cross referenced
release signed without an authorisation number
chapter coding wrong on these entries
correcting a mistake in a log entry
reconcile sector records with the flight log

atoms.obligation: Check that every recorded defect has a rectification entry stating what was found, what was done and what was tested.
atoms.lesson: Entries such as checked and serviceable, or reset and tested, carry no engineering value and destroy any chance of later fault analysis. A usable close-out names the fault confirmed, the manual reference and task used, the component removed or adjusted with part and serial numbers, and the functional or operational test performed. Where the fault could not be reproduced, that must be stated explicitly so the next occurrence is recognised as repetitive rather than treated as new.

atoms.obligation: Verify the release to service names the correct approval holder and covers exactly the work that was performed.
atoms.lesson: The certificate must carry the certifying staff authorisation reference and the approval under which the work was done, with date and place. A release signed before the work is finished, or before the required independent inspection on a control system, is invalid regardless of the outcome. Check that any component change carries its own authorised release certificate and that the fitted serial number in the log matches the paperwork filed against the aircraft.

atoms.obligation: Correct errors with a single struck line, the correction, the date and a signature, never by erasure or overwriting.
atoms.lesson: The technical log is a legal record of continuing airworthiness. Correction fluid, overwritten figures, pencil entries, torn pages and missing copies all invalidate the record and attract findings. A wrong entry stays visible: one line through it, the correct information alongside, initialled and dated by whoever made the correction. A missing page copy must be reconstructed with a documented statement of what happened, not quietly recreated as though nothing occurred.

atoms.obligation: Cross-check carried forward defects against the deferral register so nothing drops out between log pages.
atoms.lesson: A deferred defect must appear on every subsequent page until cleared, showing its raise date, category, expiry and any operational restriction the crew needs to see. The classic failure is a defect deferred at an outstation that never reaches the central register, so the interval is never tracked and the aircraft eventually flies past expiry. Reconcile log pages against the register weekly and investigate any item that appears in only one of them.

name: reliability-alert-investigation
description: Investigates a breached reliability alert level or a repetitive defect: testing whether the alert is statistically real, separating a single sick airframe from a fleet trend, attacking no-fault-found rates as a fault isolation problem, and closing the loop with a measurable change. Use it when preparing the monthly reliability review, when the same defect recurs within days, or when a component removal rate exceeds its alert threshold.
expansions: component removal rate breached alert level
same defect three times in two weeks
no fault found rate on this black box
monthly reliability meeting pack
pilot report rate climbing on air conditioning
which tail is driving the numbers
removal interval well below the published figure
propose a programme change from the data

atoms.obligation: Confirm the alert is statistically real before opening an investigation, checking the rate basis, the denominator and the sample size.
atoms.lesson: Alert levels are typically set as a rolling three-month rate against the mean plus two or three standard deviations of a stable baseline, normalised per thousand flight hours or per hundred departures. Small fleets and low-population components generate false alerts off single events, so check the underlying counts, the utilisation used as the denominator, and whether a coding change simply moved existing reports into that chapter. A rate spike built on two removals is noise.

atoms.obligation: Separate a repetitive defect on one airframe from a genuine fleet trend before choosing any corrective action.
atoms.lesson: When one tail contributes most of the events the cause is usually local: wiring chafe, a corroded connector, a poor bonding path, water ingress into a particular bay or a previous repair. A true fleet trend points instead at the design standard, a batch of components, a maintenance procedure or an environment such as a hot and humid route network. The remedies are completely different, and running a fleet campaign against one aircraft's wiring fault wastes months.

atoms.obligation: Treat a high no-fault-found rate as a fault isolation problem to be fixed rather than a vendor problem to be escalated.
atoms.lesson: No-fault-found routinely accounts for a third or more of avionics returns. The usual causes are removing the wrong line replaceable unit because troubleshooting stopped at the fault message, intermittent wiring and connector faults that do not travel with the box, and shop benches that cannot reproduce the aircraft environment. Improve the data on the removal tag, add a wiring and connector check to the isolation task, and send aircraft symptom data to the repair shop.

atoms.obligation: Close the loop by changing the programme, the procedure or the configuration, then measure the rate again against the alert level.
atoms.lesson: An investigation that ends with a report is not corrective action. What actually moves a rate is an added or shortened inspection task, a bulletin embodiment, a revised fault isolation procedure, a training point pushed to line stations, or a change of supplier or repair vendor. Set the review date, keep the alert open until the post-change rate has three months of data below the threshold, and record what was tried even when it failed.

name: rotable-spares-provisioning
description: Sets and reviews rotable stock levels and their positioning: sizing the float from removal rate and repair turnaround, classifying parts by dispatch essentiality, placing kits where they can actually be used, and reviewing holdings against consumption. Use it when opening a new base or adding a fleet, when the same part keeps being borrowed or expedited, when a summer schedule changes the network, or when slow-moving stock is tying up capital.
expansions: set stock levels for a new base
outstation kit for the summer schedule
how many spare wheels do we need
repair turnaround time is slipping
we keep borrowing the same part
review slow moving rotable stock
float quantity for the new fleet
which parts belong in the line kit

atoms.obligation: Size the float from removal rate, total repair turnaround time and the target service level, not from a rule of thumb.
atoms.lesson: The standard model treats demand over the repair pipeline as a Poisson process: expected demand equals removal rate per flight hour times fleet utilisation times the full turnaround, including transport, receipt inspection, shop time and return. The stock level is the smallest quantity meeting the target fill rate, commonly ninety-five per cent for dispatch-critical items. Understating turnaround is the usual error, because quoted shop time excludes shipping, customs and awaiting-parts delays.

atoms.obligation: Classify every part by dispatch essentiality so grounding items get stock and deferrable items do not.
atoms.lesson: An item whose failure stops the aircraft justifies stock at every station it night stops at; an item covered by a ten-day deferral can be held centrally and shipped when needed. Build the classification from the deferral list rather than from part cost, because expensive items are often deferrable and cheap ones often grounding. Wheels, brakes, tyres, batteries, filters and common seals belong at the line, deep avionics usually belong in one pool.

atoms.obligation: Position stock against the actual route network and each station's real capability rather than spreading it evenly.
atoms.lesson: A station with no certifying staff and no tooling cannot use a rotable held there, so the part is dead capital. Place kits where a night stop, a qualified engineer and a hangar or covered stand coincide, and cover thin stations by first-flight transfer from base. Factor in customs clearance and import duty at non-domestic stations, which routinely add a day or more, and pre-clear frequently moved items under a bonded arrangement where one exists.

atoms.obligation: Review holdings against actual consumption every quarter and act on both the stockouts and the non-movers.
atoms.lesson: Provisioning drifts as the fleet ages, routes change and modifications alter part numbers. Look for parts borrowed or expedited more than twice in the period, which signals under-stock, and for items with no movement in a year, which tie up capital and may be superseded, past shelf life or unusable after a configuration change. Feed observed removals back into the removal rate instead of keeping the manufacturer's initial provisioning figure forever.

name: life-limited-parts-tracking
description: Controls parts with a hard cycle or hour life: tracking them by serial number, proving unbroken traceability from manufacture, applying the right cycle counting definition and certifying destruction at expiry. Use it when building an engine, when a purchased or leased asset arrives with gaps in its records, when a thrust rating or mission profile changes the counting basis, or when a part reaches its published limit.
expansions: cycles remaining on the turbine disk
back to birth trace missing for this part
engine build with mismatched limited lives
part reached its cycle limit today
certify scrapping and mutilation of a disk
dual counters after a thrust rating change
limited parts status sheet for the shop visit
buyer is questioning our traceability records

atoms.obligation: Track each limited part by its own serial number and accumulated life, never by the assembly it happens to sit in.
atoms.lesson: Life limited parts — turbine and compressor disks, shafts, hubs, spacers, landing gear structural members and some flight control components — each carry an individual life in cycles or hours that follows the serial number through every installation. Moving a disk between engines carries its accumulated life with it. Tracking at engine or module level loses the history the moment a module is swapped, which is precisely the point where the error becomes expensive to unwind.

atoms.obligation: Prove continuous traceability from manufacture for every limited part accepted into the fleet.
atoms.lesson: Back-to-birth records must show every operator, every accumulation period and every shop visit with no gaps, evidenced by release certificates and life statements. A single missing period makes remaining life unprovable, and the conservative treatment is to assume maximum possible accumulation, which can wipe out the part's value. This is the main reason used engine purchases and lease returns stall, so verify the trace before acceptance rather than after the part is installed.

atoms.obligation: Apply the correct cycle definition and maintain separate counters where different ratings or mission profiles demand it.
atoms.lesson: A cycle is not simply a flight. Engine parts count full thermal cycles with additional partial counts for touch and go landings, air turnbacks and high thrust excursions, and a derated takeoff may count differently from a full rating one. Airframe and gear parts count landings or pressurisation cycles instead. Operators mixing short and long sectors, or changing thrust ratings, must run the counters the manufacturer specifies or the recorded life will silently diverge from reality.

atoms.obligation: Remove the part at its published limit and certify its destruction so it cannot re-enter the supply chain.
atoms.lesson: There is no extension, no concession and no on-condition assessment against a hard cycle limit. At expiry the part is removed, and where it is not returned to the manufacturer it must be mutilated so it cannot be repaired or reused, typically by cutting through the bore or hub, with the destruction recorded by photograph and a signed statement. Life-expired disks recovered from scrap yards are a recurring source of unapproved parts.

name: ndt-inspection-planning
description: Plans non-destructive inspections: choosing the technique that can actually find the expected flaw, working to an approved technique sheet with the right calibration reference, checking personnel qualification, and setting repeat intervals when an inspection stands in place of a repair. Use it when a structural task calls for a specific method, when a crack or corrosion finding must be characterised, or when a station proposes substituting equipment it happens to have.
expansions: eddy current check on the fastener holes
which technique for a subsurface crack
technician level required for this inspection
calibration standard for the ultrasonic probe
repeat interval after a damage tolerance repair
access needed for the stringer inspection
penetrant or magnetic particle here
crack found during a structural check

atoms.obligation: Select the technique from the expected flaw type, its orientation and its depth, not from what the station can do today.
atoms.lesson: Surface-breaking cracks in non-ferrous structure suit liquid penetrant or high frequency eddy current; cracks under a fastener head or in a second layer need low frequency eddy current or ultrasonic; ferrous parts such as gear components suit magnetic particle; disbonds and water in honeycomb suit tap test, ultrasonic or thermography; corrosion thinning is measured by ultrasonic thickness. Choosing by convenience produces a clean report from a technique that could never have found that flaw.

atoms.obligation: Work to an approved technique sheet naming the equipment, calibration reference, scan coverage and acceptance criteria.
atoms.lesson: A valid inspection specifies the instrument and probe or penetrant family, the frequency or sensitivity level, the calibration block with its known notch or hole size, the scan pattern and overlap, the surface preparation and the accept or reject threshold. Substituting a probe of different frequency or a reference standard with a different notch depth changes detection capability entirely. Record the calibration check before and after the inspection so a drift can be caught.

atoms.obligation: Confirm the people performing and interpreting the inspection hold current qualification in that specific method and level.
atoms.lesson: Personnel are qualified by method and level under the recognised aerospace scheme: level one performs under supervision, level two sets up, interprets and reports, level three writes and approves techniques. Qualification is method-specific, requires a periodic vision test and recertification, and is held against the employer. A level two in ultrasonic cannot sign an eddy current result, and an expired vision check invalidates the inspection however competent the technician actually is.

atoms.obligation: Set the repeat inspection interval from the damage tolerance basis whenever an inspection is left in place of a repair.
atoms.lesson: Where a crack or corrosion finding stays in service under an approved assessment, the interval derives from crack growth analysis between reliably detectable size and critical size, divided by a safety factor so at least two inspection opportunities exist before failure. That interval is a hard control, not a target date. Record it against the airframe with its threshold and repeat values and revisit it if utilisation or mission profile changes materially.

name: parts-airworthiness-verification
description: Verifies that a part is legitimately airworthy and eligible before it goes on an aircraft: checking the release certificate and its issuing approval, tracing suspicious material, controlling shelf life and packaging, and confirming eligibility for the specific airframe and position. Use it at goods receipt, when a part arrives without paperwork, when a trader's price looks impossible, or when a lessor questions whether an aftermarket part may be fitted.
expansions: check the release certificate on this part
part arrived without an airworthiness tag
suspect unapproved part in the store
shelf life expired on this sealant
is this aftermarket part acceptable for us
dual release needed for that shipment
static bag opened at the aircraft
trace this serial back to an approved source

atoms.obligation: Verify the release document, its issuing organisation and its status blocks before any part enters the stores system.
atoms.lesson: An acceptable release names the approval number of the issuing maintenance or production organisation, the part number, quantity, serial or batch and the status: new, overhauled, inspected or repaired. Check that the remarks block carries no restriction, that signature and date are present, and that a dual release is stated where the part must satisfy more than one authority. A certificate quoting a different serial number is a rejection, not a paperwork query to be chased later.

atoms.obligation: Trace the part back to an approved source and quarantine anything whose history cannot be established.
atoms.lesson: The recurring unapproved parts pattern is a genuine part carrying fabricated or transplanted paperwork, or a life-expired item recovered from scrap and re-tagged. Warning signs are prices well below market, documents that are photocopies of photocopies, serial numbers that do not match the data plate, a trader with no traceable prior operator, and tags from an organisation whose approval scope does not cover that part. Quarantine physically and report rather than returning it to the market.

atoms.obligation: Check shelf life, storage condition and packaging integrity at receipt and again at the point of issue.
atoms.lesson: Sealants, adhesives, elastomeric seals, hoses, batteries, oxygen equipment and pyrotechnic items all carry shelf lives, some cure-dated and some conditional on refrigerated storage, where a frozen sealant taken out starts a much shorter clock. Static-sensitive avionics must remain in conductive packaging until installation with a bonded wrist strap in use.
