A part whose life expires mid-check is useless, so check the date against the planned fitment day.

atoms.obligation: Confirm the part is eligible for the specific aircraft, position and modification standard, including any approval basis restriction.
atoms.lesson: Eligibility depends on the illustrated parts data effectivity for that airframe serial and modification state, not merely on the part number matching. Parts approved under an aftermarket production approval or a supplemental type certificate may be acceptable in one jurisdiction and not another, and a lease agreement may prohibit them outright. Check interchangeability direction too, since a superseding part often fits where the earlier one did but never the reverse.

name: tool-calibration-control
description: Controls measuring and special tooling: maintaining the calibration register, impounding and assessing the consequences when a tool is found out of tolerance, accounting for tools before closing panels, and checking that a tool's range and accuracy suit the task. Use it when a calibration due list needs working, when a torque wrench fails its check, when a tool goes missing in a work area, or when someone proposes substituting a tool the manual names.
expansions: torque wrench found out of calibration
recall work done with that gauge
tool missing from the shadow board
calibration due list for next month
borrowed tool with no certificate
pressure gauge reading looks wrong
foreign object search after a tool loss
personal tools brought into the hangar

atoms.obligation: Keep every measuring tool on a register with its unique identity, calibration date, due date and traceable reference standard.
atoms.lesson: Controlled tools include torque wrenches and multipliers, pressure and vacuum gauges, micrometers and dial indicators, multimeters, rigging pins and boards, weighing and jacking equipment, cable tension meters and leak test sets. Each needs a unique identifier, a certificate traceable to a national standard, an interval based on usage and manufacturer advice, and a visible label showing the due date. An uncontrolled tool from someone's personal box invalidates the work it touched.

atoms.obligation: Impound a tool found out of calibration immediately and assess every task it performed since its last valid check.
atoms.lesson: The failure is retrospective, which is what makes it serious. Work back through tool issue records and task cards to the last good calibration, then judge the consequence: an under-torqued flight control attachment or an over-torqued fitting may require re-torque, replacement of stretched fasteners or a dedicated inspection. Much of that work will be on aircraft already in service, so the assessment feeds directly into whether those aircraft may continue flying.

atoms.obligation: Account for every tool, fastener and consumable before closing an access panel or releasing the aircraft.
atoms.lesson: Loose objects left in structure cause jammed controls, chafed wiring and fuel tank contamination, and the damage often surfaces months later on a different continent. Use shadow boards or foam cutouts so a missing item is instantly visible, sign tools out and back, and count fasteners, lockwire offcuts, rags and inspection lamps. An unresolved loss keeps the area open and escalates the search rather than being written off as probably fine.

atoms.obligation: Confirm the tool's range and accuracy suit the task instead of assuming any calibrated tool will do.
atoms.lesson: A torque wrench used near the bottom of its range is inaccurate, so the target value should sit roughly in the middle band of its capacity, and an extension or crowfoot adapter changes the applied torque and needs the published correction calculation. Digital gauges read differently on pulsing systems. Where the manual names a specific tool part number, that tool has defined accuracy and geometry, and any substitute needs engineering approval first.

name: deicing-holdover-management
description: Manages winter ground de-icing and anti-icing: achieving a clean aircraft, choosing fluid type and mix for the conditions, timing and communicating the holdover, and deciding what happens when the holdover runs out on the taxiway. Use it when frost or snow is on the airframe, when the crew asks for the anti-icing code, when a slot delay eats the holdover, or when precipitation type changes during treatment.
expansions: freezing drizzle at the gate this morning
which holdover table applies now
type four fluid mix ratio check
holdover expired waiting for the slot
frost on the upper wing surface
post treatment contamination check needed
anti icing code to pass to the crew
fluid concentration test on the rig

atoms.obligation: Treat the aircraft until every critical surface is clean, then confirm the result by inspection rather than by fluid quantity used.
atoms.lesson: The clean aircraft principle means no frost, ice or snow adhering to wings, control surfaces, horizontal and vertical stabilisers, engine inlets, propellers, sensors, pitot and static ports or upper fuselage at takeoff. Cold-soaked fuel can hold frost on the upper wing in above-freezing conditions with no precipitation falling at all. A thin layer of underwing frost over fuel tanks is allowable on some types where the manual says so; upper surface contamination never is.

atoms.obligation: Select the fluid and mix from the actual precipitation type, intensity and outside air temperature at the time of treatment.
atoms.lesson: Unthickened fluid is applied heated, removes contamination and gives a very short holdover, while thickened fluids give a longer holdover but require a minimum rotation speed to shear off the wing. Each fluid has a lowest operational use temperature and a freezing point buffer, typically ten degrees for unthickened and seven for thickened. Freezing drizzle, freezing rain, ice pellets and heavy snow have their own tables, and some conditions have no holdover at all.

atoms.obligation: Start the holdover clock at the beginning of the final anti-icing application and pass the times and code to the flight crew.
atoms.lesson: Holdover is counted from the start of the last application, not from its completion and not from pushback. The anti-icing code given to the crew states the fluid type and brand where required, the fluid and water ratio such as seventy-five twenty-five, the start time of the final step, and confirmation that the post-treatment check was completed. Without that message the crew has no basis on which to make the takeoff decision.

atoms.obligation: Require a pre-takeoff contamination check whenever the holdover has been exceeded or conditions have worsened since treatment.
atoms.lesson: Holdover values are guidance derived from test data, not a guarantee, and heavy precipitation or a wind shift shortens them sharply. When the time expires during a long taxi or a slot delay, the aircraft either receives a contamination check by a qualified person from a vantage point that can actually see the wing, or returns for retreatment. Repeated treatments need care because thickened fluid residue can collect in control surface cavities and rehydrate later.

name: ramp-damage-assessment
description: Handles suspected or confirmed ground damage: taking the aircraft out of service, measuring and locating the damage properly, working the allowable damage limits before raising a repair query, and preserving evidence for cause and liability. Use it when a loader, airbridge or vehicle contacts an aircraft, when a dent is found on a walkaround, when a station wants to release an aircraft on a temporary repair, or when a handling agent disputes responsibility.
expansions: belt loader hit the fuselage
dent found near the cargo door
map the damage with depth and location
airbridge scraped the door frame
is this within allowable damage limits
raise a repair query with the manufacturer
ground handler liability for the strike
can it fly with a temporary repair

atoms.obligation: Stop the aircraft and record the event in the technical log the moment contact is reported or suspected.
atoms.lesson: Ground damage is chronically under-reported because the contact usually seems trivial to whoever caused it. Any suspected contact with a vehicle, loader, airbridge, steps, hose or container makes the aircraft unserviceable until inspected. The reported contact point is where the inspection starts, not where it ends: a loader striking the fuselage below a door can distort the door frame, the cargo floor beams and surrounding stringers well outside the visible scuff mark.

atoms.obligation: Measure and locate the damage precisely, recording depth, length, width and the nearest structural references.
atoms.lesson: A repair decision needs dent depth taken with a straight edge and depth gauge, length and width, the smoothness of the contour, whether the skin is scratched, cracked or creased, and the position by fuselage station, stringer and frame, or by wing rib and spar. Note the distance to the nearest fastener row, door cutout, splice or previous repair, because proximity to those features is usually what pushes a dent outside allowable limits.

atoms.obligation: Work the allowable damage limits first and raise a repair query only when the finding falls outside them.
atoms.lesson: The structural repair manual defines damage that may remain as is, sometimes after blend-out and corrosion protection treatment, sometimes with a repeat inspection attached. Working through those limits before contacting the manufacturer often releases the aircraft within the hour instead of the next day. Where the damage is outside limits, the query needs photographs with a scale, the measurements, precise location, the repair history of that zone and a clear statement of operational urgency.

atoms.obligation: Preserve the evidence and complete the ground damage report so cause and liability can both be established.
atoms.lesson: Photograph the aircraft, the equipment and its position before anything is moved, and record the equipment operator, the weather, lighting, stand markings and whether guidance or a wing walker was in use. Ground handling agreements set liability and reporting deadlines, and a late or thin report usually shifts the cost onto the airline. The same report feeds the safety programme, where the real fixes are stand design, equipment brake condition, training and marshalling discipline.

name: weight-balance-loadsheet
description: Controls mass and balance for a departure: using the correct dry operating figures for that airframe, distributing load so the centre of gravity stays inside the envelope throughout the flight, applying the right passenger weight basis, and handling last minute changes. Use it when a loadsheet needs checking, when the trim comes out near a limit, when the load is atypical, or when freight or passengers move after the sheet has been issued.
expansions: check the loadsheet before departure
centre of gravity outside the trim envelope
last minute change after boarding
standard passenger weights or actual
heavy freight in the aft hold
aircraft weighing is due this year
recalculate trim after a seat block
underload figure for extra cargo

atoms.obligation: Build every load calculation from the current dry operating weight and index for that specific airframe.
atoms.lesson: Dry operating weight and index change with cabin configuration, galley and catering fit, crew complement, potable water policy, seat changes, paint and accumulated repairs, so each tail carries its own figure from the weighing record and subsequent amendments. Aircraft are reweighed at a defined interval, commonly four years individually or on a fleet sampling basis, and after significant modification. Using a fleet average on a modified airframe silently shifts the whole calculation.

atoms.obligation: Distribute the load so the centre of gravity stays inside the envelope at takeoff, in cruise and at landing, not only at one point.
atoms.lesson: Fuel burn moves the centre of gravity as tanks empty in their sequence, so a load that is legal at takeoff can drift aft during cruise. Check the zero fuel, takeoff and landing conditions against their envelopes, respect compartment maximum weights and floor loading limits, and watch aft-loaded combinations of freight and rear cabin passengers. An aft centre of gravity erodes stall protection margin; a forward one raises rotation speed and trim drag.

atoms.obligation: Apply the passenger weight basis your approval allows and switch to actual weights when the load is not typical.
atoms.lesson: Standard mass values assume a representative passenger mix and break down on charters, sports teams, military rotations, small aircraft with few seats and heavy winter clothing on cold routes. Approvals normally specify values by adult, child and infant with a seasonal variation, and require actual or specific weights below a seat count threshold. Hand baggage allowance sits inside the standard figure, so a cabin-bag-heavy load can exceed it without anyone weighing anything.

atoms.obligation: Control last minute changes within the published limit and reissue the loadsheet when that limit is exceeded.
atoms.lesson: A last minute change entry lets a small variation reach the crew without producing a new document, bounded by a stated maximum weight and index shift, typically a few hundred kilograms and only in specified compartments or cabin zones. Beyond that a new loadsheet is mandatory. The change must reach the flight deck before doors close and must be reflected in the stabiliser trim setting the crew actually selects for takeoff.

name: crew-duty-limits-check
description: Checks whether a crew can legally operate a duty: computing the maximum flight duty period from report time and sectors, counting standby and positioning correctly, protecting minimum rest, and testing cumulative ceilings before a roster change is confirmed. Use it during a disruption when a delayed sector may run crew out of hours, when a standby callout is being planned, or when someone proposes shortening a rest period at an outstation.
expansions: is the crew legal for the delayed sector
flight duty period with four sectors
commander's discretion to extend duty
standby callout counting toward duty
rest at the outstation looks short
cumulative hours over the last 28 days
night duty crossing the low alertness window
roster change breaches days off

atoms.obligation: Compute the maximum duty from the reporting time, the number of sectors and whether the duty touches the low alertness window.
atoms.lesson: The maximum basic flight duty period starts near thirteen hours for an early afternoon report with one or two sectors and reduces by roughly thirty minutes for each additional sector, down to a floor around nine hours. Reports in the early morning, or duties overlapping the circadian low window of roughly two to six in the morning, cut the allowance further. The clock starts at report time, not at doors closed or off blocks.

atoms.obligation: Count standby, positioning and split duty against the limits using the rule that applies to each, never as free time.
atoms.lesson: Airport standby counts fully towards duty and usually towards the flight duty period. Home or hotel standby counts partially, often after a threshold of around eight hours, and long standby reduces the subsequent duty allowance. Positioning before an operating sector counts as duty but is not a sector for the reduction table. Split duty permits an extension only when a defined minimum break with suitable accommodation is provided, and the extension is a fraction of that break.

atoms.obligation: Protect the minimum rest before assigning the next duty and extend it where time zones or a long preceding duty demand it.
atoms.lesson: Minimum rest at home base is at least as long as the preceding duty or twelve hours, whichever is greater. Away from base it is at least ten hours, comprising an eight hour sleep opportunity plus travelling and physiological needs. Crossing multiple time zones and operating disruptive schedules attract additional requirements including local nights at home base. Rest is never shortened to save a rotation; the sector moves or the crew changes instead.

atoms.obligation: Check the cumulative totals as well as the single duty before confirming any change to the roster.
atoms.lesson: Beyond the individual duty sit rolling ceilings: block hours limited across seven days, twenty-eight days and twelve consecutive months, total duty hours over fourteen and twenty-eight day windows, and minimum days free of duty each week and month. A duty that is legal in isolation can still breach a cumulative cap. Commander's discretion, which extends a duty by a limited margin with a written report, gives no relief against those ceilings.

name: delay-code-analysis
description: Codes and analyses departure delays so the data supports decisions: attributing the cause that actually held the aircraft, splitting primary from reactionary minutes, capturing enough narrative to investigate later, and cutting the data by station, tail and wave. Use it when coding yesterday's disruptions, when punctuality drops at a base, when engineering is being charged for delays it did not cause, or when preparing a monthly performance review.
expansions: assign delay codes to yesterday's disruptions
technical delay rate for the month
reactionary delay from the first rotation
punctuality dropped at this base
coded as technical but it was a parts shortage
split primary from knock on delay
explain the departure delay to the network team
delay minutes by station and cause

atoms.obligation: Code the cause that actually held the aircraft, not the last visible event before the doors closed.
atoms.lesson: Standard delay codes group causes into families covering passenger and baggage handling, cargo and mail, aircraft and ramp handling, technical and aircraft equipment, damage and automated equipment failure, operations and crewing, weather, air traffic and airport restrictions, and reactionary causes. Coding a spares shortage as a technical fault hides a supply chain problem indefinitely, and coding a late crew as a technical delay makes engineering own a rostering issue.

atoms.obligation: Separate the primary delay from the reactionary minutes it causes downline and report both figures.
atoms.lesson: One morning technical delay can generate several times its own minutes across the day through late aircraft, late crew and missed slots. Reactionary minutes carry their own code pointing back to the originating flight, and only the primary cause is attributed to the responsible function. Measuring departments on total minutes without that split makes engineering own delays created by an early air traffic restriction, and it quietly destroys the incentive to code honestly.

atoms.obligation: Record sub-codes and free text with enough detail that the cause can still be investigated weeks later.
atoms.lesson: A code alone tells you a technical delay happened. The sub-code and narrative tell you it was an air conditioning pack change at an outstation with no spare, taking four hours of which two were spent waiting for the part to arrive on the next service. That level of detail is what converts delay data into a provisioning change or a manpower decision. Require narrative for any delay above a threshold, commonly thirty or sixty minutes.

atoms.obligation: Analyse by station, aircraft, time of day and code family before proposing any fix.
atoms.lesson: Punctuality is usually measured as departures within fifteen minutes of schedule, alongside arrival punctuality and completion rate. Cutting the data by station exposes handling and infrastructure problems, by tail exposes a sick aircraft, by first wave against later waves exposes overnight maintenance quality and turnaround buffers, and by code family shows whether the real problem is technical, handling or network. A fleet average conceals every one of those.

name: irregular-ops-recovery
description: Rebuilds the operating plan after a disruption: setting the recovery target, testing swaps against crew, aircraft and airport constraints, judging cancellation against a long delay, and publishing one plan to every station and function. Use it when a tail is stuck overnight, after a diversion or a long technical delay, when a curfew or slot threatens the rotation, or when someone asks whether to hold passengers or cancel.
expansions: aircraft stuck overnight with a defect
rebuild the rotation after a diversion
swap tails to protect the long sector
curfew at the destination airport
cancel or delay until morning
crew will time out before arrival
slot restriction pushing everything back
reaccommodate passengers on the later flight

atoms.obligation: Fix the recovery target first, naming the time and place the schedule must be whole again, then work backwards.
atoms.lesson: Recovery planning without a stated end state produces a sequence of local fixes that each look sensible and collectively wreck the following day. Decide which flights must operate, which aircraft must be at which base by morning for maintenance and for the first departure wave, and by when the rotation must rejoin the plan. Aircraft end-of-day position is usually the binding constraint, not the size of any individual delay.

atoms.obligation: Check crew qualification, aircraft capability and destination restrictions before committing to any aircraft swap.
atoms.lesson: A tail swap can break more than it fixes. Crews are type and sometimes variant rated, extended range sectors need a qualified aircraft with a valid pre-departure check, some destinations require specific navigation or performance approvals, and cabin configuration changes the seats actually sold. Add night curfews, airport opening hours, handling agent staffing at thin stations and the departure slot, which is rarely reissued at the moment you would like it.

atoms.obligation: Weigh cancellation honestly against a long delay using crew usage, passenger disruption and next-day recovery.
atoms.lesson: A delay that drags past the point where crew run out of hours or the destination closes ends as a cancellation anyway, but with aircraft and crew in the wrong place and passengers stranded overnight. Cancelling one thin flight early frequently saves several later ones. Include duty of care and compensation exposure, which in many regimes turns on arrival delay thresholds and on whether the cause was within the airline's control.

atoms.obligation: Publish the agreed plan and the passenger handling actions to every affected station and function at the same time.
atoms.lesson: Recovery only works when engineering, crewing, dispatch, the handling agents at both ends, the contact centre and the operating cabin crew are working from one version. State the revised times, the aircraft and crew assignment, the reaccommodation plan, hotel and meal arrangements with who is authorised to release them, and the point at which the plan will be reviewed again. Silence at the gate is what turns a delay into a complaint file.

name: etops-dispatch-compliance
description: Confirms an aircraft is eligible for extended range operation before dispatch: verifying the configuration standard, having the dedicated pre-departure check signed by qualified staff, keeping maintenance on the two engines independent, and trending consumption. Use it before a long overwater or remote sector, after an engine or system change, when a deferral may restrict extended range, or when a station lacks qualified certifying staff.
expansions: extended range pre departure check due
same technician worked both engines
oil consumption trend before the ocean sector
is the aircraft at the required build standard
deferral restricts extended range operation
verification flight after the engine change
diversion airport weather below minima
crew asking for the etops release

atoms.obligation: Confirm the airframe holds the required configuration standard and that no critical system has been altered without approval.
atoms.lesson: Extended range operation rests on a configuration, maintenance and procedures standard covering the propulsion system, electrical generation, hydraulics, fire suppression capacity, cargo compartment protection, equipment cooling and the auxiliary power unit's in-flight start capability. Modifications, part substitutions and repairs touching those systems must be checked against that standard before dispatch. An aircraft can be entirely airworthy for normal operation and ineligible for extended range operation on the very same day.

atoms.obligation: Have the dedicated pre-departure check performed and certified by staff holding the extended range qualification.
atoms.lesson: The pre-departure service check is a specific defined task, not the ordinary transit check, covering critical systems, fluid levels and any open items, and it must be certified by staff who hold the extended range qualification on top of their category and type approval. It carries a validity window tied to departure. Where the aircraft night stops at a station with no qualified staff, that has to be planned days ahead, not discovered at the gate.

atoms.obligation: Keep maintenance on identical systems across the two engines independent in both the people and the timing.
atoms.lesson: The dual maintenance restriction exists because a single common error applied to both engines removes the very redundancy the operation depends on. When the same task is required on both engines, different technicians perform them, or a second qualified person independently verifies, and where practical the tasks are separated by a flight. This covers oil servicing, chip detector checks, ignition and fuel system work and any similar action on both propulsion systems.

atoms.obligation: Trend oil and system fluid consumption against the programme limits and refuse dispatch when the trend is adverse.
atoms.lesson: Extended range programmes require oil consumption monitoring per engine per hour against a defined maximum and, more importantly, attention to a rising trend that has not yet reached that maximum. The same applies to hydraulic fluid and to auxiliary power unit oil, since the unit must be able to start and run at altitude. A step change in consumption before a long remote sector is a reason to change aircraft, not to top up and go.

name: dangerous-goods-acceptance
description: Accepts, refuses and loads dangerous goods correctly: working the acceptance checklist against the declaration, inspecting packages for damage, applying segregation and stowage rules with an accurate notification to the captain, and screening for hidden hazards in ordinary-looking cargo and passenger items. Use it at cargo acceptance, when a package arrives damaged or leaking, when lithium batteries are offered, or when a generic cargo description looks suspicious.
expansions: check this shipper's declaration
lithium batteries offered as cargo
package arrived damaged and leaking
notification to captain before departure
segregation of two incompatible classes
is this item forbidden on passenger aircraft
dry ice quantity in the hold
load position for a radioactive shipment

atoms.obligation: Work through the acceptance checklist item by item and refuse the consignment when any single element fails.
atoms.lesson: Acceptance covers the shipper's declaration against the dangerous goods list entry, proper shipping name, class and division, subsidiary risk, packing group, quantity per package against the packing instruction, specification marking on the packaging, hazard and handling labels, orientation arrows, overpack marking and any state or operator variation applying on that route. One missing element makes the shipment unacceptable, and correcting a declaration on the shipper's behalf is not permitted.

atoms.obligation: Inspect every package for damage, leakage and abnormal condition before loading, and remove any that fail.
atoms.lesson: A package that is damp, stained, dented, bulging, hissing, unexpectedly cold to the touch or emitting odour is refused and isolated, and any contamination of adjacent freight and the unit load device must be assessed and cleaned. Damaged lithium battery consignments are the highest consequence case, because a cell entering thermal runaway propagates to its neighbours and is not reliably extinguished by the cargo compartment suppression system.

atoms.obligation: Load according to the segregation and stowage rules and record the actual loaded position on the notification to the captain.
atoms.lesson: Incompatible classes must be separated, some substances are forbidden on passenger aircraft entirely, radioactive material carries transport index limits and separation distances from people and undeveloped film, and dry ice is limited by compartment ventilation because it sublimates and displaces oxygen. The notification states each item's shipping name, class, quantity, position by hold and unit, and emergency response code, and it must reach and be acknowledged by the commander before departure.

atoms.obligation: Screen passenger items and generically described cargo for hidden dangerous goods rather than trusting the description.
atoms.lesson: The high frequency problems are consumer items: spare lithium batteries and power banks that must travel in the cabin with terminals protected, damaged or recalled devices, electronic cigarettes, aerosols, camping stoves, wheelchairs with spillable batteries and mobility aids. Generic descriptions such as electrical equipment, machinery parts, consolidation, pharmaceuticals, samples or ships' spares routinely conceal batteries, flammable liquids, corrosives or compressed gases and should be challenged before acceptance.

name: accession-intake-record
description: Creates the accession record for archival material arriving at the repository, capturing provenance, extent, condition and title status before anything is shelved or opened. Use when a donor drops off boxes, when a campus office transfers files, when a purchased lot arrives from a dealer, or when unaccessioned material is found sitting in the backlog. Also use when someone asks how to measure a collection or what number to assign it.
expansions: donor dropped off twelve boxes
log a new manuscript accession
unaccessioned boxes in the backlog
transfer from the registrar office
measure linear feet of this gift
assign an accession number
record provenance for a purchased lot
boxes arrived with no paperwork

atoms.obligation: Assign a unique accession number and label every container before any material is separated from the grouping it arrived in.
atoms.lesson: Most repositories number accessions by year and sequence, such as 2026.014, and that number stays with the material through processing even when the collection later gets a different manuscript number. Number and label first because the physical relationship between boxes is itself evidence of provenance and original order. Once a well-meaning volunteer merges two donations on a sorting table, the distinction between a 1998 gift and a 2026 addition is gone permanently.

atoms.obligation: Record extent in linear or cubic feet along with inclusive dates, bulk dates, and the name of the source of the material.
atoms.lesson: A standard record carton is 1.25 linear feet, a letter-size document case 0.42, a legal-size case 0.5; oversize and artifacts are usually reported in cubic feet or item counts instead. Inclusive dates cover the outermost items, bulk dates the years where the substance sits, and the two often differ sharply when a collection has a few stray ancestral documents. Extent and dates drive processing estimates, shelf allocation and annual reporting.

atoms.obligation: Inspect arriving containers for mold, insects, rodent damage and water staining, and quarantine anything suspect away from the stacks.
atoms.lesson: Material from attics, basements and storage units routinely carries active mold or live pests. Hold new accessions in an isolated staging area for inspection rather than shelving them directly; look for frass, casings, grazed paper edges and the musty odour of germinating spores. Suspect items go into sealed polyethylene and, if wet or mouldy, into a freezer at minus twenty Celsius to arrest growth until a conservator can assess.

atoms.obligation: Flag missing legal title, obvious personal data and digital media in the accession record and route each to the right reviewer.
atoms.lesson: An accession without a signed transfer of title cannot be processed, digitised or deaccessioned safely, so the gap must be visible from day one rather than discovered years later. Note loose media such as floppies, optical discs and drives separately because they need forensic capture before their carriers degrade. Note visible identifiers such as student files, medical paperwork or personnel records so a restriction review happens before any researcher sees the boxes.

name: deed-of-gift-drafting
description: Drafts and reviews the agreement that transfers legal title in donated material to the repository, covering copyright, restrictions, unwanted material and future additions. Use when a donor is ready to sign, when a collection turns out to have no paperwork, when a family asks whether they can take things back, or when a donor wants to keep copyright or set an access embargo.
expansions: donor wants to keep copyright
draft a gift agreement
no signed paperwork for this collection
donor asked about tax deduction
add a restriction clause for correspondence
transfer agreement for university records
family wants materials back someday
review a deed before the donor signs

atoms.obligation: State separately whether the donor transfers physical ownership and whether the donor also transfers any copyright they personally hold.
atoms.lesson: Ownership of paper and ownership of copyright are distinct, and a deed that is silent on copyright leaves the repository unable to answer publication requests for decades. A donor can only assign the copyright they actually own, typically in their own unpublished letters, diaries and photographs they took; third-party letters received by the donor remain with those writers or their heirs. Where a donor will not assign, ask instead for a non-exclusive licence to reproduce and display.

atoms.obligation: Write any donor restriction with a defined end date or a defined event rather than leaving it open-ended or permanent.
atoms.lesson: Restrictions such as closing personnel or medical files are legitimate, but they must terminate. Common formulations close a series for a fixed term from the date of each record, or until the death of a named individual, or until a stated year. Avoid clauses that require the donor or family to approve each researcher, because within one generation there is no reachable approver and the material becomes permanently unusable while still consuming shelf space and staff time.

atoms.obligation: Include a disposition clause that lets the repository discard, transfer or return material it does not wish to retain.
atoms.lesson: Every accession contains duplicates, blank stationery, mouldy items and material outside the collecting scope. Without an explicit clause, staff must contact the donor about each shoe box of unlabelled newspaper clippings, or store them forever. Standard language grants the repository sole discretion to dispose of unwanted items by any means it considers appropriate, sometimes with an option for the donor to elect return at the donor expense within a stated window after transfer.

atoms.obligation: Decline to place a monetary value on the gift and refer the donor to an independent qualified appraiser instead.
atoms.lesson: In the United States a donee institution cannot serve as the qualified appraiser for a gift it receives, and donations valued above five thousand dollars need an independent appraisal and a signed acknowledgement form for the donor tax filing. The repository signs only to acknowledge receipt, never to endorse a value. Staff may supply a factual description and count of what was received, and may share a list of appraisers without recommending one.

name: archival-arrangement-plan
description: Plans how an unprocessed collection will be arranged into series and subseries, and at what level of detail each part will be processed and rehoused. Use when boxes arrive in no discernible order, when deciding whether to keep the creator original filing, when estimating processing hours for a large backlog collection, or when a minimal processing approach needs justifying.
expansions: boxes arrived in random order
how should i series this collection
plan minimal processing for eighty feet
should i keep the original folder order
refolder and reorder a manuscript group
split correspondence from subject files
processing plan for a photographer archive
estimate hours to process this

atoms.obligation: Survey the whole collection box by box and write the arrangement plan before rehousing or reordering a single folder.
atoms.lesson: A survey pass records what is in each container, the date ranges, formats, obvious restrictions and physical problems, and takes hours rather than the weeks the processing itself will take. Arrangement decisions made folder by folder from inside box one produce a scheme that collapses when box forty turns out to hold the creator own filing system. The survey also produces the estimate, the supply order and the restriction flags that let the work be scheduled honestly.

atoms.obligation: Preserve any meaningful order the creator imposed, and impose a new order only where the original has already been destroyed.
atoms.lesson: Original order is evidence: a lawyer files by client, a scientist by experiment, a politician by legislative session, and that structure documents how the person worked. Retain it even when it seems inefficient. Where movers, heirs or earlier staff have already scrambled the material, the arrangement is gone and cannot be reconstructed by guesswork, so impose a clear functional scheme by record type and document in the processing notes that the order is archivist-supplied.

atoms.obligation: Set the processing level per series so that the bulk of the collection gets minimal treatment and only high-value series get item work.
atoms.lesson: Minimal processing accepts folder-level or box-level description, retains original folders where they are stable, and skips unfolding, unfoldering and metal removal for routine series. Reserve item-level attention for photographs needing enclosures, audiovisual carriers, oversize and anything with acute preservation risk. The reasoning is access economics: eighty feet described at box level in three weeks serves researchers far better than ten feet described perfectly while seventy feet stay dark in the backlog.

atoms.obligation: Plan enclosures, oversize handling and separations at the same time as intellectual arrangement, and record every physical separation.
atoms.lesson: Photographs, negatives, textiles, audiovisual media and framed items usually leave the run of document cases for flat files, cold storage or media shelving. Each removal breaks the link between the item and its context, so a separation sheet stays in the original folder recording what was removed and where it now sits. Estimate supplies from the survey: acid-free folders, document cases, flat-file folders, mylar sleeves for the photographic material, and shelf space for the oversize.

name: finding-aid-drafting
description: Writes the descriptive finding aid for a processed collection, including the biographical or administrative history, scope and content, access and use conditions, and the container list. Use when drafting or revising an inventory, when a scope note reads too vaguely to help a researcher, when a student-drafted finding aid needs review, or when a collection-level record is needed quickly for a new accession.
expansions: write a scope and content note
draft the biographical sketch
container list for series two
the finding aid reads too vague
encode the inventory for the portal
collection level record for a new accession
add a conditions governing access note
review a student drafted finding aid

atoms.obligation: Supply the required descriptive elements at collection level first, so a usable record exists even if detailed listing never happens.
atoms.lesson: Single-level minimum description covers reference code, title, dates, extent, name of creator, scope and content, and conditions governing access. A collection-level record published within weeks of accessioning makes material discoverable immediately and can be deepened later with series and file description. Titles combine the creator name with the nature of the material, as in papers, records, or collection, and dates are given as inclusive with bulk dates where the distribution warrants it.

atoms.obligation: Write the scope and content note about what is actually in the boxes, naming forms, topics, people and gaps.
atoms.lesson: Researchers use the scope note to decide whether to travel. Say what document types are present, which years and which subjects are densely covered, whose voices appear, and equally what a reader would expect but will not find, such as a gap where records burned or where a series was retained by the family. Avoid biography and avoid evaluative praise; a note claiming a collection is invaluable tells a researcher nothing about whether their subject appears in it.

atoms.obligation: Keep the biographical or administrative history factual and proportionate, and cite where the information came from.
atoms.lesson: The history exists to let a reader interpret the records, not to memorialise the creator. Cover the dates and places of the life or the agency, the roles and offices held, and the functions that generated these specific records; a corporate body note should track reorganisations, name changes and the transfer of functions because those explain breaks in the series. Note whether the information derives from the material itself or from published sources, and describe contested aspects neutrally.

atoms.obligation: State access and use conditions explicitly, including restricted series, closure end dates, copyright status and preferred citation.
atoms.lesson: Access conditions and use conditions are separate: access covers who may see the physical material and when, use covers reproduction and publication. A reader must be able to tell from the finding aid that boxes 14 to 19 are closed until 2041, that fragile audio is unavailable pending reformatting, and that copyright in the correspondence was not transferred by the donor. Silence here produces disputes at the reading room desk and at publication.

name: original-item-cataloging
description: Produces a full original bibliographic description for an item with no usable existing record, covering transcription, fixed fields, extent and access points. Use when a search of the shared utility finds no match, when cataloguing a nineteenth century pamphlet, a map, a donated film or a rare volume, or when a piece has no ISBN and an uncertain publication date.
expansions: no copy record found in the utility
catalog a nineteenth century pamphlet
transcribe the title page exactly
fixed fields for a map
rare book needs full description
catalog a donated dvd set
the publication date is uncertain
this item has no isbn

atoms.obligation: Transcribe title, statement of responsibility and publication details from the item itself, without correcting or normalising what it says.
atoms.lesson: Description takes what you see: retain the typography of the title page, misspellings, and the wording of the statement of responsibility, adding a corrected form as a variant access point rather than silently fixing the transcription. Prefer the title page as chief source, then the cover, caption or colophon, recording in a note where the title was taken from when it is not the title page. Interpolations and information from outside the item are enclosed in square brackets.

atoms.obligation: Record extent, dimensions and carrier characteristics accurately, counting unnumbered sequences and noting plates and accompanying material.
atoms.lesson: Extent is more than a page count. Unnumbered leaves are counted and bracketed, plates outside the pagination are stated separately, folded maps get their folded and unfolded measurements, and a boxed set records the number of discs or reels plus running time. For non-book carriers state the medium characteristics that determine playback or use, such as sound characteristics, projection speed, scale for cartographic material, and the base and colour of photographic negatives.

atoms.obligation: Resolve uncertain dates to a defensible form and code the fixed fields to match the transcribed description.
atoms.lesson: Where no date appears, a probable single year, a decade, or a range with earliest and latest limits is supplied in brackets from internal evidence such as advertisements, a printer address, a directory listing or a watermark. The coded date type and the two date positions must agree with what the description says; a record that reads circa 1885 in the description but carries a firm single date in the coded fields will sort, limit and display wrongly for the rest of its life.

atoms.obligation: Add copy-specific information for rare and unique items in a way that stays attached to the holding rather than the title.
atoms.lesson: Provenance marks, bookplates, inscriptions, annotations, binding, and imperfections such as a lacking final leaf describe this copy and not the edition, so they belong in local copy notes rather than in the shared description others will reuse. This matters because a shared record is used by dozens of libraries whose copies are complete. Record the former owner as a searchable provenance access point when the association is significant, and photograph inscriptions before the volume goes to the stacks.

name: subject-heading-assignment
description: Chooses controlled subject and genre terms for an item or collection, applying established vocabularies, subdivision practice and local policy on outdated terminology. Use when deciding what a work is about, when no existing heading fits a new topic, when a genre term is needed for oral histories or photographs, or when harmful legacy terminology needs replacing in existing records.
expansions: assign subject headings for this book
which subdivision applies here
genre heading for oral histories
the topic is too new for a heading
propose a new subject heading
replace outdated terminology in records
headings for a local history collection
subjects for a photograph series

atoms.obligation: Determine what the work is about before searching the vocabulary, and assign headings that cover the predominant topics only.
atoms.lesson: Read the title page, contents, index, dust jacket and a sample of text to identify the topical, geographic and chronological aspects. Established practice assigns a heading only when at least twenty percent of the work concerns that topic, and caps routine assignment around six headings so that recall is not bought at the cost of precision. Cover the whole of the work with the most specific terms available, rather than layering a broad term over a specific one already assigned.

atoms.obligation: Distinguish what a work is about from what a work is, and use genre or form vocabulary for the second.
atoms.lesson: A book about detective stories takes a topical heading; a detective novel takes a genre term. Archival and audiovisual description depends on this split heavily, because researchers hunt by material type: oral histories, ledgers, glass negatives, plat maps, scrapbooks, home movies. Form and genre terms carry their own vocabularies with their own scope notes and hierarchies, so check the scope note before assuming that a term used topically means the same thing when used as a form.

atoms.obligation: Apply subdivisions only where the vocabulary authorises them, following the prescribed order of topic, place, chronology and form.
atoms.lesson: Free-floating subdivisions may be attached widely, while others are valid only under named categories of heading, and some strings must be established as a whole before use. The citation order determines meaning: a heading subdivided by a place and then a period is a different retrieval object from the reverse. Verify each string against the authority file rather than assembling it by analogy, because an unauthorised combination will not collocate with anything and will quietly strand the record.

atoms.obligation: Replace outdated or harmful legacy terminology in local records and document the substitution and its scope.
atoms.lesson: Many institutions have replaced terms such as illegal aliens or obsolete racial and disability language with community-preferred terms in local indexes while the national vocabulary catches up. Do this systematically: define the term mapping, record the date and authority for the change, retain the superseded term as a hidden search variant so old citations still retrieve, and add a statement about description language and remediation to the public catalogue rather than making silent edits.

name: name-authority-maintenance
description: Establishes and maintains authorised forms of names for people, families and corporate bodies, with the cross references and attributes that keep them distinct. Use when two creators share a name, when no authority record exists for a person being catalogued, when an organisation renames or merges, or when a pseudonym, married name or family form needs linking.
expansions: two authors with the same name
no authority record for this person
corporate body changed its name
conflicting forms of the family name
pseudonym needs a cross reference
update a heading after a name change
creator access point for a fonds
check the authority file before cataloging

atoms.obligation: Search the authority file thoroughly for existing and variant forms before establishing any new heading for a name.
atoms.lesson: Duplicate authority records split a person work across two headings and are tedious to merge later. Search inverted and direct forms, initials against spelled-out forenames, maiden and married surnames, transliteration variants, and the corporate name under both its parent body and its own name. Also check bibliographic files for how the name has already been used in uncontrolled access points, since existing usage shows the forms researchers will actually type.

atoms.obligation: Base the authorised form on how the name predominantly appears in the resources associated with that person or body.
atoms.lesson: The heading follows usage, not legal documents: a novelist publishing consistently as a shortened forename is established that way even if the birth certificate differs. For corporate bodies, use the name as the body presents itself, entering subordinate units under the parent only when the unit name is generic or implies subordination. Record the fuller form, birth and death dates, field of activity, affiliation and language as attributes, because these are what let a user tell two similar records apart.

atoms.obligation: Create a separate authorised heading whenever a new name would otherwise conflict with an existing person or body.
atoms.lesson: When two people share a name, break the conflict with dates, a fuller form of forename, or a qualifying term such as profession. If nothing distinguishing can be found, an undifferentiated record covers several people at once, which is a last resort because it defeats collocation. Never resolve a conflict by adding a random qualifier of your own invention; use the sequence of tie-breakers the standard prescribes so that other cataloguers reach the same result.

atoms.obligation: Add cross references from every variant form and record relationships between earlier and later names of a body.
atoms.lesson: References carry users from what they searched to what was established: pseudonyms, married names, acronyms, foreign-language forms, and pre-merger names. A corporate body that changes name gets a new authority record linked to the old one as earlier and later heading rather than an edit in place, because the records created under the former name legitimately stay under it. Archival creator access points follow the same file, so the fonds creator and the catalogued publications collocate.

name: classification-shelflisting
description: Assigns class numbers and shelf marks so that items sit in a browsable order and every call number is unique in the local shelflist. Use when a title spans two class numbers, when a Cutter collides with an existing shelf mark, when reclassifying a collection, or when deciding placement for oversize, serials or a local special collection code.
expansions: assign a call number for this title
cutter conflicts with the existing shelflist
the book straddles two class numbers
reclassify a run from dewey to lc
spine label for an oversize volume
where should this sit on the shelf
local collection code for juvenile
call number for a serial title

atoms.obligation: Class the work by its dominant subject and intended discipline, choosing one number even when several could arguably apply.
atoms.lesson: A book on the economics of forestry can be classed with forestry or with economics; the choice follows the discipline the author writes from and the shelf neighbourhood readers of this work will browse. Where a work treats two subjects equally, classification convention favours the one treated first or the one given emphasis, and where it covers three or more, the broader number that encompasses them. Consistency with existing local holdings matters more than defending an abstract best answer.

atoms.obligation: Build the shelf mark so it files uniquely, adjusting the author mark and adding date or work marks as needed.
atoms.lesson: Cutter numbers are decimal, so an existing mark can always be split by adding a digit rather than by displacing the neighbour. Check the shelflist in the actual sequence before committing. Editions of the same work are distinguished by publication year, translations by a language work mark, and multiple works by one author at the same number by a title-derived letter. A duplicate call number means two different books answer to one address, which breaks inventory, holds and reshelving.

atoms.obligation: Keep the physical location prefixes and size designations out of the class number itself and in a separate element.
atoms.lesson: Oversize, reference, juvenile, storage and special collections are locations, not subjects. Record them as a prefix or location code so a volume can move between a reading room and a remote store without its intellectual class changing. Oversize policy is usually driven by shelf height, commonly items above thirty or thirty-two centimetres, and needs a dummy or a catalogue note so a browser at the normal shelf position learns the volume lives elsewhere.

atoms.obligation: Plan any reclassification as a batch with label, catalogue, inventory and signage changes handled together.
atoms.lesson: Moving a run from one scheme to another is a physical project, not a cataloguing decision: every volume needs a new label, the item record needs its call number changed, holds and reserve lists need checking, and the end-panel signage and shelf map need updating on the same day the books move. Do it by whole class blocks so the sequence is never half-converted, and keep a crosswalk of old to new numbers for reference staff fielding questions about missing titles.

name: serials-check-in-claiming
description: Manages the receipt of continuing publications, including prediction patterns, claims for missing issues, holdings statements, title changes and bindery preparation. Use when an issue never arrived, when a journal changes or merges titles, when the public holdings statement is wrong, or when setting up check-in for a new subscription.
expansions: the issue never arrived this month
set up a prediction pattern
claim a missing journal issue
the journal changed its title
holdings statement is wrong in the catalog
bindery prep for volume forty seven
publisher merged two titles
the subscription lapsed mid volume

atoms.obligation: Build the prediction pattern from the publisher stated frequency and the actual enumeration printed on recent issues.
atoms.lesson: Prediction depends on knowing the frequency, the number of issues per volume, the month a volume begins, and any regular combined or skipped issues such as a July and August double number. Take these from issues in hand rather than from the vendor record, which often lags. A wrong pattern generates false claims that annoy publishers and mask real gaps, and it puts phantom expected issues in the public display where readers request items that were never published.

atoms.obligation: Claim missing issues within the publisher claiming window and escalate through the subscription agent when claims fail.
atoms.lesson: Most publishers accept claims for roughly three to six months after publication for domestic titles and longer for overseas ones; outside that window the only remedy is purchase or a duplicate exchange. Claim the specific enumeration and chronology rather than a date range, keep the claim count per issue visible, and after two unanswered claims escalate to the agent with the subscription number and the check-in history. Persistent non-supply is renewal evidence, not just an inconvenience.

atoms.obligation: Treat a title change as a new bibliographic record linked to the old one, and close the holdings on the earlier title.
atoms.lesson: A serial that changes its name substantively is described anew and linked as a continuation, so the earlier record ends with its last volume and issue and the later one starts fresh. Successive entry keeps holdings statements truthful about what is physically on the shelf under each name. Mergers and splits work the same way, with preceding and succeeding links so a reader who arrives at either record can follow the run in both directions.

atoms.obligation: Keep the public holdings statement compressed, accurate about gaps, and updated whenever volumes bind or are withdrawn.
atoms.lesson: A holdings statement records what is actually held, using ranges with breaks made explicit rather than an unqualified span that implies completeness. When issues go to the bindery they are unavailable for weeks and should show as at bindery rather than on shelf. When a print run is cancelled in favour of online access, the statement must close at the final print volume and the electronic coverage recorded separately, otherwise reference staff send readers to shelves that stop years earlier.

name: collection-development-policy
description: Writes and applies the policy that defines what the institution collects, at what depth, in what formats, and how gifts, challenges and budget allocations are handled. Use when a policy needs drafting or revising, when declining an offered donation, when dividing the materials budget across subjects, or when responding to a request to remove or add a title.
expansions: write a collection policy for the branch
what do we collect and what do we not
decline a gift politely
allocate the materials budget by subject
respond to a request to remove a book
policy for approval plan profiles
collecting scope for the archives
faculty asked us to buy everything

atoms.obligation: Define collecting scope by subject, geography, time period, language and format, and state the depth intended for each area.
atoms.lesson: Depth is usually expressed on a scale from minimal holdings, through instructional support, up to research and comprehensive levels, and only a handful of areas at any institution justify the top levels. Archival scope adds a further axis: which creators, communities and functions the repository documents, agreed with neighbouring repositories so that two institutions are not competing for the same papers. Explicit exclusions are as useful as inclusions when a would-be donor arrives with a shed full of material.

atoms.obligation: Decline offers that fall outside scope promptly and in writing, and suggest a more appropriate home where one exists.
atoms.lesson: Accepting out-of-scope material to avoid an awkward conversation costs shelf space, processing hours and preservation budget forever. A declination letter thanks the offerer, states the scope reason without disparaging the material, and names other repositories, historical societies or subject collections that do collect it. Where the material is significant but the repository cannot take it, offering to record a referral or take digital surrogates preserves goodwill without accepting custody.

atoms.obligation: Tie budget allocation to enrolment, use and cost data rather than historical shares, and review the split annually.
atoms.lesson: Weight allocations by measurable factors such as programme enrolment and degree levels, circulation and download use, average unit cost in the discipline, and inflation rates which differ sharply between science and humanities publishing. Continuing commitments to serials and databases must be carved out first, because they consume most of the budget before a single monograph is ordered, and their annual uplift needs a named source rather than a silent squeeze on book funds.

atoms.obligation: Publish a written reconsideration procedure and keep contested material available while a challenge is under review.
atoms.lesson: A defensible procedure asks the complainant to submit a form identifying the specific work and objection, routes it to a review committee that reads the whole work, weighs it against the stated selection criteria and professional reviews, and issues a written decision with an appeal route. The material stays on the shelf during review; removing it first concedes the point. Document each challenge, since patterns of coordinated challenges shape staffing and governing-board briefing.

name: weeding-deselection-review
description: Reviews circulating and reference collections for withdrawal, using age, use, condition, duplication and last-copy considerations. Use when shelves are overfull, when running a deselection list for a branch or subject area, when superseded editions accumulate, or when deciding what to do with withdrawn volumes and how to explain the decision to faculty or the public.
expansions: shelves are overflowing in the six hundreds
run a weeding list for the branch
has not circulated since 2011
last copy in the consortium
superseded editions on the shelf
faculty upset about discards
duplicate print runs after digitization
what to do with withdrawn books

atoms.obligation: Combine an age and use threshold with a physical inspection at the shelf before withdrawing any title.
atoms.lesson: Candidate lists built on years since last circulation and years since publication catch the bulk of dead stock, but the shelf check catches what data misses: a local author, an annotated copy, a title with a broken spine that still circulates, a classic whose currency does not expire. Ageing criteria vary sharply by subject, with medicine, technology, law and travel needing frequent replacement while literature, history and philosophy age gently and should not be weeded on date alone.

atoms.obligation: Check whether the copy is the last one locally or regionally before discarding, and offer it for retention where it is.
atoms.lesson: Shared print and consortial retention commitments obligate members to keep an agreed number of copies for a fixed term, so a title that looks unused locally may be the region insurance copy. Before withdrawal, check the shared catalogue for the number of retained copies and any retention flag on the item, and check whether the title carries a scarcity signal such as few holdings nationally. Withdrawal of a scarce item is effectively a preservation decision and belongs with special collections, not routine weeding.

atoms.obligation: Consult subject specialists and teaching staff on the candidate list, with a stated review window and a clear decision owner.
atoms.lesson: Weeding conflicts are almost always about process rather than particular books. Circulate lists early with the criteria attached, give a defined period for objections, and be explicit that the library makes the final decision and that a faculty save request needs a reason tied to teaching or research need. Keep a record of what was saved by request so the same titles can be reviewed later with evidence about whether the retention was justified.

atoms.obligation: Process withdrawn items so they cannot re-enter as library property, and dispose of them under the stated policy.
atoms.lesson: Withdrawal means removing the item record and holdings from the catalogue, deleting or suppressing it from discovery, and marking the physical volume as withdrawn so a returned copy is not reshelved. Disposal routes typically run to a book sale, a donation partner, a subject exchange or recycling; items bought with grant or gift funds may carry conditions. Never leave withdrawn stock in staff areas indefinitely, because unlabelled discards reliably drift back onto the shelves.

name: e-resource-license-review
description: Reviews and negotiates the terms of a licence for a database, journal package or ebook platform before signing. Use when a vendor sends an agreement, when checking whether interlibrary lending or course reserve use is permitted, when perpetual and post-cancellation access is missing, or when a renewal price rise needs a terms-based response.
expansions: vendor sent a license to sign
does this license allow interlibrary loan
no perpetual access clause
walk in users are not covered
text mining rights in the agreement
renewal price jumped eighteen percent
course reserves clause is unclear
indemnification clause worries legal

atoms.obligation: Check that the definition of authorised users covers every group the institution actually serves, including walk-in visitors.
atoms.lesson: A definition limited to current staff and enrolled students silently excludes alumni, emeritus faculty, hospital residents, visiting researchers, contractors and the public using terminals on site. Walk-in access matters for publicly funded and depository libraries and is usually granted only for on-premises use. Also check whether authentication by address ranges or federated login is permitted and whether remote access for authorised users is explicitly allowed, since some agreements still restrict use to the physical campus.

atoms.obligation: Confirm that the licence permits interlibrary supply, course reserves, and teaching use rather than forbidding them silently.
atoms.lesson: Many agreements narrow lawful uses that copyright exceptions would otherwise permit. Look for permission to supply a single article copy to another library, to place material in a course management system or on electronic reserve, to make copies for classroom use, and to use excerpts in coursepacks. A clause stating that the agreement supersedes statutory exceptions should be struck or qualified with wording preserving rights under applicable copyright law, because otherwise the contract governs.

atoms.obligation: Require perpetual and post-cancellation access terms in writing, naming the content covered and the delivery mechanism.
atoms.lesson: Subscription without perpetual rights means that cancelling ends access to years already paid for. Terms should state which volumes are covered, how access continues after termination, whether by continued hosting, a fee-based hosting arrangement, or file delivery, and which preservation archive the content is deposited in. Verify the preservation deposit claim rather than accepting it, since a promise of archiving is worthless if the title is not actually enrolled in the archive.

atoms.obligation: Push back on indemnification, confidentiality and governing law clauses that the institution cannot lawfully accept.
atoms.lesson: Public institutions frequently cannot indemnify a vendor, cannot agree to a foreign or out-of-state governing law, and cannot bind themselves beyond an annual appropriation. Non-disclosure clauses on price should be resisted because they prevent benchmarking. Route these clauses to institutional counsel or procurement rather than negotiating them at the librarian desk, and keep a file of previously accepted alternate wording so the same battles are not refought at every renewal.

name: interlibrary-loan-mediation
description: Handles borrowing and lending requests between libraries, including copyright compliance, unfilled requests, conditional lending and purchase-instead decisions. Use when a reader needs an article by a deadline, when a request keeps bouncing unfilled, when a request would exceed copyright limits, or when another library asks to borrow something fragile or valuable.
expansions: patron needs an article by friday
the request keeps coming back unfilled
sixth article from the same journal
lend a rare volume to another library
borrower wants a whole book scanned
copyright compliance for loan copies
conditional lending for in library use
buy it instead of borrowing

atoms.obligation: Verify and complete the citation before sending a request, resolving the volume, year, pagination and correct title.
atoms.lesson: The great majority of unfilled requests are bad citations: a truncated journal title, a year that belongs to a different volume, an article that appeared in a supplement, or a chapter attributed to a book the author only edited. Check the citation against an index or the publisher site, supply a standard identifier where one exists, and note the exact edition needed. A verified request routes automatically and fills in days; an unverified one bounces through lenders for a week.

atoms.obligation: Track copies requested from a single journal title within the current year and stop before the limit is exceeded.
atoms.lesson: The widely used guideline treats more than five copies from articles published in the last five years of a single periodical title, within one calendar year, as exceeding fair borrowing. Beyond that the library must own the issue, buy the article, or acquire a licence. Keep the count per title rather than per requester, record whether each request was filled under the guideline or under a licence, and use a title that repeatedly hits the limit as evidence for subscribing.

atoms.obligation: Set explicit lending conditions for fragile, rare or heavily used items instead of refusing or lending unconditionally.
atoms.lesson: Conditional lending lets material circulate while managing risk: supervised use only in the borrower reading room, no photocopying, use of a book cradle, a shortened loan period, or a surrogate supplied in place of the original. Special collections generally lend only for exhibition under a facility report, not for reading room use. State conditions on the shipping paperwork, insure to a declared value, and require the borrower to confirm the item was returned in the same housing.

atoms.obligation: Compare the cost and speed of borrowing against purchase or document delivery, and buy when purchase wins.
atoms.lesson: A recent monograph requested twice, or an article available for a modest fee against a multi-day wait, is usually cheaper bought than borrowed once staff time and shipping are counted. Purchase-on-demand programmes set thresholds by price, publication date and format, and route the item to the requester first and the shelf afterwards. For urgent article needs, licensed document delivery or a pay-per-view purchase meets the deadline where a lending queue cannot.

name: reference-interview-protocol
description: Structures the conversation that turns a vague or misstated question into an answerable one, at the desk, on the phone or in chat. Use when a reader asks for everything on a topic, when a chat question gives no context, when a genealogy or legal question arrives, or when a search failed and the real need was never established.
expansions: patron asks a very vague question
chat reference question is unclear
researcher wants everything on a topic
genealogy question at the desk
what did the patron actually need
hand off a question to a specialist
phone question about a legal form
follow up after the search failed

atoms.obligation: Open with questions that invite description rather than yes or no answers, and let the reader restate the need.
atoms.lesson: The presented question is rarely the real one: a request for books on the Civil War often means a school assignment with a page count and a due date, and a request for a map often means a property boundary dispute. Ask what they would like to know about the topic, what they have already found, and what they will do with it. Avoid leading with the catalogue; a search launched before the need is clear commits the interview to the wrong track.

atoms.obligation: Establish the scope, format and depth needed, including deadline, quantity, currency and acceptable formats.
atoms.lesson: Answering well requires knowing whether the reader needs one fact or a literature review, whether a 1920s source is acceptable or only recent research, whether they can use microfilm, whether they can travel to a remote store, and when they need it. A researcher flying in on Thursday needs paging and reading room capacity checked now. A student needing three peer-reviewed articles by tonight needs a different answer from a dissertation writer needing exhaustive coverage.

atoms.obligation: Keep questions neutral and avoid probing why the reader wants the information beyond what the search requires.
atoms.lesson: Reader confidentiality is a professional obligation and in many jurisdictions circulation and reference records have legal protection. Ask only what refines the search, do not record identifying details of the enquiry beyond what a follow-up needs, and handle sensitive subjects such as health, immigration status, addiction or legal trouble without commentary. When a question calls for professional advice in law, medicine or tax, supply the sources and the referral rather than an interpretation.

atoms.obligation: Confirm at the close that the answer met the need, and offer a defined next step when it did not.
atoms.lesson: The follow-up question, asking whether this completely answers the question, is the single step most often skipped and the one that catches misunderstandings before the reader leaves. Where the search failed, say what was searched and what was not, and offer a concrete route: an interlibrary request, a referral to a subject specialist or another repository, a scheduled consultation, or a request the reader can leave for later research. Record unanswered questions, since they show collection gaps.

name: information-literacy-lesson
description: Plans and evaluates teaching sessions for classes and workshops, from learning outcomes through activities to assessment. Use when a one-shot session is scheduled, when an instructor asks for a database demonstration, when students cannot evaluate sources, or when a lecture-heavy workshop needs rebuilding as active learning.
expansions: one shot session next tuesday
faculty wants a database demo
write learning outcomes for the class
students cannot evaluate sources
activity for a fifty minute session
assess whether the session worked
embed instruction in a writing course
redo a lecture heavy workshop

atoms.obligation: Agree the assignment and the students current difficulty with the instructor before designing anything for the session.
atoms.lesson: Ask for the assignment prompt, the due date, what students have already been taught, and where previous cohorts struggled, because these determine everything else. A session pitched at finding scholarly articles is wasted on a class whose actual problem is narrowing a topic or reading a citation. Confirm what the instructor will do before and after the visit, since a session with no assignment attached and no follow-up produces almost no measurable change in student work.

atoms.obligation: Write two or three observable outcomes for the session and cut any content that does not serve them.
atoms.lesson: Outcomes stated as what students will be able to do, using verbs such as distinguish, construct, evaluate or locate, make both design and assessment possible. Two or three is the realistic ceiling for fifty minutes. Framing concepts such as authority being constructed and contextual, and searching as strategic exploration, give the conceptual anchor, but the outcome must be concrete enough to observe in the room, for example that students can turn a research question into search terms with alternatives.

atoms.obligation: Give students something to do with their own topic during the session rather than demonstrating searches from the front.
atoms.lesson: Watching an expert search teaches confidence, not skill. Replace demonstration with short cycles: a two-minute think-pair-share on where authority comes from in this discipline, a keyword brainstorm on their own topic, a worksheet comparing two sources retrieved for the same query, a live search students run while the librarian circulates. Reserve the projector for a single modelled example and hand the keyboard over, keeping database mechanics to what the immediate task requires.

atoms.obligation: Collect evidence of learning during the session and share the results with the instructor afterwards.
atoms.lesson: Usable classroom assessment is small: collect the search-term worksheets, run a one-minute paper asking the muddiest point, or use a short poll on a source-evaluation judgement. Reading the artefacts shows whether the outcome landed and what to change next time. Sending the instructor a brief note with what students found hard is also the most reliable way to be invited back and to move from a one-shot visit towards embedded instruction across the course.

name: digitization-imaging-spec
description: Sets the capture specification for a digitisation project, covering resolution, colour, targets, file naming, derivatives and handling of fragile originals. Use when deciding what resolution suits glass negatives or bound volumes, when writing a specification for an outside imaging vendor, when images look colour-shifted, or when quality checking a delivered batch.
expansions: what resolution for these glass negatives
write a digitization spec for a vendor
scanner settings for bound volumes
colour target in every batch
the images look washed out
file naming for a scanning project
digitize oversize maps
quality check a vendor delivery

atoms.obligation: Set capture resolution from the size and detail of the original rather than applying one number to everything.
atoms.lesson: Reflective textual material is commonly captured so that the smallest significant detail is well resolved, often around four hundred pixels per inch for typical documents, while photographic prints go higher and small-format negatives and transparencies are captured at a resolution that yields a comparable pixel dimension across the frame. Oversize maps are specified by long-edge pixel count as much as by density. The test is whether the file supports the intended use, including reading fine annotations and printing at scale.
